body.translated_text: Reference: Jaim_ = <s>Jaimini</s>, <s>Mīmāṃsāsūtra</s>

body.text: (?) = unclear
body.translated_text: (?) = unclear

body.text: śāstradīpikā /
body.translated_text: <s>Śāstradīpikā</s> (The Lamp of the Science) /

body.text: prathamādhyāye prathamastarkapādaḥ /
body.translated_text: In the first chapter (<s>adhyāya</s>), the first reasoning section (<s>tarkapāda</s>):

body.text: lakṣmīkaustubhavakṣasaṃ muraripuṃ śaṅkhāsikaumodakīhastaṃ padmapalāśatāmranayanaṃ pītāmbara śārṅgiṇam /
body.translated_text: He whose chest bears <s>Lakṣmī</s> and the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem, the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, holding conch, sword, and <s>modaka</s> in his hands,

body.text: medhaśyāmamudārapīvaracaturbāhuṃ pradhānātparaṃ śrīvatsāṅkamanāthanāthamamṛtaṃ vande mukundaṃ mudā //1 //
body.translated_text: with lotus-petal-reddish eyes, wearing yellow garments, bearing the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, dark as a rain-cloud, generous, with four mighty arms, supreme beyond <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> sign, the Lord of the lordless, immortal—I joyfully bow to <s>Mukunda</s>. ||1||

children.text: nyāyābhāsatamaśchannaśāstratattvārthadarśikām /
children.translated_text: Illuminating the true meaning of the science (<s>śāstra</s>), which has been concealed by the darkness of fallacious reasoning (<s>nyāyābhāsa</s>),

children.text: kumārilamatenāhaṃ kariṣye śāstradīpikām //2 //
children.translated_text: I shall compose this <s>Śāstradīpikā</s> (Lamp of the Science) following the doctrine of <s>Kumārila</s>. ||2||

body.text: athāto dharmajijñāsā // Jaim_1,1.1 //
body.translated_text: 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>.' || <s>Jaimini</s> 1.1.1 ||

children.text: anena sūtreṇa prārīpsitasya śāstrasya śrotṛpravṛttisiddhaye dharmajñānaṃ prayojanaṃ kathyate /
children.translated_text: By this sūtra, the knowledge of <s>dharma</s> is stated as the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) for engaging the student in the desired science.

children.text: yadā hi dharmajijñāsā kartavyetyukte śāstramārabhyamāṇaṃ dṛśyate tadā nūnamidaṃ śāstraṃ dharmajñānaprayojanamityavagamyate* ////
children.translated_text: For when 'the inquiry into <s>dharma</s> is to be undertaken' is stated, and a science is seen being commenced, it is understood that 'this science surely has the knowledge of <s>dharma</s> as its purpose.'

body.text:
viditaṃ tāvatprayojanam /
saṃbandho 'pi śāstrasya prastāvaheturvaktavyaḥ /
yathā śastrāntareṣu śiṣyapraśnānantaryādisaṃbandhaḥ prastāvako varṇyate tathehāpi śāstrārambhe śiṣyapraśnānantaryādisaṃbandhaḥ prastāvako varṇyate tathehāpi śāstrārambhe prayojakānāṃ saṃbandhānāmanyatamo vaktavyaḥ- anena saṃbandhenedaṃ śāstramāyātamiti /
anyathā hyasaṃbaddhapralapitaṃ syāt /

children.text: satyam /
children.translated_text: True.

children.text: ihatu ya evāyaṃ prayojanena saha śāstrasya sādhyasādhanatvasaṃbandhaḥ sa eva śāstrasya prastāvako nānyaḥ /
children.translated_text: But here, the very relationship of the science with its purpose—the relation of means and end (<s>sādhyasādhanatva</s>)—is itself the occasion for the science, not another.

children.text: bhavati hi sādhanatvameva sādhyārthinaḥ sādhane pravṛttihetuḥ /
children.translated_text: For it is indeed the instrumentality [of the science] that is the cause of the aspirant's engagement in the means [of achieving the end].

children.text: sacāyaṃ saṃbandhaḥ prayojanoktyaivārthajjñāyata iti na sūtrakāreṇa pṛthagukta ityadoṣaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: And this connection is known by implication from the mere statement of the purpose; hence, there is no fault in the sūtra-author not having stated it separately.

body.translated_text: The purpose is thus understood. The connection (<s>sambandha</s>) of the science too, being the occasion for its commencement, must be stated. Just as in other sciences, a connection such as the student's question or [the text's] sequence is described as the occasion, so here too, at the commencement of the science, one of the motivating connections must be stated—[namely] 'through this connection this science has come about.' Otherwise, it would be incoherent babbling.

body.text:
atredaṃ cintyate- kimadhyayanānantaraṃ dharmajijñāsayā gurugṛhe 'sthātavyam, uta gurugṛhātsamāvartitavyamiti /
yadi hi svādhyāyādhyayanavidhinā dharmamātrārthamadhyayanaṃ svardādyarthena vidhīyate tatasmānmātreṇaiva śāstrārthasya samāptatvāt 'adhītyasnāyāt' iti smṛtivacanabalena ca samāvartitavyamiti /
body.translated_text: Here this is to be considered: after completing Vedic study (<s>adhyayana</s>), should one remain at the teacher's house for the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>, or should one return home from the teacher's house? For if Vedic study is enjoined by the self-study injunction (<s>svādhyāyādhyayanavidhi</s>) merely for [the unseen merit of] <s>dharma</s>, and is [separately] enjoined for the purpose of heaven and the like, then since the purpose of the science is accomplished by that [study] alone, and by the force of the <s>smṛti</s> statement 'having studied, one should bathe [i.e., graduate],' one should return home.

body.text: adhyayanavidhivicāraḥ /
body.translated_text: Examination of the Vedic-study injunction:

children.text: athākṣaragrahaṇādiparamparopajāyamānavākyārthajñānārthamadhyayanaṃ vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: But if Vedic study is enjoined for the purpose of knowledge of the meaning of sentences, arising through the succession beginning with the apprehension of syllables—

children.text: tatastasya vicāramantareṇāsaṃbhavādadhyayanavidhinaivārthādvicāro vihita iti gurugṛha evāvasthāya vicārayitavyo dharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: then, since [meaning-knowledge] is impossible without inquiry (<s>vicāra</s>), inquiry is implicitly enjoined by the study-injunction itself; therefore, one should remain at the teacher's house and inquire into <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tatra- 'vināpi vidhinā jñānalābhānnahi tadarthatā //
children.translated_text: On this, [the objection is]: 'Since knowledge is obtained even without an injunction, there is no purposefulness [for an injunction];

body.text: kalpyastu vighisāmarthyātsvargo viśvajidādivat'* ////
body.translated_text: but a result should be postulated from the capacity of the subsidiary [ritual], like heaven in the case of the <s>Viśvajit</s> and similar [rites].'

body.text:
svādhyāyasaṃskāradvāreṇādhyayanasyārthajñānahetutvaṃ vinaiva vidhinā pramāṇāntareṇa siddhameveti tādardhye vidhyānarthakyam /
nacāvaghātādividhivanniyamārthatvam /
avadhāto hi darśapūrṇamāsapūrve niyamyate /
avaghātaniṣpannaireva taṇḍulairapūrvaṃ sidhyatīti na taṇḍulasvarūpe, pramāṇāntaravirodhāt /
tadvadihāpi jñānasyādhyayanamantareṇāpi darśanāttatsvarūpe niyamāsaṃbhavāt kratvapūrveṣvevādhyayananiyamo vidhātavyaḥ /

children.text: adhītaireva vedairavagatāni karmāṇi phaladānīti /
children.translated_text: —[meaning that] the rituals known through the Vedas that have been studied are productive of results.

children.text: nacaivaṃ yuktam /
children.translated_text: But this is not correct.

children.text: akratvarthatvādadhyayanasya anārabhyādhītatvāt, śrutyādyabhāvāccākratvarthatvam /
children.translated_text: Because study is not for the purpose of ritual (<s>akratvarthatva</s>), since it is not commenced for [ritual purposes]; and the non-ritual-purpose is [established] because of the absence of <s>śruti</s> and other [evidence for the ritual purpose].

children.text: tasmādadṛṣṭārthameva svādhyāyādhyayanamityadhyayanamātreṇa samāpte śāstrārthe gurugṛhātsamāvartitavyamiti prāpte 'bhidhīyate- 'labhyamāne phale dṛṣṭe nādṛṣṭaparikalpanā //
children.translated_text: Therefore, self-study and Vedic recitation are only for unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>). When the conclusion is reached that one should return home from the teacher's house since the purpose of the science is accomplished by study alone—it is replied: 'When a visible result is obtainable, one should not postulate an unseen [result];

body.translated_text: Since the instrumentality of study for knowledge of meaning, through the conditioning effected by self-study, is already established by other means of valid knowledge without any injunction, an injunction for that purpose would be purposeless. Nor can it serve the purpose of restriction (<s>niyama</s>), as in the case of the threshing injunction. For threshing is restricted to [the rite] preceded by the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new and full moon) sacrifice—since the unseen merit is accomplished only with rice grains produced by threshing; [the restriction] does not apply to the nature of the grains themselves, because it would contradict other means of valid knowledge. Similarly here too, since knowledge is observed even without study, restriction to the nature [of knowledge itself] is impossible; therefore, the restriction of study should be applied only to ritual performances (<s>kratvapūrvas</s>)—

body.text: vidheśca niyamārthatvānnānarthakyaṃ bhaviṣyati* ////
body.translated_text: and since the injunction has the purpose of restriction, there will be no purposelessness.'

children.text: tathāhi asatyadhyayanavidhāvagnihotrādiśāstrāṇi vidvāṃsamalabhamānānyavidvāṃsamevādhikṛtya vidyāmantareṇānuṣṭhānāsaṃbhavādvidyāmākṣipatyaviśeṣāccaturo varṇānadhikuryuḥ /
children.translated_text: For thus: if there were no study-injunction, the scriptures on <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, not finding a learned person [to perform them], would have to authorize even an unlearned person, and since performance is impossible without knowledge, they would implicitly require knowledge, and without distinction would authorize all four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes).

children.text: satitvadhyayanavidhau traivarṇikānāmeva viduṣāmadhikāro bhavati na turīyādeḥ* ////
children.translated_text: But when there is a study-injunction, [ritual] authority belongs only to the learned among the three [upper] <s>varṇas</s>, not to the fourth and so on.

body.text:
tathāhi- vasante brāhmaṇamupanayīta, grīṣme rājanyaṃ, śaradivaiśyam' iti dvitīyānirdeśādupanayanasaṃskṛtāstraivarṇikāḥ kimasmābhiḥ kartavyamityapekṣante /
tatsaṃnidhau cādhyayanamanirdiṣṭakartṛkaṃ vidhīyamānaṃ kartāramapekṣate /
body.translated_text: For thus: 'One should initiate a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in spring, a <s>kṣatriya</s> in summer, a <s>vaiśya</s> in autumn'—since the accusative case-ending [in this rule] indicates that the three <s>varṇas</s> who have undergone the <s>upanayana</s> sacrament are the ones who expect [to know] 'what is to be done by us?' And in that context, the study-injunction, being enjoined without specifying an agent, requires an agent.

body.text:
tatrāpekṣāsaṃnidhiyogyatvairevaṃ vijñāyate- traivarṇikairevopanītairakṣaragrahaṇenādhyayanādiparamparayārthajñānaṃ kartavyamiti /
evañca phalavadadhyayanakarkatṛbhūtamāṇavasaṃskāratvādupanayanamadhyayanīṅgaṃ, adhyayanamapi dṛṣṭārthajñānārtham, arthajñānaṃ tvanuṣṭhānaupayikatvātprasiddhaphalakameveti sarveṣāṃ phalavattvam /
body.translated_text: There, from expectancy, proximity, and fitness, it is understood thus: the three <s>varṇas</s> who have been initiated should, through the apprehension of syllables and the successive process of study, acquire knowledge of meaning. And thus: <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), being a sacrament of the boy who is the agent of the fruitful study, is an ancillary to study; study too is for the purpose of visible knowledge of meaning; and knowledge of meaning, being conducive to performance, is of well-known fruitfulness—thus all [these stages] are fruitful.

body.text: adhyayanādhikāraniyamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Restriction of authority for Vedic study:

children.text: evañca traivarṇikeṣu vidvasu labdheṣu nāgnihotrādividhayaścaturthavarṇasya vidyāmākṣipanti, kintu traivārṇikāneva viduṣo 'dhikurvanti /
children.translated_text: And thus, when learned persons among the three <s>varṇas</s> are obtained, the injunctions of <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like do not implicitly require knowledge for the fourth <s>varṇa</s>, but rather authorize only the learned among the three <s>varṇas</s>.

children.text: so 'yamadhikāraniyamo 'paśūdrādhikaraṇe vakṣyamāṇo 'dhyayanavidhiprasādalabhya iti phalavāneva vidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: This restriction of authority, to be discussed in the <s>Apaśūdrādhikaraṇa</s> (the section on the exclusion of <s>Śūdras</s>), is obtained through the blessing of the study-injunction—thus the injunction is indeed fruitful.

children.text: tenārthajñānāvasānamadhyayanamadhyayanavidhinā vidhīyata iti vicāramantareṇa tadanupapatteradhyayanavidhireva vicāramākṣipaṃstadviruddhaṃ smārtā snānaṃ bādhayata iti siddhamadhyayanānantaraṃ dharmajijñāsā kartavyeti* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, study culminating in knowledge of meaning is enjoined by the study-injunction; and since this is impossible without inquiry, the study-injunction itself, by implicitly requiring inquiry, overrides the <s>smṛti</s>-prescribed [graduation] bathing which contradicts it. Thus it is established that after study, the inquiry into <s>dharma</s> is to be undertaken.

body.text: kecitpunarācāryakaraṇavidhiprayuktatvamadhyayanasyāṅgīkṛtya kimācāryakasiddhirevādhyayanasya prayojanamutārthajñānamiti vicārya
body.translated_text: Some, however, accepting that study is motivated by the teacher-making injunction (<s>ācāryakaraṇavidhi</s>), inquire whether the accomplishment of teacher-status alone is the purpose of study, or knowledge of meaning—

children.text: antaraṅgatvādarthajñānamityāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: and they say: knowledge of meaning, because it is more proximate (<s>antaraṅga</s>).

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇamācāryakaraṇavidhiprayuktatve 'dhyayanasya, adhyayanavidheradhikāriśūnyatvādācāryakaraṇavidhiprayuktyā cātmalābhe viśvajidādivatphalakalpanānupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: But what is the reason for study being motivated by the teacher-making injunction? Because the study-injunction lacks a qualified person [to whom it applies], and because, when the self is obtained through the motivation of the teacher-making injunction, the postulation of a result like the <s>Viśvajit</s> is improper.

children.text: kaḥ punarācāryakaraṇavidhiḥ, kathaṃ vā tenādhyayanasya prayuktiḥ /
children.translated_text: What then is the teacher-making injunction, and how does it motivate study?

children.text: ucyate- upanīya tu yaḥ śiṣyaṃ vedamadhyāpayeddvijaḥ //
children.translated_text: It is said: 'The twice-born who, having initiated a student, teaches him the <s>Veda</s>

body.text: sakalpaṃ sahahasyaṃ ca tamācārya pracakṣate //
body.translated_text: together with the ritual instructions (<s>kalpa</s>) and the secret teachings (<s>rahasya</s>)—him they call the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>).'

body.text:
iti smṛtyanumitaḥ /
upanīyādhyāpanenācāryakaṃ kuryād' ityācāryakaraṇavidhiḥ /
atra cādhyāpanamācāryatvasādhanam /

children.text: upanayanaṃ tu ktvāpratyayāttasyaivāṅgam /
children.translated_text: And <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), by the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix [indicating 'having done X'], is an ancillary of that very [instruction].

children.text: tacca kena dvāreṇādhyāpalasyopakarotītyapekṣāyāṃ upaneyāsattirevājya dvāramaṅgīkriyate liṅgāt /
children.translated_text: When the question arises through what means initiation assists instruction, it is accepted that the mere proximity of the person to be initiated serves as the means, based on textual indication (<s>liṅga</s>).

children.text: tadupaneyo 'pi nākiñcitkaro 'ṅgamiti tadvyāpāratvenādhyavasīyate /
children.translated_text: Thus the person to be initiated too is not functionless, but is understood as serving in that capacity [of being an ancillary].

children.text: tadevaṃ svāṅgabhūtamupanayanaṃ prayuñjāno 'dhyāpanavidhistaddvāreṇādhyayanaṃ prayuṅkte* ////
children.translated_text: Thus the instruction-injunction, employing <s>upanayana</s> as its own ancillary, through that [upanayana] motivates study.

body.translated_text: —this is inferred from <s>smṛti</s>. 'Having initiated, one should make oneself a teacher through instruction'—this is the teacher-making injunction. Here, instruction (<s>adhyāpana</s>) is the means of attaining teacherhood.

children.text: tadetadanupapannam /
children.translated_text: But this is untenable.

children.text: tathāhi- niyogārthasyādhyayanasyācāryakaprayojanārthajñānaprayojanatā vā na śakyate śāstreṇa bodhayituṃ sādhyadvayasyaikatrāsaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: For thus: it is not possible for the science to convey that study, which is the object of an injunction, has both the purpose of teacher-status and the purpose of knowledge of meaning—since two objects to be accomplished cannot [both] reside in one [injunction].

children.text: niyogārthataiva śāstreṇa bodhyate arthajñānārthatāyāṃ tvanujñāmātramiticet tathāpyarthadvayaṃ syādeva* ////
children.translated_text: If [one says] only the injunctive purpose is conveyed by the science, and the purpose of knowledge of meaning is merely a permission (<s>anujñā</s>)—even so, there would be two objects.

body.text:
kiñcaivaṃ sakṛduccaritasya liṅpratyayasya vidhyarthatvamanujñārthatvaṃ ceti vairūpyamapi syāt tena saṃśaya evānupapannaḥ /
tathā siddhānto 'pyanupapanna eva- pramāṇāntarasiddhatvādarthajñānārthatvaṃ na śāstragocaratāmanubhavatīti /

children.text: tatra yadevāsmadabhipretaṃ vidherniyamārthatvaṃ mahatā prayatnena bhavadbhirdūṣitaṃ tadeva bhavadbhirapi muktalajjairananyagatikatvādāśrayaṇīyamāpannam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the doctrinal conclusion too would be untenable: since the purpose of knowledge of meaning, being established by other means of valid knowledge, does not fall within the scope of the science.

children.text: niyamānaṅgīkāre ca pūrvapakṣa eva śreyānāpadyate /
children.translated_text: There, what we hold—that the injunction has the purpose of restriction—which was refuted by you with great effort—that very [position] must be resorted to even by you, shamelessly, having no alternative.

children.text: ācāryatvasyādṛṣṭatvena prayojanatopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: And if restriction is not accepted, the prima facie position alone turns out to be preferable,

children.text: arthajñānārthatve cādhyayanaṃ svādhyāyasaṃskāro niyogārthatve tu pradhānakarmeti vairūpyamapi syāt* ////
children.translated_text: because the purpose of teacher-status, being unseen, can be established [as the result]. And if [study is] for knowledge of meaning, study would be a subsidiary purificatory rite (<s>svādhyāyasaṃskāra</s>), whereas if for an injunctive purpose, it would be a principal ritual action—this dual character too would arise.

body.translated_text: Moreover, thus the optative suffix (<s>liṅ-pratyaya</s>), uttered only once, would have the dual character of being both injunctive and permissive—and therefore even the doubt [about its function] would be untenable.

body.text:
arthājjātamarthajñānaṃ prayojanaṃ na śāstrata iticet, ācāryatvamapi prayojanaṃ na syāt tasyāpyarthājjātatvāt /
smṛtibādhena ca snānotkarṣo na syādaśāstrasvīkṛtatvādvicārasya /
body.translated_text: If [one says] knowledge of meaning is the purpose [arising] by implication, not from the science—then teacher-status too should not be the purpose, since it too arises by implication. And there would be no superiority of bathing [being overridden] by the <s>smṛti</s>, since inquiry has not been accepted by the science.

body.text: adhyayanavidhau niyojyakalpanā /
body.translated_text: Postulation of the person to be enjoined in the study-injunction:

children.text: kiñca- niyojyaḥ kalpanīyo 'tra vidhyarthānupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover: a person to be enjoined (<s>niyojya</s>) must be postulated here, [since otherwise] the purpose of the injunction would not be established.

children.text: nacopanayanasyāṅgabhāvo 'styadhyāpanaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: And <s>upanayana</s> does not have ancillary status with respect to instruction (<s>adhyāpana</s>).

children.text: dvitīyāśrutisāmarthyātsā māṇavakasaṃskriyā //
children.translated_text: By the force of the accusative case in the <s>śruti</s>, that sacrament is for the boy.

body.text: tathāsatyantaraṅgatvādaṅgamadhyayanasya tat* ////
body.translated_text: And if that is so, then that [<s>upanayana</s>], being more proximate, is an ancillary of study [for the boy].

body.text:
yattāvanniyojyābhāvādaprayojakatvamadhyayanavirodheriti, tadayuktaṃ, abhāvāsiddheḥ, aśrutasyāpi viśvajitādivatkalpanāt /
kāryaṃ hi vidhyarthaḥ, saṃbandhiśabdaścāyaṃ kāryamiti, kasyaciddhi kiñcitkāryaṃ
body.translated_text: As for [the objection] that the study-injunction is purposeless because there is no person to be enjoined—that is improper, because the absence [of such a person] is not established, since even what is not stated [in the text] can be postulated, as in the case of the <s>Viśvajit</s> and similar [rites]. For the object of an injunction is what is to be done (<s>kārya</s>); and this word '<s>kārya</s>' is a relational term, for something is to be done for someone—not everything for everyone. Therefore there is the expectation of a related [party]: 'for whom is this to be done?' That [expectation] must necessarily be fulfilled by some supplied [agent]: 'this is to be done by him'—he for whom this is to be done is called the person to be enjoined (<s>niyojya</s>).

body.text: bhavati na sarvaṃ sarvasya, ataḥ kasyedaṃ kāryamityasti saṃbandhyapekṣā, sāvaśyamadhyāhṛtena kenacinnivartanīyā- asyedaṃ kāryamiti, yasyedaṃ kāryaṃ sa eva niyojya ityucyate* ////

children.text: yadyapi kathañcitparaprayuktānuṣṭhānādevātmalābhaḥ syāt, tathāpi na tāvatā kāryatvaṃ sidhyati /
children.translated_text: Even if the attainment of selfhood [teacher-status] were somehow accomplished merely through performance motivated by another, still, by that alone, the character of being 'to be done' (<s>kāryatva</s>) is not established.

children.text: nahi kṛtisādhyatāmātraṃ kāryatvam /
children.translated_text: For mere accomplishability through effort is not what constitutes being 'to be done.'

children.text: kiṃ tarhi, yatkṛtisādhyaṃ kṛtiṃprati pradhānabhūtaṃ tatkāryamityucyate /
children.translated_text: Rather, what is accomplished through effort and is the principal [aim] with respect to that effort—that is called 'to be done' (<s>kārya</s>).

children.text: prādhānyaṃ ca kṛtestaduddeśena pravṛttiḥ, tataścādhyayananiyogena kāryeṇa bhavatāvaśyaṃ puruṣavyāpāroddeśyena bhavitavyam* ////
children.translated_text: And principality with respect to effort means that activity is directed toward that [aim]; therefore, the duty (<s>kārya</s>) enjoined as study must necessarily be directed toward a human activity as its aim.

body.text:
nacāsati niyojye taduddeśena kaścitpravarteta /
adhyāpanavidhinā hi pravartyamāno māṇavakaḥ kathañcidadhyayanamātramanutiṣṭhannatvapūrvamuddiśet /

children.text: nahi tasya taduddeśyaṃ pramāṇābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: for that [knowledge of meaning] would not be his aim, since there is no means of valid knowledge [establishing it as such for him].

children.text: prayājādyapūrvāṇi darśapūrṇamāsāpūrvopakāritvāttadhikṛtena puruṣeṇa tatsiddhyarthamuddiśya kriyamāṇānīti yuktaṃ yadasatyapi sākṣānniyojyopādāne kāryatvaṃ labhante, adhyayananiyogasya tu nānyaupayikatvaṃ yatastadrūpeṇoddeśyatā syāt /
children.translated_text: It is reasonable that the subsidiary unseen merits of the <s>prayāja</s> and the like obtain the character of being 'to be done' even without the direct mention of a person to be enjoined—because they contribute to the unseen merit of the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, and so the authorized person performs them aiming at the accomplishment of that [main rite]. But the study-injunction has no such subsidiary usefulness that would give it that character of being aimed at [by another injunction].

children.text: arthajñānasya ca niyāmaphalatvena niyogāpekṣatvāt /
children.translated_text: And because knowledge of meaning, having the character of a restrictive result (<s>niyāmaphala</s>), depends on an injunction [to establish it].

children.text: tasmādasya kāryatvasiddhaye 'vaśyaṃ niyojyaḥ kalpanīyaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, for establishing the character of this [study] as 'to be done,' a person to be enjoined must necessarily be postulated.

body.translated_text: And no one would engage toward that [aim] in the absence of a person to be enjoined. For a boy, being directed [merely] by the instruction-injunction, while somehow merely performing study, would aim at his own unseen merit [<s>apūrva</s>]—

children.text: yaccādhyāpanavidherupanayanadvāramadhyayaprayojakatvamuktam, tadapyayuktam- upanayanaprayukterevābhāvāt, taddvāreṇādhyayanaprayuktirdūrāpāstā /
children.translated_text: As for what was said—that the instruction-injunction motivates study through the medium of <s>upanayana</s>—that too is improper, because the motivation of <s>upanayana</s> itself is not established; study-motivation through that medium is far removed.

children.text: ktvāpratyayena hi samānakartṛkatvamevocyate tena caikaprayogatā kalpyate, aṅgāṅgibhāvastvekaprayogatāvaśātkalpanīyaḥ, dvitīyayā tu sākṣādaṅgitvamevocyate, ato yathā trivṛtā yūpaparivyāṇāṃ yūpārthaṃ nopākaraṇārthaṃ evamupanayanamapi māṇavakasaṃskārārthaṃ nādhyāpanārtham /
children.translated_text: For the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix merely states identity of agent; and from that, unity of performance is postulated. The ancillary relationship, however, is to be postulated as a consequence of the unity of performance. But the accusative case directly states ancillary status [of the boy to the rite]. Therefore, just as the wrapping of the sacrificial post with three threads is for the sake of the post, not for the sake of the preparatory rite—so too, <s>upanayana</s> is for the sake of the boy's sacrament, not for the sake of instruction.

children.text: smṛtigataśca ktvā pratyayaḥ, pratyakṣavedagatā tu vasante brāhmaṇam' iti dvatīyā, ato 'pi maṇavakārthatvam* ////
children.translated_text: And the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix belongs to <s>smṛti</s>, whereas the accusative in 'a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in spring' belongs to the directly perceived <s>Veda</s>; therefore, by this too, [<s>upanayana</s>] is for the sake of the boy.

body.text:
bhavatu māṇavakasaṃskārastaddvāreṇa tvadhyāranāṅgaṃ nādhyayanāṅgamiticet, maivaṃ, antaraṅgatvādadhyayanasya tadarthyameva saṃskārasya yuktam /
adhyayanamapi phalavadadhyāpanamapi tayoḥ kasyāyaṃ māṇavakasaṃskāro 'ṅgaṃ bhavatvityapekṣāyāmadhyāpanasya puruṣāntaragāmitvena bahiraṅgatvānmāṇavakagatādhyayanārthatvameva yuktam /
yathaiva hyadhyayanasyācāryakasiddhiprayojanatāmanāhṛtya vedamadhītya snāyād' iti smṛtiṃ bādhitvāntaraṅgatvādarthajñānārthataivāśrīyate, tathopanayanasyāpyadhyayanārthatā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: Even if the <s>māṇavaka</s>-consecration (boy's sacrament) be [accepted], if one objects that through it, it is an auxiliary to study (<s>adhyāpana</s>) and not to learning (<s>adhyayana</s>) — do not say so, for since learning is more intimately connected, it is proper that the sacrament be for its purpose. Learning too has a result, and teaching also — of the two, to which does this boy's [sacrament belong]?

body.text:
vyākaraṇādapi pāṇinīyādadhyayanāṅgataivopanayanasyānagamyate /
adhyayanāṅgatā hi smarannācāryakaraṇe nayaterātmanepadaṃ vidhatte, adhyāpanāṅgatve hi kartrabhiprāyatvātkriyāphalasya tritvādevātmanepadaṃ sidhyet /
'upanīya tu yaḥ śiṣyam' iti ktvāpratyayo hi kathañcit 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāmiṣṭvetivadasatyapyaṅgāṅgibhāve 'vakalpyate punarvidhānaṃ
body.translated_text: Even from grammar — from <s>Pāṇini</s>'s [system] — only the auxiliary relation of <s>upanayana</s> to learning (<s>adhyayana</s>) is understood. For the <s>smṛti</s> that remembers the auxiliary relation to learning prescribes the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) in the verb 'nayati' in the sense of performing as teacher. If it were auxiliary to teaching, then since the result of the action belongs to the agent, the <s>ātmanepada</s> would follow merely from the threefold [agency] —

body.text: cātmanepadasyātyantānarthakam, tasmādadhyayanāṅgamupanayanaṃ syāt* ////
body.translated_text: And the <s>ātmanepada</s> would be utterly meaningless. Therefore, <s>upanayana</s> should be an auxiliary to learning (<s>adhyayana</s>). ////

children.text: na syāt /
children.translated_text: It should not be so.

children.text: tajjanyaḥ saṃskāro hi māṇavakasamavāyī /
children.translated_text: For the sacrament produced by it (<s>upanayana</s>) inheres in the boy.

children.text: satyam, māṇavakasamaveto 'pi na tadarthaḥ, kartrarthatvaṃ ca phalasya kartrabhiprāyatvaṃ natu tatsamavāyaḥ, anyathāhi 'agnīnādadhītetyātmanepadaṃ na syāt- ādhānaphalasyāhavanīyatvāderagnisamavetatvena kartṛsamavāyābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: True, even though it inheres in the boy, it is not for his purpose. And 'belonging to the agent' means that the result is intended by the agent, not that it inheres in him. For otherwise, the <s>ātmanepada</s> in 'he establishes the fires' (<s>agnīnādadhīta</s>) would not obtain — since the result of the <s>ādhāna</s> ritual, namely the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire and the like, inheres in the fire [and not the agent] —

children.text: iyaṃ ca smṛtiḥ 'upanīya tu yaḥ śiṣyam' iti, ato balīyasī dvitīyā śrutiḥ, tasmānnādhyāpanāṅgamupanayanamiti na taddvāreṇādhyāpanasya prayuktiḥ //
children.translated_text: And this <s>smṛti</s> [says]: 'having initiated the pupil' — therefore the second <s>śruti</s> (Vedic text) is stronger. Hence <s>upanayana</s> is not an auxiliary to teaching (<s>adhyāpana</s>), and through it there is no prompting of teaching. //

body.text: prābhākaramatakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the <s>Prābhākara</s> view:

body.text: yacca 'upanītasya vyāpārāpekṣāyāmupanayanaṃ prakramya vihitamadhyayanaṃ tadvyāpāratvenādhyavasīyata' iti, tadapyabuddhipūrvakam- evaṃ hi vadatādhyāpanāṅgamadhyayanamityupapāditaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: And the [claim] that 'when the activity of the initiated person is required, learning (<s>adhyayana</s>), having been enjoined after undertaking <s>upanayana</s>, is ascertained as that activity' — this too is thoughtless. For one who speaks thus establishes that learning is an auxiliary to teaching.

children.text: yadāhyadhyāpanārthatvenopanītasya māṇavakasya tadupayogivyāpārāpekṣāyāmadhyayanavidhiradhyayanaṃ tadupayogivyāpāratayā vidhatte- traivarṇikairupanītairadhyāpanaupayikavyāpārāpekṣairadhyayanavyāpāraḥ kartavya iti tadāpi spaṣṭamevādhyayanamarthajñānārthatayā vidhatte nādhyāpanaupayikatayā, tadāhyadhyayanasya tadaupayikatvaṃ kena pramāṇena gamyate, nahyatra pratyakṣādīni kramante /
children.translated_text: For when, for the boy initiated for the purpose of teaching, there is the need for activity useful to that [teaching], the injunction of learning enjoins the activity of learning as useful to that — [the implication would be that] the three castes, having been initiated, needing activity useful to teaching, should perform the activity of learning —

children.text: saṃnidhānāditi cet, na saṃnidhānaṃ nāma svayaṃ pramāṇaṃ śabdasya tvarthaṃ pratipādayataḥ saṃnidhyapekṣāyogyatvānītikarmatavyatā netrasyevonmīlanam /
children.translated_text: If [one says] 'because of proximity' — no, for proximity is not itself a means of knowledge. Rather, for a word that conveys its meaning, the eligibility for requiring proximity is like the opening of an eye — it is what-is-to-be-done.

children.text: śabdaścedadhyāpanaupayikatayā vidadhyāt nārthajñānārthatā sidhyet /
children.translated_text: If the word were to enjoin [learning] as useful to teaching, then its purpose of conveying meaning would not be established.

children.text: ato nopanayanasaṃnidhau 'svādhyāyo 'dhyetavya' iti vihitasyādhyayanasyopanayanadvārādhyāpanavidhinā prayuktisaṃbhavaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no possibility of the prompting of learning — enjoined [by the text] 'one's own Veda is to be studied' (<s>svādhyāyo'dhyetavyaḥ</s>) — in proximity to <s>upanayana</s>, through the injunction of teaching. ////

body.text:
yadi paramadhyāpanasyādhyayanamantareṇāsaṃbhavāttadarthādhyayanamākṣipyate, tathāsatyavihitena laukikenādhyayanena tatsaṃbhavānna vihitasyādhyayanasya niyogatastatprayuktiḥ /
naca prayuktilāghavādapi vihitopajīvanam /

children.text: tadupajīvane 'pi prayuktyanavalopāt /
children.translated_text: Even when it depends on that, the prompting is not lost.

children.text: vihitamapyadhyayanamadhyāpanavidhinaiva tvanmate prayujyate na svavidhinā /
children.translated_text: Even the enjoined learning, on your view, is prompted only by the injunction of teaching and not by its own injunction.

children.text: tasmāllaukikamevādhyayanamupanītānāmadhyāpanavidhirākṣipet /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the injunction of teaching would imply only ordinary learning on the part of the initiated.

children.text: vidhivihitamadhyayanaṃ paraprayuktyabhāvādadhikāraṃ prakalpayet* ////
children.translated_text: The learning enjoined by [its own] injunction, in the absence of prompting by another, would establish [independent] eligibility. ////

body.translated_text: If, on the other hand, because teaching is impossible without learning, learning for its sake is implied — even so, since that [teaching] is possible through non-enjoined, ordinary learning, the enjoined learning is not necessarily prompted for that purpose. And not even from economy of prompting —

body.text: kiñca yadyupanayanamadhyāpanāṅgaṃ tato 'dhyayanavidhirarthajñānārthaḥ sannādhyāpanārthatayopanītaistraivarṇikaiḥ saṃbadhyeta, ye 'dhyāpanārthatayopanītastraivarṇikāstadupayogivyāpāramapekṣante te 'rthajñānārthamadhīyīran-ityasaṃbaddhameva syāt /

children.text: tataścopanītairasaṃbadhyamāno 'dhyayanavidhiścaturṇāmapi varṇānāṃ syāditi śūdrādhikāraprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Consequently, the injunction of learning, being unconnected with the initiated, would apply to all four <s>varṇas</s> (castes) — and thus the absurd consequence of <s>śūdra</s>-eligibility [for Vedic study would arise].

children.text: tasmādupanītānāṃ prayojanāpekṣiṇāmadhyayanakaraṇikārthajñānabhāvanā vidhīyata ityadhyayanāṅgamevopanayanaṃ, svavidhiprayuktaṃ cādhyayanam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for the initiated who seek a purpose, the cultivation of meaning-knowledge through the instrument of learning is enjoined — thus <s>upanayana</s> is indeed an auxiliary to learning, and learning is prompted by its own injunction.

children.text: prapañcenāyaṃ pakṣonyāyaratnamālāyāmeva nirasta ityaparamyate /
children.translated_text: This position has been refuted at length in the <s>Nyāyaratnamālā</s> itself — hence we pass over it.

children.text: tasmātpūrvokta eva vicāraḥ- kimadṛṣṭārthamadhyayanamutākṣaragrahaṇādiparamparayārthajñānārthamiti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the previously stated inquiry [stands]: Is learning for the sake of unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), or for the sake of meaning-knowledge through the succession of letter-apprehension and the like? //

body.translated_text: Moreover, if <s>upanayana</s> is an auxiliary to teaching, then the injunction of learning, being for the purpose of knowing meaning, would be connected with the three castes initiated for the purpose of teaching — those three castes who, having been initiated for the purpose of teaching, require activity useful to it, and who [seek] knowledge of meaning —

body.text: adhyayanavidhyupasaṃhāraḥ /
body.translated_text: Conclusion of the injunction of learning:

body.text:
athavā nātra kiñcidvicāryeta, nāvamikanyāyenaivādhyayanasyākṣarasaṃskārādiparamparayārthajñānārthatvasiddheḥ /
navame hi-- sāmnāmṛgakṣarābhivyaktidvāreṇa stutyupayogitvadarśanāttādarthyameva nādṛṣṭārthatvamiti vakṣyate /
tenaiva nyāyenādhyayanasyārthajñānārthatvasiddheradhyayanānantaraṃ dharmajijñāsā kartavyeti siddhamevaitatprayojanavivakṣayā sūtrakāreṇocyate /

children.text: yadāhuḥ-- "dharmākhyaṃ viṣayaṃ vaktuṃ mīmāṃsāyāḥ prayojanam" iti /
children.translated_text: As they say: 'The purpose of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> is to expound the subject-matter called <s>dharma</s>.'

children.text: nanvatra kaścidvedavākyārtho vicāryate /
children.translated_text: But is not some meaning of a Vedic sentence being investigated here?

children.text: tadapyāhuḥ--"nacātra codanāvyākhyā gauravaṃ tatra coditam" iti tatsiddhamadhyayanānantaraṃ dharmajijñāsā kartavyeti /
children.translated_text: To that too they say: 'And here the explanation of injunctive [texts] is not [the main concern]; weightiness is enjoined therein.' Thus it is established that after learning, the inquiry into <s>dharma</s> is to be undertaken.

children.text: sā caturvidhā-- dharmasvarūpa- pramāṇa- sādhana- phalaiḥ //
children.translated_text: That [inquiry] is fourfold — by the nature of <s>dharma</s>, its means of knowledge, its means of accomplishment, and its result. //

body.translated_text: Or rather, nothing need be investigated here, since by the analogy of the ninth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>] alone, the purpose of learning as meaning-knowledge through the succession of letter-refinement and the like is established. For in the ninth — since the manifestation of the <s>Ṛk</s>-syllables of the <s>Sāmans</s> is seen as useful for praise, that purposive relation alone [is established], not an unseen-merit purpose —

body.text:
nanvadhyayanavidhinā vedavākyārthavicāramātrākṣepāddharmasvarūpapramāṇajijñāsayoḥ kaḥ prasaṅgaḥ /
ucyate-- upoddhātatvātprasaṅgaḥ /

children.text: yadi hi vedavākyārtho dharmaḥ syādvedaśca pramāṇaṃ tato 'sau vicāraḥ kartavyo bhavati /
children.translated_text: For if the meaning of Vedic sentences is <s>dharma</s>, and the Veda is a means of knowledge, then that investigation is to be undertaken.

children.text: itarathā kākadantaparīkṣāvatsyāt, tadadhyayanavidhireva pramāṇādivicāramākṣipati /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, it would be like examining crow's teeth. Therefore, the injunction of learning itself implies the investigation of means of knowledge and the like.

children.text: dharmagrahaṇaṃ copalakṣaṇārtham-- adharmasyāpi hānāya jijñāsyatvāt /
children.translated_text: And the mention of '<s>dharma</s>' is by way of indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) — since <s>adharma</s> too is to be inquired into for the sake of its avoidance.

children.text: akārapraśleṣaṇe vā sūtramadharmajijñāsāyāmapi vyākhyeyamiti niravadyam //
children.translated_text: Or, with the elision of the letter 'a', the <s>sūtra</s> is to be explained as concerning the inquiry into <s>adharma</s> as well — thus it is faultless. //

body.translated_text: But if the injunction of learning implies only the investigation of Vedic sentence-meaning, what occasion is there for inquiry into the nature and means of knowledge of <s>dharma</s>? It is replied: The occasion arises because they are introductory [to that investigation].

body.text: codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharmaḥ // Jaim_1,1.2 //
body.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is that purpose which is characterized by injunction (<s>codanā</s>). // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.2 //

body.text: prathamaṃ tāvat ko dharmaḥ kathaṃlakṣaṇakaḥ ityetadvayamanena sūtreṇa śrutyarthābhyāṃ nirūpyate- yo dharmaḥ
body.translated_text: First of all — what is <s>dharma</s>? Of what character? — these two [questions] are determined by this <s>sūtra</s> through the word and its meaning. That which is <s>dharma</s> —

children.text: sa yodanālakṣaṇaḥ codanaiva tasya lakṣaṇaṃ pramāṇam /
children.translated_text: it is characterized by injunction (<s>codanālakṣaṇa</s>); injunction alone is its characteristic, i.e., its means of knowledge.

children.text: codanā ca tasya lakṣaṇameveti śrutyā pramāṇavidhāvarthāccodanāgamya evāgnihotrādidharmo nātallakṣaṇaścaityavandanādiriti svarūpamapi siddhyati /
children.translated_text: And [the fact that] injunction is its defining characteristic — through the <s>śruti</s>, in the establishment of the means of knowledge, and through the meaning, it follows that <s>dharma</s> such as <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like is knowable only through injunction, and not characterized by other [means]; thus the nature [of <s>dharma</s>] such as <s>caitya</s>-worship and the like [as non-<s>dharma</s>] is also established.

children.text: tathā yaścodanālakṣaṇaḥ sa dharma iti svarūpavidhāvarthatpramāṇasiddhirveditavyā //
children.translated_text: Likewise, [the statement] 'that which is characterized by injunction is <s>dharma</s>' — in the establishment of the nature [of <s>dharma</s>], the establishment of the means of knowledge through its meaning is to be understood. //

body.text:
kaścitvāha- kāryarūpo vedārtho na siddharūpa ityetadanena sūtreṇocyate, codanālakṣaṇaśabdena kāryamucyate, dharmaśabdena vedārtha iti /
tadayuktam- yāni tāvadvidhivākyāni teṣāṃ vidhāveva prāmāṇyaṃ vastusvarūpaṃ cāprāmāṇyaṃ vispaṣṭameveti na tatra kiñcidvaktavyam /
kṣepiṣṭādivākyānāmapi vidhyekavākyatayā tatraiva prāmāṇyam /
body.translated_text: Someone, however, says: 'What is stated by this <s>sūtra</s> is that the meaning of the Veda is of the nature of what-is-to-be-done (<s>kārya</s>), not of the nature of what-is-established (<s>siddha</s>). By the term <s>codanālakṣaṇa</s>, what-is-to-be-done is meant; by the term <s>dharma</s>, the meaning of the Veda is meant.' That is improper — for as regards injunctive sentences, their authority lies only in injunction —

body.text: mantrāṇāmapi prakaraṇena pradhānavidhiśeṣatvaṃ dvitīyapāde vakṣyata iti na tatrāpi vaktavyamasti /

children.text: tena kasyātra siddhārthatāṃ nirasya kāryārthatocyate /
children.translated_text: Then, for whom here is the established-meaning refuted and the duty-meaning stated?

children.text: 'avināśī vā are ayamātme'tyādīnāmupaniṣadvākyānāmiticet /
children.translated_text: If [one says] 'for the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> sentences such as "this self is indeed imperishable" and the like' —

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: teṣāmapi yadi vidhyekavākyatvamasti tator'thavādādhikaraṇena gatam, atha nāsti kathaṃ teṣāṃ kāryārthatā syāt* ////
children.translated_text: For those too — if they have syntactic unity with an injunction, then that is settled by the <s>arthavāda</s> chapter (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>). And if they do not, how could they have the purpose of enjoining duty? ////

body.translated_text: And of the <s>mantras</s> too, their subsidiary relation to the primary injunction through context will be stated in the second chapter — so nothing need be said about that either.

children.text: atha teṣāṃ vidhyaśravaṇādividhyantareṇaikavākyatvābhāvācca kāryārthatvānupapattervyutpattivirahācca sigaddhyarthe prāmāṇyayogādaprāmāṇyamevābhimatam /
children.translated_text: Now, since those [<s>Upaniṣadic</s> sentences], not being heard as injunctions, and lacking syntactic unity with any other injunction, cannot have the purpose of enjoining duty, and since in the absence of semantic derivation (<s>vyutpatti</s>) they have validity regarding established entities — the view [of that opponent] is that they simply lack validity.

children.text: kimidānīmātmādivākyānāmaprāmāṇyapratipādanaparamidaṃ sūtraṃ, suvyāhṛtaṃ tarhi śāstrārambhe prathamaṃ tāvatsūtrakāro 'prāmāṇyameva vedavākyānāṃ pratipādayatīti* ////
children.translated_text: Is this <s>sūtra</s> then devoted to establishing the invalidity of sentences about the self and the like? Well said then — at the very beginning of the <s>śāstra</s>, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> first establishes the invalidity of Vedic sentences! ////

body.text:
kathaṃ ca kāryaṃ eva prāmāṇyam /
tatraiva vyutpatteḥ- pravṛttyadhīnā hi vyutpattiḥ, sā ca kāryāvagamādhīneti vyutpattirapi tatraiva bhavatīti cet /
avaśyaṃ pravṛttyadhīnaiva vyutpattiḥ- kāṣṭhaiḥ sthālyāmodanaṃ pacatītyādivartamānāpadeśeṣvapi prasiddhatṛtīyārthanāmaprasiddhakāṣṭhaprātipadikārthānāṃ ca puruṣāṇāṃ kāṣṭhārthe vyutpattidraśanāt /
body.translated_text: And how is it that validity belongs only to injunctions? [If one says] 'because semantic derivation (<s>vyutpatti</s>) occurs only there — for <s>vyutpatti</s> depends on activity, and that depends on the apprehension of duty, so <s>vyutpatti</s> occurs only there' — it must be that <s>vyutpatti</s> depends on activity [in the sense that]: with logs, a pot —

body.text: prathamavyutpattiḥ /
body.translated_text: The first semantic derivation (<s>vyutpatti</s>):

body.text:
atha prathamavyutpattiḥ kāryaviśeṣayaiva- nahi tadā śabdāntaravaśena śabdāntarasyārthe vyutpattiḥ saṃbhavati sarvasya dharmasyāprasiddhatvāditi cet /
astvevam /
tathāpi paścādbahuśaḥ siddhārthe śabdaprayogadarśanāt 'ko 'yaṃ rājā' 'pāñcālaḥ' ityādiṣu praśnaprativacanādiṣu kāryasya vyabhicārādavyabhicāryārthamātraṃ vācyamiti sujñānam /
yathaiva hi kasyāñcidvyaktau prathamaṃ gośabdasya prayogadarśanātsaiva vācyetyavagame satyapi paścādvaktyantare prayogaṃ pūrvavyaktivyabhitārādavyabhicārisāmānyamevārthaṃ ityadhyavasīyate tathā kāryaparatāmavagatāmapi paścātsiddhārthaprayogadarśanena bādhitatvārthamātramevāvyabhicārādvācyamiti yuktam /
kiñca prathamavyutpattau katipayānāmeva śabdānāṃ kāryārthatvamavagataṃ na sarvaśabdānāṃ paurvāparyaniyamo 'sti, ataḥ sarve śabdāḥ paścādvyutpādyamānāḥ kaiścitsiddhārthā bhavanti /

children.text: sarveṣāṃ tu kāryārthatve siddhārthapareṣu laukikavākyeṣu sarvaśabdānāṃ lākṣaṇikatvānna kaścidanvitābhidhāyī syāt /
children.translated_text: But if all [sentences] had only duty-meaning, then in ordinary sentences that concern established facts, all words would be figurative (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>), and no word would have direct denotation in connected meaning (<s>anvitābhidhāna</s>).

children.text: tatrānvitapratītiḥ kathaṃ siddhyet /
children.translated_text: How then would the cognition of connected meaning be established?

children.text: vaktṛjñānamanumātavyam /
children.translated_text: [One might say:] The speaker's knowledge is to be inferred.

children.text: nacānvitapratipādakaṃ vākyamuccāritamiti kathamanvitajñānānumānam* ////
children.translated_text: But since no sentence has been uttered that conveys connected meaning, how can there be inference of connected-meaning knowledge? ////

body.translated_text: Now, if the first <s>vyutpatti</s> is through duty-specification alone — for at that [initial stage], <s>vyutpatti</s> of one word through another word is not possible, since all <s>dharma</s> is unknown — let it be so. Even then, subsequently, through repeated [experience] when the meaning is established, the word-understanding —

body.text:
athārthasvarūpasmārakaiḥ padairanvitajñānamanamīyate, tataḥ kāryavācake 'pyasiddheranvitābhidhānaṃ na syāt /
kiñca prathamameva kāryavyabhicāraḥ śakyo 'nagantum /
yadā hi putraste jāta ityuktasya kasyācinmukhavikāsaṃ pārśvasthaḥ paśyati tadā harṣaheturanena śabdena pratipādita iti harṣahetubhūtasiddhārthapratipādane śabdasya sāmarthyaṃ kalpayati /
yadyapi ca tadānīmarthaviśeṣo na jñāyate harṣahetūnāṃ bahūnāṃ saṃbhavāttathāpi siddhārthatā tāvadavagatā, tāvatāpi kārye vyabhicāraḥ siddhaḥ /
kiñca bahuśaḥ putrajanane sati evaṃ śabdaprayogādanyeṣu harṣahetuṣvaprayogāt putrajananarūpārthaviśeṣo 'pi sujñāna
body.translated_text: If connected-meaning knowledge is inferred through words that remind of the nature of objects — then even for [a word] denoting duty, since that [direct denotation] is unestablished, there would be no <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> (denotation of connected meaning). Moreover, the deviation from duty-meaning can be readily seen from the very first [instance]. For when someone is told 'a son has been born to you,' [the listener experiences] —
[this is evident]. ////

body.text: kiñca pravṛttyadhīnāpi vyutpattirnāvaśyaṃ kāryaviṣayaiva bhavati, tathāhi yadā kaścitpravṛttāvatyantāsamarthaṃ vṛddhamāturaṃ vā prativinodārthaṃ vākyaṃ prayuṅkte 'nadyāstīre pañca phalāni santī'ti tatrānyo daivasaṃgataḥ kaścidarthī tadvākyamarthācchrutvā nadītīraṃ gatvā phalānyāharati, etatsarvaṃ paśyannanyo vyutpitsuḥ phalasadbhāvapratipādane śabdasya sāmarthyaṃ vyutpadyate, tasmānnaikāntataḥ kāryārthatā śabdānām /
body.translated_text: Moreover, even though <s>vyutpatti</s> (linguistic comprehension) depends on <s>pravṛtti</s> (activity), it is not necessarily confined to action (<s>kārya</s>) as its object. For example, when someone addresses a person completely incapable of activity, or an old sick person, with a sentence intended for amusement—'On the bank of the river there are five fruits'—and another person, there by chance, having some need, hearing that sentence for its meaning, goes to the riverbank and takes the fruits, another person observing all this, wishing to learn language, comprehends the capacity of words to convey the existence of fruits. Therefore, the action-referentiality of words is not absolute.

body.text: prābhākaraktadvitīyasūtrārthasya khaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the <s>Prābhākara</s> interpretation of the second <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: kā cāsya sūtrasya vacanavyaktiḥ, yadi tāvat 'yatkāryaṃ tadvedārtha eve'ti kāryamuddiśya vedārthatā vidhīyate, tathā satyuddeśyasyopādeyena svaraniyamātsarvasya lokikasyāpi gavānayanādikāryasya vedārthatā syāt /
children.translated_text: And what is the verbal import of this <s>sūtra</s>? If it means 'whatever is action, that alone is the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>'—so that Vedic meaning is prescribed with reference to action—then, since the subject would be qualified by the predicate through the rule of accent, all worldly actions too, such as fetching cows, would become the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>.

children.text: kiñca upādeyasya vedārthasyoddeśena dhūmenāvyāpterakārye 'pi vedasya prāmāṇyanirastaṃ syāt* ////
children.translated_text: Moreover, if the Vedic meaning as the predicate qualifies action as the subject, then since action is not pervaded by smoke-like [inference], the authoritativeness of the <s>Veda</s> would be negated even regarding non-action.

body.text: atha 'vedārthaḥ sa kāryarūpa eve'ti, tato 'yo dharmaḥ sa codanālakṣaṇaḥ' iti vatanavyaktiḥ syāt, tatrārthaśabdo 'bhyudayavācī kasya viśeṣaṇaṃ, yadyupādeyasya codanālakṣaṇapadārthasya, tataḥ sarvasya vedārthasya kāryatvamarthatvaṃ ca vidhīyate iti śyenādiniyogānāmapyarthatvaṃ syāt* ////
body.translated_text: If instead it is said that 'the meaning of the <s>Veda</s> is of the nature of action alone,' then the verbal import would be '<s>dharma</s> is that which is characterized by <s>codanā</s> (injunction).' There, the word 'artha' (meaning/purpose) denoting what is beneficial—of what is it a qualifier? If it qualifies the predicate, i.e., the referent of the term '<s>codanālakṣaṇa</s>,' then both being-action and being-purposeful would be predicated of all Vedic meaning, and so even injunctions like the <s>Śyena</s> sacrifice would have purposefulness.

body.text:
athoddeśyavedārthaviśeṣaṇaṃ, tato 'yamartho bhavati yor'thātmako 'bhyudayātmako vedārthaḥ sa kāryarūpaḥ, tataśca śyenādiniyogānāṃ niṣiddhaphalatvenānabhyudayarūpāṇāṃ kāryatā na syāt /
mābhūditi cet /
teṣāmapi liṅga kāryatāvagamāt /

children.text: śyenayāgasya kāryatā nivārayituṃ śakyate na niyogasya /
children.translated_text: The action-nature of the <s>Śyena</s> sacrifice can be denied, but not that of the <s>niyoga</s> (injunction),

children.text: tasya kāryaikasvabhāvatvāt /
children.translated_text: because its very nature is exclusively that of action.

children.text: asati ca kāryatve śyenavākyasya kāryārthatvābhāvātsiddhārthataiva vaktavyā syāt, naca tathā saṃbhavati vidhipratyayayogāt /
children.translated_text: And in the absence of action-nature, the <s>Śyena</s> sentence, lacking action-referentiality, would have to be declared as conveying an established fact. But that is not possible, because of the presence of the optative verbal suffix.

children.text: siddhe cārthe vyatpattivirahādapramāṇāṇyameva śyenādivākyānāṃ syāt* ////
children.translated_text: And if it conveyed an established fact, the <s>Śyena</s> and similar sentences would become non-authoritative due to the impossibility of linguistic comprehension regarding established things.

body.translated_text: If instead it qualifies the subject 'Vedic meaning,' then the meaning would be: that Vedic meaning which is purposeful, i.e., conducive to well-being (<s>abhyudaya</s>), is of the nature of action. In that case, injunctions like the <s>Śyena</s> sacrifice, being of the nature of prohibited results and thus not conducive to well-being, would not have the nature of action. If one says 'let it not be so'—even for those, the nature of action is understood from the <s>liṅga</s> (optative suffix).

children.text: atha pūrvasūtrādvedārthaparaṃ dharmapadamanuyujya codanālakṣaṇo vedārthaḥ ityekaṃ vākyam, artho dharmaḥ ityaparaṃ vākyam /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, taking the word '<s>dharma</s>' from the previous <s>sūtra</s> as referring to Vedic meaning, one sentence would be 'the Vedic meaning is characterized by <s>codanā</s>,' and another sentence would be 'the purpose is <s>dharma</s>.'

children.text: tadidaṃ svaprajñāvilasitamātram, anuṣaṅgavākyabhedayorvināphalamāśrayaṇāt /
children.translated_text: This is merely a display of one's own ingenuity, since the resort to splitting into connected statement and separate sentence is without purpose.

children.text: apratijñātasya ca dharmasya lakṣaṇamasaṃgatam* ////
children.translated_text: And defining <s>dharma</s> that has not been announced [as the topic] is incongruous.

children.text: atha pratijñātasyaiva vedārthasya kāryatvasiddhaye dharmatvamucyate /
children.translated_text: If it is said that <s>dharma</s>-hood is stated of the already-announced Vedic meaning in order to establish its action-nature,

children.text: kiṃ kāryaṃ eva dharmarūpo vedārthaḥ sa eva jijñāsyo nānyaḥ, tathācet ya eva jijñāsyo dharmastasyaiva sūtrākṣaravināśena jijñāsā pratijñāsyeti vedārthapratijñāvacanārthakam* ////
children.translated_text: does it mean that the Vedic meaning, which is of the form of action alone and of the nature of <s>dharma</s>, is alone to be inquired into and nothing else? If so, then through the destruction of the <s>sūtra</s> letters themselves, the inquiry would be stated for that very <s>dharma</s> which is to be inquired into, making the statement of the Vedic-meaning thesis meaningless.

body.text: atha tvarthaśabdamanādṛśya yo vedārthaḥ sa kāryarūpa ityucyate tator'thapadamanarthakaṃ vastumātraparyāyamanuvādakaṃ syāt /

children.text: anarthavyudāsārthatā cāsya bhāṣyakāreṇoktā, tasmādviśeṣaṇamevaitat /
children.translated_text: But its purpose as excluding what is meaningless has been stated by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>; therefore this is indeed a qualifier.

children.text: viśeṣaṇatve cābhyudayarūpasya vedārthasya kāryatvābhidhānādanabhyudayarūpasya vādārthasya kāryatvaṃ na syāditi sarvasya vedasya eva prāmāṇyamiti niyogo na syāt /
children.translated_text: And if it is a qualifier, since action-nature is predicated of Vedic meaning that is conducive to well-being, the action-nature of Vedic meaning that is not conducive to well-being would not hold, and thus the authoritativeness of the entire <s>Veda</s> would not be established as a fixed rule.

children.text: tataśca avināśī vā are ayamātmetyādīnāmātmasvarūpaparatvaṃ na nirākartavyamityastāṃ tāvat /
children.translated_text: And consequently, the self-referentiality of passages like 'this Self is indeed imperishable' would not be refutable—but let that be for now.

children.text: tasmāddharmasvarūpapramāṇapratipādanārthamevedaṃ sūtram* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, this <s>sūtra</s> is intended solely for establishing the means of knowing the nature of <s>dharma</s>.

body.translated_text: If, however, disregarding the word 'artha,' it is said that 'the Vedic meaning is of the nature of action alone,' then the word 'artha' would be meaningless, a mere synonym for 'thing,' and merely reiterative.

children.text: tadiha dharmaṃ viṣayīkṛtya cintyate-- kimasya na kiñcitpramāṇamasti, kiṃ vā pratyakṣādikameva pramāṇam, uta codanaiva, athavā vikalpaḥ, athavā samuccayaḥ iti /
children.translated_text: Here, with <s>dharma</s> as the subject of inquiry, it is considered: does it have no means of knowledge at all, or is perception and the like itself the means of knowledge, or is <s>codanā</s> (injunction) alone [the means], or is there an alternative, or a combination?

children.text: tatra śabdasya pramāṇāntaraprāptaprāpakatvena svayapramāṇatvāpratyakṣādīnāṃ cāsāmarthyādapramāṇako dharma ityekaḥ pakṣaḥ, pratyakṣādigamya evetyekaḥ pakṣaḥ, yogināṃ pratyakṣagamyaḥ, arvācīnānāṃ tu codanāgamya ityaparaḥ, jagadvaicitryārthāpatyā kimapyadṛṣṭamastīti sāmānyena prasiddho dharmaścodanayāgnihotrādiviśeṣarūpeṇa gamyate tasmātsamuccaya ita pakṣāntaram, codanaiva sāca pramāṇameveti siddhāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: Among these, one position is that <s>dharma</s> has no means of knowledge, since verbal testimony merely conveys what is already known through other means of knowledge and has no independent authority, while perception and the like are incapable. Another position is that it is knowable through perception and the like alone. Another is that it is perceivable by <s>yogins</s> through direct perception but knowable by ordinary people through <s>codanā</s>. Yet another alternative position is that from the variety of the world, through presumption, some unseen [force] must exist, and thus <s>dharma</s>, generally known, is known through <s>codanā</s> in the specific form of <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like—therefore a combination. The established conclusion is: <s>codanā</s> alone [is the means], and it is indeed a valid means of knowledge.

children.text: tadiha codanaiva pramāṇaṃ sāca pramāṇamevetyavadhāraṇadvayaṃ pratijñāyate //
children.translated_text: Here, the double assertion is made: <s>codanā</s> alone is the means of knowledge, and it is indeed a valid means of knowledge.

body.text: prathamapādapratipādyārthasaṃgrahaḥ /
body.translated_text: Summary of the topics established in the first <s>pāda</s> (section).

children.text: nimittasūtre tu prathamadvitīyasūtramātrālocanayā vedo dharmamūlamityādivadupadeśaśāstratāśaṅkā mā bhūditi parīkṣāśāstramevadamiti jñāpayituṃ parīkṣāpratijñānam /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Nimittasūtra</s>, however, by considering only the first and second <s>sūtras</s>, lest there be the suspicion that this is merely an instructional text like 'the <s>Veda</s> is the root of <s>dharma</s>,' the assertion of examination is made to indicate that this is indeed an investigative treatise.

children.text: yadyapi coparitanavyāpārādeva parīkṣāśāstratvaṃ gamyate tathāpi vakṣyamāṇameva śrotṛbuddhisamādhānāya kīrtitam* ////
children.translated_text: Although the character of being an investigative treatise is understood from the subsequent treatment itself, nevertheless the forthcoming [examination] is stated for the satisfaction of the listeners' minds.

body.text: pratyakṣasūtre tu pratyakṣasya vidyamānopalambhanatvādbhaviṣyati dharme prāmāṇyāsaṃbhavāttatpūrvakatvenetareṣāmapyaprāmāṇyātpramāṇāntaraniyamavikalpasamuccayanirākaraṇāccodanaivetyayamarthaḥ siddhyati* ////
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pratyakṣasūtra</s>, however, since perception apprehends only what exists [in the present], it cannot be authoritative regarding <s>dharma</s> which will exist in the future; and since the other [means of knowledge], being dependent on perception, are also non-authoritative—through the rejection of the restriction to other means of knowledge, the alternative, and the combination—the meaning that '<s>codanā</s> alone [is the means]' is established.

children.text: autpattikasūtre tu svataḥprāmāṇyamarthānyathātvakāraṇadoṣajñānābhyāmaprāmāṇyamityāśrityāgnihotrādicodanābhyo 'saṃdigdhajñānotpatteḥ svataḥ prāmāṇyaṃ prāptam /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Autpattikasūtra</s>, however, relying on the principle that validity is intrinsic (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>) while invalidity arises from knowledge of the object being otherwise or from knowledge of defects in the cause, validity is obtained intrinsically from injunctions regarding <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, since undoubted knowledge arises from them.

children.text: nacāpavādakamarthānyathātvajñānaṃ sākṣādasti, nāpi kāraṇadoṣajñānaṃ, puruṣāśrayatvācchabdadoṣāṇām /
children.translated_text: And there is no direct sublating knowledge of the object being otherwise, nor knowledge of defects in the cause, since verbal defects pertain to persons,

children.text: padapadārthasaṃbandhasyākṛtrimatvāntaddvāreṇa puruṣānupraveśābhāvāccodanānāmiti sthite samāhite, mābhūtpadārthasaṃbandhadvāreṇa puruṣānupraveśaḥ, vākyavākyārthayostu loke saṃbandhādarśanānnirmūlo 'gnihotrādivākyārthapratyaya ityato vyāmohaḥ /
children.translated_text: and since the connection between words and their meanings is uncreated (<s>akṛtrima</s>), there is no entry of human [agency] through that channel—thus it stands established for <s>codanās</s> (injunctions). Let there be no entry of human agency through the channel of word-meaning connection; but since in the world no connection is seen between sentences and sentence-meanings, the cognition of <s>Agnihotra</s> and similar sentence-meanings is groundless—hence the confusion.

children.text: sāmayiko vā, ato na vākyārthe vedasya prāmāṇyamityāśaṅkya, padārthānāṃ saṃbandhagrahaṇaṃ samayaṃ cānapekṣamāṇānāmeva vākyārthe prāmāṇyaṃ saṃbhavatīti tadbhūtādhikaraṇena pratipādite* ////
children.translated_text: Or it is conventional (<s>sāmayika</s>), and therefore the <s>Veda</s> has no authority regarding sentence-meaning—anticipating this objection, the <s>Tadbhūtādhikaraṇa</s> establishes that authority regarding sentence-meaning is possible for [words] that do not depend on the apprehension of the connection of word-meanings nor on convention.

body.text:
punarvedānāṃ vākyātmakatvāt kāṭhakādisamākhyānācca pauruṣeyatvāttaddvāreṇa doṣasaṃsparśamāśaṅkya smartavyatve satyasmaraṇādyogyonupalabdhinirastasya karturanumānāsaṃbhavātsamākhyāyāśca pravacananimittatvādapauruṣeyā vedāḥ iti tadekadeśānāṃ codanānāṃ siddhaṃ prāmāṇyamityevaṃ samastaḥ prathamaḥ pādaścodanāsūtrapratijñātārthopapādena tasyaiva parikaraḥ /
so 'yaṃ bhāṣyakārānusāreṇa pādārtho 'nukrāntaḥ /
vṛttikāramataṃ tu paścādanukramiṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Again, since the <s>Vedas</s> consist of sentences and have designations like <s>Kāṭhaka</s>, they would be of human origin, and thereby susceptible to defects—anticipating this objection, [the text establishes that] since the author, whose existence is negated by the non-apprehension of a competent [author] when he should be remembered but is not, cannot be inferred, and since the designations are based on [modes of] recitation, the <s>Vedas</s> are not of human origin. Thus the validity of <s>codanās</s>, which are parts of them, is established. In this way, the entire first <s>pāda</s> is an elaboration of the thesis asserted in the <s>Codanāsūtra</s>, providing support for that very thesis. This summary of the <s>pāda</s>'s content follows the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>. The view of the <s>Vṛttikāra</s> we shall summarize afterwards.

body.text: dharmasya pratyakṣādipramāṇagamyatvam /
body.translated_text: The knowability of <s>dharma</s> through perception and other means of knowledge.

children.text: prakṛtamanusarāmaḥ- pratijñātaṃ tāvaccodanaiva pramāṇaṃ sā ca pramāṇameveti /
children.translated_text: Let us follow the main topic—the assertion was: <s>codanā</s> alone is the means of knowledge, and it is indeed a valid means of knowledge.

children.text: nanu pratyakṣāderanyānapekṣaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ saṃbhavatīti tasyaiva dharme prāmāṇyaṃ, śabdasya tu sarvadaiva pramāṇāntarapramitaviṣayatvānna tadanapekṣaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ saṃbhavatīti /
children.translated_text: Objection: Since the validity of perception and the like is possible without dependence on anything else, perception itself should be authoritative regarding <s>dharma</s>; but for verbal testimony, since it always has as its object what is already known through other means of knowledge, validity independent of those is not possible.

children.text: ucyate /
children.translated_text: Reply:

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ tāvatsaṃyuktaviṣayatvena vidyamānopalambhanatvādbhaviṣyati dharme na samartham* ////
children.translated_text: Perception, being apprehensive of objects in contact [with the senses] and thus apprehending only what exists [in the present], is not capable regarding <s>dharma</s>, which pertains to the future.

body.text: yadyapi godohanādidravyaṃ, yāgādikriyā, nīcaistvādiguṇaśca, phalasādhanatvāddharmaśabdenocyate nāpūrvādaya iti śreyaskarabhāṣye vakṣyate, tathāpi teṣāṃ phalasādhanarūpeṇa dharmatvāt phalasya ca janmāntarādibhāvitvāddharmasvarūpeṇa pratyakṣaviṣayatvaṃ na saṃbhavati, tatpūrvakatvāccānumānādikamapi na pramāṇam* ////
body.translated_text: Although substances such as those used in milking cows, actions such as sacrifices, and qualities such as speaking softly are called by the word '<s>dharma</s>' because they are means to the result—as will be stated in the <s>Śreyaskarabhāṣya</s>—not <s>apūrva</s> and the like, nevertheless, since their <s>dharma</s>-hood consists in being means to a result, and since the result pertains to future lives, their perception as <s>dharma</s> in its essential nature is not possible; and since inference and the like depend on perception, they too are not valid means [for knowing <s>dharma</s>].

body.text:
bhāvanābalajaṃ tu yogipratyakṣaṃ bhaviṣyatyapi dharme samarthamiti manorathamātram /
bhāvanā hyanubhūtagocaraniyatānubūteṣveva niścayarūpāṃ smṛtiṃ janayet /

children.text: naca sātra pramāṇaṃ smṛtitvādeva, nitarāṃ pratyakṣamanindriyajatvāt /
children.translated_text: and that [memory] is not a means of valid knowledge here, precisely because it is memory; still less is it perception, since it does not arise from the senses.

children.text: nendriyajatvaṃ pratyakṣalakṣaṇamapitu kalpanāpoḍhatvamiticet, sutarāṃ dharmasyāpratyakṣatvaṃ phalasādhanarūpasyāvikalpagrahaṇasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: If it is objected that the definition of perception is not 'arising from the senses' but rather 'being free from conceptual construction'—then all the more is <s>dharma</s> not perceptible, since it is impossible to apprehend that which has the nature of being a means to results through non-conceptual cognition.

children.text: tasmādanimittaṃ pratyakṣam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, perception is not the instrument [for knowing <s>dharma</s>],

children.text: tatpūrvakatvāccānumānādyapi* ////
children.translated_text: and since they depend on perception, inference and the like are also not [valid instruments].

body.translated_text: But the <s>yogipratyakṣa</s> (yogic perception) born of the power of meditation will be capable even regarding <s>dharma</s>—this is mere wishful thinking. For meditation can produce only a definitive cognition in the form of memory, confined to things previously experienced,

children.text: kāśyapīyāḥ punaḥ prātibhajñānamṛṣīṇāṃ dharmo pravartata ityāhuḥ, tattu liṅgādyabhāsajatvātpramāṇameva na bhavati kiṃ punardharme /
children.translated_text: The <s>Kāśyapīyas</s>, however, say that <s>dharma</s> proceeds from the intuitive knowledge (<s>prātibhajñāna</s>) of the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages). But that, arising without a basis such as a mark [of inference], is not even a valid means of knowledge at all, let alone regarding <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: śabdasya tu buddhijanakatvīdasatyapavāde yuktaṃ prāmāṇyam* ////
children.translated_text: But for verbal testimony, validity is appropriate when there is no sublating cognition, since it generates cognition.

children.text: nanu na buddhijananamātrātprāmāṇyaṃ yuktaṃ ayathārtheṣvapi vākyeṣu buddhijananāviśeṣāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: Validity is not appropriate merely from generating cognition, since there is no difference in the generation of cognition even in sentences that do not correspond to reality.

children.text: satyam /
children.translated_text: True.

children.text: tatra tu kāraṇadoṣabādhakapratyayābhyāṃ yuktamaprāmāṇyaṃ, vedetu tadbhāvātsataḥprāptaṃ prāmāṇyamanapoditaṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: But in those cases, invalidity is appropriate due to knowledge of defects in the cause and sublating cognition; whereas for the <s>Veda</s>, in the absence of such [defects], the naturally obtained validity remains unsublated.

body.text: atha prāmāṇyavicāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Now, the investigation of validity.

children.text: kathaṃ punaḥ pramāṇasya svataḥprāpti, tadarthamidaṃ sarvajñānānyadhikṛtya cintyate kiṃ prāmāṇyamaprāmāṇyaṃ cobhayaṃ svata evāvagamyate, athavānyataradapi svabhāvenānirupitaṃ kāraṇaguṇadoṣapratyayābhyāmavagamyate, āhosvidaprāmāṇyaṃ svato 'vagamyate, prāmāṇyaṃ svataḥprāptaṃ sadarthānyathātvakāraṇadoṣajñānābhyāmavagamyamānenāprāmāṇyenāpodyate iti /
children.translated_text: But how is validity naturally obtained? For this purpose, taking all cognitions as the subject, this is considered: is both validity and invalidity apprehended intrinsically, or is one of them, being undetermined by nature, apprehended through knowledge of merits or defects in the cause? Or is invalidity apprehended intrinsically, while validity, being naturally obtained, is sublated by invalidity apprehended through knowledge of the object being otherwise or defects in the cause?

children.text: tatra sarvakāraṇānāṃ svakāryaśakteḥ svabhāvikatvādubhayamapi jñānasya svarasādevāvagamyata iti kecit /
children.translated_text: Among these, some hold that since the capacity of all causes to produce their effects is natural, both [validity and invalidity] of cognition are apprehended spontaneously.

children.text: tadayuktam /
children.translated_text: That is incorrect.

children.text: nahi jñānaṃ svaviṣayasya tathātvamatathātvaṃ ca yugapacchaknoti vedayituṃ virodhāt* ////
children.translated_text: For cognition cannot reveal both the truth and the falsity of its own object simultaneously, due to contradiction.

body.text:
atha kāpi jñānavyaktiḥ svaprāmāṇyaṃ svato bodhayati kāpyaprāmāṇyamityucyate, tathāpi na yuktam /
kāraṇāntaranirapekṣasya jñānasyaivopalambhahetutve kiṃ kva jñāne bhavatīti na śakyaṃ vivektum /

children.text: ato dvayamapi svasvabhāvenānirūpitaṃ kāraṇaguṇadoṣajñānābhyāmavagamya ityapare /
children.translated_text: Therefore, others hold that both, being undetermined by their own nature, are apprehended through knowledge of merits and defects in the cause.

children.text: tadapyapeśalam /
children.translated_text: That too is inelegant.

children.text: evaṃ hi guṇadoṣāvadhāraṇātprāganyatareṇāpyākāreṇārthamanavagamayadvijñānaṃ niḥsvabhāvaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: For thus, prior to the ascertainment of merits and defects, cognition, not presenting the object in either form, would be devoid of any nature.

children.text: tasmādaprāmāṇyaṃ svataḥ, prāmāṇyaṃ tu saṃvādajñānādibhirityedadeva yuktam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, invalidity is intrinsic, while validity [is established] through knowledge of correspondence and the like—this alone is correct.

body.translated_text: If it is said that some particular cognition reveals its own validity intrinsically while another reveals invalidity—even so, this is not correct. When cognition itself, without depending on any other cause, is the basis of apprehension, it cannot be determined in which cognition [validity occurs and in which invalidity occurs].

body.text: yuktidarśanam /
body.translated_text: Demonstration of the reasoning.

body.text:
tathāhi na jñānamutpannamityetāvatārthatathātvāvadhāraṇaṃ yuktaṃ vyabhicārādaniścayācca aprāmāṇyameva tasyāṃ velāyāṃ prāptaṃ, paścātkāraṇaguṇajñānādarthakriyājñānādvā prāmāṇyāvagamādapodyate /
śabde cāptapraṇītatvaṃ guṇaḥ /

children.text: naca vede tadasyapauruṣeyatvābhyupagamāt /
children.translated_text: But that does not apply to the <s>Veda</s>, since it is accepted as not being of human origin.

children.text: valaspatayaḥ satramāsata śṛṇota grāvāṇaḥ' ityevamādīnāmunmattapralapitakalpatvāt, apratyayitatarapraṇītatvādaprāmāṇyameva vedānāmiti prāpte 'bhidhīyate- parāpekṣaṃ pramāṇatvaṃ nātmānaṃ labhate kvacit /
children.translated_text: Because [Vedic passages] like '<s>vanaspatayaḥ satram āsata</s>' (the trees sat in a sacrificial session) and '<s>śṛṇota grāvāṇaḥ</s>' (listen, O pressing stones) are like the ravings of a madman, and because they are composed by one who is even less trustworthy—thus invalidity alone belongs to the <s>Vedas</s>—having raised this objection, [the reply is:] validity that depends on something else does not obtain itself anywhere.

children.text: mūlocchedakaraṃ pakṣaṃ ko hi nāmādhyavasyati yadi hi sarvameva jñānaṃ sivaviṣayatathātvāvadhāraṇe svayamasamarthaṃ vijñānāntaramapekṣeta tataḥ kāraṇaguṇasaṃvādārthakriyājñānānyapi svaviṣayabhūtaguṇādyavadhāraṇe paramapekṣeran, aparamapi tatheti na kaścidartho janmasahasreṇāpyadhyavasīyeteti prāmāṇyamevotsīdet /
children.translated_text: Who indeed would accept a position that destroys the very root? For if all knowledge whatsoever were itself incapable of ascertaining the truth regarding its own object and required another cognition, then causal congruence (<s>kāraṇaguṇasaṃvāda</s>), practical efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>), and other such cognitions would also require yet another [cognition] for ascertaining the qualities and so forth that constitute their own objects, and that other [cognition] likewise — thus no object whatsoever could be ascertained even in a thousand births, and validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) itself would be destroyed.

children.text: atha- arthakriyājñānaṃ svataḥpramāṇamiticet ko viśeṣaḥ, avyabhicāra iti cet, na, svapnāvasthāyāmasatyapyudakāharaṇer'thakriyāvijñānadarśanāt* ////
children.translated_text: If [one says]: 'The cognition of practical efficacy is intrinsically valid' — what distinction [does it have]? If [one says]: 'Non-deviation' — no, because even in the dream state, a cognition of practical efficacy in fetching water is observed despite the absence of [real] water.

body.translated_text: For it is not appropriate that merely because a cognition has arisen, the object's being-so is ascertained, due to deviation and uncertainty. At that moment, invalidity alone is obtained. Afterwards, through knowledge of merits in the cause, or through knowledge of successful activity, validity is apprehended and [invalidity] is sublated. And for verbal testimony, being composed by a reliable person is the merit.

body.text:
atha sukhajñānamevārthakriyā taccāvyabhicāryeva nahi kvacidapyasati sukhe sukhajñānamasti /
satyametat /
natu tena pūrvajñānasya prāmāṇyādhyavasānaṃ saṃbhavati, apramāṇenāpi priyāsaṃgamavijñānena svapnāvasthāyāṃ sukhadarśanāt /
tasmātsvataḥprāmāṇyaṃ prāptamarthānyathātvakāraṇadoṣajñānābhyāmapodyata ityavaśyamaṅgīkaraṇīyam /
evañca śabdenāptapuruṣasparśakṛtatvāddoṣāṇāmapauruṣeye vede tadabhāvātsākṣāccārthānyathātvajñānābhāvadapoditaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ bhavati /
pauruṣeyavacanāni tu puruṣabuddhiprabhavatvādbhrāntyā vipralipsayā vā prayuktāni mūladoṣeṇa duṣṭatvādayathārthāni bhavantīti vaiṣamyam /

children.text: kecitbāhuḥ- na loke 'pi śabdasyāyathārthātvamasti tadabhāvāt, na hi loke śābdaṃ pramāṇamasti vakrabhiprāyānumāpakatvātpuruṣavacasām, tenānumānasyaivāyaṃ vyabhicāro na śabdasya /
children.translated_text: Some say: even in the worldly domain, verbal testimony does not have inaccuracy, due to the absence thereof. For in the world, verbal testimony is not a [separate] valid means of knowledge, since human utterances merely serve to infer the speaker's intention — therefore this deviation belongs to inference alone, not to verbal testimony.

children.text: navā tasyāpi vivekāgrahaṇādaliṅge liṅgavyavahārapravṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: Or rather, even for that [inference], due to the failure to discriminate, there is the application of the term 'inferential mark' (<s>liṅga</s>) to what is not [truly] an inferential mark.

children.text: yadi tu śabdasyaivāyaṃ vyabhicāro 'bhyupeyate /
children.translated_text: If, however, one accepts that this deviation belongs to verbal testimony itself,

children.text: svābhāvikamevāpramāṇaṃ syāt, na hi puruṣadoṣeṇa śabdasya doṣo bhavati yathāvasthitaśabdābhivyaktimātre puruṣasya vyāpārāt* ////
children.translated_text: it would be intrinsically invalid. For a defect in the person does not constitute a defect in the word itself, since the person's activity consists merely in manifesting the word as it inherently is.

body.translated_text: If [one says]: it is the cognition of pleasure itself that constitutes practical efficacy, and that is indeed unfailing — for nowhere does a cognition of pleasure exist when pleasure itself is absent — this is true. But it is not possible for the validity of a prior cognition to be ascertained by that [pleasure-cognition], because even in the dream state, pleasure is observed through a cognition of meeting with a beloved, which is not a valid means of knowledge. Therefore, it must necessarily be accepted that validity is intrinsic (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>), and is sublated by the cognition of a defect that is the cause of the object being otherwise, or by [cognition of] the object being otherwise [itself]. And thus, since verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) is free from defects — because defects arise from contact with fallible persons — and since in the authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) <s>Veda</s> there is an absence of such [defects], and because there is no direct cognition of the object being otherwise, its validity stands. Human utterances, however, being produced by human intellect, may be employed through error or the desire to deceive, and being vitiated by a root defect, may be inaccurate — this is the difference.

children.text: tadidamasāram /
children.translated_text: This [argument] is without substance.

children.text: yadi loke śābdaṃ nāsti tadā vede 'pi kathaṃ tatsyāt /
children.translated_text: If verbal testimony does not exist in the worldly domain, then how can it exist in the <s>Veda</s> either?

children.text: nahyabhiprāyānumānakṣīṇasya śabdasyārthaṃ prati vācakatve pramāṇamastītyuktaṃ nyāyaratnamālāyām* ////
children.translated_text: For there is no valid means of knowledge establishing that a word, whose capacity to signify meaning has been exhausted by inference of [the speaker's] intention, has [any remaining] denotative power with respect to the object — thus it has been said in the <s>Nyāyaratnamālā</s>.

body.text:
yacca vyabhicārābhyupagame svābhāvikamaprāmāṇyaṃ bhavati puruṣadoṣasya śabde 'navatārāditi /
syādetadevaṃ yadi yadīyaṃ yadvākyaṃ tat sa puruṣo 'bhivyañjyāt /
tattu
body.translated_text: And as for [the argument] that upon accepting deviation, invalidity would be intrinsic, since the defect of the person does not transfer to the word — this would be so if whatever sentence belongs to whomever, that person were the one who manifests it. But —

body.text:
tenaiva kriyate varṇā nityāḥ padāni ca, vākyāni tu puruṣaireva kriyante pauruṣeyatvādeva /
yathāvasthitāni vyajyamānāni vedavākyavadapauruṣeyāṇyeva syuḥ /
tataśca vaktrabhiprāyānumāpakatvamapi na syāt, tadyathādhyetṛbhirabhivyajyamānāni vedavākyāni nādhyetṝṇāmabhiprāyaṃ sūcayanti tathā puruṣavākyānyapi na sūcayeyuḥ /

children.text: yadi hi vyabhicāraśaṅkyā loke śabdasya prāmāṇyaṃ na saṃbhavatītyucyate, tarhi tadvaktrabhiprāyānumāne 'pi tulyam /
children.translated_text: If it is said that due to the suspicion of deviation, verbal testimony cannot have validity in the worldly domain, then the same applies to the inference of the speaker's intention as well.

children.text: anyathāsaṃvidānasyāpyanyathāvākyaracanādarśanāt /
children.translated_text: Because even one who does not know [the matter] otherwise is seen to construct sentences as if he does know otherwise.
