children.text: kiṃ ca śabdasya cakṣurāderiva svasāmarthyena bodhakatvādvyabhicāre 'pi na bodhakatvahāniḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, just as the eye and other [sense organs], verbal testimony has the capacity to produce knowledge through its own power; therefore, even when there is deviation, there is no loss of its capacity to produce knowledge.

children.text: liṅgasyāvyabhicāriṇa eva gamakatvamiti vyabhicāriṇo 'liṅgatvamupapannam* ////
children.translated_text: An inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) has indicative power only when it is non-deviating; therefore, it is proper that what deviates is not an inferential mark.

body.translated_text: It is by that very [person] that phonemes are produced; phonemes and words are eternal, but sentences are indeed produced by persons, precisely because of their human origin. [If] the manifested [sentences], being as they inherently are, were authorless just like Vedic sentences — then they would not serve to infer the speaker's intention either. Just as Vedic sentences, when manifested by reciters, do not indicate the intention of the reciters, so too human sentences should not indicate [any intention either].

children.text: atha vaktumāptatvādvyabhicāraśaṅkāṃ nirvartyanumānaṃ, tathāsati śabdamevārthe pramāṇamastu pratibandhakāyāḥ śaṅkāyā nirastatvāt /
children.translated_text: If [one says]: the trustworthiness (<s>āptatva</s>) of the speaker removes the suspicion of deviation, and then inference [of the speaker's intention operates] — if so, let verbal testimony itself be the valid means of knowledge regarding the object, since the obstructing suspicion has been removed.

children.text: avaśyaṃ hi buddhiviśeṣamanumitsatā prathamaṃ padārthāsteṣāṃ cānvayayogyatālocayitavyā, te ālocyamānā drāgeva vākyārthaṃ bodhayantīti nānumānaṃ pratīkṣante* ////
children.translated_text: For one who wishes to infer a particular cognition must first consider the word-meanings and their fitness for mutual connection — and when these are being considered, they immediately produce knowledge of the sentence-meaning, without waiting for inference.

body.text: kiñcānumite buddhiviśeṣe paścādanuvādabhūtaṃ vākyaṃ vākyārthamavabodhayatīti vaḥ siddhāntaḥ, tataśca yo nāmānāpta evābuddhyā gṛhītastadvākyādayathārthameva jñānamutpannamityabhyupagantavyam, tataśca doṣādhīnatvādapramāṇyasya vaktṛdoṣāṇāṃ ca śabde saṃkrāntyanabhyupagamātsvārasikameva śabde
body.translated_text: Furthermore, your established doctrine is that after the particular cognition has been inferred, the sentence, being a mere reiteration, produces knowledge of the sentence-meaning. Therefore, when someone who is not trustworthy (<s>anāpta</s>) is apprehended through error, it must be accepted that from his sentence, only inaccurate knowledge arises. And thus, since invalidity depends on defects, and since defects of the speaker are not accepted as transferring to the word, an inherent

children.text: duṣṭatvamāpannamiti balādapramāṇyaṃ vedasya prasajyata ityāstāṃ tāvat /
children.translated_text: vitiation would be incurred — and consequently the invalidity of the <s>Veda</s> would forcefully follow. But let this be set aside for now.

children.text: tasmādanāptāvacasāṃ satyevāprāmāṇye vaktṛdoṣādhīnatvādvede ca tadabhāvātprāmāṇyameva vaktavyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, given that the utterances of untrustworthy persons are indeed invalid, and that this invalidity depends on the speaker's defects, and that such defects are absent in the <s>Veda</s>, its validity alone must be affirmed.

children.text: tasmāccodanālakṣaṇa eva dharmaḥ śreyaskaraḥ ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>dharma</s>, which leads to the highest good (<s>śreyas</s>), is defined precisely by Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>) — this is the meaning.

children.text: yadeva śreyaḥsādhanarūpaṃ yāgahomādi tadeva dharma ityucyate loke, nāpūrvamantaḥkaraṇapravṛttyādi vā lokaprasiddhivirahāt //
children.translated_text: That which has the nature of being a means to the highest good — such as sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>), oblation (<s>homa</s>), and the like — that alone is called <s>dharma</s> in common usage, not <s>apūrva</s> (the unseen potency) or inner mental activity and the like, due to their absence from common understanding.

body.text: dharmalakṣaṇavicāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Discussion of the definition of <s>dharma</s>.

body.text:
nanvapūrvameva śreyaḥsādhanam /
na /

children.text: avāntaravyāpārāmātratvāt /
children.translated_text: because it is merely an intermediate operation.

children.text: tasmādyāgādireva śreyaḥsādhanarūpeṇa dharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) and the like alone constitute <s>dharma</s> in the form of being the means to the highest good.

children.text: tadrūpābhāvācca na śūdrakṛtasya dharmatāpattiḥ /
children.translated_text: And since that nature is absent [in unauthorized rites], the <s>dharma</s>-status of what is performed by a <s>Śūdra</s> does not arise.

children.text: codanālakṣaṇamātrasya dharmatvaṃ mābhūdityarthaśabdena viśeṣyate* ////
children.translated_text: The word '<s>artha</s>' qualifies [the definition] so that not everything merely defined by Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>) should be considered <s>dharma</s>.

body.translated_text: Objection: <s>apūrva</s> alone is the means to the highest good. No —

body.text: codanāśabdena ca pravartakaṃ nivartakaṃ ca vākyamucyate tataśca niṣedhavākyaiḥ na hiṃsyāt ityādibhiranarthatvena lakṣyamāṇānāṃ hiṃsādīnāmapi dharmatvaṃ syāt tadvyāvṛttyarthaṃ ya evārtharūpeṇa pravartakavākyairlakṣyate tasyaiva dharmatvaṃ vaktumarthagrahaṇam* ////
body.translated_text: By the word '<s>codanā</s>' (injunction), both enjoining and prohibiting sentences are denoted. Consequently, acts like <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence) and the like, which are characterized as harmful (<s>anartha</s>) by prohibitive sentences such as 'one should not harm,' would also become <s>dharma</s>. To exclude those, the word '<s>artha</s>' is used — to state that only what is defined by enjoining sentences as being a purposeful good (<s>artha</s>) has the status of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: bhāṣye ca śyenādigrahaṇam tatsādhyahiṃsādilakṣaṇārtham /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, the mention of the <s>Śyena</s> and similar [rites] is for the purpose of [illustrating] violence and similar harmful results that those rites accomplish.

children.text: upariṣṭāt hiṃsā hi sā, sā ca pratiṣiddhā iti vivaraṇāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the later explanation: 'for that [Śyena rite] is violence, and that is prohibited.'

children.text: kecittu lakṣaṇāṃ pariharantaḥ śyenādisvarūpamevārthapadasya vyāvartya manyante, teṣāmeva śyenādayaḥ kartavyā vijñāyante, iti vidheyatvanirākaraṇena pratiṣedhaviṣayatvasamarthanāt /
children.translated_text: Some, however, avoiding [this] interpretation, consider that the word '<s>artha</s>' excludes the very nature of the <s>Śyena</s> and similar rites. [They argue that] those very <s>Śyena</s> rites are understood as not to be performed — since their status as something enjoined is negated, their being the object of prohibition is thereby established.

children.text: kathaṃ punasteṣāṃ vidheyatvaṃ nirākriyate, tatrāhuḥ- yasya hi vidhiḥ svasiddhyanyathānupapattyānuṣṭhānamākṣipati tadvidheyamityucyate, kāmyeṣu ca karmasu kāmanāvaśādeva pravṛttisiddhestata eva vidhiḥ siddhyannanyathānupapattyabhāvānna svayamanuṣṭhānamākṣipati* ////
children.translated_text: But how is their status as something enjoined negated? To this they say: that which an injunction, by the impossibility of its own accomplishment otherwise, implies as requiring performance — that is called 'to be enjoined' (<s>vidheya</s>). In the case of optional (<s>kāmya</s>) rites, since engagement is already accomplished through desire alone, the injunction, being accomplished through that [desire] alone, does not itself imply performance due to the absence of impossibility otherwise.

body.text: nanu kartavyatābodhanameva pravartanam, kartavyatā ca vede yāgasya vinaiva bodhiteti kathamavidheyatvam /

children.text: satyam /
children.translated_text: True.

children.text: natu yāgasya kartavyatā liṅā(?)bhidhīyate, svārthasya kartavyatāṃ liṅā(?)bhidhatte, yāgaśca tasya viṣayaḥ karaṇaṃ ca, so 'yaṃ kartavyatātmā niyogārtho 'nyathānupapattyā svaviṣayasya kartavyatāṃ bodhayannanuṣṭhāpaka ityucyate /
children.translated_text: But it is not the obligatoriness of the sacrifice that the optative suffix (<s>liṅ</s>) denotes; the optative denotes the obligatoriness of its own object, and the sacrifice is its content and instrument. This injunctive purpose (<s>niyoga</s>), having the nature of obligatoriness, communicating through the impossibility otherwise the obligatoriness of its own content, is called the prompter (<s>anuṣṭhāpaka</s>).

children.text: śyenādīnāṃ tu rāgādevānuṣṭhānasiddherna niyogasteṣāmanuṣṭhānamākṣipatīti na teṣāṃ vidheyatvam /
children.translated_text: But in the case of the <s>Śyena</s> and similar rites, since performance is accomplished through passion alone, the injunction does not imply their performance — therefore they do not have the status of being enjoined.

children.text: asati ca vidheyatve teṣāṃ niṣedhaviṣayatvādanarthatvamiti tadvyāvṛttyarthamarthapadamiti* ////
children.translated_text: And in the absence of enjoined status, since they are objects of prohibition, they are harmful (<s>anartha</s>) — to exclude those, the word '<s>artha</s>' is used.

body.translated_text: Objection: the communication of obligatoriness (<s>kartavyatā</s>) is itself what constitutes prompting, and the obligatoriness of sacrifice is communicated in the <s>Veda</s> without any [other means] — so how can there be non-enjoinability?

body.text:
tatredaṃ vaktavyam- kasminnaṃśe teṣāṃ vyāvṛttiriti /
dharmatva iti cet /
na /
tatsvarūpānabhidhānāt /
idaṃ hi sūtraṃ vedārthasya kāryatvapratipādanārthaṃ na karmasvarūpalakṣaṇārtham /
yataḥ śyenādīnāṃ dharmatvaṃ mā prasāṅkṣīdityarthapadena
body.translated_text: Here the following must be said: in what respect are they excluded? If [one says] from <s>dharma</s>-status — no, because the <s>sūtra</s> does not express their intrinsic nature. For this <s>sūtra</s> is for the purpose of establishing the actionable nature of Vedic meaning, not for defining the intrinsic nature of ritual actions. Since one might think that the <s>Śyena</s> and similar rites should not have <s>dharma</s>-status, the word '<s>artha</s>' would effect

body.text: vyāvṛttiḥ kriyeta* ////
body.translated_text: the exclusion.

children.text: yadi paraṃ kāryatvavyāvṛttiḥ syāt sā cāyuktetyuktaṃ prāk /
children.translated_text: If, however, it is only the exclusion from actionability (<s>kāryatva</s>) [that is intended], that too has been previously shown to be improper.

children.text: bhavatu vā vākyabhedāṅgīkāreṇa dharmalakṣaṇārthamapi sūtram /
children.translated_text: Or let the <s>sūtra</s> also serve the purpose of defining <s>dharma</s>, by accepting a division of the sentence.

children.text: tathāpi codanālakṣaṇāpadena kāryātmakamapūrvamuddiśya tasya dharmatvamucyata iti vo matam, tatra śyenādiyāgasya kaḥ prasaṅgo yadvyāvṛttyarthamarthapadaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Even so, your view is that by the term '<s>codanālakṣaṇa</s>' (defined by injunction), the unseen potency (<s>apūrva</s>) having an actionable nature is referred to and its <s>dharma</s>-status is stated. In that case, what relevance does the sacrifice of <s>Śyena</s> and the like have, such that the word '<s>artha</s>' would serve to exclude them?

children.text: nahi jyotiṣṭomādiyaigasyāpi dharmatvamasti, apūrvasya dharmatvābhyupagamāt* ////
children.translated_text: For even the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice does not have <s>dharma</s>-status [on your view], since <s>apūrva</s> is accepted as having <s>dharma</s>-status.

body.text:
atha śyenādyapūrvasyaiva dharmatvamarthapadena vyāvartyate tato bhāṣye śyenādiśabdena karmanāmadheyena tatsādhyamapūrvaṃ lakṣyata ityaviśiṣṭā lakṣaṇā syāt /
yadi cāpūrvameva pratyudāharaṇaṃ tato hiṃsā hi sā sā ca pratiṣiddheti bhāṣyamasaṃgataṃ syāt /

children.text: śyenayāgo vā tatphalaṃ vā hiṃsā, nanvapūrvaṃ kathañcidapi hiṃsāpadāspadam /
children.translated_text: Whether it is the <s>Śyena</s> sacrifice or its result that is violence — <s>apūrva</s> is in no way a locus for the term 'violence.'

children.text: asmiṃśca kalpe kathaṃ punarasāvanarthaḥ kartavyatayopadiśyata iti codyam /
children.translated_text: And on this interpretation, how [can it be asked] whether this harmful [rite] is taught as obligatory — that objection

children.text: naiva śyenādayaḥ kartavyā vijñāyante iti cottaramapūrvaviṣayaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: and the response 'the <s>Śyena</s> rites are not understood as to be performed' would both pertain to <s>apūrva</s>.

children.text: na ca tasya kartavyatvaṃ śakyate vārayituṃ kāryasvabhāvatvāt* ////
children.translated_text: And the obligatoriness of that [<s>apūrva</s>] cannot be denied, because it has the nature of what is to be done (<s>kārya</s>).

body.translated_text: If the <s>dharma</s>-status of the <s>apūrva</s> of the <s>Śyena</s> and similar rites is what is excluded by the word '<s>artha</s>', then in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, by the word '<s>Śyena</s>' (a ritual name), the <s>apūrva</s> accomplished by that ritual is indicated — so the interpretive move would be no different. And if <s>apūrva</s> alone is the counter-example, then the <s>Bhāṣya</s> statement 'for that is violence, and that is prohibited' would be incoherent.

children.text: evañca yāgakartavyatāniṣedhārthamidaṃ bhāṣyamaṅgīkṛtyayat tatsamādhānāya prayatyate kartavyatāviṣayo hi niyogo na punastasya kartavyatāmāheti tadapārthakam /
children.translated_text: And thus, having accepted that this <s>Bhāṣya</s> is for the purpose of negating the obligatoriness of the sacrifice, the attempt made to resolve [the difficulty] — that 'the injunction pertains to obligatoriness, but does not state the obligatoriness of that [sacrifice]' — is pointless.

children.text: kāmyeṣvapi vidhireva pravartako na phalaṃ, tasya vidhyadhīnotpattikatvena yāgāpekṣābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Even in optional (<s>kāmya</s>) rites, it is the injunction alone that prompts, not the result — because the result, having its arising dependent on the injunction, does not require the sacrifice.

children.text: vidhistu yāgādhīnaniṣpattitvādyāgamanuṣṭhāṃpayatīti yuktam //
children.translated_text: The injunction, however, having its accomplishment dependent on the sacrifice, properly impels one to perform the sacrifice.

body.text: kāmyeṣvapi karmasu vidhereva pravartakatvam /
body.translated_text: Even in optional rites, it is the injunction alone that has the power to prompt.

children.text: yadi ca vidhirapravartakaḥ kāmyeṣu syāditikartavyatāpyavidheyā syāt, tasyāmapi phalata eva pravṛttisiddheḥ sāṅgapradhānasādhyatvātphalasya /
children.translated_text: And if the injunction were not the prompter in optional rites, then obligatoriness too would not be enjoined — since in that case too, engagement would be accomplished through the result alone, because the result is to be accomplished through the principal act together with its subsidiaries.

children.text: vakṣyati hi tadyukte tu phalaśrutistasmātsarvacikīrṣeti /
children.translated_text: For it will be stated: 'when that is conjoined, the mention of the result [shows that] therefore one desires to perform all [the subsidiaries].'

children.text: tataścāgnīṣomīyahiṃsāyā api vidhyabhāvena niṣedhaviṣayatvāttadyuktasya jyotiṣṭomasyāpyanarthatvāpatteḥ kor'tho yo niḥśreyasāya jyotiṣṭomādiriti bhāṣyānupapattiḥ //
children.translated_text: Consequently, since the violence in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [sacrifice] too, in the absence of being enjoined, would become the object of prohibition, there would follow the harmful character of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> conjoined with it — and the <s>Bhāṣya</s> statement 'who then is the purposeful good that leads to the highest welfare, namely the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like' would be untenable.

children.text: nanu na hiṃsyāditi niṣedho nārabhyādhītatvātpuruṣārthaḥ tenānena puruṣārtho eva hiṃsāḥ pratiṣeddhavyāḥ, kratvarthaniṣedhe hi so 'pi kratvarthaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: the prohibition 'one should not harm' is person-oriented (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) because it is not commenced for [ritual] purposes. Therefore, by this [prohibition], only person-oriented acts of violence are to be prohibited — for if the prohibition pertained to ritual-purpose [violence], it too would become ritual-oriented.

children.text: aviśeṣe tvekasya pratiṣedhavidheḥ kratvarthatvapuruṣārthatvāpattyā vairupyaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: But if there is no distinction, then one and the same prohibitive injunction would incur the incongruity of being both ritual-oriented and person-oriented.

children.text: tasmātpuruṣārthānāmeva hiṃsānāmiha pratiṣedho na kratvarthānāmiti* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, the prohibition here is of person-oriented acts of violence only, not of ritual-oriented ones.

body.text:
tadidaṃ bālasaṃmohanam /
nahyaviśeṣaṇāpi pratiṣedhe vairūpyam /
yadi hi kratvarthatvapuruṣārthatvarūpaṃ viśeṣeṇoddiśya pratiṣedhaḥ kriyeta tataḥ syādapi vairūpyaṃ pratiṣedhyopasthāpitakratupuruṣagocaratvātpratiṣedhasya /
yadātu hiṃsāmātramuddiśya pratiṣedhaḥ kriyate tadāsya kiṃ vairūpyam /
tadyathā yā bhojanārthaṃ māṃsotpādane hiṃsā, yā ca vairiniryātanārthatayā sākṣātpuruṣārthā tasyāmubhayyāmaviśeṣeṇa pratiṣidhyamānāyāmapi nāsti
body.translated_text: This is a mere delusion of the ignorant. For there is no incongruity even in a non-specific prohibition. If the prohibition were made by specifically targeting the two aspects of ritual-orientation and person-orientation, then there might be incongruity, because the prohibition would pertain to both ritual and personal domains presented by the object to be prohibited. But when the prohibition is made targeting violence in general, what incongruity does it have? Just as with violence for the purpose of eating — that which is for producing meat for food — and violence that is directly person-oriented for the purpose of retaliating against an enemy — when both are prohibited without distinction, there is no

body.text:
vairūpyamevamihāpi /
itarathā tatrāpi bhojanāṅgatā puruṣārthatā ca pratiṣedhasya syāditi vairūpyaṃ syāt /

children.text: tasmādyaiva kācidyena kenāpi prakāreṇa prasaktā hiṃsā sā sarvā sāmānyena pratiṣidhyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever violence is entailed by whatever means — all of it is generally prohibited.

children.text: puruṣārthaśca pratiṣedho 'nārabhyādhītatvāt /
children.translated_text: And the prohibition is person-oriented, because it is not commenced for [ritual] purposes.

children.text: tasmādagnīṣomīyahiṃsāpyasati vidheyatve pratiṣedhagocaraḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, violence in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [sacrifice] too, when not enjoined, would become the object of prohibition.

children.text: vidheyatve tu vidherviśeṣaviṣayatvātsāmānyaviṣayo niṣedhastadvirodhāddhisāntarāṇyavalambate //
children.translated_text: But when it is enjoined, since the injunction pertains to a specific [case] and the prohibition pertains to the general [case], the prohibition, being overridden by the [specific] injunction, rests upon other [non-ritual] acts of violence.

body.translated_text: incongruity — so too here. Otherwise, even there [in the food case], the prohibition would have the dual character of pertaining to an ancillary of eating and to a personal purpose, and so there would be incongruity.

body.text: hiṃsāyāṃ sāṃkhyamataṃ tatkhaṇḍanaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: The <s>Sāṃkhya</s> view regarding <s>hiṃsā</s> (injury) and its refutation:

body.text:
nanu satyapi vidheyatve vidheḥ kratvarthātpratiṣedhasya ca puruṣārthatvādviṣayabhedenāvirodhānna bādhaḥ /
nahīdaṃ viruddhaṃ kratorhiṃsayā bhavitavyaṃ puruṣasya tu tadvarjaneneti /
satyam /
aṅgavidhimātrālocanāyāṃ nāsti virodhaḥ /
jyotiṣṭomavidhistu sāṅgaṃ pradhānaṃ puruṣasya vidadhatpuruṣārthāhiṃsāniṣedhamagnīṣomīyahiṃsāyāmavatarantaṃ niruṇaddhiḥ /
nahyagnīṣomīyahiṃsāṃ varjayatā
body.translated_text: Objection: Even if there is prescriptive authority, since the injunction serves the purpose of the rite and the prohibition serves the purpose of the person, there is no conflict due to the difference of subject-matter, hence no sublation. For this is not contradictory: 'the rite must have injury' and 'the person should avoid it.' True. When considering merely the subsidiary injunction, there is no contradiction. But the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> injunction, prescribing the principal [rite] together with its subsidiaries for the person, obstructs the prohibition against injury serving the person's purpose when it descends upon the injury [required for] the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [animal sacrifice]. For one who avoids the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> injury

children.text: jyotiṣṭomaḥ śakyate 'nuṣṭhātum /
children.translated_text: cannot perform the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: tasmādasti virodha iti sāmānyasya bādhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore there is a contradiction, and hence the sublation of the general [prohibition].

children.text: vidhau tvapravartake satyagnīṣomīyahiṃsāpi pratiṣidhyeta* ////
children.translated_text: But if the injunction were non-operative, the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> injury too would be prohibited. ////

children.text: kimarthaṃ ca śyenasya vidheyatvaṃ nirākriyate, pratiṣedhasiddhyarthamiti cet, kaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ na hiṃsyātsarvabhūtāni iti /
children.translated_text: For what purpose is the prescriptive status of the <s>Śyena</s> [rite] rejected? If it is said: for establishing the prohibition — what prohibition? 'One should not injure any living beings.'

children.text: nāyaṃ niṣedhaḥ śyene pravartate hiṃsāviṣayatvāt /
children.translated_text: This prohibition does not apply to the <s>Śyena</s> [rite], because [the prohibition] has injury as its subject-matter [not the rite itself].

children.text: śyenaphalaṃ ca hiṃsā na śyenaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the fruit of the <s>Śyena</s> is injury — not the <s>Śyena</s> [itself].

children.text: tathā coktam, yo hiṃsitumicchettasyāyamabhyupāya iti hi teṣāmupadeśa iti* ////
children.translated_text: And thus it has been stated: 'For one who wishes to injure, this is the means — such is their teaching.' ////

body.text:
kaścitvāha- śyenasya kartavyatve sati balāttatphalamapi hiṃsā kartavyā bhavatīti na niṣeddhuṃ śakyate /
ataḥ phalakartavyatānirāsārthaṃ śyenakartavyatā balānnirasyata iti /

children.text: tadidamasaṃbaddham /
children.translated_text: This is irrelevant.

children.text: yathaiva hi śyenāpūrvasya kartavyatāyāṃ satyāmapi tatsādhyaphalasya kartavyatā na prasajyate tathā yāgasya kartavyatve satyapi rāgaprāptasya phalasya nāsti kartavyatāpattiḥ /
children.translated_text: For just as even when the <s>Śyena</s>-<s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency) has obligatory status, the obligatory status of the fruit to be accomplished by it does not follow — so too, even when the sacrifice has obligatory status, there is no entailment of obligatory status for the fruit obtained through desire.

children.text: tasmādanarthakaṃ śyenakartavyatānirākaraṇam /
children.translated_text: Therefore the rejection of the <s>Śyena</s>'s obligatory status is purposeless.

children.text: tasmāddhisaivātra pratyudāharaṇam* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>hiṃsā</s> (injury) alone is the counter-example here. ////

body.translated_text: But someone says: if the <s>Śyena</s> has the status of being obligatory, then its fruit, injury, also necessarily becomes obligatory — and thus cannot be prohibited. Therefore, to remove the obligatory status of the fruit, the obligatory status of the <s>Śyena</s> is necessarily rejected.

body.text:
idañcāparamekadeśinaḥ praṣṭavyāḥ- arthaśabdena kimucyate iti /
yadi śreyaḥsādhanaṃ, nityānāṃ dharmatvaṃ na syāt /
atha yanniṣiddhaphalaṃ na bhavati tadarthaśabdenocyate, tathāsati nañarthaviṣayasyāpūrvasya dharmatvaprasaṅgaḥ, codanālakṣaṇatvānniṣiddhaphalatvābhācca /
bhavatviticet /
na /

children.text: lokavirodhāt /
children.translated_text: Because it contradicts common usage.

children.text: yo hi hiṃsāyāmudyuktaḥ pratiṣedhavaśānnivartate na taṃ dhārmika ityācakṣate kintvadharmānnivṛtta ityetāvat /
children.translated_text: For one who, being engaged in injury, desists under the force of a prohibition — people do not call him 'righteous' (<s>dhārmika</s>), but merely say 'he has turned away from unrighteousness.'

children.text: tadāhuḥ- lokasiddhasya lakṣaṇaṃ parīkṣakairvaktavyaṃ na vṛddhyādivatparibhāṣaṇamityāstāṃ tāvat /
children.translated_text: To this they reply: the definition of what is established in common usage must be stated by the examiners — it is not a stipulation like interest and the like. But let that be.

children.text: iti codanāsūtram //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the <s>codanā-sūtra</s> (aphorism on injunction). //

body.translated_text: And these partial-viewists (<s>ekadeśins</s>) are to be asked this further question: what is meant by the word <s>artha</s> (purpose/good)? If [it means] a means to the highest good (<s>śreyas</s>), then the obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) [rites] would not have the status of <s>dharma</s>. But if the word <s>artha</s> means 'that which does not have a prohibited result' — then there would be the undesirable consequence that the <s>apūrva</s> connected with a negation would also have the status of <s>dharma</s>, because it has the characteristic of being enjoined by an injunction and because it does not have a prohibited result. If it is said 'let it be so' — no.

body.text: dharmapramāṇaparīkṣādhikaraṇam //3 //
body.translated_text: The topic of examining the means of knowing <s>dharma</s>: //3//

body.text: tasya nimittaparīṣṭiḥ // Jaim_1,1.3 //
body.translated_text: [Sūtra:] The examination of its cause. // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.3 //

body.text: anena sūtreṇa codanākhyasya nimittasya parīkṣaṇamasminpāde vakṣyamāṇam athātaḥ śeṣalakṣaṇam', atha viśeṣalakṣaṇam' itivatsukhagrahaṇārthamanukīrtyate* ////
body.translated_text: By this sūtra, the examination of the cause called <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction), which will be discussed in this section, is announced for easy comprehension — as with 'now, therefore, the definition of the remainder' and 'now, the definition of the particular.' ////

body.text: codanaivetyarthasya sādhanāya pratyakṣādīnāmanimittattvamucyate-
body.translated_text: To establish the meaning that <s>codanā</s> alone [is the means of knowing <s>dharma</s>], the non-causal nature of perception and the rest is stated:

body.text: dharme pratyakṣādyagamyatvādhikaraṇam //4 //
body.translated_text: The topic on the unknowability of <s>dharma</s> through perception and the rest: //4//

body.text: satsaṃprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanma tatpratyakṣamanimittaṃ vidyamānopalambhanatvāt // Jaim_1,1.4 //
body.translated_text: [Sūtra:] When there is contact of a person's sense-organs [with an object], there arises a cognition — that is perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>); it is not a means [for knowing <s>dharma</s>], because it apprehends [only] what is present. // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.4 //

body.text: pratyakṣaṃ tāvadindriyārthasaṃprayogajanyatvena vidyamānopalambhanatvādbhaviṣyati dharme na nimittam /

children.text: satsaṃprayogajanyatvamābhāse 'pi tulyatvādalakṣaṇamiti naiyāyikā dūṣayanti, tattu lakṣaṇānabhidhānādadūṣaṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: The <s>Naiyāyikas</s> object that 'being produced by contact with what exists' is not a [valid] definition, since it equally applies to error (<s>ābhāsa</s>). But that is not a [valid] objection, since no definition [of perception] is being proposed here.

children.text: nahīdaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ pratyakṣasya, kintvanimittatlakathanamātram /
children.translated_text: For this is not a definition of perception, but merely a statement of why it is not a means [for knowing <s>dharma</s>].

children.text: tatra heturvidyamānopalambhanatvaṃ tatsādhanaṃ ca satsaṃprayogajatvam /
children.translated_text: Therein, the reason is 'because it apprehends only what is present,' and its proof is 'being produced by contact with what exists.'

children.text: nahi satsaṃprayogajamavidyamānopalambhanaṃ saṃbhavati* ////
children.translated_text: For it is impossible that something produced by contact with what exists should apprehend what is not present. ////

body.translated_text: Perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), first of all, being produced by the contact of the sense-organ with its object, and thereby apprehending only what is present, will not be a means [of knowing] <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: indriyārthasaṃprayogajatvaṃ sukhādijñāneṣvavyāpteraheturiticet /

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: teṣāmapi manaḥsaṃjñakendriyasaṃprayogajatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because those [cognitions of pleasure, etc.] are also produced by contact with a sense-organ called <s>manas</s> (mind).

children.text: manaḥsadbhāve ca sukhādijñānameva pramāṇam, aparokṣāvabhāsajñānasyendriyādhīnatayā rūpādijñāneṣu vyāptidarśanāt sukhādiviṣayamaparokṣajñānamindriyamanumāpayati /
children.translated_text: And the very cognition of pleasure and the like is the proof for the existence of <s>manas</s>; since cognition that manifests as non-mediate (<s>aparokṣa</s>) is observed to be dependent on sense-organs in the case of cognitions of color and the like — the non-mediate cognition whose object is pleasure and the like leads to the inference of a sense-organ [for those cognitions].

children.text: tatra cakṣurādīnāmasaṃbhāvāttebhyo 'nyadavatiṣṭhate* ////
children.translated_text: And since the eyes and other [external organs] cannot [produce] that, another [organ] besides them is established. ////

body.translated_text: Objection: 'Being produced by the contact of a sense-organ with its object' is a non-pervasive reason, since it does not cover cognitions of pleasure and the like.

body.text:
atra kaścit- nityadravyagataviśeṣaguṇatvātsukhādīnāṃ dravyāntarasaṃyogajatvam, pārthivaparamāṇugatarūpādīnāmagnisaṃyogajatvadarśanāt, yacca dravyāntaraṃ tanmana ityāha -tanna yuktam /
śarīraṃ hi bhogāyatanam /
kiñca tasya bhogāyatanatvamanyat tatsaṃyogāpekṣasukhādyutpatteḥ, aśitapītādyādhāratvācca na bahiḥ śarīrātsukhādyutpattiḥ /
ataḥ śarīrasaṃyogādeva siddherna dravyāntarānumānam /
kiñca pārthivaguṇānāmeva dravyāntarasaṃyogāpekṣā dṛṣṭā na dravyamātraguṇānām /
tejaḥsaṃyoga eva ca katāraṇatayā dṛṣṭo na dravyamātrasaṃyogastasmānnaivaṃ manaḥsiddhiriti
body.translated_text: Herein someone says: since pleasure and the like are particular qualities residing in an eternal substance, they are produced by conjunction with another substance — as seen with colors residing in earthen atoms being produced by conjunction with fire. And that other substance is <s>manas</s>. That is not correct. For the body is the receptacle of experience. Moreover, its being the receptacle of experience is other [than what is claimed] — since the arising of pleasure and the like depends upon conjunction with that [body], and since it is the substratum of what is eaten, drunk, and the like, pleasure and the like do not arise from anything external to the body. Therefore, since it is established from conjunction with the body alone, the inference of another substance is unnecessary. Moreover, the dependence on conjunction with another substance is observed only for the qualities of earthy [substances], not for the qualities of substances in general. And conjunction with fire alone is observed as the cause — not conjunction with substance in general. Therefore <s>manas</s> is not established in this way.

body.text: sukhādyaparokṣajñānameva manaso liṅgam //
body.translated_text: The non-mediate cognition of pleasure and the like alone is the inferential sign (<s>liṅga</s>) of <s>manas</s>. //

body.text: indriyalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: The definition of a sense-organ:

body.text:
kiṃpunarindriyalakṣaṇaṃ cakṣurādiṣu manasi cānusyūtam /
ucyate- yatsaṃprayukte viśadavabhāsaṃ vijñānaṃ janayati tadindriyamityucyate, tacca dvividham, bāhyamābhyantaraṃ ca, bāhyaṃ pañcavidhaṃ ghrāṇarasanacakṣustvakśrotrātmakam /
āntaraṃ tvekaṃ manaḥ /
body.translated_text: What then is the definition of a sense-organ, pervading both the eyes and the rest and the mind? It is said: that which, when in contact [with an object], produces a vivid cognition — that is called a sense-organ. And it is of two kinds: external and internal. The external is fivefold, consisting of smell, taste, sight, touch, and hearing. The internal is one: <s>manas</s> (mind).

body.text:
tatrādyāni catvāri ca pṛthivyaptejovāyuprakṛtīnītyakṣupādadarśanavadabhyupagamyate /
śrotraṃ tvākāśātmakaṃ tairabhyupagatam /
vayaṃ tu- diśaḥ śrotramiti darśanāddigbhāgameva karṇaśaṣkulyavacchinnaṃ śrotramācakṣmahe /

children.text: manastu pṛthivyādīnāmevānyatamātmakaṃ tebhyo 'nyadvā sarvathā tāvadasti manaḥ /
children.translated_text: As for <s>manas</s>, it is either of the nature of one of earth and the rest, or something other than them — in any case, <s>manas</s> exists.

children.text: taccātmatadguṇeṣveva svatantraṃ pravartate na bāhyeṣu rūpādiṣvityāntaramityucyate /
children.translated_text: And it operates independently only with respect to the self and its qualities, not with respect to external [objects] like color and the like — hence it is called 'internal.'

children.text: rūpādijñāneṣvapi taccakṣurādisahāyaṃ pravartate, evamanumānādiṣvapi liṅgādisahāyaṃ, anyamanaskasya saṃprayukteṣvapi rūpādiṣu jñānānutpatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Even in cognitions of color and the like, it operates as a co-assistant with the eyes and the rest; similarly in inference and the like, it operates as a co-assistant with the inferential sign and the like — since for one whose mind is elsewhere, no cognition arises even when the sense-organs are in contact with colors and the like.

children.text: smṛtāvapi saṃskāraparatantraṃ pravartate svatantram* ////
children.translated_text: Even in memory, it operates dependently upon impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>), though independently [of external organs]. ////

body.translated_text: Therein, the first four are accepted as having earth, water, fire, and air as their material cause — as [established by the argument] like the perception of feet by a footless one. But the organ of hearing is accepted by them as having ether (<s>ākāśa</s>) as its nature. We, however — since from the statement 'the directions are the organ of hearing,' we declare that a portion of direction delimited by the ear-conch (<s>karṇaśaṣkulī</s>) is the organ of hearing.

body.text:
nanvanumānādīnāṃ manojanyatvātteṣāṃ ca bhūtabhaviṣyatorapi pravṛtterindriyajanyatvaṃ vidyamānopalambhanatvenānaikāntikaṃ syāt /
na syāt /
nahīndriyajanyatvaṃ hetuḥ kintvindriyasaṃprayogajatvam /
nacānumāne 'tītāyā bhaviṣyantyā vā vṛṣṭeranumīyamānāyā manasā saṃprayogo 'stītyavyabhicāraḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection: since inference and the like are produced by <s>manas</s>, and since those operate with respect to the past and future as well, being produced by a sense-organ would be inconclusive [as a reason for] apprehending only what is present. Not so. For the reason is not 'being produced by a sense-organ' but 'being produced by the contact of a sense-organ [with an object].' And in inference — when past or future rain is being inferred — there is no contact of <s>manas</s> with it. Hence there is no deviation.

body.text: atha pratyakṣam /
body.translated_text: Now, perception:

children.text: tadevaṃ pratyakṣaṃ tāvadanimittaṃ tatpūrvakatvāccānumānādyapi /
children.translated_text: Thus, perception first is not a means [for knowing <s>dharma</s>]; and since inference and the like are preceded by it [perception], they too [are not means for knowing <s>dharma</s>].

children.text: nahyagṛhīte dharme tena saha kasyacitsaṃbandhagrahaṇaṃ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: For when <s>dharma</s> is not apprehended [by perception], it is impossible to grasp the relation of something with it.

children.text: sādṛśyaviṣayakatvāccopamānaṃ dūrabhraṣṭam /
children.translated_text: And <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) is far removed, since its subject-matter is similarity.

children.text: arthāpattirapi dharmeṇa vinānupapadyamānasya kasyacidadarśanādasamarthā* ////
children.translated_text: <s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) too is incapable, since it does not perceive something that would be inexplicable without <s>dharma</s>. ////

body.text: nanu jagadvaicatryamanupapannam /

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: svābhāvikatvenopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because it is explicable through its being natural.

children.text: yadyapi tadanupapattyā kiñcidadṛṣṭaṃ kalpyeta tathāpi ko dharmaḥ ko vādharma iti vivekābhāvādavaśyaṃ codanaivārthanīyā /
children.translated_text: Even if some unseen [force] (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) were postulated due to inexplicability, still, in the absence of discrimination as to what is <s>dharma</s> and what is <s>adharma</s>, <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction) alone is necessarily required. And that [codanā] is accepted — either through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) or through general inference (<s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>). ////

children.text: sā cedaṅgīkṛtā kṛmarthāpattyā, sāmānyato dṛṣṭena vā* ////

body.translated_text: Objection: the diversity of the world is inexplicable [without <s>dharma</s>].

children.text: nanu vikalpanimittaṃ saṃbandhagrahaṇaṃ tatkathaṃ pratyakṣapūrvakatvam /
children.translated_text: Objection: the grasping of a relation, which is the cause of conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>), — how can it be preceded by perception?

children.text: savikalpakamapyanuparatendriyavyāpārasya jāyamānamaparokṣāvabhāsatvātpratyakṣamevetyadoṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: Even conceptual cognition (<s>savikalpaka</s>), arising while sense-organ activity has not ceased, is perception itself, because it manifests as non-mediate (<s>aparokṣa</s>) — hence there is no fault. //

body.text: pratyakṣabauddhamatam /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bauddha</s> (Buddhist) view on perception:

children.text: vikalpapaścāparokṣāvabhāsaśceti citram /
children.translated_text: It is strange [to claim] that what follows conceptualization is non-mediate in its manifestation.

children.text: aparokṣamiti hi svalakṣaṇamucyate tadviṣayo 'vabhāsato 'parokṣāvabhāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: For 'non-mediate' means a particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) — that which has a particular as its object is 'non-mediate in manifestation' because it manifests [it directly].

children.text: vikalpastvabhilāpasaṃyogyapratibhāsatvānna svalakṣaṇaṃ spṛśati, nahyabhilāpaḥ svalakṣaṇaṃ spṛśati, yadi spṛśedabhilāpamātreṇāpi vinākṣavyāpāramaparokṣāvabhāsaḥ syāt, nacāsāvasti, taduktam- anyathaivāgnisaṃyogāddāhaṃ dagdho hi manyate //
children.translated_text: But conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>), because it manifests as connected with verbal expression, does not touch the particular. For verbal expression does not touch the particular. If it did, then by mere verbal expression alone, without sense-organ activity, there would be non-mediate manifestation — but that does not exist. Thus it has been said: 'One who is burned by contact with fire thinks of the burning in one way;

body.text:
anyathā dāhaśabdena dāhārthaḥ saṃprakāśate iti /
yastvayaṃ visphāritākṣasya- gaurayam- iti vikalpo viśadāvabhāsaḥ sa samānakālaviśadavabhāsanirvikalpakasaṃsargakṛtaḥ, tadabhāve 'bhilāpamātre 'numāne ca vikalpākārapratibhāse vaiśādyābhāvāt /
tasmānnirvikalpakameva pratyakṣam /
tatraiva hi viśadasya svalakṣaṇasyāvabhāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: in another way, through the word "burning," the meaning of burning is illuminated.' But as for that conceptual cognition 'this is white' — vivid in manifestation — that arises for one whose eyes are wide open: it is produced by the co-occurrence of a simultaneous, vividly manifest, non-conceptual [perception]. In its absence — in mere verbal expression or in inference — where a conceptual form manifests, there is no vividness. Therefore, only non-conceptual cognition (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) is perception. For only therein is the vivid particular manifested.

body.text: bauddhamatakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the Buddhist view:

body.text:
maivam /
unmīlitanetrasya vikalpo 'pi gaurayamityaparokṣāvabhāsa eva pratīyate nacāsāvanyasaṃsargakṛtaḥ pramāṇābhāvāt /
abhilāpasaṃsargayogyasyāpi sāmānyākārasyābhilāpaliṅgādibhiravaiśadyamindriyaiśca vaiśādyamupapadyata eva /
nahyayaṃ parokṣāparokṣavibhāgo viṣayakṛtaḥ, yadi hi tathā syāt sarvadaiva sāmānyaṃ parokṣaṃ syāt, nacaivamasti,
body.translated_text: Not so. For even the conceptual cognition 'this is white' of one whose eyes are open is experienced as indeed having a non-mediate manifestation — and that is not produced by combination with another [cognition], due to the absence of a proof [for that claim]. For even the universal-form (<s>sāmānyākāra</s>), which is fit to be associated with verbal expression, has non-vividness through verbal expression, inferential signs, and the like, but vividness through the sense-organs — this is quite consistent. For this division into mediate and non-mediate is not object-produced; if it were, then the universal would always be mediate — but that is not the case,

body.text: sāmānyākārasyāpi parokṣāparokṣavibhāgadarśanāt /

children.text: tathāhi - dūrācchvetaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ paśyannanirdhāritagavāśvajātiviśeṣo heṣāviśeṣo heṣāśabdaśravaṇādaśvatvaṃ tasminneva svalakṣaṇe 'numimāno 'pi parokṣaṃ budhyate /
children.translated_text: For example: one seeing a white particular from afar, without having determined the specific class — whether cow or horse — upon hearing a neighing sound, even while inferring horse-ness in that very same particular, cognizes it as mediate.

children.text: vadanti hi aśvo 'pyayaṃ na cakṣuṣā tathāvabhāsata iti /
children.translated_text: For they say: 'This is indeed a horse, but it does not so appear to the eye.'

children.text: pratyāsannastu vadati- saṃpratyaśvatvamapyasya cakṣuṣā paśyāmi na pūrvamiti /
children.translated_text: But one who is nearby says: 'Now I see its horse-ness too with my eyes, which I did not [see] before.'

children.text: svalakṣaṇaṃ tu prāgapi viśadameveti sāmānyāṃśagata evāyaṃ dūrasamīpavartinaḥ parokṣāparokṣavibhāgaḥ, tasmātkāraṇakṛto 'yaṃ vibhāgaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: But the particular was vivid even before — hence this division into mediate and non-mediate belongs to the universal-aspect alone, for one far and near. Therefore, this division is caused by the means [of cognition]. ////

body.translated_text: since the division into mediate and non-mediate is observed even for the universal-form.

body.text:
ekasminnapi hi viṣaye 'kṣairjāyamānaṃ vijñānamāparokṣyaṃ janayati liṅgādijaṃ tu neti kiṃ nopapadyate /
jñānajanyo viṣayagataḥ phalaviśeṣo 'yamāparokṣyaṃ nāma sarvasya saṃvedyaḥ /
yadbhāvābhāvābhyāṃ liṅgābhyāmakṣaiḥ paśyāmi na paśyāmīti visphāritākṣāṇāmeva vyavahāraḥ pravartate /
ato 'sti vikalpasyāpi viśadāvabhāsitvamiti pratyakṣatvopapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: For what is inconsistent in this: that cognition produced by the sense-organs, even regarding a single object, produces non-mediacy, while that produced by inferential signs and the like does not? This [non-mediacy] is a particular result residing in the object, produced by cognition, cognizable by all. The evidence: from whose presence and absence the practical behavior of those with wide-open eyes — 'I see with my eyes,' 'I do not see' — proceeds — [that is the distinguishing mark]. Therefore, even conceptual cognition has vivid manifestation — hence its being perception is established.

body.text: jñānasya savikalpakatvaniyamastatkhaṇḍanaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: The doctrine that all cognition is necessarily conceptual, and its refutation:

body.text:
kecittu savikalpakameva sarvaṃ jñānaṃ na nirvikalpakaṃ nāma kiñcidastīti manyante /
tattu pratīti viruddhaṃ- pratīmo hi vayamakṣasaṃnipātānantaramavivaviktasāmānyaviśeṣavibhāgaṃ saṃmugdhavastumātrahagocaramālocanajñīnam /
tadabhāve tu vikalpa eva na jāyeta /
vikalpatayā hi pūrvānubhūtaṃ jātiviśeṣaṃ saṃjñāviśeṣaṃ cānusmṛtya tena puraḥsthitaṃ vastu vikalpayitavyam /
nacārthamadṛṣṭavatastatsmaraṇamākasmikamevotpadyate /
tasmādasti nirvikalpakamapi jñānam /
body.translated_text: But some hold that all cognition is conceptual (<s>savikalpaka</s>) alone, and that there is nothing called non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) cognition. But that contradicts experience — for we do experience, immediately upon sense-contact, a cognition whose object is mere undifferentiated entity, without distinction of universal and particular having been discriminated. In its absence, conceptual cognition itself would not arise. For in conceptualization, one must recollect a previously experienced specific class and specific name, and conceptualize the present object through those. And for one who has not [previously] perceived the object, that recollection does not arise spontaneously. Therefore, non-conceptual cognition too exists.

body.text: advaitamatena nirvikalpakasya sanmātraviṣayatvāt /
body.translated_text: According to the <s>Advaita</s> (non-dualist) doctrine, since non-conceptual [cognition] has mere being (<s>sanmātra</s>) as its object —

body.text:
tacca sanmātraviṣayamiti kecit /
bhedasya vikalpavedyatvādagṛhīte ca bhede viśeṣāṇāmagrahaṇāt /
kiñcetarābhāvo bhedo pratyakṣeṇa grahītuṃ śakyate natarāṃ avikalpena /
ataśca neha nānāsti kiñcanetyādiniṣedhānāṃ pratyakṣavirodhābhāvāt ekamevādvitīyamityādiśrutibhiradvitīyam brahma siddham /
body.translated_text: And some [say] that [perception] has mere being (<s>sanmātra</s>) as its object, since difference (<s>bheda</s>) is knowable only through conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>), and when difference is not apprehended, specific [properties] are not apprehended. Moreover, mutual absence (<s>itarābhāva</s>), which is difference, cannot be grasped by perception, much less by non-conceptual [perception]. Therefore, since negations such as 'there is not here any diversity whatsoever' (<s>neha nānāsti kiñcana</s>) and the like do not contradict perception, through <s>śrutis</s> such as 'One only, without a second' (<s>ekam evādvitīyam</s>) and the like, the non-dual <s>Brahman</s> is established.

body.text: advaitamatakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the <s>Advaita</s> doctrine:

children.text: tadidamatisāhasam- kiṃ bhavato nīlapītayostiktamadhurayoḥ śītoṣṇayoḥ sukhaduḥkhayoścāvilakṣaṇā buddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: This is extreme rashness — do you [mean to say that] blue and yellow, bitter and sweet, cold and hot, pleasure and pain produce an undifferentiated cognition?

children.text: yadyevaṃ nātrottaraṃ vaktavyam /
children.translated_text: If so, no answer need be given to this.

children.text: naca satsvarūpe savikalpena viśeṣagrahaṇamiti vācyam, avikalpena vikalpasyāpi vilakṣaṇasyotpattyasaṃbhavāt* ////
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that conceptual cognition grasps the specific in the nature of being (<s>sat</s>), since even the arising of conceptual [cognition], which is itself distinct [from non-conceptual], would be impossible without non-conceptual [cognition]. ////

children.text: yaccāvaśyamidamasmādbhinnamityevaṃ vikalpenaiva bhedo grahītavyo nāvikalpena tasya saṃbhavatīti /
children.translated_text: And [as for the claim] that difference must necessarily be grasped only by conceptual cognition as 'this is different from that,' and not by non-conceptual [perception], since that is possible —

children.text: na brūmo bhedasya grahaṇaṃ kintu bhinnānām /
children.translated_text: We do not say [there is] apprehension of difference, but [apprehension] of distinct things.

children.text: teṣāmapi na bhinnatayā kintu svarūpeṇa- yadanyasmādbhinnaṃ nīlaṃ pītaṃ vā tadgṛhyata iti brūmaḥ /
children.translated_text: And even of those [distinct things], not as distinct, but in their own nature — we say that what is blue or yellow, being different from another, is apprehended [in its own form].

children.text: nahi nīlaṃ pītaṃ vā bhedaḥ, tayorhi dharmo bhedaḥ, tadagrahe 'pi dharmiṇāṃ grahaṇaṃ nānupapannam* ////
children.translated_text: For neither blue nor yellow is difference; difference is their property. Even when that [property] is not apprehended, the apprehension of the property-bearers is not impossible. ////

children.text: yadica sanmātraṃ pratyakṣeṇa gṛhyate na nīlaṃ pītaṃ vā tato vikalpenāpīdamasmādbhinnamiti kathaṃ bhedo gṛhyeta /
children.translated_text: Moreover, if only mere being is grasped by perception and not blue or yellow, then how could difference be grasped even by conceptual cognition as 'this is different from that'?

children.text: na hi sadeva sato bhinnamiti saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: For it is not possible that being itself is different from being.

children.text: tasmānnīlādiguṇānāṃ pṛthivyādidravyāṇāṃ ca pratyakṣeṇa grahaṇātprapañcāpalāpaḥ pratyakṣaviruddha eva* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, since blue and other qualities and earth and other substances are grasped by perception, the denial of the phenomenal world is indeed contradicted by perception. ////

children.text: yadi tu pṛthivyādiprapañcaṃ nāpahnumahe taddharmaṃ tu bhedameveti brūyāt, tadapyaśakyam, nīlapītayoritaretarābhāvasya pratyakṣānupalabdhisiddhasyāpahnavāsaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: But if one were to say 'we do not deny the phenomenal world of earth and the like, but only difference, which is their property' — even that is impossible, since the mutual absence between blue and yellow, which is established through the non-apprehension that is itself perceptual, cannot be denied.

children.text: pratyakṣābhāvo 'pi hi pratyakṣavadeva pramāṇāntarebhyo balīyān, itarathā śaśe catuṣpāttvādviṣāṇitvamanumīyate, ato bhedāpalāpo na saṃbhavati* ////
children.translated_text: For even perceptual absence is as strong as perception itself against other means of knowledge; otherwise, horns would be inferred in a hare from its four-footedness. Therefore, the denial of difference is not possible. ////

body.text: yadi tvitaretarāśrayatayā itaretarābhāvagrahaṇasyānavakḷpteravidyāmātranimittaṃ tadityucyate, tadapi - yadi bhinnatayā pratiyoginamāśrayaṃ ca gṛhītvā tata itaretarābhāvo gṛhyeta tataḥ syāt, nīlapītayostvitaretarābhāvānādareṇa svarūpeṇa gṛhītayoḥ paścādataretarābhāvagrahaṇe
body.translated_text: But if it is said that, due to mutual dependence, the apprehension of mutual absence cannot be established [independently] and is therefore caused merely by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) — even to that [we reply]: if, having grasped the counter-correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>) and the locus (<s>āśraya</s>) as distinct, mutual absence were then grasped, there would be [mutual dependence]; but when blue and yellow, having been grasped in their own nature without regard to mutual absence, and [only] subsequently mutual absence is apprehended —

body.text: kimitaretarāśrayatvam* ////
body.translated_text: what mutual dependence is there? ////

body.text:
yadi tu dvitvamapahnūyate na pṛthivyādayasteṣāṃ ca mitho bhedaḥ tadapi pratyakṣaviruddham /
saṃkhyāyāḥ pratyakṣatvāt /

children.text: satyapi pratyakṣavirodhe tadapamardena pravartamānastadbādhenāvāgamo 'dvaitamavagamayatīticet /
children.translated_text: Even if there is contradiction with perception, [if one says that] scripture, operating by overriding that [perception], makes non-duality known through refuting it —

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: pravṛttyasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: Because the operation [of scripture against perception] is impossible.

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ hi nirapekṣaṃ śīghraṃ jāyamānaṃ svaviruddhasyāgamikajñānasya padapadārthasaṃnidhyapekṣāyogyatvanyāyālocanasāpekṣatayā vilambitapravṛtteḥ pravṛttimeva niruṇaddhi* ////
children.translated_text: For perception, being independent and arising swiftly, blocks the very operation of scriptural cognition that contradicts it — since that [scriptural cognition], requiring the proximity of words and their meanings and depending on reasoning and logical analysis, has a delayed operation. ////

body.translated_text: But if duality is denied — not earth and the like, nor their mutual difference — even that contradicts perception, since number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>) is perceptual.

body.text:
kiñcāśakyameva śrutyā prapañcasyāsatyatvaṃ boddhum /
budhyamāne hi śrutirapi prapañcāntargatatvādasatī boddhavyā syāt /
kathaṃ ca śrutyaiva śruterasatvaṃ budhyeta /

children.text: asatvena hi pratīyamānā na pramāṇaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: For if cognized as unreal, it would not be a valid means of knowledge.

children.text: pramāṇatve tvavasthite sattayā pratīyamānāyāḥ śruterna mithyātvaṃ śakyaṃ vaktum /
children.translated_text: But if its validity remains, then since scripture is cognized as real, its falsity cannot be stated.

children.text: nahyekasyaiva vastuno yugapadeva sattvamasatvaṃ ca samuccitya boddhuṃ śakyam, anyataropamardena hyanyataradbuddhāvārohati /
children.translated_text: For it is not possible to cognize one and the same thing as both real and unreal simultaneously; one [cognition] overrides the other, and the other [alone] arises in the intellect.

children.text: tataśca śrutirastīticet, na prapañcāpalāpaḥ saṃbhavati* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, if scripture exists [as valid], the denial of the phenomenal world is not possible. ////

body.translated_text: Moreover, it is simply impossible for scripture to convey the unreality of the phenomenal world. For if [unreality] were being conveyed, scripture too, being part of the phenomenal world, would have to be [considered] unreal. And how could the unreality of scripture be conveyed by scripture itself?

children.text: nanu svayaṃprakāśaṃ brahma kimasyānyena pramāṇena /
children.translated_text: Objection: <s>Brahman</s> is self-luminous — what need has it of another means of knowledge?

children.text: bhavatu brahma svayaṃprakāśaṃ prāpañcābhāvasya kimāyātaṃ, sa hi pramāṇamapekṣata eva* ////
children.translated_text: Let <s>Brahman</s> be self-luminous; what follows from that regarding the non-existence of the phenomenal world? For that [non-existence] indeed requires a means of knowledge. ////

body.text:
kathaṃ cāvidyamānasya prapañcasya pratibhāsaḥ /
avidyayeticet, kasya punariyamavidyā /
jīvānāmiticet, na, teṣāmabhāvāt /
bhāve vā dvaitaprasaṅgaḥ /
brahmaṇi tu viśuddhavijñānātmake niravakāśaivāvidyā /
vidyātmakamapi brahmavidyāśabalamiva bhrāntyāvagamyata iti cet, kasyeyaṃ bhrāntiḥ, yadi na kasyacitsūktam /
jīvānāmiti cet, na, tadabhāvāt /
yadi brāhmaṇaḥ, nāsya bhrāntiḥ saṃbhavatītyuktam /
yadi ca vidyārūpe 'pyavidyā syāt kenāsāvucchidyeta /
dhyānādibhiriticet /
na, teṣāmapyabhāvāt, bhāve tu dvaitāpattiḥ /
brahmaṇi tu sahāvasthānādaviruddhāvidyā na tenocchettuṃ sā śakyā /
tataścānirmokṣaprasaṅgaḥ /
tasmādbrahmaṇaḥ praśaṃsārthairasthāyitvena prapañcasyāsattvamupacaradbhiraupaniṣadairvādaistadanusāribhiścetihāsapurāṇairbhrāntānāṃ vākyatātparyamajānānānāṃ nyāyābhiyogaśūnyānāṃ pralāpomadvaitavāda ityupekṣaṇīyaḥ /
tatsiddhamavikalpasya pratyakṣasya viśeṣaviṣayatvam /
body.translated_text: And how can there be appearance of a non-existent phenomenal world? [If one says] 'through ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>)' — whose is this ignorance? [If one says] 'of the individual souls (<s>jīvas</s>)' — no, because they do not [really] exist [on your view]. Or if they do exist, the absurd consequence of duality [arises]. But in <s>Brahman</s>, which is of the nature of pure consciousness, there is simply no room for ignorance. [If one says] 'even <s>Brahman</s>, though of the nature of knowledge, is apprehended through error, just as knowledge [may appear as] weakness of knowledge' — whose is this error? If no one's — well said. [If one says] 'of the <s>jīvas</s>' — no, because they don't exist. If of <s>Brahman</s> — it has been said that error is not possible for it. And if ignorance exists even in what is of the nature of knowledge, by what could it be removed? [If one says] 'by meditation and the like' — no, because those too do not exist [on your view]; and if they exist, the absurd consequence of duality. Moreover, in <s>Brahman</s>, since [ignorance] co-exists [with it], ignorance is not contradicted by it — so it cannot be removed by it. And therefore, the absurd consequence of non-liberation. Therefore — the <s>Advaita</s> doctrine, which is the prattle of those deluded ones who do not understand the purport of <s>Upaniṣadic</s> statements that praise <s>Brahman</s> through non-permanent denials of the phenomenal world's reality, and of the supportive <s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s> passages, and who are devoid of logical rigor — is to be disregarded. Thus it is established that non-conceptual perception has specific objects as its content.

body.text: nirvikalpakaviṣayakabauddhamatakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the Buddhist doctrine regarding the object of non-conceptual [perception]:

body.text:
apare tu svalakṣaṇamātragocaraṃ nirvikalpakamicchanti /
tadapi pratītiviruddham /
pratīyate hi saṃmugdhākāraṃ vastu sahasaiva yatpañcājjātidravyaguṇakriyānāmabhiḥ pañcadhā savikalpakena vikalpyate gaurayam, daṇḍayam, śaklo 'yam,gacchatyayam, ḍittho 'yamiti /
tatra nirvikalpakamanekākāraṃ vastu saṃmugdhaṃ gṛhṇāti, savikalpaṃ tvekaikākāraṃ jātyādikaṃ vivicya viṣayīkaroti /
body.translated_text: Others, however, hold that non-conceptual [perception] has only the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) as its object. That too contradicts experience. For a thing of confused appearance is directly experienced, which is then differentiated fivefold by conceptual cognition through five [categories] — universal (<s>jāti</s>), substance (<s>dravya</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), action (<s>kriyā</s>), and name (<s>nāman</s>): 'this is a cow,' 'this is a stick,' 'this is white,' 'this goes,' 'this is <s>Diṭṭha</s>.' Therein, non-conceptual [perception] grasps the thing with multiple aspects in a confused manner, while conceptual [perception] discriminates each single aspect such as universal and so on.

body.text: nanu ṣaṣṭho 'pi vikalpo 'sti tadevedamiti tatkathaṃ pañcadhā vikalpa ityucyate /

children.text: natvayaṃ jātivikalpo vyaktipratyabhijñā hīyam /
children.translated_text: But this is not a universal-conceptualization; it is recognition of an individual (<s>vyakti-pratyabhijñā</s>).

children.text: na saṃjñāvikalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is not a name-conceptualization.

children.text: anavagatasaṃjñānāmapi bhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Because it occurs even for those who have not learned the name.

children.text: tiryañco 'pi hyadyajātāḥ svamātaraṃ prathamamupalabhya kṣaṇāntare punarupalabhamānāḥ saiveyamiti śabdānuvedhaśūnyameva pratyabhijānanti, tasmādiyaṃ ṣaṣṭhī kalpanetipṭhacavidhatvānupapattiḥ* ////
children.translated_text: For even animals born just now, having perceived their mother at first and perceiving her again the next moment, recognize [her] as 'this is the same one' — without any verbal accompaniment. Therefore, this is a sixth conceptualization — so the impossibility of fivefoldness [does not hold]. ////

body.translated_text: Objection: There is also a sixth conceptualization — 'this very thing is that' — so how can it be said that conceptualization is fivefold?

body.text:
ucyate- iyamevāsmābhirnāmakalpanetyucyate /
tathāhi ḍittho 'yamiti tāvadgaurayamitivadbhāvātmanā ḍitthātmanā vastu vikalpyate, nadaṇḍītivattatsaṃbandhitayā matvarthānupādānāt /
tatra na ḍitthaśabdena jātivadarthasyātmā atyantabhinnatvāt yatastenaivārtho 'nurajyeta /
tadetadevaṃ vijñeyam- ḍitthaśabdena tadvācyaṃ pūrvāvagataṃ ḍitthamupasthāpya tadātmanā puraḥsthitor'tho vikalpyate ḍittho 'yamiti /
kimuktaṃ bhavati, yo 'sāvasmākaṃ ḍitthaḥ so 'yaṃ puraḥsthito nānya iti /
seyaṃ vyaktipratyabhijñaiva
body.translated_text: It is replied: this is what we call name-conceptualization (<s>nāmakalpanā</s>). For just as 'this is a cow' conceptualizes the thing through its nature as a cow, so too 'this is <s>Diṭṭha</s>' conceptualizes the thing through its nature as <s>Diṭṭha</s> — not as related to it in the manner of 'owner of a staff' (<s>daṇḍī</s>), since there is no use of a possessive suffix. Therein, the term '<s>Diṭṭha</s>' does not [denote] the essence of the object as a universal does, since [names] are entirely different [from universals], so that the object would be colored by that alone. This is to be understood thus: by the word '<s>Diṭṭha</s>,' having brought to mind the previously known <s>Diṭṭha</s> as its referent, the object present before one is conceptualized through that identity as 'this is <s>Diṭṭha</s>.' What is meant is: he who is our <s>Diṭṭha</s> is this one standing before [us], not another. This very thing is individual recognition (<s>vyakti-pratyabhijñā</s>) —

body.text:
pañcamīkalpanā /
sāca śabdavidāṃ nāmarūṣitaiva bhavatīti nāma vikalpeneti vyavahriyate /
etena yadāhuḥ-
body.translated_text: the fifth conceptualization. And for those who know words, it is tinged with the name — hence it is called 'name-conceptualization.' By this, what they say —

body.text:
ḍittho 'yamityaśabdākārasyārthasya śabdākāreṇa vikalpanādapramāṇaṃ savikalpam, iti tadapi nirastam /
nahyatra śabdākāreṇārthaḥ pratīyate kintu pūrvāvagatārthasmaraṇamātre śabdasya vyāpāraḥ, tena ca smṛtenārthena tādātmyena puraḥsthitārthavikalpanāt /

children.text: āhaca- yadā tu yādṛśaḥ piṇḍaḥ pūrvaṃ śabdātpratīyate /
children.translated_text: And it is said: 'When a mass [of meaning], of such a nature as was previously known from a word,'

children.text: tādṛśasmaraṇe hetuḥ śabdastatra yathārthateti /
children.translated_text: 'the word is the cause of remembering that — and therein it is veridical.'

children.text: tasmānnāmavikalpe 'pi jātyādivannāstyatadrūpāropaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even in name-conceptualization, there is no superimposition of what is not its nature, just as with universal and the like.

children.text: kiṃ punarjātyādibhirvikalpyate, dravyaṃ, kiṃ punaridaṃ dravyaṃ nāma, pṛthivyudakatejovāyuprabhṛti //
children.translated_text: But what is conceptualized through universal and the like? Substance (<s>dravya</s>). And what is this substance? Earth, water, fire, air, and so forth. //

body.translated_text: that conceptual [perception] is not a valid means of knowledge because it conceptualizes an object that has no word-form through a word-form as 'this is <s>Diṭṭha</s>' — that too is refuted. For here the object is not cognized through a word-form; rather, the function of the word is merely to recall the previously known object, and through that remembered [object], the object present before [one] is conceptualized as identical.

body.text: dravyābhāve bauddhamatena pūrvapakṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) by the Buddhist doctrine regarding the non-existence of substance:

body.text:
nanu rūpādivyatiriktaṃ dravyaṃ nāma na kiñcidupalabhāmahe /
na ca tasyopalambhakamasti, cakṣurādīnāṃ pañcānāṃ rūpādiṣvevopakṣīṇatvāt /
gandharūparasasparśasaṃghātaḥ pṛthivī /
rasarūpasparśasaṃghāta āpaḥ /
rūpasparśasaṃghātastejaḥ /
śabdasparśasaṃghāto vāyuḥ /
eva rūpādisaṃghātabhedāveva pṛthivyādivibhāgo na dravyaṃ nāma kiñciditi saugatāḥ /
tadayuktam- āgamāpāyiṣu rūpādiṣu yadanuyāyipratyabhijñā jāyate taddravyam /
darśanasparśanābhyāṃ cāsya grahaṇam /
pratyabhijñā ca- yathā badaraphalaṃ śyāmāvasthāyāṃ raktāvasthāyāṃ ca yathā vā ghaṭapiṇḍakapālāvasthāsu mṛddravyam /
asti hi tatra piṇḍāvasthābhede śyāmaraktarūpabhede 'pi dravyapratyabhijñā- mṛdiyaṃ piṇḍāvasthāmapahāya ghacāvasthā saṃjātā śyāmimānaṃ ca tyaktvā pakvā satyaruṇimānaṃ gṛhītavatī /
anantaraṃ ghaṭāvasthāmapahāya kapālikā jāteti /
evaṃ tantupaṭādyavasthāsvapi draṣṭavyam /
body.translated_text: Objection: We do not apprehend any substance apart from color and the like. Nor is there a means of apprehending it, since the five [sense organs] — the eye and the like — are exhausted in [apprehending] color and the like. Earth is an aggregate of smell, color, taste, and touch. Water is an aggregate of taste, color, and touch. Fire is an aggregate of color and touch. Air is an aggregate of sound and touch. Thus, the division into earth and the like is based on differences of aggregates of color and the like alone — there is no such thing as substance — so say the <s>Saugatas</s> (Buddhists). That is unjustified — substance is that in which, when colors and the like come and go, a continuing recognition (<s>anuyāyin pratyabhijñā</s>) arises. And its apprehension is through seeing and touching. And the recognition [is as follows]: just as a jujube fruit in its dark state and in its red state, or just as the clay substance in the states of lump, pot, and potsherd. For even though there is difference of state from lump [to pot] and difference of color from dark to red, there is recognition of the substance: 'this clay, having left the lump-state, has attained the pot-state; and having abandoned its dark color, upon being fired, has assumed a reddish color.' Subsequently, 'having left the pot-state, it has become potsherds.' Similarly, this is to be observed in the states of thread, cloth, and so forth.

body.text: tarkamatenāvayaveṣvavayavyutpattiḥ /
body.translated_text: The origination of the composite (<s>avayavin</s>) from the parts (<s>avayava</s>) according to the <s>Tarka</s> (logic) school:

children.text: nanu tantupaṭādiṣu dravyāntarotpattirevābhimatā, anyathā hyavayavyapalāpaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: In thread-cloth and the like, the origination of a different substance is indeed accepted [by <s>Naiyāyikas</s>]; otherwise, there would be denial of the composite.

children.text: nāvayavinamapahnumahe, dravyāntarotpattiṃ tu necchāmaḥ pratipattyabhāvāt /
children.translated_text: We do not deny the composite; but we do not accept the origination of a different substance, due to the absence of apprehension.

children.text: tantava eva hi saṃyogaviśeṣādekadravyatāmāpadyante, avayavī ca bhavanti tādṛśāśca paṭajātiṃ sthaulyaṃ ca bibhrata ekapaṭasthūlabuddhyā gṛhyanta iti laukikī pratipattiḥ /
children.translated_text: For the threads themselves, through a particular conjunction, attain the state of being one substance and become the composite, and bearing such [properties as] the cloth-universal and grossness, they are grasped by the single cognition 'one [and] gross cloth' — this is the ordinary understanding.

children.text: ato na dravyasya kadācidāgamo 'pāyo vā, ghaṭapaṭagavāśvaśuklaraktādyavasthānāmevāgamāpāyau* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, substance never comes into being or perishes; only the states — such as pot, cloth, cow, horse, white, red, and the like — come and go. ////

body.text: āhaca- āvirbhāvatirobhāvadharmakeṣvanuyāyi yat //
body.translated_text: And it is said: 'That which continues (<s>anuyāyin</s>) through [properties] that appear and disappear —'

body.text:
taddharmi yatra ca jñānaṃ prāgdharmagrahaṇādbhavediti /
tathā- yādṛśamasmābhirabhihitaṃ dravyaṃ tādṛśasyaiva hi sarvasya guṇa eva bhidyate na svarūpamiti /
tatsiddhaṃ dravyam /
tacca jātyādibhiḥ pañcadhā savikalpena vibhajyate /
ataḥ savikalpakamapi pratyakṣaṃ, tatpūrvakaṃ cānumānādīti siddhaṃ teṣāmapyanimittatvamiti pratyakṣasūtram /
body.translated_text: 'that is the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>); and the cognition that arises before the apprehension of the [new] property [is the recognition].' Likewise: 'Of such substance as we have described, it is only the quality that changes, not the essential nature.' Thus substance is established. And that [substance] is differentiated fivefold by conceptual [cognition] through universal and the like. Therefore, conceptual [perception] too is perceptual, and inference and the like, which are based on it [are also valid] — thus it is established that those [means of knowledge] too are not causeless. Thus [concludes] the <s>pratyakṣa-sūtra</s> (aphorism on perception).

body.text: dharme vedaprāmāṇyādhikaraṇam //5 //
body.translated_text: The <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic) on the authority of the <s>Veda</s> regarding <s>dharma</s>: // 5 //

body.text: autpattikastu śabdasyārthena saṃbandhaḥ, tasya jñānamupadeśo 'nyatirekaścārthe 'nupalabdhe tatpramāmāṇaṃ bādarāyaṇasyānapekṣatvāt // Jaim_1,1.5 //
body.translated_text: 'But the relation of the word with its meaning is innate (<s>autpattika</s>); the instruction regarding that [meaning] is knowledge; and the exclusion [of other meanings] — regarding an object not apprehended [by other means], that [<s>Veda</s>] is the means of valid knowledge, according to <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, because of [its] independence.' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.5 //

body.text:
uktaṃ pratyakṣādīnāmanimittatvam /
tata eva /
tanmūlapuruṣavacanasyāpyanimittatvam /
evaṃ tarhi śabdasya sarvatra pramāṇāntarāpekṣayaiva prāmāṇyadarśanāttadabhāve tasyāpyaprāmāṇyādabhāvagamyatvamevāyātaṃ dharmasyetyāśaṅkānirākaraṇāya codanāyāḥ prāmāṇyamucyate /
satyam /
loke pramāṇāntaramūlānāṃ prāmāṇyaṃ atanmūlānāṃ cāprāmāṇyaṃ dṛśyate, nanvemapi sāpekṣaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ kintu svata eva /
anāptavākyasya tvaprāmāṇyaṃ na mūlavirahāt kintu duṣṭamūlatayā śabdasya duṣṭatvātsvābhīvikasya prāmāṇyasyāpavādāt /
body.translated_text: It has been stated that perception and the like are not the cause [of knowing <s>dharma</s>]. From that very [fact], even the human statement based on those [means of knowledge] is not the cause [of knowing <s>dharma</s>]. If so, then since the authority of words is everywhere seen only in dependence on other means of knowledge, in the absence of those [means], its invalidity too would follow — and thus <s>dharma</s> would remain unascertainable. To remove this apprehension, the authority of injunction (<s>codanā</s>) is stated. True — in the world, the authority of [statements] based on other means of knowledge, and the invalidity of those not so based, are seen. But even that authority is not dependent [on other means] but is intrinsic (<s>svataḥ</s>). The invalidity of the statement of a non-trustworthy person (<s>anāpta</s>) is not due to the absence of a basis, but due to a defective basis — from the defectiveness of the word, which overrides its intrinsic authority.

body.text: vedasyāpauruṣeyatvāt /
body.translated_text: Because of the <s>Veda's</s> being authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>). //

children.text: apauruṣeye tu vede yadyapyāptapraṇītatvaṃ nāsti prāmāṇyasya tadapekṣābhāvādanāptasparśanimittadoṣābhāvāccānapoditaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: But in the case of the authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) Veda, even though there is no composition by a trustworthy person, since validity does not depend on that, and since there is no defect caused by contact with an untrustworthy person, its validity remains unimpeached.

children.text: tredhā hyatra puruṣānupraveśaḥ- padapadārthasaṃbandhadvāreṇa vākyavākyārthasaṃbandhadvāreṇa grandhasyaiva vā bhāratādivatpauruṣeyatvāt /
children.translated_text: For the involvement of a person [in the Veda] is threefold: through the relation of words and word-meanings, through the relation of sentences and sentence-meanings, or through the text itself being authored like the <s>Bhārata</s> and so forth.

children.text: natvetannayamapyasti, padapadārthasaṃbandhasya nityatvamatrautpattikaśabdenoktaṃ, vākyārthasya ca padārthamūlatvaṃ vedasya cāpauruṣeyatvamupariṣṭādvakṣyate //
children.translated_text: But this approach is not [applicable here either]: the eternality of the word-meaning relation is stated here by the term <s>autpattika</s> ('innate'); that sentence-meaning is grounded in word-meaning, and that the Veda is authorless — these will be stated later. //

body.text: sāmānyataḥ pramāṇalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: General definition of a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>):

body.text:
naca sākṣādbādhakamastītyavyatirekaśabdenocyate /
anupalabdhārthatvācca nānuvādalakṣaṇamaprāmāṇyamastīti arthe 'nupalabdhe ityanenoktam /
etacca viśeṣaṇatrayamupāgadadānena sūtrakāreṇa kāraṇadoṣabādhakajñānarahitamagṛhītagrāhijñānaṃ pramāṇamiti pramāṇalakṣaṇaṃ sūcitam /
body.translated_text: And since there is no direct contradicting [evidence], this is stated by the word <s>avyatireka</s> ('non-deviation'). And since the object is not [already] apprehended, there is no invalidity of the kind that characterizes mere restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) — this is stated by the phrase 'the object being unapprehended.' And by adopting this triad of qualifications, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> [addresses] defect in the cause, contradiction, and —

body.text: prabhākaramatena pramāṇalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: Definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> according to the <s>Prābhākara</s> view:

body.text: nanvevaṃ dhārāvāhikeṣuttareṣāṃ pūrvagṛhītārthaviṣayakatvādaprāmāṇyaṃ syāt tasmādanubhūtiḥ pramāṇamitipramāṇalakṣaṇam,
body.translated_text: But if so, in a continuous stream [of cognitions], the later ones, having as their object what was previously grasped, would be invalid. Therefore, 'experience (<s>anubhūti</s>) is the means of knowledge' — this is the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: smṛtivyatiriktā ca pratītiranubhūtiḥ /
children.translated_text: And cognition other than memory (<s>smṛti</s>) is experience (<s>anubhūti</s>).

children.text: smṛtiśca saṃskāramātrajaṃ jñānamabhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: And memory is defined as knowledge born from impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) alone.

children.text: mātragrahaṇaṃ ca saṃskārasaghrīcīnendriyajasya pratyabhijñānasya smṛtitvaprasaṅgenāprāmāṇyaṃ māprasāṃkṣīdityelamartham /
children.translated_text: The word 'alone' (<s>mātra</s>) is for the purpose of preventing the invalidity — lest it be extended — to recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>), which is born of a combination of impressions and sense-organs, through the unwanted consequence of its being classified as memory.

children.text: tadevaṃ saṃskārātiriktakāraṇajanyaṃ jñānaṃ pramāṇamityuktaṃ bhavati, tadidaṃ svapnadarśane tāvadavyāpakam, saṃskāramātrajasyāpi jñānasya svarūpe kartari ca prāmāṇyamiṣṭaṃ bhavatām* ////
children.translated_text: Thus it has been stated that knowledge produced by a cause other than mere impressions is <s>pramāṇa</s>. But this is inapplicable to dream-perception, since even knowledge born from impressions alone is accepted by you as valid regarding its own form and its agent. ////

children.text: atha smartavyāpekṣayaiva smṛteḥ smṛtitvaṃ tadviṣayasaṃskārajatvāt, svarūpakartrapekṣayā tvanubhūtireva, ataḥ siddhyati prāmāṇyamityucyate /
children.translated_text: If it is said that memory has the character of memory only in relation to the object remembered — because it is born from an impression of that object — but in relation to its own form and agent, it is experience itself, and therefore validity is established —

children.text: evaṃ tarhi mātragrahaṇamanarthakam, pratyabhijñānasyāpi pūrvānubhūtāṃśāpekṣayaiva smṛtitvāttatra cāprāmāṇyamiṣṭameva, yatra tvaṃśe prāmāṇyaṃ tatrānubhūtireva sā* ////
children.translated_text: If so, then the word 'alone' (<s>mātra</s>) is purposeless, since even recognition, being memory only with respect to the previously experienced aspect, is [rightly] invalid in that respect, and in the aspect where it is valid, it is experience itself. ////

body.text:
kiñcānuvādānāṃ ya evaṃ vidvānpaurṇamāsīmityādīnāmapi saṃskāramātrajatvābhāvātprāmāṇyaṃ syāt /
bhavatviticet /
na /

children.text: lokavirodhāt /
children.translated_text: Because it contradicts common experience.

children.text: tathā laukikamapi vākyaṃ vaktṛjñānānumiterthe 'nuvādakatayā pravartamānaṃ pramāṇaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Likewise, even an ordinary statement, operating as a restatement of something [already known] through inference from the speaker's knowledge, would be a means of knowledge.

children.text: nacaitadiṣṭhaṃ bhavatām /
children.translated_text: And this is not accepted by you.

children.text: asaṃnikṛṣṭagrahaṇamanuvādānāṃ śāstratvanivṛttyarthamityaṅgīkaraṇāt* ////
children.translated_text: Because [you] accept that the non-apprehension of what is not in contact [with the senses] serves to exclude the scriptural status of restatements. ////

body.translated_text: Moreover, even restatements (<s>anuvāda</s>) such as 'he who knows thus [offers] on the full-moon day' and the like, not being born from mere impressions, would be valid. If [one says] 'let it be so' — no.

children.text: athānapekṣaṃ pramāṇaṃ yatsvaviṣaye pramāṇāntaraṃ nāpekṣate tatpramāṇam /
children.translated_text: Now, [consider another definition:] 'a means of knowledge is that which is independent — which does not require another means of knowledge regarding its own object — that is <s>pramāṇa</s>.'

children.text: anuvādānāṃ tu purovādasāpekṣatvādaprāmāṇyamiti /
children.translated_text: And restatements, being dependent on a prior statement, are invalid.

children.text: evaṃ tarhi laukikaṃ vākyamapyanumiter'the pravartamānamanumānasya śaṅkānirākaraṇamātraupayikatvādarthapratipādane tadapekṣābhāvātpramāṇaṃ syāt* ////
children.translated_text: If so, then even an ordinary statement that operates regarding what is [already known] through inference — since inference is useful only for removing doubt, and [the statement] does not depend on it for conveying the meaning — would be a means of knowledge. ////

body.text:
tathānumānasya prāmāṇyaṃ na syāt, taddhi niyamagrahaṇamapekṣate /
na ca gṛhītamarthaṃ mātrayāpyadhikaṃ gṛhṇātīti bhavatāṃ darśanam /

children.text: pītaśaṅkhajñānamapyanubhūtitvātpramāṇaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Even the cognition of a yellow conch-shell, being an experience, would be a means of knowledge.

children.text: iṣṭameveti vadato lokavirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: [If one says] 'that is indeed accepted' — that contradicts common experience.

children.text: tasmādyathārthamāgṛhītagrāhijñānaṃ pramāṇamiti vaktavyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it should be stated that knowledge which grasps what has not been grasped and corresponds to the object is a means of knowledge.

children.text: dhārāvāhikeṣvapyuttarottareṣāṃ kālāntarasaṃbandhasyāgṛhītasya grahaṇādyuktaṃ prāmāṇyam //
children.translated_text: Even in a continuous stream [of cognitions], the validity of later ones is justified, since they grasp the temporal relation that was not grasped [by the earlier ones]. //

body.translated_text: Likewise, inference would not be valid, for it requires the apprehension of the invariable concomitance (<s>niyama</s>). And it is your view that [a cognition] does not grasp anything even slightly additional to what has [already] been grasped.

body.text: kālapratyakṣanirūpaṇam /
body.translated_text: Investigation of the perception of time:

body.text:
sannāpi kālabhedo 'tisūkṣmatvānna parāmṛṣyata iti cet, aho sūkṣmadarśī devānāṃpriyaḥ /
yo hi samānaviṣayayā vijñānadhārayā ciramavasthāyoparataḥ so 'nantarakṣaṇasaṃbandhitayārthaṃ smarati /
tathāhi kimatra ghaṭo 'vasthita iti ṣaṣṭhaḥ kathayati- asminkṣaṇe mayopalabdha iti /

children.text: tathā prātarārabhyaitāvatkālaṃ mayopalabdha iti /
children.translated_text: 'It was perceived by me from morning for this much time' — thus.

children.text: kālabhede tvagṛhīte kathamevaṃ vadet /
children.translated_text: But if temporal difference were not grasped, how would one speak thus?

children.text: tasmādasti kālabhedaparāmarśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, apprehension of temporal difference does exist.

children.text: tadādhikyācca siddhamuttareṣāṃ prāmāṇyam* ////
