children.translated_text: And due to that additional [content], the validity of later [cognitions] is established. ////

body.translated_text: If [one says] that even though temporal difference exists, it is not apprehended due to extreme subtlety — oh, what a subtle-sighted dear friend of the gods! For one who, having remained for a long time with a stream of cognitions having the same object, and then having ceased, remembers the object as connected with the immediately preceding moment — for instance —

body.text:
nanu yathārthatāmapi cetprāmāṇalakṣaṇam, uṣṇajalajñānapramāṇaṃ syāt /
iṣṭamevaitat /
nanu lokavirodhaḥ syāt /
syāt yadyayathārthatāṃ jānanta eva laukikāḥ prāmāṇyaṃ
body.translated_text: But if correspondence with reality (<s>yathārthatā</s>) is also the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>, then the cognition of hot water would be a means of knowledge. 'That is indeed accepted.' But would there not be a contradiction with common experience? There would be, if ordinary people, while knowing the non-correspondence with reality, were to consider it —

children.text: manvīran /
children.translated_text: valid.

children.text: te tu yathārthatāmevaitasya manvānaḥ prāmāṇyamabhrāntatvaṃ ca manyante /
children.translated_text: But they, considering it to correspond with reality, regard it as valid and as non-erroneous.

children.text: yetvayathārthatāṃ jānanti te naiva prāmāṇyaṃ manyante, nāpyabhrāntatām, tasmānnāsti virodhaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Those who know its non-correspondence with reality neither regard it as valid nor as non-erroneous. Therefore, there is no contradiction. ////

body.text: pītaśaṅkhajñānasyāpi smṛtitvābhimānādanubhūtitvāparijñānādaprāmāṇyaṃ manyante, ato 'smākamapi nāsti virodha iti cet, tadayuktam /

children.text: nahi laukikāḥ śuktirajatajñāne 'pi smṛtitvaṃ manyante, natarāṃ pītaśaṅkhajñāne /
children.translated_text: For ordinary people do not consider even the cognition of silver in a shell to be memory, much less the cognition of a yellow conch-shell.

children.text: tasmātsūktam arthe 'nupalabdhe iti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, well said is 'the object being unapprehended.'

children.text: vṛttikārastvanyathedaṃ varṇayāñcakāretyevamādinopavarṣamatena /
children.translated_text: But the <s>Vṛttikāra</s> explains this differently — thus, according to <s>Upavarṣa</s>'s view.

children.text: tasya nimittaparīṣṭirityevamādisūtratrayamanyathākṛtvā vyācaṣṭe bhāṣyakāraḥ, tatra nimittasūtreṇa tāvatpratijñātasya codanāprāmāṇyasya parīkṣāpadeśena svataḥprāmāṇyaṃ heturityucyate //
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) interprets it differently by reconstruing the three <s>sūtras</s> beginning with 'the examination of the cause thereof' — there, by the <s>sūtra</s> on 'cause,' what is stated is that self-validity (<s>svataḥprāmāṇya</s>) is the reason, under the pretext of examining the validity of injunction (<s>codanā</s>) that was asserted. //

body.translated_text: If [one says] that even regarding the cognition of a yellow conch-shell, people consider it invalid because they assume it to be memory and do not recognize it as experience, and therefore there is no contradiction for us either — that is improper.

body.text: prāmāṇānāṃ svataḥprāmāṇyam /
body.translated_text: Self-validity of the means of knowledge (<s>svataḥprāmāṇya</s>):

children.text: prasiddhāni hi pratyakṣādīni pramāṇāni tadantargataṃ ca śāstraṃ, atastadapi prasiddhameva /
children.translated_text: For the well-known means of knowledge — perception and the like — are well-established, and scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) is included within them; therefore, it too is well-established.

children.text: na ca prasiddhasya pramāṇasya prāmāṇyamanyena parīkṣitavyam, svata eva tasya svaviṣayopasthāpanasāmarthyāt /
children.translated_text: And the validity of a well-established means of knowledge need not be tested by another, since it has of itself the capacity to present its own object.

children.text: yadi ca parīkṣyeta, tato yena parīkṣyeta tasyāpyanyenetyavasthā syāt /
children.translated_text: And if it were to be tested, then that by which it would be tested would also [need to be tested] by another — and thus an infinite regress would result.

children.text: tasmātprasiddhatvātpramāṇasya codanāpi pramāṇamiti* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the means of knowledge is well-established, injunction (<s>codanā</s>) too is a means of knowledge. ////

body.text: nanu na jñānamutpannamityevārthatathātvamadhyavasātuṃ śakyam- prasiddhatarasyāpi pratyakṣasyāyathārthasyotpattidarśanāt, yathā- śuktikāyāṃ rajatamiti pratyakṣamevāyathārthaṃ na śuktikāyāṃ rajatajñānasya, pratyakṣābhāsātvāt //
body.translated_text: But one cannot determine the correspondence of knowledge with reality merely from the fact that knowledge has arisen — since even the most well-established perception is seen to arise erroneously, as in 'this is silver in a shell' — that is perception itself, yet erroneous. It is not the case that the cognition of silver in a shell —

body.text: pratyakṣalakṣaṇaṃ, pratyakṣakhaṇḍaḥ /
body.translated_text: Definition of perception; the chapter on perception:

body.text:
kiṃpunarābhāsaṃkīrṇaṃ pratyakṣalakṣaṇam /
taddarśayati- tatsaṃprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanmasatpratyakṣam- yadābhāsaṃ vijñānaṃ tenendriyāṇāṃ saṃprayoge yadvijñānaṃ tatsatpratyakṣam /

children.text: tatsatorvyatyayādābhāsāsaṃkarasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: By the transposition of 'real' (<s>sat</s>), the exclusion of semblance is accomplished.

children.text: taditi cāvyayaṃ tṛtīyāntaṃ tenetyarthe /
children.translated_text: And the indeclinable <s>tat</s> is in the instrumental sense, meaning 'by that.'

children.text: nanvasatyapi vyatyaye nāsti saṃkaraḥ- indriyasaṃprayogajaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣam- ityetāvadeva vaktavyam /
children.translated_text: But even without the transposition, there is no confusion — one need only say 'knowledge born from sense-contact is perception.'

children.text: nahi śuktikāyāṃ rajatajñānamindriyasaṃprayogajaṃ, kiṃ tarhi, indriyasaṃprayogacchuktiśakalaṃ rajatasādhāraṇena bhāsvaratvādirūpeṇa gṛhītam, asādhāraṇaṃ tu śuktikātvamindriyadaurbalyādgṛhītam, anantaraṃ ca saṃskārādbodhādrajataṃ smṛtaṃ, tataḥ smṛtarajatātmanā śuktivyaktirdeṣavaśādgṛhyate, ato nendriyasaṃprayogajaṃ rajatavijñānamiti nātiprasaṅgaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: For the cognition of silver in a shell is not born from sense-contact; rather, the shell-fragment in contact with the senses is grasped through the common characteristic of brilliance shared with silver, while the distinctive characteristic of being a shell is not grasped due to weakness of the sense-organ; then immediately —

body.translated_text: What then is the definition of perception, unmixed with semblance (<s>ābhāsa</s>)? He shows: 'Perception is the cognition that arises from the contact of a person's senses with the real object' — whatever cognition is a semblance, when the senses are in contact, whatever cognition [arises with] the real [object], that is perception.

body.text:
praṇāḍyāstīndriyasaṃprayogajatvamiti tadvyāvṛttyarthaṃ tatsaṃprayogajatvamiti /
viśeṣaṇaṃ vaktavyamiti cet , tanna /
nahīha yathākathañcitsaṃprayogajanyatvaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ, kintu sākṣāttajjanyatvam /
yadica yathākathañcidityāśrīyeta tato viśeṣaṇe satyapyativyāptimallakṣaṇaṃ syāt- ārādignimadhyakṣayato
body.translated_text: Because even the nerve-channel has sense-contact-born-ness — for the exclusion of that, 'born from contact with that [real object]' — [if one says] a qualifier must be stated — that is not so. For here the definition is not being born from contact in any manner whatsoever, but being directly produced by it. If —

children.text: yadauṣṇyaviṣayamanumānaṃ tadapi pratyakṣaṃ syāt, praṇāḍyendriyasaṃprayogajatvāt saṃprayukta viṣayatvācca, astihyauṣṇyasyendriyasaṃprayogaḥ saṃyuktasamavāyalakṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even inference about heat would be perception, since it is born from the contact of the nerve-channel sense-organ and since the object [heat] is in contact — for heat does have sense-contact of the type 'conjunction-with-what-is-conjoined' (<s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s>).

children.text: tasmādavaśyaṃ sākṣātsaṃprayogajatvaṃ lakṣaṇamityaṅgīkartavyam, ataḥ śuktirajatavedane 'pi vyabhicārābhāvanarthakastatsatorvyatyayaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, being directly produced from contact must be accepted as the definition. Hence, even in the cognition of shell-silver, since there is no deviation [from the definition], the transposition of 'real' is purposeless. ////

children.text: satyam- sākṣātsaṃprayogajatvaṃ lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: True — being directly produced from contact is the definition.

children.text: satyaṃ ca śuktirajatajñāne 'pi vyabhicārābhāvādanarthakastatsatorvyatyayaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: And true, even in the cognition of shell-silver, since there is no deviation, the transposition of 'real' is purposeless. ////

body.text: satyam- sākṣātsaṃprayogajatvaṃ lakṣaṇam /

children.text: satyaṃ ca śuktirajatajñāne 'pi nātiprasaṅgaḥ, pītaśaṅkhadvicandrādijñāneṣvativyāptiḥ syāt sākṣātsaṃprayogajatvāt /
children.translated_text: And true, even in the cognition of shell-silver there is no over-extension; but in the cognitions of a yellow conch-shell, double moon, and the like, there would be over-extension, since they are directly produced from sense-contact.

children.text: api ca smṛtena rajatākāreṇa yatsaṃnihitasya śuktiśakalasya tādātmyagrahaṇaṃ tadanuparatendriyavyāpārasya bhavatsākṣātsaṃprayogajamevāparokṣatvāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the apprehension of identity of the shell-fragment present [before the senses] with the remembered form of silver — that, occurring while the sensory activity has not yet ceased, is directly produced from sense-contact and is non-mediate (<s>aparokṣa</s>).

children.text: tasmādābhāsanivṛttyarthatyaya iti sūktam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, well said is the [inclusion of] 'real' for the exclusion of semblance.

children.text: bhāṣye tvābhāsapradarśanārthaṃ śuktikārajatajñānodāharaṇamityanavadyam* ////
children.translated_text: But in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, the example of shell-silver cognition is for the purpose of illustrating semblance — thus there is no fault. ////

body.translated_text: True — being directly produced from contact is the definition.

body.text: tatsaṃprayogajatve kathaṃ vivacyete /
body.translated_text: How are [these two] explained given that [perception is] born from contact with the real [object]?

body.text:
ucyate- jñānasvarasādeva viṣayasya tathātvamadhyavasīyate, tadanyathātvaṃ tu kāraṇadoṣajñānādarthānyathātvajñānādvāvagandavyam /
ato yatra prayatnenānviṣyamāṇo 'pi kāraṇadoṣo bādhakajñānaṃ vā nopalabhyate tatpramāṇam, itaraccāpramāṇam /
codanārthajñānasya
body.translated_text: It is replied: By the natural force of knowledge itself, the object's being-such is determined. Its being-otherwise, however, is to be understood from knowledge of a defect in the cause or from knowledge of the object's being otherwise. Therefore, where, even when sought with effort, neither a defect in the cause nor contradicting knowledge is found —

children.text: tūbhayābhāvātsiddhaṃ ṭaprāmāṇyam /
children.translated_text: due to the absence of both, [self-]validity is established.

children.text: ityautpattikasūtram* ////
children.translated_text: Thus [concludes] the <s>autpattika</s> sūtra. ////

children.text: nanu sarva eva nirālambanaḥ' ityādinā pūrvoktahetudvayākṣepanimittamithyātvākṣepeṇa śūnyavādī pratyavatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: But a proponent of the void (<s>śūnyavādin</s>) objects by imputing falsity through the rejection of both the aforementioned grounds, [saying] 'all [cognitions] are without a basis' and so forth.

children.text: tathāhi - yatra kāraṇadoṣajñānaṃ bādhakajñānaṃ vā tatra mithyātvam, anyatra satyatvamiti vyavasthā nopapadyate, sarvajñānānāṃ mithyātvāt //
children.translated_text: For thus: 'Where there is knowledge of a causal defect or contradicting knowledge, there is falsity; elsewhere, truth' — this distinction is untenable, since all cognitions are false. //

body.text: bāhyārthaśūnyavādenākṣepaḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection by the doctrine of the external-object-void (<s>bāhyārthaśūnyavāda</s>):

body.text:
sarvameva hi jñānamātmāṃśaparyavasitamanādivāsanāvaśādātmānameva bāhyatayādhyavasyanmithyaiva /
kathaṃ punarātmāṃśaparyavasā yitvaṃ gamyate, anumānāt, bāhye ca pravṛttyasāmarthyāt /

children.text: yathācāsāmārthye tathā vakṣyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: How there is such incapacity — that we shall state.

children.text: saṃpratyanumānamucyate- stambhādipratyayāḥ svāṃśameva bāhyatayādhyavasyanto mithyābhūtāḥ pratyayatvāt svapnapratyayavat śuktakārajatādipratyayavacca /
children.translated_text: For now, the inference is stated: Cognitions of pillars and the like, determining their own aspect alone as external, are false — because they are cognitions — like dream-cognitions, like cognitions of shell-silver and the like.

children.text: svapnādipratyayā hi yathāvagamyamānabāhyārthābhāvāddeśāntarakālāntaravartināṃ ca saṃnihitadeśakālatayā pratibhāsasaṃbhavāt kvacitkadācidapyasaṃbhavatāṃ svaśiraśchedādīnāṃ svapne pratibhāsādavaśyaṃ svātmānameva bahirvadgṛhṇantītyabhyupagantavyam /
children.translated_text: For dream-cognitions and the like, since there is no external object as it is apprehended, and since it is possible for things existing in other places and times to appear as present in the immediate place and time, and since things impossible anywhere at any time — such as the cutting of one's own head — appear in dreams, necessarily they are [confined to] their own —

children.text: atastatsāmānyājjāgrajjñānānāmapi svāṃśaparyavasāyitvānmithyātvam- iti prāpte* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, by similarity with those, even waking cognitions, being confined to their own aspect, are false — thus it is concluded. ////

body.translated_text: For all knowledge, being confined to the self's aspect, due to beginningless impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), determining the self alone as external — is simply false. How, then, is it known that [cognition] is confined to the self's aspect? By inference, and from the incapacity to operate upon external [objects].

children.text: abhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: It is replied:

children.text: na tāvatsvapnādipratyayāḥ svāṃśāvalambanāḥ, te 'pi bāhyārthamevānyathāsantamevānyathā gṛhṇantīti vakṣyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: First, dream-cognitions and the like are not based on their own aspect. They too grasp only an external object — grasping what actually exists as something else — this we shall state.

children.text: bhavatu vā tatrātmakhyānaṃ, naitāvatā nīlādipratyayāstathā bhavitumarhanti, tatra hi nīlamidaṃ pītamidaṃ stambho 'yaṃ ghaṭo 'yamityevamidamākārāspadībhūtaṃ bāhyaṃ nīlādi pratyakṣeṇāvagamyamānaṃ na śakyamanumānenāpahnotum /
children.translated_text: Or let there be self-manifestation (<s>ātmakhyāna</s>) in that case. But not on that account should cognitions of blue and the like be so, for there, the external blue and the like — apprehended by perception as 'this is blue,' 'this is yellow,' 'this is a pillar,' 'this is a pot' — being the locus of the 'this'-form, cannot —

children.text: ātmagrāhitve hyahaṃ nīlamiti syāt* ////
children.translated_text: For if [cognition] grasped itself, it would be 'I am blue.' ////

body.text: tadevaṃ pratyakṣameva bāhyārthamupasthāpya tadapahnavapravṛttasyānumānasyodayaṃ niruṇaddhi /

children.text: svapnādiṣu tu bādhakena jñānāntareṇa bāhyasadbhāvanirākaraṇādyujyetātmakhyātiḥ /
children.translated_text: But in dreams and the like, since external existence is negated by another cognition that sublates [the dream], <s>ātmakhyāti</s> (error as self-manifestation) would be reasonable.

children.text: natviha tathā bādhakamastyanyat bhavaduktādanumānāt /
children.translated_text: But here there is no other sublating [cognition] apart from the inference you have stated.

children.text: nacānumānamalaṃ bādhitumityuktam /
children.translated_text: And it has been said that inference is not capable of sublating [perception].

children.text: dūṣaṇasahasraṃ cāsyānumānasya vārtike prapañcitamityuparamyate //
children.translated_text: And a thousand refutations of this inference have been elaborated in the <s>Vārtika</s> — hence we desist. //

body.translated_text: Thus, perception itself, having presented the external object, blocks the arising of inference that proceeds to deny it.

body.text: yogācārasautrāntikayoḥ kalahaḥ //
body.translated_text: The dispute between the <s>Yogācāra</s> and the <s>Sautrāntika</s>:

body.text: evamanumāne pratyakṣavirodhena nirākṛte pratyakṣasya bahiḥpravṛttau sāmarthye nāstītyevaṃ pūrvoktākṣepeṇa śūnyastvityādinā sa eva śūnyavādī punaḥ pratyakṣavatiṣṭhate /

children.text: tadihaivaṃ cintyate- yadidaṃ nīlamidaṃ pītamidamiti nīlādyākāraṃ vastu prathate tatkiṃ vijñānameva tathā prathate kiṃvā bāhyaṃ vastviti /
children.translated_text: Here, then, the following is considered: This reality that manifests as 'this is blue, this is yellow, this is [something]' with the form of blue and so on — does consciousness itself manifest in that way, or is it an external object?

children.text: tadarthamidaṃ vicāryate- kiṃ vijñānaṃ pratyakṣamutānumeyamiti, pratyakṣatve sati nirākārasya pratyakṣagrahaṇayogāt, ākārasya caikasyaiva grahaṇāt gṛhyamāṇa ākāro jñāna evāvatiṣṭhata ityarthasyāgṛhyamāṇatvādasattvameva bhavati /
children.translated_text: For this purpose the following is examined: Is consciousness perceptual or inferential? If perceptual, then since a formless [consciousness] can be grasped by perception, and since only one form alone is grasped, the grasped form subsists in consciousness alone — and since the object is not grasped, its very non-existence follows.

children.text: anumeyatve tu bāhyārthaṃ vinānumānāsaṃbhavādbāhyārthasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: But if [consciousness is] inferential, then since inference is impossible without an external object, the existence of the external object is established.

children.text: tatra- jñānamevaivamākāramātmanā prathate kutaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therein — 'Consciousness itself manifests with such form by itself — from what [evidence]?

body.translated_text: Thus, when inference has been refuted through its contradiction with perception, the same <s>Śūnyavādin</s> (Mādhyamika), by the previously stated objection that 'perception has no capacity for apprehending external [objects],' again takes his stand on perception with the words 'the <s>Śūnyavādin</s>' and so forth.

body.text: nāpratyakṣasya tasyāsti pramāṇāntarato gatiḥ //
body.translated_text: For that which is not perceived has no apprehension through any other means of knowledge.

body.text: saṃvedyatvācca nīlāderjñānākāratvaniścayaḥ //
body.translated_text: And because blue and the like are objects of awareness, the determination that they are forms of consciousness [follows].

body.text: arthāntarasya ca grāhyalakṣaṇaṃ nahi yujyate* ////
body.translated_text: And for something that is a different entity, the definition of being an object of apprehension is not tenable.' ////

body.text:
yo hi vijñānapratyakṣamicchati tasya jñānameva na sidhyet pramāṇāntarasaṃbhavāt /
anumānamiti cet /
na liṅgābhāvāt /
na tāvadartho liṅgam, vināpi tena suṣuptyādyavasthāyāmarthasadbhāvābhyupagamāt /
arthavyavahāro liṅgaṃ - sa hi kādācitkaṃ kāraṇaṃ kalpayatīticet, evantu prāgvyavahārājjñānapratibhāso na syāt /
avyavahārannapi ghaṭaṃ paśyan jāne 'haṃ ghaṭamiti jñānamanusaṃdhatte
body.translated_text: For one who maintains that consciousness is perceptual, consciousness itself would not be established, since there is no possibility of another means of knowledge. [If one says] 'inference' — no, because of the absence of a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>). The object is not a logical mark, for even without it, the existence of the object is accepted in states such as deep sleep and the like. [If one says] 'practical activity regarding the object is the logical mark — for it posits an occasional cause' — then, prior to practical activity, there would be no appearance of consciousness. Yet even without practical activity, one seeing a pot reflects 'I know the pot' —

body.text:
iti pratītisākṣikam /
arthadharmo jñānajanmā liṅgamiticet /

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: tatsadbhāve pramāṇābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Because there is no means of knowledge for the existence of that [property].

children.text: atītānāgatayoścārthayordharmāsaṃbhavādatītādyanumāne jñānasiddhirna syāt, tasmādavaśyaṃ vijñānaṃ pratyakṣameṣitavyam /
children.translated_text: And since properties are impossible for past and future objects, the establishment of consciousness through inference of past [objects] and the like would not be possible. Therefore, consciousness must necessarily be accepted as perceptual.

children.text: evaṃ ca tasyaivāyamākāra iti niṣpramāṇakor'thaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: And thus, [the claim that] 'this form belongs to that [consciousness] alone' — the object is without any means of knowledge. ////

body.translated_text: this is witnessed by direct experience. [If one says] 'a property of the object, namely the production of cognition, is the logical mark' —

body.text: kiñca vedyatvādapi nīlāderjñānākāratvaṃ, nahyanātmano nīlasya pītavadvedyatā
body.translated_text: Moreover, because of being knowable (<s>vedyatva</s>), blue and the like are forms of consciousness; for blue, which is not the self [of consciousness], cannot be known like yellow,

body.text:
saṃbhavati /
yadi cārthāntaraṃ nīlaṃ tato 'sya kiṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vedyatvam /
yadyarthatvalakṣaṇaṃ syāt, sarvaṃ sarvasya vedyaṃ syāt vyavasthāhetutvabhāvāt /

children.text: atha vyavasthāpakaṃ - ya evārtho jñānasya hetuḥ, sa eva vedyo nānya iti cet /
children.translated_text: Now, if there is a differentiator — 'that very object which is the cause of cognition is the knowable, not another' —

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: netrāderapi vedyatvaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: Because there would be the absurd consequence that the eye and the like would also be knowable [objects of that cognition].

children.text: sādṛśyaṃ hetutvaṃ ca viṣayatvam, nīlārthaśca nīlajñānena sadṛśo na netramiticet, evamapi samanantarapratyayasya hetutvāt vijñānatvena ca sādṛśyādviṣayatvaṃ syāt* ////
children.translated_text: [If one says] 'objecthood consists in both similarity and causality, and the blue object is similar to the cognition of blue, whereas the eye is not' — even so, since the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>) is also a cause, and is similar [to the cognition] in being a consciousness, it too would have objecthood. ////

body.translated_text: that is possible. And if blue were a separate entity, then what would be its defining characteristic — knowability? If its defining characteristic were objecthood, then everything would be knowable to everything, since there would be no basis for differentiation.

children.text: athāsādhāraṇatvena viṣayākāreṇa sādṛśyaṃ viṣayalakṣaṇam- jñānatvaṃ hi sarvajñānasādhāraṇaṃ nīlādyākārastu keṣāñcidevāsādharaṇastena tadākāreṇa sādṛśyaṃ viṣayatvam /
children.translated_text: Now, [if one says] 'objecthood is defined as similarity through the distinctive object-form — for consciousness-hood is common to all cognitions, but the form of blue and the like is distinctive to some alone, so objecthood consists in similarity through that form' —

children.text: evamapi dhārāvāhikeṣu pūrvamuttarasya viṣayaḥ syāt- ubhayornīlarūpatvāddhetutvācca* ////
children.translated_text: Even so, in a continuous stream [of cognitions], the preceding [cognition] would be the object of the succeeding one, since both have the form of blue, and the former is the cause [of the latter]. ////

children.text: syānmatam- na sādṛśyaṃ viṣayatvaṃ kintu yo jñāne nīlādyākāraviśeṣasamarthako hetuḥ sa viṣayaḥ, samanantarapratyayastu na nīlādyākārāṇāṃ samarpakaḥ /
children.translated_text: It may be held that objecthood is not similarity, but rather that cause which is capable of producing the specific form of blue and the like in cognition is the object, and the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>) does not produce the forms of blue and the like.

children.text: tathāsati nīlajñānāntaraṃ sarvadaiva nīlavijñānaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: [If so,] then a subsequent cognition of blue would always be a cognition of blue [regardless of the object present].

children.text: tatraikasminsaṃtāne nīlapītādivicitrārthasaṃnidhiviśeṣakṛtaścāyaṃ vicitrākārodaya ityarthasyaiva grāhyatvam //
children.translated_text: In that case, within a single mental continuum, this variety of forms arises due to the specific proximity of various objects such as blue, yellow, and so on — thus objecthood belongs to the [external] object alone. //

body.text: punaryogācāraśaṅkā /
body.translated_text: A further <s>Yogācāra</s> objection:

children.text: nanu kāryabhūtasamaye kāraṇabhūtasyārthasya kṣaṇikatvenātītatvātkathaṃ pratyakṣagrāhyatvam, etadevārthasya grāhyatvaṃ yajjñānākārarpaṇakṣamahetutvam /
children.translated_text: Objection: Since at the moment that is the effect, the object that is the cause, being momentary, has already passed — how can it be perceptually apprehensible? This alone is the apprehensibility of the object: that it is a cause capable of imparting its form to cognition.

children.text: yathāhuḥ- bhinnakālaṃ kathaṃ grāhyamiti cedgrāhyatāṃ viduḥ //
children.translated_text: As they say: 'How can what belongs to a different time be apprehensible? They understand apprehensibility

body.text:
hetutvameva tadyuktaṃ jñānākārārpaṇakṣamam iti /
yadyevaṃ kasyāyamākāro yo vartamānaḥ prathate, yadi jñānasyaiva tarhi arthasyāprathamānasya sadbhāve jñānaṃ prati hetutve ca kaṃ pramāṇam /
jñānavaicitryameva, na hi tatsamanantarapratyayamātrātsaṃbhavatītyuktam /
evaṃ tarhyanumeyor'thaḥ kathaṃ pratyakṣagrāhya ityucyate /
etadeva hi pratyakṣagrāhyatvamarthasya yatsākṣādākārasamarpaṇena hetutvam, yastu paraṃparayā jñānākārasamarpako hetuśca so 'numeyaḥ /
tadyathā- vahnisvalakṣaṇaṃ dhūmasvalakṣaṇataddarśanatadvikalpapraṇāḍyā vahnijñānaṃ janayadanumeyam /
ata eva pratyakṣamanumānaṃ ca dve eva pramāṇe jñānārthayorbhinnatvāt /
asati tādātmye tadutpattinibandhana eva jñānādarthaniścayaḥ /
tatra sākṣādutpattau pratyakṣaṃ praṇāḍyau tvanumānamiti dve eva vidhe /
eta eva viṣayasādṛśyameva prāmāṇyaṃ tadadhīnatvādarthaviśeṣavyavasthāpanasya /

children.text: na hi jñānamityeva nīlavedanaṃ bhavati pītādāvapi tulyatvāt /
children.translated_text: For it is not the case that something is cognition of blue merely because it is a cognition, since that [character] is equal in the case of yellow and the like.

children.text: nīlimnā tu nīlavedanasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Rather, the cognition of blue is established through [its possessing] the form of blue.

children.text: yathāhuḥ- nahi saṃvittisattayaiva tadvedanā yuktā tasyāḥ sarvatrāviśeṣādaviśeṣaprasaṅgāt, tāṃ tu sārūpyamāviśat sarūpayituṃ ghaṭayediti /
children.translated_text: As they say: 'For it is not reasonable that it should be the cognition of that [object] merely by virtue of being an awareness, since there would be the absurd consequence of non-differentiation because that [awareness-character] is common to all; but similarity [to the object] qualifies it and makes it correspond [to a particular object].'

children.text: tasmātsākāre vijñāne siddhamarthasya sattvaṃ grāhyalakṣaṇaṃ ceti sautrāntikāḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, since in consciousness that possesses form, the existence of the object and the definition of apprehensibility are established — thus [say] the <s>Sautrāntikas</s>. //

body.translated_text: to be precisely that causality which is capable of imparting its form to cognition.' If so, then whose is this form that manifests as present? If it is of consciousness alone, then what is the means of knowledge for the existence of the object — which does not manifest — and for its causality with respect to cognition? [If one says] 'the variety of cognitions themselves [is the evidence]' — [but] it has been said that this is not possible from the immediately preceding condition alone. Then, if the object is inferred, how can it be said to be perceptually apprehensible? This alone is the perceptual apprehensibility of the object: that it is a cause through directly imparting its form. But a cause that imparts its form to cognition indirectly is inferential — just as: fire, through the chain of the particular mark of smoke, the seeing of that, and the conceptualization of that, generates cognition of fire, and is [therefore] inferential. Hence perception and inference are indeed only two means of knowledge, because cognition and object are distinct. In the absence of identity, the determination of the object from cognition is based only on the production [of cognition by the object]. There, direct production is perception; indirect [production through a] chain is inference — thus there are only two kinds. And the validity [of cognition] consists in similarity to the object, since the differentiation of particular objects depends on that.

children.text: atra vadāmaḥ- syādidaṃ grāhyalakṣaṇaṃ yadyarthasyākārasamarpakatve hetutve vā pramāṇaṃ syāt, natu tadasti, samanantarapratyayaviśeṣādeva vicitrākārodayasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: To this we reply: This definition of apprehensibility would hold only if there were a means of knowledge for the object's capacity to impart its form or for its causality — but there is none, since the arising of varied forms is possible from the specific immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>) alone.

children.text: tathāhi- tvayāpi hi svapnāvasthāyāmasatyapyarthasaṃnidhau jñānavaicitryadarśanādavaśyaṃ samanantarapratyayakṛtatvamaṅgīkartavyam /
children.translated_text: For indeed, even you must accept that [variety of forms] is produced by the immediately preceding condition, since in the dream state, variety of cognitions is observed even in the absence of any proximity of objects.

children.text: evañcejjāgratpratyayānāmapi tathaivāstu kimarthagrahaṇena, ato na hetutvaṃ grāhyalakṣaṇam* ////
children.translated_text: If so, let it be the same for waking cognitions too — what need is there for apprehension of objects? Therefore, causality is not the definition of apprehensibility. ////

body.text: atha jñāninibandhano yatropādānādivyavahāraḥ sa viṣaya ityucyate, tathāsati nīlajñānasya nīlāntargatāḥ paramāṇavo rasādayaśca viṣayabhāvamaśruvīran, upādīyaṃmānatvāt* ////
body.translated_text: Now, if it is said that 'that with respect to which there is practical activity such as appropriation, based on the cognition, is the object' — then, for the cognition of blue, the atoms contained within the blue [object], as well as taste and the like, would partake of objecthood, since they too are appropriated. ////

body.text:
atha dravyasyaivopādānaṃ na guṇānāṃ rasādīnām /
evaṃ tarhi rūpasyāpi viṣayatvaṃ na syāt /
kiñca sukhārthaḥ sarvo
body.translated_text: [If one says] 'only the substance is appropriated, not qualities like taste and the like' — then even color would not be an object.

body.text: vyavahāro 'to 'nubhūte sukhe na kaścitsukhaviṣayo vyavahāro 'sti na ca saṃbhavati, yataḥ sukhapratibaddhavyavahāro 'stīti kathaṃ tasya viṣayatvam* ////
body.translated_text: Moreover, all practical activity is for the sake of pleasure; hence, once pleasure has been experienced, there is no practical activity directed toward pleasure, nor is it possible — so how can [pleasure] have objecthood, since practical activity is bound to pleasure? ////

children.text: nanu nopādānameva vyavahāraḥ śabdaprayogasyāpi vyavahāratvāt, ato nīlajñānanibandhanaśabdaprayogagocaratvānnīlimno viṣayatvam, evaṃ sukhāderapi /
children.translated_text: Objection: Practical activity is not only appropriation, since verbal expression too is practical activity; therefore, blue has objecthood because it is the object of verbal expression based on the cognition of blue — and similarly for pleasure and the like.

children.text: evamapyupādānasyāpi vyavahāratvāttagadviṣayabhūtānāṃ paramāṇūnāṃ viṣayattvāpattistadavasthaiva* ////
children.translated_text: Even so, since appropriation too is a practical activity, there would be the absurd consequence that the atoms that are objects of that [appropriation] would also be objects [of cognition] — the difficulty remains the same. ////

children.text: kiñca na śabdaprayogavaśena jñānasya viṣayanirūpaṇaṃ śakyaṃ viparītatvāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, it is impossible to determine the object of cognition by means of verbal expression, because [the relationship is] the reverse.

children.text: arthasaṃbaddhaśabdaprayogo hi lakṣaṇaṃ na śabdamātraprayogaḥ, pratyāyyapratyāyakatvameva hi śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandho 'to yadarthaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ yaḥ śabdo janayati sa tasya vācyaḥ, ato jñānaviṣayanirūpaṇapūrvakaṃ śabdaviṣayanirūpaṇaṃ, tadadhīne tu tasmin duruttaramitaretarāśrayamāpadyeta* ////
children.translated_text: For the defining characteristic is verbal expression connected with the object, not mere verbal expression. The relation of word and meaning is precisely that of what-is-to-be-conveyed and what-conveys. Therefore, that meaning which is the object of a cognition, and which a word expresses — that [meaning] is its denotatum. Hence the determination of the object of a word presupposes the determination of the object of cognition; but if the former depends on the latter, an inextricable mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>) results. ////

body.text: jñānajanyātiśayabhāktvameva grāhyatvamiti cet, nāsāvupalabhyate, na ca saṃbhavati bhūtabhaviṣyatorityuktam /

children.text: atha saṃprayuktendriyajaṃ jñānaṃ yatvyāptaliṅgajaṃ vā sa viṣaya iti matam /
children.translated_text: Now, if it is held that 'that object is the <s>viṣaya</s> (object) which is known through cognition born of a sense-organ in contact [with it], or through cognition born of a valid inferential mark' —

children.text: tato netrajanyasya nīlajñānasya sparśo viṣayaḥ syāt, asti ca sparśasyāpi rūpasyaiva saṃyuktasamavāyalakṣaṇaḥ saṃbandho netreṇa /
children.translated_text: Then, for the cognition of blue that arises from the eye, touch would be an object, since touch too has the connection of conjoined-inherence (<s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s>) with the eye, just as color does.

children.text: tathā gandhaliṅgasya rasānumānasya rūpamapi viṣayaḥ syāt, rūpeṇāpi raseneva tasya vyāptatvāt /
children.translated_text: Likewise, for the inference of taste from the inferential mark of smell, color too would be an object, since it pervades [taste] just as taste does.

children.text: tasmāt jñānātmakatvameva nīlāderviṣayalakṣaṇamiti siddhaṃ tādātmyam* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that the defining characteristic of objecthood for blue and the like is nothing but being of the nature of consciousness — thus identity [of object and consciousness] is proved. ////

body.translated_text: [If one says] 'apprehensibility is precisely the capacity to produce a special effect in the cognizer' — that is not observed, nor is it possible for past and future [objects], as has been said.

body.text:
sahopalambhaniyamo 'pi jñānārthayoraniyamavyāptaṃ bhedaṃ vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhyā pratiṣedhanna bhedamupasthāpayati, bhinnānāṃ ghaṭapaṭādīnāmaniyatasahopalambhatvāt /
na cāsiddhau vedyopalambhasamaye vitterupalambha iti vācyam /
uttarakālaṃ sahaiva jñānena viṣayasmaraṇadarśanāt- jñāto ghaṭa iti /
nacānubhūtasya smaraṇaṃ saṃbhavati, tasmādutpattivelāyāmeva jñānasya
body.translated_text: The rule of co-apprehension (<s>sahopalambhaniyama</s>) too, between cognition and object, does not establish difference — it negates difference through the apprehension of what contradicts the pervader, [namely] the invariable absence of separation, since things that are distinct like pot and cloth are not invariably co-apprehended. Nor should it be said that at the time of apprehension of the knowable, there is no apprehension of awareness — for subsequently, the recollection of the object together with the cognition is observed: 'the pot was known.' And recollection of what was not experienced is impossible; therefore, the manifestation of consciousness must be accepted at the very moment of its arising.

body.text:
prakāśanamaṅgīkartavyam /
na ca nirākārasyopalabdhirastīti siddhaṃ jñānātmakatvaṃ nīlādeḥ /
avaśyaṃ ca svapnādibodhe bandhyāsuto yāti, aṅgulyagre hastiyūthaśatamityādau cātyantāsaṃbhavādbāhyasya jñānātmakatvamevākāraṇāmabhyupagantavyam /
tathānyatrāpyastu, tasmānna bāhyamastīti prāpte /
body.translated_text: And there is no apprehension of a formless [consciousness] — thus the identity of blue and the like with consciousness is established. And necessarily, in [cases like] awakening from dreams and the like, 'the barren woman's son goes,' and 'a hundred herds of elephants on a fingertip' — since the external [object] is utterly impossible, the identity of [appearances] with consciousness alone must be accepted. Let it be so elsewhere too — therefore, nothing external exists. — Thus [argues the <s>Yogācāra</s>]. //

body.text: yogācāramatakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the <s>Yogācāra</s> position:

children.text: abhidhīyate nīlādivitterātmāṃśagrāhitvaṃ kena gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: We reply: By what is the self-apprehending character of the cognition of blue and the like grasped?

children.text: nātmanā nānyasaṃvittyā sāpi hyātmāvasāyinī //
children.translated_text: Not by itself, nor by another awareness — for that [other awareness] too would be self-apprehending. //

body.text: ajñānasthiracitratvabāhyatvāderanātmanaḥ //
body.translated_text: From [the facts of] ignorance, persistence, variety, externality, and the like, which are not [properties] of the self [of consciousness] —

body.text: asato vā sato vāpi kathaṃ vijñānavedyatā //
body.translated_text: How can there be knowability by consciousness, whether [the object] is non-existent or existent? //

children.text: vijñānavādī hi sarvameva vijñānamātmanameva gṛhṇāti nānyat, atmanaiva ca gṛhyate nānyena, tasyāpyanyasya svātmaparyavasāyitvāditi vadati /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vijñānavādin</s> (Yogācāra) indeed [claims that] all consciousness grasps itself alone and nothing else, and is grasped by itself alone and not by another — since that other too would culminate in self-apprehension.

children.text: yathoktam- nānyo 'nubhāvyo buddhyāsti tasyā nānubhavo 'paraḥ //
children.translated_text: As stated: 'There is nothing other to be experienced by awareness, nor is there another experience of it. //

children.text: grāhyagrāhakavaidhuryātsvayaṃ saiva prakāśate iti tamevaṃvādinaṃ pratyucyate- nīlajñānasyātmāvasāyitvaṃ nīlasya ca vijñānakāraṇatvaṃ kena jñānena gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: Due to the absence of the duality of apprehender and apprehended, it itself illuminates itself.' Against one who argues thus, it is replied: By what cognition is the self-apprehending nature of the cognition of blue, and the fact that blue is a form of consciousness, grasped?

children.text: na tāvadātmanaiva - nahi nīlamidamityatra svātmaparyavasāyitvaṃ nīlākārasya ca jñānātmakatvaṃ prakāśate nīmamātraprakāśanāt /
children.translated_text: Not by itself — for in [the experience] 'this is blue,' the self-apprehending nature and the identity of the blue form with consciousness do not manifest, since only blue is manifested.

children.text: saṃvedyatvagrāhyalakṣaṇayogasahopalambhaniyamādiliṅganimittakena tvanumānenaiva tadavagantavyaṃ- tadapi tvanumānamātmāṃśagrāhi cet, na jñānāntarasya svātmaparyavasāyitāṃ grahītumalam* ////
children.translated_text: But this is to be understood only through inference based on marks such as knowability (<s>saṃvedyatva</s>), the definition of apprehensibility, the rule of co-apprehension (<s>sahopalambhaniyama</s>), and the like — but if that inference too is self-apprehending, it is incapable of grasping the self-apprehending nature of another cognition. ////

body.text:
athānumānaṃ na svātmāṃśagrāhi, tato nīlādivijñānaiḥ kimaparāddhaṃ, yena tānīdaṅkārāspadībhūtabāhyanīlādiprakāśakatvenāvabhāsamānānyapi svātmanyevāvarudhyante /
na hi tadaitadvaktuṃ śakyam- nānātmanaḥ saṃvedanaṃ grāhyalakṣaṇaṃ sahopalambhaniyamo vā saṃbhavatīti /
teṣāṃ sarveṣāmevātasminnaiva bhavadīye 'numāne vyabhicārāt /
tatkhalvātmānamatikramya nīlādivitternīlādyātmabhūtasvātmāṃśāvasāyitāṃ gṛhṇātītyabhyupagantavyam /
tasyāpi
body.translated_text: Now, if inference does not apprehend its own aspects, then what offense have cognitions of blue and the like committed, that even though they appear as manifesting external blue and the like which are the locus of the demonstrative 'this,' they are confined to their own self alone? For it cannot be said at that point that the apprehension of what belongs to another self, the characteristic of the knowable, or the rule of co-perception is impossible — since all of these deviate in your very inference. That [inference] must be admitted to transcend itself and apprehend the cognition of blue and the like as determining its own aspect that is of the nature of blue and the like. And if that [inference] too

children.text: svātmaparyavasāyitve nīlabuddhestadvaśena svātmāṃśagrāhitā na siddhyet /
children.translated_text: terminates in its own self, then the self-aspect-apprehending nature of blue-cognition through it would not be established.

children.text: āhaca- caitrādipratyayānāṃ ca nirālambanatā yadi /
children.translated_text: And it is said: if the cognitions of <s>Caitra</s> and the like are without a [real] support,

children.text: dharmabhūtā na gṛhyeta sādhanotthitayā dhiyā //
children.translated_text: their <s>dharma</s>-nature would not be apprehended by the cognition arising from the proof.

children.text: tato viṣayanānātvātpratiyogyanirākṛtā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the objects are diverse, the counter-correlate has not been refuted,

children.text: rūpātsālambanaprāptiḥ satī kena nicāryate iti* ////
children.translated_text: and the attainment of having-a-support, which is real due to [their having] form — by whom is it denied?

children.text: kiñcājñānamityasya jñānasya jñānābhāvo grāhyaḥ, na ca jñānābhāvasya jñānātmatā saṃbhavati, atyantaviparītatvāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, for the cognition 'this is ignorance,' the object to be apprehended is the absence of knowledge, and the absence of knowledge cannot have the nature of knowledge, since they are utterly opposed.

children.text: tathā- tadevegadamiti jñāne pūrvāparakālāvasthāyitvaṃ prakāśate, naca kṣaṇikasya jñānasya sthāyitvamātmā saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the cognition 'this is the same thing,' permanence across earlier and later times is manifest, but permanence cannot be the nature of a momentary cognition.

children.text: tathā- citrabuddhau nānākāraṇāmavabhāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, in a composite (<s>citra</s>) cognition, there is the appearance of manifold forms,

children.text: nacaikasya jñānasya nānākāratā saṃbhavati* ////
children.translated_text: but manifold forms cannot belong to a single cognition.

children.text: nanvarthasyāpi sthāyitvamekasya ca nānākāraṇatvaṃ na saṃbhavatyeva, saṃbhavatu vā mā vā, jñānātmatā tāvanna saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: Objection: permanence and manifold forms are not possible even for the object. Reply: let them be possible or not — at any rate, they cannot have the nature of cognition.

children.text: tadasaṃbhave cārthākārau vā sthāyitvacitratve syātām, atyantāsadrūpe vā, dvaidhāpi jñānānātmakayorjñānena grahaṇātsiddhaṃ naḥ samīhitam* ////
children.translated_text: And in the impossibility of that [having the nature of cognition], either permanence and compositeness would be forms of the object, or they would be of an utterly unreal form — in either case, since what is not of the nature of cognition is apprehended by cognition, our desired conclusion is established.

children.text: tathā bāhyaṃ nāstīti niṣedhayatāvaśyaṃ buddhāvāropayitavyam, jñānātiriktaṃ ca bāhyam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, one who denies the external must necessarily superimpose [externality] upon cognition, and the external is other than cognition.

children.text: na ca jñānākāratā tasya saṃbhavati, tasmādevamādisiddhyarthamavaśyaṃ vijñānānāmanātmagrāhitvaṃ balādabhyupagantavyam, bhavadīyānumānārthaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: And it cannot have the form of cognition. Therefore, for establishing these and similar [points], it must be forcefully admitted that cognitions apprehend what is not their own self — and also for the sake of your own inference.

children.text: tadevaṃ saṃvidbalasiddhasya bāhyasya saṃbhave vedyatvādibhirnāpahnavaḥ saṃbhavati, bāhyasyaiva hi tadā saṃvedyatvaṃ darśanabalādabhyupagamyate /
children.translated_text: Thus, when the external, established by the force of awareness, is possible, its denial through 'being known' and the like is not possible, for it is precisely the external that is then admitted as the object of awareness by the force of experience.

children.text: pratyutātmana eva saṃvedyatvaṃ na saṃbhavati- nīlādivittīnāmidaṃ nīlamidaṃ pītamityanātmāvabhāsitvāt ātmāvabhāsitvābhāvāt* ////
children.translated_text: On the contrary, the self's being the object of awareness is not possible — since cognitions of blue and the like appear as 'this is blue,' 'this is yellow,' manifesting what is not the self, and do not manifest the self.

children.text: ahaṃpratyayastarhi jñānāvalambano bhavatu /
children.translated_text: Let the 'I'-cognition then have cognition as its support.

children.text: so 'pi kartravalambano na jñānāvalambana ityātmavāde vakṣyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: That too has the agent [i.e., the self] as its support, not cognition — we shall discuss this in the section on the doctrine of the self.

children.text: tathā grāhyalakṣaṇamapi bāhyasyaiva kiñcideṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, some characteristic of the knowable must be accepted as belonging to the external alone.

children.text: anyathā nīlādivittīnāṃ svāṃśaparyavasāyitvasādhanārthasya tadīyānumānasya nīlādivittigataṃ svāṃśaviṣayatvaṃ grāhyaṃ na syāt, sthāyitvādayaśca tadbuddhīnām //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, for the inference that seeks to establish the self-aspect-terminating nature of cognitions of blue and the like, the object to be proved — namely, the self-aspect-referentiality belonging to blue-cognitions — would not hold, nor would permanence and the like of those cognitions.

body.text: jñānānumeyatvasthāpanam /
body.translated_text: Establishment of the inferability of cognition.

body.text: tallakṣaṇaṃ cetareṣāmuktadoṣatvāt jñānajanyaphalabhāgitvamevāśriyatavyam /

children.text: jñānakriyā hi sakarmikā karmabhūter'the phalaṃ janayati pākādivat, tacca phalamindriyakajñānajanyamāparokṣyam, liṅgādijñānajanyaṃ tu pārokṣyamityucyate /
children.translated_text: For the action of knowing, being transitive, produces a result in the object that is its grammatical object, like cooking and the like. That result, when generated by sense-produced cognition, is directness (<s>āparokṣya</s>); when generated by cognition from inferential marks and the like, it is called indirectness (<s>pārokṣya</s>).

children.text: asti hi viṣayāviṣayavibhāgaḥ viṣayeṣvapi parokṣāparokṣavibhāgaḥ sārvajanīnaḥ /
children.translated_text: For there is a universally recognized distinction between what is an object [of cognition] and what is not, and among objects, a distinction between what is direct and what is indirect.

children.text: na ca phalamantareṇāyaṃ vibhāgaḥ saṃbhavatīti tadāśrīyate /
children.translated_text: And since this distinction is not possible without a result, that [result] is relied upon.

children.text: tadeva ca phalaṃ kāryabhūtaṃ kāraṇabhūtaṃ vijñānamupakalpayatīti siddhyatyapratyakṣamapi jñānam* ////
children.translated_text: And that very result, being an effect, presupposes cognition as its cause — thus even imperceptible cognition is established.

body.translated_text: Since the other [proposed] characteristics have the aforementioned defects, the characteristic [of the knowable] that must be relied upon is being a recipient of the result produced by cognition.

body.text: athavā jñānakriyādvārako yaḥ kartṛbhūtasyātmanaḥ karmamabhūtasya cārthasya parasparaṃ saṃbandho vyāptṛvyāpyatvalakṣaṇaḥ sa mānasapratyakṣāvagato vijñānaṃ klapayati, nahyāgantukakāraṇamantareṇātmanor'thaṃ prati vyāptṛtvatvamutpattumarhati /

children.text: tacca kāraṇaṃ loke jñānaśabdenābhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: And that cause is denoted in common usage by the word 'cognition.'

children.text: ye 'pi svaprakāśaṃ saṃvidamātiṣṭhante tairapyayaṃ saṃbandho mānasapratyakṣagamyo 'vaśyamabhyupagamanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even those who maintain that awareness is self-luminous must necessarily accept this relation as apprehended by mental perception.

children.text: anyathā jñāto mayā ghaṭaḥ iti jñānajñeyasaṃbandho vā na vyavahartuṃ śakyate /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, the relation between knowledge and the known expressed in 'the pot was known by me' could not be practically employed.

children.text: yanmātraṃ hi prakāśitaṃ tanmātrameva vyavahartuṃ śakyate nānyat* ////
children.translated_text: For only that which is illuminated can be the subject of practical usage, nothing else.

body.translated_text: Alternatively, the mutual relation between the self as agent and the object as grammatical object, which has the character of pervader and pervaded and is mediated by the action of knowing, is apprehended by mental perception and presupposes cognition. For the pervading relation of the self toward the object cannot arise without an adventitious cause.

body.text:
ihaca saṃvinmātraṃ svayaṃprakāśitaṃ, artho 'pi tadvaśāt, jñānasaṃbandhastu kena prakāśitaḥ /
so 'pi tayaiva saṃvidā prakāśata iti cet /
na /
tadutpattyavasthāyāṃ saṃbandhasyāniṣpannatvāt /
prakāśakatvameva hi saṃvidā viṣayeṇa saṃbandho nānyaḥ, tena jātāyāṃ saṃvidi viṣaye ca prakāśite
body.translated_text: Here, awareness alone is self-luminated, and the object too [is illuminated] through it; but by what is the relation to knowledge illuminated? If one says it too is illuminated by that very awareness — no, because at the time of its arising, the relation has not yet been accomplished. For the relation of awareness with the object is precisely its being the illuminator and nothing else. Hence when awareness has arisen and the object has been illuminated,

children.text: niṣpadyamānaḥ saṃbandho na tayā saṃvidā śakyate viṣayīkartum, viramyavyāpārāsaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: the relation that is being accomplished cannot be made the object of that awareness, since it is impossible for it to operate after ceasing.

children.text: nahi prathamamarthaṃ prakāśya punaḥsaṃbandhaṃ prakāśayitumarhati kṣaṇikatvāt* ////
children.translated_text: For [awareness] cannot first illuminate the object and then illuminate the relation, since it is momentary.

body.text:
atha saṃbandho 'pi svayaṃprakāśata iti manyethāḥ, nātra pramāṇamasti /
tasmānmānasapratyakṣagamyor'thena sahātmanaḥ saṃbandho jñānaṃ kalpayatīti
body.translated_text: If you think the relation too is self-luminous — there is no evidence for this. Therefore, the relation of the self with the object, apprehended by mental perception, presupposes cognition — this is

body.text:
ramaṇīyam /
asti hi ko 'pi saṃbandhor'thena sahātmano mānasapratyakṣagamyaḥ sarvajanīnaḥ sa jñānasya kalpakaḥ /
arthagato vā jñānajanyo 'tiśayaḥ kalpayati jñānam, avaśyamaṅgīkaraṇīyaścāyamatiśayastritayapratibhāsavādibhirapi /

children.text: tritayaṃ pratibhāsata iti vadatā jñānajñeyajñātṛṣu triṣvapyanugataṃ prakāśanapadavācyamavaśyamaṅgīkartavyam /
children.translated_text: One who says 'the triad appears' must necessarily accept something common to all three — knower, known, and knowledge — denoted by the word 'illumination.'

children.text: tatra jñānatvaṃ tāvannānugatam- taddhi jñāne eva na jñātṛjñeyayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, 'knowledge-hood' is not that common element — for it belongs to knowledge alone, not to the knower and the known.

children.text: jñeyatvamapi jñeya eva na jñātṛjñānayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor is 'knowability' — for it belongs to the known alone, not to the knower and knowledge.

children.text: jñātṛtvaṃ jñānajñeyayoḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Nor is 'knower-hood' — [for it does not belong to] knowledge and the known.

body.translated_text: elegant. For there is some universally recognized relation of the self with the object, apprehended by mental perception, and that presupposes cognition. Or alternatively, an excellence (<s>atiśaya</s>) in the object, produced by cognition, presupposes cognition. And this excellence must necessarily be accepted even by those who hold the doctrine of triple appearance [of knower, known, and knowledge].

body.text:
vyavahāraviṣayatvaṃ prakāśamānatvamitacet, na, saṃvidi vyavahārābhāvādvinaṣṭatvāt /
śabdaprayogo vyavahāra iti cet, na, uktadoṣatvāt /
tadavaśyaṃ prakāśanabhāsanādiparyāyo dharmaviśeṣastriṣvapyanuvṛtto gotvamiva govyaktiṣvasti /
saca dharmo jñātari jñeye ca jñānavaśājjñāyate, jñānasya tu svābhāviko 'gnerivauṣṇyaumiti svaprakāśaṃ jñānam /
itarau paraprakāśyāvityāśrayaṇīyam /
tannimittaṃ ca viṣayasya viṣayatvam /
vyavahārādīnāṃ hi viṣayalakṣaṇatvaṃ prāgeva dūṣitam /
ekadeśināṃ tu- vyavahāranibandhanaviṣayatāṅgīkaraṇe rajatavitteḥ śaktikā viṣayaḥ syāt, nacaivamicchanti /
tadevavivādasiddher'thagate 'tiśaye tenaiva jñānasyānumānaṃ pūrvoktena vā mānasapratyakṣagamyena saṃbandhena saṃbhavati /
atikrāntadivasagatadaśatvādisaṃkhyāvaccāsatorbhūtabhaviṣyatoravidyamānatve 'pi dharmiṇaḥ prakāśanadharmo jāyata iti pramāṇabalādabyupagamyate /
ato na pratyakṣatvaṃ saṃvido 'bhyupagantavyam /
body.translated_text: If [one says] 'being the object of practical usage' or 'being manifest' [is the common element] — no, since there is no practical usage regarding awareness, as it has perished. If verbal usage is practical usage — no, due to the aforementioned defect. Therefore, there must necessarily be a particular property, synonymous with 'illumination' and 'manifestation,' that is common to all three, like cow-hood in individual cows. And that property in the knower and in the known is cognized through cognition, while for cognition itself it is natural, like heat for fire — thus cognition is self-luminous. The other two are illuminated by another. And the objecthood of the object is caused by that [cognition]. For the definition of objecthood in terms of practical usage and the like has already been refuted. The <s>Ekadeśins</s>, however, [hold that] if objecthood based on practical usage were accepted, then a shell would be the object of silver-cognition, but they do not accept this. Thus, since the excellence residing in the object is established through the dispute itself, inference of cognition is possible either through that [excellence] or through the aforementioned relation apprehended by mental perception. And just as past-ness of ten days and the like — even when the substratum, whether past or future, does not exist — the property of illumination arises by the force of the means of valid knowledge, and this must be accepted. Therefore, the perceptuality of awareness should not be maintained.

body.text: punarvijñānavādakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Further refutation of <s>Vijñānavāda</s> (the doctrine of consciousness-only).

body.text:
na ca pratītibalādapi pratyakṣatvam- arthāū(?)asasamaye saṃvidaḥ pratibhāsa eva nāsti, natarāmāparokṣyam /
evaṃ ca sahopalambhasyaivābhāvāttanniyamo ya uktaḥ sa dūrāpāsta iti pratyuktametat- sahopalambhaniyamādabhedo nīlataddhitayoḥ iti /

children.text: yattu paścātsmaraṇasya darśanajjñānamapi prāganubhūtamiti /
children.translated_text: As for [the argument] that from subsequent remembering, it follows that cognition too was previously experienced —

children.text: tadapyasiddham /
children.translated_text: that too is unestablished.

children.text: artha eva hi tadā smaryate, tattatsmaraṇācca tadaivārthavyāptirātmano manasāvagamyate, taddhaśācca tadārthe tāvajjñānaṃ kalpayati /
children.translated_text: For it is the object alone that is remembered at that time, and from the respective rememberings, the self's pervading relation with the object is then apprehended by the mind, and from that relation, cognition is then presupposed with respect to the object.

children.text: tasya jñānasyendriyādikāraṇābhāvātsmṛtitvaṃ niścitya smṛtikāraṇabhūtaṃ pūrvajñānaṃ tadaiva kalpayatīti nāsya smaraṇam* ////
children.translated_text: Having determined that this cognition is memory because of the absence of sense-organ and other causes, one then presupposes a prior cognition as the cause of the memory — so there is no remembering of it [i.e., cognition].

body.translated_text: Nor is there perceptuality even by the force of experience — at the time of apprehending the object, there is no appearance of awareness at all, much less directness. And thus, since co-perception itself is absent, the rule of co-perception that was stated is thoroughly refuted. This serves as the reply to: 'due to the rule of co-perception, there is non-difference between blue and the cognition of it.'

children.text: itaśca na nīlāderjñānātmakatvam, anumānādiṣu viṣayākārāṇāṃ parokṣatvāt, jñānasya ca sarvatra pratyakṣatvābyupagamāt, nahi parokṣāparokṣayorekatvaṃ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, blue and the like are not of the nature of cognition, because in inference and the like the forms of the objects are indirect, while cognition is accepted as always being direct. For identity between the indirect and the direct is not possible.

children.text: evamatyantāsadrūpatvenābhimatasya sthāyitvādeḥ sadrūpajñānātmakatvamatyantāṃsaṃbhāvyam /
children.translated_text: Similarly, permanence and the like, which are accepted as being of an utterly unreal form, having the nature of cognition which is of a real form — this is utterly impossible.

children.text: tathā bhūtānumāneṣu bhūtatvamavabhāsate /
children.translated_text: Likewise, in inferences about the past, past-ness is manifest,

children.text: na ca vartamānasya jñānasya bhūtatvamātmā saṃbhavati* ////
children.translated_text: but past-ness cannot be the nature of present cognition.

body.text: bhinnatve 'pi grāhakādgrāhyasya jñānamevātītamuttarasya grāhyaṃ nārtha iti cet, na, pramāṇābhāvāt /

children.text: atra cātītaṃ tredhā vikalpya atītaṃ yacca vijñānamityādinā dūṣaṇamityuktam /
children.translated_text: Here, the past is analyzed in three ways, and the refutation beginning with 'a past cognition...' has been stated — this is to be understood.

children.text: uttaramapi tredhaiva vikalpya dvyākāraklapanāyāṃ ca ityādinā dūṣaṇamityuktamiti vivecanīyam /
children.translated_text: The subsequent [cognition] too is analyzed in three ways, and the refutation beginning with 'in the construction of a dual form...' has been stated — this should be examined.

children.text: tasmādidamapi vaibhāṣikamatamayuktameva /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> view too is indeed untenable.

children.text: tasmād bāhyārthākāra eva nīlādirna jñānākāraḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, blue and the like are indeed the form of external objects, not the form of cognition.

body.translated_text: Objection: even though the apprehended is different from the apprehender, what is apprehended by the subsequent [cognition] is past cognition alone, not the object. Reply: no, due to the absence of a means of valid knowledge.

body.text:
kathaṃ tarhi svapne, tatrāpi bāhyameva deśakālāntaragatamadṛṣṭodbodhitasaṃskāravaśātsmaryamāṇaṃ nidrā- dūṣitamanaskatayā bhrāntyā saṃnihitadeśakālamiva manyate /
vispaṣṭaṃ caitadanantaradivasānubhūtasya svapne vartamānavabhāsadarśanāt, anyatrāpi svapne tathāṅgīkartuṃ yuktam /
śiraśchedo 'pyanyatrāvagataḥ svasaṃbandhitayā doṣavaśādavagamyate /
sarvatra saṃsargamātramasadevāvabhāsate /

children.text: saṃsargiṇastu santa eva /
children.translated_text: while the things connected are real.

children.text: seyaṃ viparītakhyātirucyate mīmāṃsakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: This is called <s>viparītakhyāti</s> (erroneous apprehension) by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>.

children.text: asatkhyātivādinasyaiva śuktikāśakalasyānātmabhūtaivātmatayāvagamyate /
children.translated_text: For even the proponent of <s>asatkhyāti</s> (apprehension of the unreal) [must admit that] the shell-fragment itself, which is not of the nature of silver, is apprehended as being of that nature.

children.text: tathā vandhyāsutādiṣvapi vidyamāna eva sutaśabdārtho vandhyānvitatayā tatpadasaṃnidhidoṣādavagamyate //
children.translated_text: Similarly, even in cases like 'son of a barren woman,' the real meaning of the word 'son' is apprehended as connected with a barren woman due to the defect of proximity of that word.

body.translated_text: How then [is perception explained] in dreams? Even there, it is the external alone, located in another place and time, that is remembered due to latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) awakened by unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), and through the error of a mind vitiated by sleep, one imagines it as if present in the current place and time. And this is clearly [seen] from the fact that what was experienced on the previous day appears as present in a dream; even in other dreams, it is proper to accept the same. Even decapitation, known from elsewhere, is apprehended as pertaining to oneself due to the defect. Everywhere, it is only the connection that appears as unreal,

body.text: svīyaviparītakhyātimatopanyāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: Exposition of the <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> theory of <s>viparītakhyāti</s> (erroneous apprehension).

children.text: yattu kaiścidevamādiṣu tadākārāvabhāsamapahnutya bhrāntirityuktaṃ, tatsaṃvidvirodhādevopekṣaṇīyam /
children.translated_text: As for what some have said, denying the appearance of that form in such cases and calling it error — that should be disregarded precisely because it contradicts awareness.

children.text: ko hi nāmāṅgulinipīḍitadṛṣṭiścandradvitvaṃ na prakāśata iti brūyāt /
children.translated_text: For who would say that the duality of the moon does not appear to one whose vision is affected by pressing the eye?

children.text: kiñcaikaṃ evāyaṃ candro na dvāvivekaṃ candrasya vispaṣṭamanusaṃdadhānasya cakṣuṣā dvitvabhramo jāyamānaḥ kathaṃ vivekāgrahaṇanimittaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, for one who distinctly observes the unity of the moon — 'this is indeed one moon, not two' — how can the visual error of duality that arises be caused by non-apprehension of the distinction?

children.text: evamavagatadikkasya digbhramo nāgrahanimittaḥ saṃbhavati* ////
children.translated_text: Similarly, for one who has ascertained the directions, directional error cannot be caused by non-apprehension.

children.text: kathaṃ punardvitvasyāvagamaḥ, na smaraṇam /
children.translated_text: But how is the apprehension of duality [explained]? It is not memory,

children.text: taddhetvabhāvāt, na grahaṇam, aprāptasya cakṣuṣā grahaṇasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: because of the absence of a cause for that; nor is it perception, because of the impossibility of perceiving by the eye what has not been reached [by it].

children.text: ucyate- deśadvayaṃ netreṇa prāptaṃ candraśca, tayośca saṃsargo doṣavaśādavagamyate, deśadvaye candraṃpratītyadeśagataṃ dvitvaṃ doṣavaśāccandre 'dhyavasyati /
children.translated_text: Reply: two locations are reached by the eye, and so is the moon; and the connection between them is apprehended due to the defect. Apprehending duality with respect to the moon in two locations, [the mind] due to the defect superimposes upon the moon the duality that belongs to the locations.

children.text: tathā pittavartipītatvaṃ śaṅkhasvarūpaṃ ca cakṣuṣā gṛhṇandoṣavaśātsaṃbandhaṃ budhyata ityavagantavyam* ////
children.translated_text: Similarly, when the eye apprehends the yellowness [caused by] bile or jaundice and the true form of the conch, one should understand that [the mind] cognizes the connection [between them] due to the defect.

body.text:
kiñca yadi samyagrajatabodhe tādātmyavabhāsate na śuktirajatavedane tato 'vabhāsyabhedādavabhāsasya vailakṣaṇyaṃ prāgeva bādhakādanusaṃdhātuṃ śaknuyāt /
vailakṣaṇyavagamācca na pravarteta /
kiñca yadi rajatārthī śukterupādānaṃ kāryatayāvagacchet,
body.translated_text: Moreover, if in veridical cognition of silver there is an appearance of identity [between the object and silver], but not in the cognition of nacre-silver, then due to the difference in what is made to appear, the difference in the appearances could be discerned even before the sublating cognition. And from the discernment of that difference, one would not engage [toward it]. Moreover, if one desiring silver were to apprehend nacre as the material cause in the form of an effect,

children.text: tato 'kāryasya kāryatayā bhānāgadviparītakhyātyāpattiḥ /
children.translated_text: then, since what is not an effect would appear as an effect, the fallacy of <s>viparītakhyāti</s> (contrary apprehension) would arise.

children.text: atha nāvagacchet, na pravarteta- tatkāryāvagamādhīnatvātpravṛtteḥ* ////
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, one does not apprehend [nacre as the cause], one would not engage — since engagement depends on the apprehension of [something as] an effect of that [cause].

children.text: atha kāryatvānavagame 'pi tatkāryāvagatisādṛśyātpravṛttiḥ, tatastatkāryāvagatisādṛśyamapyastīti nivṛttirapi syāt sādṛśyayoraviśeṣāt /
children.translated_text: If [one says] that engagement occurs even without the apprehension of causal status, due to the similarity to the apprehension of its effect — then, since there also exists a similarity to the apprehension of its not being an effect, desistance too should occur, there being no distinction between the two similarities.

children.text: nacāsati kāraṇe kāraṇasadṛśaṃ tatkāryaṃ sādhayitumarhati- māsīṣadhacchuktikārajatakāryamābharaṇam* ////
children.translated_text: And in the absence of the cause, something merely similar to the cause cannot produce its effect — may the ornament that is the effect of nacre-silver never come into being!

children.text: nanu vrīhikāryamapūrvaṃ nīvāraḥ sādhayanti /
children.translated_text: Objection: wild rice (<s>nīvāra</s>) produces the <s>apūrva</s> that is the effect of cultivated rice (<s>vrīhi</s>).

children.text: naivam /
children.translated_text: Not so.

children.text: vrīhyaṃśā eva tatra kāryaṃ kurvanti, teca vikalāḥ santo 'pyaśaktyavasthāyāṃ tatsādhanatvena yathāśaktiprayogavidhānādavagatā iti nākāraṇāttatsadṛśātkāryotpattiḥ* ////
children.translated_text: It is the rice-components themselves that produce the effect there; and they, though incomplete, are understood as the means for that [effect] in a state of diminished capacity, through the injunction of their use to the extent possible — so there is no production of an effect from what is not a cause but merely similar to one.

body.text:
atha tvakāryānavagatireva pravṛtteḥ kāraṇaṃ, tato bāhyā api vedārthe pravarteran akāryatvānavagamāt /
atha tvakāryameva te 'vagaccheyuḥ, tataḥ kāryasyākāryatayāvagamādviparītakhyātirityāstāṃ tāvat /
tasmātsvapnādiṣvapi bāhyasyaivānyathābhūtasyaivānyathāvabhāsātsiddhaṃ sarvatra bāhyālambanatvam /
body.translated_text: If, however, the non-apprehension of non-effectness alone is the cause of engagement, then even outsiders (<s>bāhya</s>, non-Vedic people) should engage toward Vedic purposes, since they too do not apprehend non-effectness. If, alternatively, they would apprehend it as non-effect, then since what is an effect would be apprehended as non-effect, that would be <s>viparītakhyāti</s> (contrary apprehension) — but let this be set aside. Therefore, even in dreams and the like, since an external [object] that exists otherwise appears otherwise, the externality of the object of cognition is established in all cases.

body.text: yogācāramatakhaṇḍanam / 59 /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the <s>Yogācāra</s> position. Section 59.

body.text: atha svapnapratyayatvātstambhādivijñānamanyathābhūtamityanumīyate, tadasat, tathāsati pratyayatvāviśeṣāttvadīyamapyanumānaṃ mithyā syāt /

children.text: mithyātvagrāhiṇo 'numānasyāmithyātve vā tatraiva hetorvyabhicāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, if the inference that grasps falsity is itself not false, then the very reason [advanced] would be deviant with respect to that [inference itself].

children.text: tasmātsūktaṃ yasya ca duṣṭaṃ karaṇaṃ yatra ca mithyeti pratyayaḥ sa evāsamīcīnaḥ pratyayo nānyaḥ śābhā iti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it has been well said: only that cognition whose instrument is defective or regarding which there is a cognition of falsity — that alone is an incorrect cognition, not any other.

children.text: tasmādavyabhicārātpratyakṣaṃ na parīkṣitavyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, perception, being non-deviating, need not be examined [for validity].

children.text: iti śūnyavādaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [concludes the discussion of] the <s>Śūnyavāda</s> (doctrine of emptiness).

body.translated_text: If it is inferred that cognition of pillars and the like is erroneous because it has the nature of a mental representation, just as in dream — that is wrong; for if so, since your own inference also has the nature of a mental representation without distinction, it too would be false.

body.text: anumānaparicchedaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter on inference (<s>anumāna</s>).

children.text: pratyakṣasya satsaṃprayogajanyatvalakṣaṇena lokasiddhenāvyabhicāramuktvā, idānīmanumānāderavyabhicārārthe lokasiddhameva lakṣaṇamāha- anumānaṃ jñātasaṃbandhasyaikadeśadarśanīdekadeśāntare 'saṃnikṛṣṭerthe buddhiḥ śā bhā /
children.translated_text: Having stated the non-deviation of perception through the well-known definition of being produced from genuine contact [with an existing object], he now states the well-known definition for [establishing] the non-deviation of inference and the like: 'Inference is the cognition that arises in one who knows the relation [between two things], from seeing one part [of that relation], regarding the other part that is not in sensory contact.'

children.text: yasya yādṛśasya yena yādṛśena saha sākṣādvā praṇāḍyā vā yādṛśaḥ saṃbandhaḥ saṃyogaḥ samavāya ekārthasamavāyaḥ kāryakāraṇatvamanyo vā dṛṣṭāntadharmiṣu niyato jñātastaṃ tādṛśaṃ sādhyadharmiṣu dṛṣṭavatastasmiṃstādṛśe tādṛśasaṃbandhasaṃbana adhini prabalena pramāṇena tādrūpyatadviparyayābhyāmaparicchinne yā buddhiḥ sānumānam /
children.translated_text: One who has ascertained — in exemplary instances (<s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s>) — the invariable relation of a certain kind, whether direct or through a chain, between a certain kind of thing and another certain kind of thing — such as conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), co-inherence in a single substratum (<s>ekārthasamavāya</s>), cause-effect relation, or any other — and who, seeing [one such thing] in the locus to be proved (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>), [forms] a cognition regarding that [locus] having such a relation, which has not been determined to be otherwise by a stronger valid means of knowledge through either conformity or non-conformity — that cognition is inference.

children.text: yathā dhūmasyānuparatordhvagamanasyāgnisāhityaṃ mahānasādiṣu niyatamupalabdhavataḥ parvate taddarśanādagnijñānam* ////
children.translated_text: For example, one who has ascertained in kitchens and similar [places] the invariable co-occurrence of smoke — rising upward without cessation — with fire, upon seeing that [smoke] on a mountain, [forms] the cognition of fire.

body.text: anumāne prābhākaramatam /
body.translated_text: The <s>Prābhākara</s> view on inference.

body.text:
nanu niyamāvadhāraṇādhīnatve kathaṃ tādrūpyeṇāparicchinne pravṛttiḥ, īdṛśo hi niyamaḥ- yatra yatra dhāmastatratatrāgniḥ, yadyadrasavattattadrūpavaditi /
evañcedyāvaddhūmamagnisadbhāvo 'vagata eveti nāparicchinnaviṣayatvamanumānasya saṃbhavatīti /
ata eva codyādbibhyataḥ kecidasaṃnikṛṣṭagrahaṇaṃ smaraṇābhimānanirāsārthaṃ vyācakṣate gṛhītagrāhitvamevānumānasya svīkurvāṇaḥ /

children.text: tathāpi nāprāmāṇyam /
children.translated_text: Even so, there is no invalidity [of inference].

children.text: nahyagrahītagrahaṇaṃ pramāṇalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: For 'apprehending what has not been apprehended' is not the definition of a valid means of knowledge.

children.text: anubhūtirhi tallakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Rather, experience (<s>anubhūti</s>) is its definition.

children.text: anumānaṃ ca gṛhītagrāhitve 'pi pratyutpannaliṅgakāraṇajanyatvena saṃskāramātrajanyatvābhāvādanubhūtireveti yuktamasya prāmāṇyam* ////
children.translated_text: And inference, even if it apprehends what is already apprehended, since it is produced by the present inferential mark as its cause and not by mere latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) alone, is indeed an experience — therefore its validity is proper.

body.translated_text: Objection: if [inference] depends on the ascertainment of an invariable concomitance, how can it operate with respect to what is undetermined? For the invariable concomitance is of this form: 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire,' and 'whatever has taste has color.' If so, then the existence of fire is already known wherever smoke exists — so inference cannot possibly have an undetermined object. It is precisely out of fear of this objection that some explain the [qualifier] 'not in sensory contact' as being for the purpose of excluding memory and mistaken identification, thereby accepting that inference apprehends what is already apprehended (<s>gṛhītagrāhitva</s>).

body.text: atha smṛtipramoṣaḥ kasmānnāśrīyate, pratyutpannakāraṇasadbhāvāt, saṃskāratiriktakāraṇasadbhāvena hi idaṃ rajatam, ityatrānubhavarūpasyāpi rajatajñānasya balātsmṛtitvamāśritya pramoṣo 'ṅgīkṛtaḥ /

children.text: atratu liṅgasyānubhavakāraṇasya sadbhālādayuktaṃ pratītisiddhasyānubhavarūpasyāpahnavena smṛtipramoṣāṅgīkaraṇamiti /
children.translated_text: But here, since the inferential mark — which is a cause of experience — is present, it is improper to deny the experiential character of what is established by cognition and accept it as memory-error.

children.text: so 'yameṣāmakāraṇakastrāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: This fear of theirs is without cause.

children.text: tathāhi- yadi yāvadvyāpyavyāpakasadbhāvo 'vagataḥ syāttato gṛhītagrāhitvamāśaṅkyetāpi, natvevamasti, mahānasādiṣveva hi dṛṣṭāntadharmiṣu prāganumānāddhūmasyāgnisāhityamavagataṃ na sarvatra, pramāṇasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: For thus: if the existence of the pervaded and the pervader had been apprehended [everywhere], then the suspicion of apprehending-the-already-apprehended might arise. But this is not the case — for prior to inference, the co-occurrence of smoke with fire has been apprehended only in exemplary instances such as kitchens, not everywhere, because there is a [different] valid means of knowledge [needed for each case].

children.text: yathācāsaṃbhavastathā nyāyaratnamālāyāmeva prapañcitam* ////
children.translated_text: And how that impossibility [of universal apprehension] obtains has been elaborated in the <s>Nyāyaratnamālā</s> itself.

body.translated_text: Then why is memory-error (<s>smṛtipramoṣa</s>) not resorted to? Because a present cause exists [for inference]. For [in the case of nacre-silver], even though a cause other than the latent impression exists, the cognition of silver — which even has the form of experience — was forcibly treated as memory by resorting to memory-error (<s>smṛtipramoṣa</s>).

children.text: dṛṣṭāntadharmiṣveva bahuśo 'gnisāhityamupalabdhavato 'nagnau ca kvacidapi prayatnenānviṣyamāṇe dhūmadṛṣṭavataḥ sādhyadharmiṣvagnimattājñānamutpadyate /
children.translated_text: For one who has observed the co-occurrence with fire many times in exemplary instances, and who has never, despite diligent search, observed smoke where there is no fire — in such a person, the cognition of fire arises regarding the loci to be proved.

children.text: āha ca- sāhitye mitadeśatvātprasiddhe vahnidhūmayoḥ //
children.translated_text: And it has been said: 'Since the co-occurrence of fire and smoke is established in a limited area,

body.text:
vyatirekasya cādṛṣṭergamakatvaṃ prakalpyate iti /
mamatvadṛṣṭimātreṇa gamakaḥ sahācāriṇaḥ ithi ca /

children.text: tataścānumitsatā na sarveṣāṃ dhūmavatāmagnimattāvagantavyā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who wishes to infer need not ascertain the fire-possession of all smoke-possessing [loci].

children.text: nāpi sarvatrānagnau dhūmasyābhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor [need one ascertain] the absence of smoke in all [places] without fire.

children.text: bhūyo 'gnisāhityaṃ vyabhicārādarśanamityetāvadevānumānārthibhirabhyarthanīyaṃ nādhikaṃ kiñcit /
children.translated_text: Frequent co-occurrence with fire and non-observation of deviation — this much alone is to be sought by those desiring inference, nothing more.

children.text: yattvidaṃ yatra yatra dhūmastatratatrāgniriti jñānaṃ tadanumānameveti tatraivoktam //
children.translated_text: As for the cognition 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire' — that itself is inference, as has been stated in that very context.

body.translated_text: and since non-co-occurrence has not been observed, indicative power is postulated.' And also: 'A co-occurring [mark] is indicative merely through the observation of co-occurrence.'

body.text: gṛhītagrāhitvakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the apprehending-the-already-apprehended [theory].

body.text:
nanvevamapyanenaiva sāmānyānumānena sarvadhūmavatāmagnimattāvagateti yatpunaḥ parvatādideśaviśeṣeṣu dhūmadarśanādagnyanumānaṃ tasya gṛhītagrāhitvaṃ tadavasthameva syāt /
maivam /
sāmānyaviśeṣabhedāt /
sāmānyena hi dhūmavatāmagnimattāvagatā, parvatādestu deśaviśeṣasya svarūpamapi prāgamavagataṃ, natarāmagnimattvam /
yastvavagatameveti manyate, tena parvatasvarūpameva tāvadaprāptaṃ parvatasamīpasthaiḥ kena pramāṇenāvagatamiti vaktavyam, napratyakṣeṇa, nānyena pramāṇena /
body.translated_text: Objection: even so, by this very general inference, the fire-possession of all smoke-possessing [loci] is known; therefore, the subsequent inference of fire from seeing smoke in particular locations such as mountains would still have the character of apprehending what is already apprehended. Not so — because of the distinction between the general and the particular. For by the general [inference], the fire-possession of smoke-possessing [loci in general] is known; but the very nature of the particular location such as a mountain was not previously known — much less its fire-possession. And one who thinks it was already known must state by what valid means of knowledge the very nature of the mountain was apprehended by those standing near it — not by perception, and not by any other means of knowledge.

children.text: nacānavagataparvatastasyāgnimattāmavadhārayitumalam /
children.translated_text: And one who has not apprehended the mountain is incapable of ascertaining its fire-possession.

children.text: yadi cedānīntanaṃ parvatasyāgnimattvaṃ prāgevāvagataṃ syāt tato 'gnyarthī vinaiva dhūmadarśanenāgnaye parvatamārohet /
