children.translated_text: If the present fire-possession of the mountain were already known previously, then one desiring fire would climb the mountain for fire without even seeing smoke.

children.text: nahyagnyarthino 'vagategnau dhūmadarśanenārthaḥ kaścit* ////
children.translated_text: For one desiring fire has no use whatsoever for seeing smoke when the fire is already known.

children.text: kiñca dhūnopalakṣitasya parvatādideśaviśeṣasyāgnisaṃbandho 'vagata iti vadatā dhūmasaṃbandho 'pyavagata iti vaktavyam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, one who says that the fire-relation of the particular location such as the mountain — as indicated by smoke — is already known, must also say that the smoke-relation is already known.

children.text: nahyajñātasaṃbandhamupalakṣyamupalakṣayituṃ kṣaṇam* ////
children.translated_text: For something whose relation [to a qualifier] is unknown cannot serve as an indicator even for a moment.

children.text: atha deśamātrasya dhūmenopalakṣaṇaṃ na deśaviśeṣasya, tato 'gnimattvamapi tanmātrasyāvagataṃ na deśaviśeṣasya, ato liṅgaliṅginoraviśeṣāt liṅgasyaiva deśakālātireko na liṅginaḥ iti pralāpamātram /
children.translated_text: If [one says] that smoke serves as an indicator of mere location, not of a particular location — then fire-possession too is known only of that mere [location], not of the particular location. Therefore, [the claim that] since there is no distinction between the inferential mark and what is marked, only the mark exceeds in space and time and not what is marked — is mere prattle.

children.text: api ca yatrāgnīndhanasaṃyogastatra dhūma ityanena dhūmo 'pyavagata eveti na kiñcidapyavagantavyamavaśiṣyate dhūmajñānenetyalaṃ bālajalpitena* ////
children.translated_text: Moreover, [if one says] 'where there is contact with fuel and fire, there is smoke' — by this, smoke too is already known, so nothing at all remains to be known through the cognition of smoke — enough of this childish babble!

body.text:
yadi cāvagatamevānumānenāvagamyate tataḥ smaraṇameva pramuṣitatadbhāvamanumānajñānaṃ syāt /
naca pratyutpannakāraṇajatvādasmṛtitvam, saṃskāraścodbodhitaḥ smṛtiṃ janayatītyavivādam, smṛteśca pramoṣaḥ śuktikārajatādivedaneṣu kḷpta eva /
tadevaṃ kḷptenaiva
body.translated_text: And if what is already known is known [again] by inference, then that inferential cognition would be nothing but memory with its [mnemonic] character concealed. Nor [can one say] that it is not memory because it arises from a present cause — for it is undisputed that a latent impression, when awakened, produces memory; and the concealment of memory has already been posited in cases like the cognition of nacre-silver. Thus, when the production of the cognition of fire from smoke is [explained] through a path already

body.text:
mārgeṇa dhūmādagnijñānotpattau konāmākḷptam liṅgasya liṅgajñānahetutvaṃ kalpayet /
klapanāyāṃ vā śuktāvapi rajatavedanasyānubhavarūpatvāttadupapattaye doṣasyaivānubhavahetutvaṃ kalpanīyam /
nanvagniviśeṣasyāgṛhītasaṃbandhasyaimananumeyatvātsāmānyamevānumeyaṃ tacca prāgavagatameveti kathamagṛhītagrāhitvam /

children.text: yathāhuḥ- viśeṣe 'nugamābhāvaḥ sāmānye siddhasādhyatā /
children.translated_text: As they say: 'In the particular, there is no general rule; in the universal, there is the fallacy of proving what is already established —

children.text: anumābhaṅgapaṅke 'sminnimagnā vādidantinaḥ iti /
children.translated_text: sunk in this mire of the destruction of inference are the elephants among debaters.'

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault.

children.text: avagatasyāpi sāmānyasya deśāntarakālāntarasaṃbandhasyāgṛhītasyagrahaṇādupapannaṃ prameyatvam* ////
children.translated_text: For even when the universal is already known, since its relation to another place and another time — which has not been apprehended — is now apprehended, its status as something to be known is proper.

body.translated_text: established [i.e., memory-error], who would postulate the unestablished [theory that] the inferential mark is the cause of inferential cognition? And if such postulation is made, then even in the case of nacre, since the cognition of silver has the form of experience, one must postulate that a defect alone is the cause of experience, in order to account for that [cognition]. Objection: since a particular fire, whose relation [to this locus] has not been apprehended, cannot be inferred, it is the universal alone that is inferred, and that is already known — so how is there the apprehending of what has not been apprehended?

body.text:
idañcāparamekadeśinā vaktavyaṃ- kena pramāṇena dhūmadarśanasyāgnijñānahetutvamavagamyata iti /
tadānantaryāditicet /
na /
tasya saṃskāradvāreṇāpyupapatteḥ /
anubhavarūpatvamanupapannamiticet /
na /

children.text: smaraṇasyāpi tatparāmarśapramoṣeṇānubhavābhimānopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: If [one says] its experiential character is unexplained [on that account] — no, because even for memory, the concealment of the recognition of its [mnemonic] character can explain the semblance of experience.

children.text: vastuto 'nubhavatvaṃ tvasiddhameva pramāṇābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: In reality, the experiential character [of inference] is itself unestablished, due to the absence of a valid means of knowledge [proving it].

children.text: nahyagnijñānasyānubhavatve pratyakṣamanyadvā pramāṇamasti /
children.translated_text: For there is no perception or other valid means of knowledge establishing the experiential character of the cognition of fire [from smoke].

children.text: asti tu smṛtipramoṣatve* ////
children.translated_text: But there is [evidence] for its being memory-error.

body.translated_text: And the proponent of the [gṛhītagrāhitva] position must further answer: by what valid means of knowledge is the causal relation between seeing smoke and the cognition of fire known? If [one says] through temporal succession (<s>tādānantarya</s>) — no, because that [cognition] can also be explained through the medium of latent impressions.

children.text: atha smṛtipramoṣasyāpyabādhadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: If [one says]: even memory-error is not sublated [in some cases] —

children.text: maṇiprabhādarśino maṇibuddhistāvadatsmṛtipramoṣa eva, anyathā viparītakhyātiprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: the cognition of a gem by one who sees a gem's luster is certainly memory-error, for otherwise the fallacy of <s>viparītakhyāti</s> (contrary apprehension) would arise.

children.text: atha ca pravṛttasya maṇilābhānna bādhakamasti, tasmātsmṛtirevānumānamityapramāṇyāpattiḥ* ////
children.translated_text: And yet, for one who has engaged [toward the luster] and obtained the gem, there is no sublating cognition. Therefore, [if] memory alone were inference, the consequence of invalidity would follow.

body.text: kathaṃ ca gṛhītagrāhitvamanumāsya, atyantāparidṛṣṭe deśe kāle cāgniranumīyate sa kena pramāṇena prāgavagataḥ /

children.text: na pratyakṣeṇa /
children.translated_text: Not by perception,

children.text: tasya vidyamānopalambhanatvāt /
children.translated_text: since perception apprehends only what is present.

children.text: nacānyena kenacit /
children.translated_text: Nor by any other [means of knowledge].

children.text: kiñcāgnidhūmayormithaḥ saṃbandho deśakālānavacchinnaḥ pratyakṣeṇāvagata ityetāvadeva bhavānbravīti, nacaitāvatā deśāntarakālāntarasaṃbandho 'gneravagato bhavati, tasmādagṛhītagrāhyevānumānam* ////
children.translated_text: Moreover, you say only this much — that the mutual relation of fire and smoke, unrestricted by place and time, is known through perception. But this much does not suffice for knowing the relation of fire to another place and another time. Therefore, inference indeed apprehends what has not been apprehended.

body.translated_text: And how can inference have the character of apprehending what is already apprehended? Fire is inferred in locations and at times that are completely unseen — by what valid means of knowledge was it previously known?

body.text:
kimatrāgṛhītam, agnisāmānyaṃ tāvadgṛhītameva, parvato 'pi pratyakṣeṇāvagataḥ, agniviśiṣṭastu parvato na kenāpyavagata iti so 'numeyo bhaviṣyati /
tatra ca prāptāprāptavivekena saṃbandhamātraṃ prameyamavaśiṣyate /
yathā dadhnā juhotīti viśiṣṭaviṣayo 'pi vidhirviśeṣaṇaparo bhavati tathehāpi, viśiṣṭaviṣayamevānumānam, viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyayostu prāptatvāt yajuryuktaṃ rathamadhvaryave dadātītivatsaṃbandhaviṣayaṃ bhavatīti /
body.translated_text: What is unapprehended here? Fire-in-general is certainly apprehended, and the mountain too is perceived. But the mountain as qualified by fire has not been apprehended by any [means] — so that will be what is to be inferred. And there, by distinguishing what is already established from what is not, the relation alone remains as what is to be known. Just as the injunction 'one should offer with curds,' though having a qualified object, pertains to the qualifier — so too here, inference has a qualified object, but since both the qualifier and the qualified are already established, it pertains to the relation, as in 'one gives the chariot yoked with <s>Yajus</s>-verses to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>.'

body.text: anumānāvayavanirūpaṇam /
body.translated_text: Examination of the components of inference (<s>anumānāvayava</s>).

children.text: yastu pratipannamarthaṃ paramanumānena pratipādayiṣati tena sādhanaṃ prayoktavyam /
children.translated_text: One who wishes to communicate to another, through inference, an object that he himself has already understood, must employ a demonstration (<s>sādhana</s>).

children.text: yena vākyena yasyānumānabuddhirutpadyate /
children.translated_text: [This is] the sentence by which the inferential cognition arises in another person.

children.text: - tacca keciddvayamanye vayaṃ trayam /
children.translated_text: Some [say] it has two [components], others — we [say] it has three:

children.text: udāharaṇaparyantaṃ yadvodāharaṇādikam* ////
children.translated_text: [Either] ending with the example, or beginning with the example.

children.text: akṣapādīyastāvat- pratijñāhetūdāharaṇopanayananigamanaiḥ pañcāvayavaṃ sādhanaṃ manyante /
children.translated_text: The followers of <s>Akṣapāda</s> (the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>) hold that the demonstration has five components: thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>), reason (<s>hetu</s>), example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>), application (<s>upanaya</s>), and conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>).

children.text: anityaḥ śabda iti pratijñā, kṛtakatvāditi hetuḥ yatkṛtakaṃ tadanityaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā ghaṭādītyujāharaṇam, kṛtakaśca śabda ityupanayaḥ, tasmādanitya iti nigamanam* ////
children.translated_text: 'Sound is non-eternal' — this is the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>); 'because it is produced' — this is the reason (<s>hetu</s>); 'whatever is produced is seen to be non-eternal, like a pot and the like' — this is the example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>); 'and sound is produced' — this is the application (<s>upanaya</s>); 'therefore it is non-eternal' — this is the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>).

children.text: ayaṃ tvativistaro gatārthakha iti manvānaḥ saugatā dvyāyavamudāharaṇopanayātmakaṃ manyante /
children.translated_text: But the Buddhists (saugata), considering this extensive [five-membered syllogism] to be redundant, hold it to be of only two members: example and application.

children.text: smaryamāṇaniyamaṃ hi liṅgaṃ sādhyadharmiṇyanusaṃdhānasya svayameva liṅgabuddhirutpadyate /
children.translated_text: For the inferential mark (liṅga), bringing to mind the invariable concomitance, when connected with the subject of proof (sādhyadharmin), itself produces the cognition of the mark.

children.text: tena yatkṛtakaṃ tadanityamiti kṛtakatvasyānityatvena vyāptiniyamaṃ smārayitvā kṛtakaśca śabda ityupanayamātre kṛte śabdasyānityatvamavagamyata eveti kṛtamavayavāntaraiḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, having recalled the invariable concomitance — 'whatever is produced is impermanent' — through the kṛtakatva (being produced) with impermanence, and having made only the application 'and sound is produced,' the impermanence of sound is understood — hence other members are unnecessary. ////

body.text:
evaṃ tvatyantasākāṅkṣameva vākyaṃ kleśagamyārthaṃ bhavatīti tryavayavameva yuktam- anityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvāt yatkṛtakaṃ tadanityaṃ yathā ghaṭādītyevamudāharaṇāntaṃ sādhanaṃ sarvatra vārtikakāraḥ prayuṅkte /
athavā yatkṛtakaṃ tadanityaṃ yathā ghaṭādi, kṛtakaśca śabdastasmādinityaḥ- ityudāharaṇaprabhṛti prayoktavyam /
evamapyanyūnādhikameva sādhanam /
tathā ca yatkarma tatphalavat homo 'pi karma tenāpi tatphalavatā bhavitavyamityeva sarvatra
body.translated_text: But thus, the statement being extremely incomplete and its meaning accessible only with difficulty, only three members are appropriate: 'Sound is impermanent, because of being produced; whatever is produced is impermanent, like a pot and the like' — thus the proof ending with the example is employed everywhere by the <s>Vārtikakāra</s> —

body.text:
bhāṣyakāraḥ prayuṅkte /
pratijñādoṣāḥ pratyakṣavirodhādayo 'prasiddhaviśeṣaṇatvādayaśca vārtike prapañcitāḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> employs [it]. The defects of the thesis — contradiction with perception and the like, and having an unestablished qualifier and the like — are elaborated in the <s>Vārtika</s>.

body.text: hetvābhāsanirūpaṇam /
body.translated_text: Investigation of fallacies of the reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>):

body.text:
asiddhiḥ, anaikāntikatvaṃ, bādhakatvaṃ, ceti trayo hetudoṣāḥ pañcadhā- buddho dharmādharmavedī sarvajñatvāditi svarūpāsiddhiḥ, nahi sarvajñatvasvarūpaṃ kvacidasti? /
vahniradāhakaḥ śītatvāditi saṃbandhāsiddhiḥ, śaityasya
body.translated_text: Non-establishment (<s>asiddhi</s>), inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatva</s>), and contradictoriness (<s>bādhakatva</s>) — these three defects of the reason are fivefold: '<s>Buddha</s> knows <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, because of omniscience' — this is non-establishment of the essential nature (<s>svarūpāsiddhi</s>), for the nature of omniscience exists nowhere. 'Fire is non-burning, because of being cold' — this is non-establishment of the relation —

body.text: vahnisaṃbandhābhāvāt2* ////
body.translated_text: because of the absence of the relation [of coldness] with fire. ////

body.text:
nanvevaṃ samudravṛddhau candrodayasya hetutvaṃ na syāt, udayasya samudrasaṃbandhābhāvāt, ekakālasaṃbandhādubhayoradoṣaḥ /
yadā tarhi candrasya nabhomadhye sthitiṃ dṛṣṭvā pañcadaśanāḍikātikrāntā samudravṛddhiranumīyate tadā kathaṃ, tatrāpi paramparāsaṃbandhādubhayoradoṣaḥ /
nahi sākṣātsaṃbandha eva sarvatrāśrīyate, yaddhi yena sākṣātpraṇāḍyā vā kenāpi saṃbandhena niyataṃ tattasya tathaivānumāpakaṃ bhavatīti darśitamevaitat /

children.text: tena yādṛśaḥ saṃbandho hetorvādinā darśitastadasiddhau doṣo bhavati nānyathā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever relation the proponent has shown for the reason — if that is unestablished, the fault obtains, and not otherwise.

children.text: gośabdaḥ sāsnādimadvacano gośabdatvāditi vyatirekāsiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The word 'cow' denotes [what possesses] a dewlap and the like, because of being the word 'cow' — this is non-establishment of the negative concomitance (<s>vyatirekāsiddhi</s>).

children.text: nahi dharmivyatirekeṇa gośabdatvaṃ nāma kiñcidasti3 /
children.translated_text: For without the exclusion of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), there is nothing called 'being the word cow.' ////

children.text: nityamākāśamanavayavadravyāditi vyaptyasiddhiḥ mūrtatvasyākāśe vyaptyabhāvāditi5* ////
children.translated_text: 'Space is eternal, because of being an uncompounded substance' — this is non-establishment of the pervasion (<s>vyaptyasiddhi</s>), because the pervasion of corporeality in space is absent. ////

body.translated_text: But then, the causality of the moonrise for the ocean's tide would not hold, since the moonrise has no [direct] relation with the ocean. [Reply:] Due to the simultaneous relation of both, there is no fault. But when, having seen the moon stationary in mid-sky, and more than fifteen <s>nāḍikās</s> having elapsed, the ocean —

children.text: anaikantikatvaṃ dvividham- savyabhicāraṃ sapratisādhanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Inconclusiveness (<s>anaikantikatva</s>) is twofold: deviating (<s>savyabhicāra</s>) and counter-provable (<s>sapratisādhana</s>).

children.text: nityaḥ śabdo mūrtatvāditi karmādiṣvanityeṣvapyamūrtatvasya saṃbhavādvyabhicāryamūrtatvam /
children.translated_text: 'Sound is eternal, because of being incorporeal' — since incorporeality is possible even in action and the like, which are non-eternal, incorporeality is deviating (<s>vyabhicāri</s>).

children.text: apratyakṣo vāyurdravyatve satyarūpatvāt pratyakṣo vāyurmahattve sati sparśavattvāditi saṃpratisādhanatvādubhayamapyanirṇāyakaṃ saṃdhayahetuḥ, agṛhyamāṇabalābalatvādubhayoḥ* ////
children.translated_text: 'Wind is imperceptible, because of being formless while being a substance'; 'Wind is perceptible, because of being tangible while being great' — since both are counter-provable, both are inconclusive and constitute doubt-producing reasons, since the relative strength of the two cannot be ascertained. ////

children.text: kaścittvāha- na viruddhārthaṃ hetudvayaṃ tulyabalamekatra saṃbhavati, tadbhāve vastuni nityaṃsaśayāpatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Someone, however, says: Two reasons proving contradictory conclusions cannot both be of equal strength in the same [subject], since otherwise there would always be doubt regarding the thing.

children.text: dravyatve satyarūpatvasyāparokṣāvabhāsīvirodhādapratyakṣatvamanumāpayitumasāmathryāddaurbalyam /
children.translated_text: The [reason] 'being formless while being a substance' — because of its contradiction with the manifest appearance of perceptibility — lacks the capacity to prove imperceptibility, and hence is weak.

children.text: spārśanānumānaṃ tvaviruddhaṃ balavaditi na dvayostulyabalavattvaṃ, ato nāsti sapratisādhano heturiti /
children.translated_text: The inference from touch, however, is uncontradicted and strong — thus the two are not of equal strength, and hence there is no counter-provable reason.

children.text: sa vaktavyaḥ- savyabhācāro 'pi tarhi na saṃśayahetuḥ syānnityasaṃśayāpattiprasaṅgādeva* ////
children.translated_text: He should be told: Then even the deviating [reason] should not produce doubt, for the same absurd consequence of perpetual doubt would follow. ////

children.text: satyapi tasya saṃśayahetutve pramāṇāntareṇa nirṇayasaṃbhavānna nityasaṃśayāpattiriti cet, tarhīhāpi pramāṇāntareṇa nirṇayasaṃbhavādadoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: If [one says:] Even though it produces doubt, since determination is possible through another means of knowledge, there is no perpetual doubt — then here too, since determination is possible through another means of knowledge, there is no fault.

children.text: tathāsati yatpramāṇāntaraviruddhaṃ tasya durbalatvāditarasya balīyastvādatulyabalatvamitacet, kena coktamubhayaṃ tulyabalamiti, kintvagṛhyamāṇabalābalatvamātram* ////
children.translated_text: If [one says:] In that case, whichever is contradicted by another means of knowledge is weak, and the other is stronger, and hence they are not of equal strength — then who has said that both are of equal strength? It is merely that the relative strength cannot be ascertained. ////

body.text: tathāhi- yaḥ sthāṇutvaṃ puruṣatvaṃ vā nāvadhārayati tasyordhvatvaṃ saṃśayaheturbhavati, nirṇīte tvanyatarasminrūpe saṃśayo nivartate /

children.text: tathā yo vāyoraparokṣāvabhāsaṃ nāvadhāritavān tasya pṛthivyādiṣu pratyakṣatvavyāptaṃ sparśavattvaṃ vyomādiṣu cāpratyakṣatvavyāptamarupatvaṃ vāyāvupalabhamānasya bhavatyeva saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, for one who has not ascertained the manifest appearance of wind — perceiving in wind tangibility, which in earth and the like is pervaded by perceptibility, and formlessness, which in space and the like is pervaded by imperceptibility — doubt indeed arises.

children.text: satu pramāṇāntareṇa nirṇaye sati nivartata ityāstāṃ tāvat /
children.translated_text: And that [doubt] ceases when determination is made through another means of knowledge — let that be for now.

children.text: tasmātsapratisādhanamapi savyabhicāravatsaṃśayahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the counter-provable [reason], like the deviating one, is a doubt-producing reason.

children.text: tathā ca bhāṣyakāraḥ yatkarma tatphalavat homo 'pi karma tenāpi phalavatā bhavitavyamityasya- uparate karmaṇi dravyāṇāṃ tatsaṃyogānāṃ ca dravyāntaraṃ phalaṃ dṛṣṭamiti dravyamapi phalavatsyāt iti pratisādhanaṃ bruvansapratisādhanatvamapi dūṣaṇamiti darśayati, tasmātso 'pi saṃśayahetuḥ* ////
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>, to [the argument] 'whatever is an action has a result; <s>homa</s> too is an action, therefore it too must have a result' — [replies:] 'When the action has ceased, a result in the form of another substance is seen for substances and their conjunctions; therefore, substance too would have a result' — thus the counter-proof —

body.translated_text: For instance: For one who has ascertained neither that it is a post nor that it is a person, the uprightness [of the figure] produces doubt. But when one of the two forms is ascertained, the doubt ceases.

children.text: asādharaṇaṃ tu gandhavatvaṃ pṛthivyāṃ dṛṣṭaṃ na kvacidapi buddhimādadhātīti na saṃśayahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: But the uncommon [reason] — smell-possessing-ness — is seen [only] in earth; it never produces cognition [in any other case], and hence is not a doubt-producing reason.

children.text: sādhāraṇaṃ hi dvayoḥ sādhyatadabhāvayordṛṣṭatvādubhayatrāpyanavasthayā buddhimādadhatsaṃśayaheturiti yuktam /
children.translated_text: For the common [reason], being seen in both the property-to-be-proved and its absence, produces cognition in both cases with indeterminacy, and hence is justly a doubt-producing reason.

children.text: tathā viruddhārthavyāptamapi hetudvayamekatra dṛśyamānaṃ svavyāpakamekasmindharmiṇyupasaṃharadekasya viruddhobhayarūpadharmatvāsaṃbhavātsaṃśayaṃ janayati /
children.translated_text: Likewise, even a pair of reasons pervaded by contradictory conclusions, when seen in the same [subject], applying their respective pervaders to one subject — since the possession of both contradictory properties is impossible for a single [subject] — generates doubt.

children.text: nacaivaṃ bhāvo 'sādhāraṇasya saṃbhavatīti nāyaṃ saṃśayahetuḥ* ////
children.translated_text: But since such a state is not possible for the uncommon [reason], it is not a doubt-producing reason. ////

body.text:
tathā bādhako nāma hetvābhāso yo viruddha iti tārkikairabhidhīyate /
saca ṣaḍvidhi iti kecit, dharmadharmyubhayeṣāṃ svarūpasya viśeṣasya ca bādhāt /
body.translated_text: Now, the fallacy called 'contradicted' (<s>bādhaka</s>) is that which the logicians call 'the contradicted [reason]' (<s>viruddha</s>). Some [say] it is sixfold, due to the contradiction of the essential nature and the specific [form] of both the property (<s>dharma</s>), the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), and both together.

body.text: catudhati kecit /

children.text: ubhayabādhasya dharmadharmibādhāntargatatvāt /
children.translated_text: Since the contradiction of both is included within the contradiction of the property and the property-bearer.

children.text: ekadhetyapare- sarvadhā samīhitadharmaviparyayasādhanatvāt, idameva ca yuktam, avāntarabhedasyānupayogāt /
children.translated_text: Others [say] it is of one kind only — since in every case it proves the opposite of the desired property. And this alone is correct, since sub-distinctions serve no purpose.

children.text: yadyavaśyamavāntarabhedo vaktavyastarhi dvaividhyameva vaktavyam- dharmasvarūpabādhanaṃ ceti /
children.translated_text: If sub-distinctions must necessarily be stated, then only a twofold [division] should be stated: contradiction of the essential nature of the property [and of the property-bearer].

children.text: nahi dharmitadviśeṣabādhakatvaṃ nāma hetordūṣaṇaṃ saṃbhavatīti svayameva vārtikakāreṇa- dharmisvarūpabādhena viruddho yo 'bhidhīyata ityādinā darśitam* ////
children.translated_text: For the contradiction of the property-bearer and its specific [form] is not possible as a defect of the reason — this has been shown by the <s>Vārtikakāra</s> himself: 'What is called contradicted (<s>viruddha</s>) through the contradiction of the essential nature of the property-bearer' and so forth. ////

body.translated_text: Some [say] it is fourfold.

children.text: tathā hi dravyātiriktaḥ samāvāya iha pratyayahetutvātsaṃyogavaditi atreha pratyayahetutvasamavāyatvena bhedena ca vyāptaṃ saṃyoge dṛṣṭam, samavāyasyāsamavāyatvaṃ bhedaṃ cāpādayat samavāyadharmisvarūpaṃ tadviśeṣaṇaṃ caikatvaṃ bādhata ityudāhṛtam /
children.translated_text: For instance: '<s>Samavāya</s> (inherence) is different from substance; here, because of being the cause of cognition, like conjunction' — here, 'being the cause of cognition,' being pervaded in conjunction by difference and the nature of conjunction, when made to entail that <s>samavāya</s> is non-<s>samavāya</s> and is different, [seemingly] contradicts the essential nature of <s>samavāya</s> as the property-bearer —

children.text: tadayuktam /
children.translated_text: That is improper.

children.text: iha pratyayahetutvaṃ hi samavāye dharmiṇi dṛṣṭaṃ na vā, yadyadṛṣṭaṃ tato 'siddhatvānna kasyacidapi sādhakaṃ bādhakaṃ vā bhavati, yadi dṛṣṭaṃ tatkathaṃ tatraiva dṛśyamānaṃ tasyaiva bādhanaṃ kuryāt, virodhe hi sati bādheta, nacataddharmatayā dṛśyamānasya kathañcidapi tena virodhaḥ saṃbhavati //
children.translated_text: For 'being the cause of cognition' — is it seen in <s>samavāya</s> as the property-bearer or not? If not seen, then being unestablished, it is neither a prover nor a contradicter of anything. If seen, then how could what is seen in it contradict that very thing? For there would be a contradiction —

body.text: samavāyatvabādhe praśnaḥ /
body.translated_text: Question regarding the contradiction of <s>samavāya</s>-hood:

body.text:
nanu samavāyatvaṃ bādhata ityuktam /
yadi samavāyatvaṃ nāma samavāyadharmiṇo 'tiriktaṃ tadbādhe 'pi na dharmisvarūpaṃ bādhitaṃ syāt /
atha dharmyeva tanna tasya bādhakaṃ saṃbhavatītyuktam /
tasmānna dharmisvarūpabādhanaṃ nāma hetudoṣaḥ kvacitsaṃbhavati bādho natvetaddūṣaṇam /

children.text: yadi khalviha pratyayahetutvaṃ samavāyasyaikatvaṃ virundhyāt tato dravyātirekaṃ sādhayataḥ kiṃ hīyate /
children.translated_text: If indeed 'being the cause of cognition' here were to contradict the oneness of <s>samavāya</s>, then what would be lacking in proving its difference from substance?

children.text: na hi dravyātirekasādhanakṛtamekatvasādhanaṃ, yatastasya dūṣaṇatvena saṃbhāvyeta /
children.translated_text: For proving the oneness [of <s>samavāya</s>] is not something accomplished by proving its difference from substance, such that it could be considered as its refutation.

children.text: tasmāddharmasvarūpasya tadviśeṣasya ca bādhanāddvividhameva bādhakam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the contradicted [reason] is only twofold: from the contradiction of the essential nature of the property and its specific [form].

children.text: tatra nityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvāditi kṛtakatvamanityatvena vyāptatvānnityasvarūpameva bādhate* ////
children.translated_text: There, 'sound is eternal, because of being produced' — producedness, being pervaded by impermanence, contradicts the very essential nature of eternality. ////

body.translated_text: But it was said that it contradicts <s>samavāya</s>-hood. If <s>samavāya</s>-hood is something additional to the property-bearer <s>samavāya</s>, then even with its contradiction, the essential nature of the property-bearer would not be contradicted. But if it is the property-bearer itself, then its contradiction is not possible — as stated. Therefore, the contradiction of the property-bearer —

body.text: yastu- svarūpameva śabdānāmabhidheyaṃ nārthāntaramityetamarthaṃ pratipipādayiṣustatsiddhyarthamevaṃ prayuṅkte- agṛhītasaṃbandhāvastho 'pi śabdaḥ svābhidheyamarthaṃ pratipādayati vibhaktimattvāt gṛhītasaṃbandhavaditi, tasya dharmaviśeṣaviparyayasādhano hetuḥ, paścāddhi saṃbandhagrahaṇādasvarūpapratipādanaṃ
body.translated_text: But one who wishes to establish the view that words denote only their own form and not anything else, and employs [an argument] for its establishment: 'A word, even in the state of not having grasped its relation, conveys its denoted meaning, because of being inflected (<s>vibhaktimattva</s>); and one whose relation has been grasped —'

children.text: dṛṣṭamiti tadvadeva prāgasvarūpārthatvaṃ tenāva hetunā prasajyeta, svarūpapratipādane ca bādhiter'thapratipādanamapi taddharmasvarūpaṃ bādhitameva /
children.translated_text: 'As seen' — thus, in the same way, the [reason] would entail non-reference-to-own-form by that very reason; and if own-form-denoting is contradicted, meaning-denoting is also contradicted as a property of that very nature.

children.text: nahi prāk saṃbandhagrahādarthāntarapratipattiḥ śakyate vaktuṃ pratītivirodhādeva* ////
children.translated_text: For it cannot be said that before the grasping of the [word-meaning] relation, there is comprehension of another meaning — because of the very contradiction with cognition. ////

children.text: sarvatra yo heturyādṛgviśeṣaviśeṣṭena sādhyena dṛṣṭāntadharmiṣu niyataḥ sa tādṛgviśeṣaviśiṣṭasya sādhyasya dharmiṇi pramāṇāntaravirodhātsādhanāsamabhavena viparītaṃ viśeṣaṃ niyamabalātsvayameva bādhamāno nirviśeṣasya ca sādhyasyāsaṃbhavātsādhyameva na sādhayati /
children.translated_text: In every case, a reason which is determined in the example-subjects with a provable [property] qualified by a specific qualifier of such-and-such a kind — that [reason], when there is the impossibility of proving in the subject [a property] qualified by that specific qualifier due to contradiction with another means of knowledge, by the force of invariable concomitance itself contradicts the opposite qualifier —

children.text: yathā śarīricetanakartṛkatvena ghaṭādiṣu vyāptamutpattimattvaṃ dehāṅkurādīnāṃ cetanakartṛkatvasādhanāyocyamānaṃ śarīriṇaścetanasyānupalabdhivirodhena sādhayitumaśakyatvādaśarīrasya tenaiva hetunā ghaṭādivannivāraṇādvidhādvayaśūnyasya cetanasyāsaṃbhavāccetanakartṛkatvamevāṅkurādīnāṃ na sādhayati /
children.translated_text: Just as 'being produced,' which is pervaded in pots and the like by having an embodied conscious agent, when stated for proving that bodies, sprouts and the like have a conscious agent — since it is impossible to prove [this] due to the contradiction of non-perception of an embodied conscious being — by that very reason, in pots and the like —

children.text: tena dharmaviśeṣavirodho hetoḥ sādhyasiddhimeva niruṇaddhīti bhavati dūṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the contradiction with a specific property of the reason obstructs only the establishment of the provable — and thus it constitutes a defect.

children.text: dharmiviśeṣavirodhastu sādhyāvirodhitvānna dūṣaṇaṃ, pratyuta siddhāntāntaradūṣaṇatvātprativādina eva nigrahasthānatvāddūṣaṇaṃ tadbhavati na vādinaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: But the contradiction with a specific [form] of the property-bearer does not constitute a defect, since it does not contradict the provable; on the contrary, since it refutes another established doctrine, it is a ground for defeat for the opponent, not for the proponent. ////

body.text: yastu dṛṣṭāntaparidṛṣṭasādhyaviśeṣavirodhasaṃbhave 'pi tadrahitaṃ sādhyamātraṃ hetuḥ sādhayatyeva, tacca viśeṣāntaramākṣipya siddhyatīti vadati, tasya- uṣṇāgniniyatastṛṇādivikāro hime dṛśyamānaḥ śaityapratyakṣavirodhādauṣṇyasaṃbhave 'pyanuṣṇamevāgniṃ sādhayet, tasmāddharmiviśeṣaviparyayasādhanatvaṃ hetoradūṣaṇameva /
body.translated_text: But one who says that even when there is a possibility of contradiction with the specific [form] of the provable as observed in the example, the reason proves only the provable stripped of that, and that [the provable] is established by implying another specific [form] — to him [we reply]: The transformation of grass and the like, which is invariably connected with hot fire, when seen in frost, [would prove] coldness —

body.text: anumāne dṛṣṭāntanirūpaṇam /
body.translated_text: Investigation of the example in inference:

body.text:
udāharaṇaṃ dvividham- sādharmyodāharaṇaṃ, vaidharmyodāharaṇaṃ ca /
sādharmyaṃ- liṅgamuddiśya liṅgena upādānam- yo yo dhīmavān mahānasādiḥ sa sarvo 'gnimān dṛṣṭa iti, samyagukte ca sādharmyena na vaidharmyaṃ vaktavyaṃ gatārthatvāt /
yadā vaktavyamāpatati tadā liṅgyabhāvamuddiśya liṅgābhāvopādānam- yatrāgnirnāsti tatra dhūmo 'pi nāsti yathā toyādiṣviti /

children.text: yata bhāvena bhāvaḥ sādhyate tatraiva vidhirūpaṃ sādharmyaṃ tatpratiṣedharūpaṃ ca vaidharmyam /
children.translated_text: Where an existent [property] is proved by an existent [property], the positive form there is similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>), and its negation-form is dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>).

children.text: yatra tu medhābhāvādinā vṛṣṭyādyabhāvaḥ sādhyate tatra sādharmyameva pratiṣedharūpaṃ yathā- yadā yatra meghotpattirnāsti tadā tatra vṛṣṭirnāstīti /
children.translated_text: But where the absence of rain and the like is established through the absence of clouds and the like, there the agreement (<s>sādharmya</s>) itself takes the form of negation — for example: 'when and where there is no arising of clouds, then and there there is no rain.'

children.text: vaidharmye tu vidhirūpam- yatra vṛṣṭirasti tatra meghotpattirastīti /
children.translated_text: And in the [argument by] difference (<s>vaidharmya</s>), [the statement] takes the form of affirmation: 'where there is rain, there is the arising of clouds.'

children.text: tena yadbhikṣuṇoktaṃ- prasajyapratiṣedhātmakameva iti tadanādaraṇīyam* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, what was said by the Buddhist monk — 'it is only of the nature of a <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (simple negation)' — that should be disregarded. ////

body.translated_text: The example is twofold: example by similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) and example by dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>). Similarity is the citation of [something] possessing the mark for the purpose of [illustrating] the mark — 'whatever is smoky, like a kitchen and the like, is all seen to possess fire' — and when similarity is correctly stated, dissimilarity [need not be stated separately] —

body.text: sādharmyābhāsāśca sādhyavikalatvādayaḥ, vaidharmyābhāsāśca sādhyābhāvavaikalyādayo vārtika eva draṣyavyā iti //
body.translated_text: And the fallacies of agreement (<s>sādharmyābhāsa</s>) such as absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and the like, and the fallacies of difference (<s>vaidharmyābhāsa</s>) such as incompleteness regarding the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> and the like — these are to be seen in the <s>Vārtika</s> itself. //

body.text: anumāne prābhākarānuvādaḥ //
body.translated_text: Recapitulation of the <s>Prābhākara</s> view on inference:

children.text: tattu dvividhamiti dṛṣṭasvalakṣaṇaviṣayamevānumānamiti manvānānnirākartumadṛṣṭasvalakṣaṇaviṣayamapyanumānaṃ kriyādiviṣayamastīti darśayituṃ dvaividhyābhidhānam /
children.translated_text: But [in saying] 'that [inference] is of two kinds,' in order to refute those who think that inference has only seen particulars (<s>dṛṣṭasvalakṣaṇa</s>) as its object, the twofold division is stated to show that there also exists inference having unseen particulars as its object, pertaining to action (<s>kriyā</s>) and the like.

children.text: nahi kriyā svalakṣaṇaṃ pratyakṣeṇa kadācidgṛhyate pūrvottaradeśasaṃyogavibhāgamātrasya pratyakṣeṇa grahaṇam, yābhyāmevāgantukābhyāmāgantukaṃ kāraṇamanumīyate, tacca kriyetyucyate* ////
children.translated_text: For action (<s>kriyā</s>) as a particular is never grasped by perception — only the conjunction and disjunction with prior and subsequent locations are grasped by perception; and from these two adventitious [properties], an adventitious cause is inferred, and that is called action (<s>kriyā</s>). ////

body.text:
nanu dravyameva kāraṇaṃ syāt, na /
tasya prāgapi sadbhāvāt /
nanu kṣaṇāntare 'nyaddravyaṃ sarvasaṃskārāṇāṃ kṣaṇikatvāt, sādṛśyāttu pratyabhijñānam /
tadyadā samānadeśe pūrvapūrvamuttarottaramārabhate tadā tiṣṭhatīti lakṣyate /
yadā tvanantaradeśe pūrvapūrvamuttarottaramarabhate tadā gacchatīti lakṣyate /
dīpagamanavacchāyāgamanavacca sadṛśāparāparakṣaṇānāmuttarottaradeśaprārabdhānāṃ gamanābhāsanimittatvātkṛtaṃ kriyayā /
kiñcānutpannasya kṣaṇasya kriyāśrayatvāyogāt, utpannasya ca vināśagrastatvātkathaṃ kriyārambhakatvam /
yathāhuḥ- kṣaṇikāḥ sarvasaṃskārā asthirāṇāṃ kutaḥ kriyā iti /
tadidaṃ śabdādhikaraṇe nirākariṣyāmaḥ /
tataḥ sthiratve sati tanmātreṇānupapatteḥ kriyānumānaṃ yuktamiti /

children.text: na yuktam /
children.translated_text: It is not justified.

children.text: kāryaṃ hi kāraṇamātramapekṣate tacceha dṛṣṭamevāsti /
children.translated_text: For the effect requires only a cause, and that is already observed here.

children.text: prayatnaviśeṣānantaraṃ hi śarīre deśasaṃyogavibhāgākhyaṃ phalamutpadyamānamupalabhyate tataḥ sa eva nimittam /
children.translated_text: For after a specific effort (<s>prayatna</s>), the effect called conjunction and disjunction with respect to location is observed to arise in the body — therefore that [effort] alone is the cause.

children.text: tadvadātmaśarīrasaṃyogaścāsamavāyiśarīraṃ ca samavāyīti kimatrādṛṣṭakāraṇānumānena //
children.translated_text: Similarly, the conjunction of the self with the body is the non-inherent cause, and the body is the inherent cause — so what need is there for inferring an unseen cause in this case? //

body.translated_text: Objection: The substance itself may be the cause. No — because it exists even before [the effect]. Objection: At the next moment, there is a different substance, since all composite things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are momentary; recognition is due to similarity. When [a series of momentary entities] successively originates in the same location, it is characterized as 'standing.' When it successively originates in an adjacent location, it is characterized as 'going.' Like the movement of a lamp [flame] or the movement of a shadow — since the successive moments, being similar, originating in successive locations, give the appearance of movement — what need is there for [the category of] action? Moreover, since an unarisen moment cannot be the locus of action, and since an arisen [moment] is seized by destruction — how can it initiate action? As they say: 'All composite things are momentary — whence can there be action for things that are unstable?' This we shall refute in the section on <s>śabda</s> (word/testimony). Therefore, given permanence, since [the effect] cannot be accounted for by [permanence] alone, the inference of action is justified.

body.text: paramukhena prābhākarakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Indirect refutation of the <s>Prābhākara</s> [view]:

body.text:
nanvasamavāyikāraṇabhūtasya saṃyogasya svāśraye svāśrayasamavete vā kāryaṃ nānyatra, tantusaṃyogānāmiva svāśrayeṣu tantuṣu paṭaḥ, tantuturīsaṃyogasya vā paṭaturīyasaṃyogaḥ /
prayatnavadātmasaṃyogastvanevaṃvidhe vyomni kathaṃ saṃyogamārabhate /
ataḥ kāraṇāntaraṃ kalpanīyamiticet / na /

children.text: tantusaṃyogānnodanākhyādyugapadeva paṭasya bahutantuvyāpitatvāt, saṃyogānāṃ ca dvayordvayoreva vṛtteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because, from the conjunction of threads called impact (<s>nodana</s>), the cloth simultaneously pervades many threads; and conjunctions exist only between pairs.

children.text: kiñca śarajyāsaṃyogānnodanākhyādyugapadeva śare śarāvayaveṣu ca sarveṣvantarbahirvirtiṣu bahūnikarmāṇyutpadyate, tatra yeṣāmavayavānāṃ jyosaṃyogo nāsti teṣvāśrayeṣu svāśrayāsamaveteṣu ca jyāsaṃyogaḥ karmārabhata iti vyabhicāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, from the conjunction of arrow and bowstring called impact, simultaneously in the arrow and in all its parts, both inner and outer, many motions (<s>karmas</s>) arise. In those parts that have no conjunction with the bowstring, the bowstring-conjunction produces motion in substrata [i.e., parts] that are not the substrata in which [the conjunction] inheres — hence there is a deviation [from the proposed rule].

children.text: nahi te saṃyogāśrayībhūte śare samavetāḥ śarasyaiva teṣu samavāyāt* ////
children.translated_text: For those [parts] are not inherent in the arrow which is the substratum of those conjunctions, since the arrow alone inheres in them. ////

body.translated_text: Objection: A conjunction that is a non-inherent cause produces its effect only in its own substratum or in what inheres in its own substratum, not elsewhere — just as the conjunctions of threads [produce] cloth in the threads which are their substrata, or the conjunction of thread and shuttle [produces] the conjunction of cloth and shuttle. But the conjunction of the self possessing effort, being in space (<s>vyoman</s>) which is not of that kind — how can it produce conjunction [in the body]? Therefore, another cause must be posited. [Reply:] No.

body.text:
kiṃ ca prayatnavagātmasaṃyogānantaraṃ yugapadeva haste prayatnavadātmasaṃyukte tatsaṃyuktecāṅgade 'aṅgulīyake ca tallagne maṇau ca karmotpadyate, athaivamādiṣu na codanāt na prayatnavadātmasaṃyogācca tadanantare /
tathātmasaṃyogāddhaste, tatsaṃyogādaṅgade, tatsaṃyogānmaṇāvapīti /
evaṃ tarhyatrāpi śakyate vaktum /
body.translated_text: Moreover, simultaneously after the conjunction of the self possessing effort, motion arises in the hand — which is conjoined with the self possessing effort — and in the bracelet conjoined with that [hand], and in the ring attached to it, and in the jewel set in that. But in such cases, it is not from impact, nor from the conjunction with the self possessing effort, nor immediately after that. Rather, [it would have to be:] from the conjunction of the self, [motion arises] in the hand; from the conjunction with that, in the bracelet; from the conjunction with that, in the jewel too. If so, then here too the same can be said:

body.text: prayatnavadātmasaṃyuktaśarīrākāśasaṃyogāccharīrākāśadeśavibhāgastatsaṃyogācca tadanantaradeśasaṃyoga iti dṛṣṭenaiva saṃyogena saṃyogavibhāgasiddherna karmakalpanāvakalpate* ////
body.translated_text: From the conjunction of the body with space — the body being conjoined with the self possessing effort — there arises disjunction from that location of body-space, and from that conjunction arises conjunction with the next location. Thus, since conjunction and disjunction are established through observed conjunction alone, there is no room for positing action (<s>karma</s>). ////

body.text: kiñca na saṃyogasyaivāyaṃ dharmaḥ, sarvāṇyevāsamavāyikāraṇāni svāśraye svāśrayamavete vā kāryamārabhate nānyatra /

children.text: tataśca karmāpyasamavāyikāraṇatvenānumīyamānaṃ viyati vihaṅgame cobhayatrānumīyeta /
children.translated_text: Consequently, action (<s>karma</s>) too, being inferred as a non-inherent cause, should be inferred in both cases — in space and in a bird [flying through it].

children.text: na hi vihagakarmaṇā viyati kāryaṃ saṃbhavati, tataśca viyatyapi calatīti buddhiḥ syāt, ato nānumeyaṃ karma /
children.translated_text: But an effect in space is not possible through the action of a bird; and consequently, there would be the cognition that 'space too moves.' Therefore, action should not be inferred.

children.text: kimidānīṃ nāstyeva kriyātatvam /
children.translated_text: Then, does the reality of action not exist at all?

children.text: asti pratyakṣāvagamāt* ////
children.translated_text: It does exist, because it is known through perception. ////

body.translated_text: Moreover, this property does not belong to conjunction alone — all non-inherent causes produce their effect in their own substratum or in what inheres in their own substratum, not elsewhere.

body.text:
nanu saṃyogavibhāgāgiriktaṃ na kiñcidatra /
dṛśyate hi sarpati sarpe bhūmeḥ sarpasya ca dvayormithaḥ saṃyogavibhāgāviśeṣe 'pi sarpameva calatīti buddhirālambatela na bhūmim /
ato 'syā buddherālambanamasti sarpe calanaṃ nāma tatvam /
tadbhāvābhāvābhyāṃ sarpabhūmyoścalatīti buddherbhāvāvityaṅgīkāryam /
naceyamānumānikī saṃbhavatītyuktam, tasmānnaivamabhiprāyamidaṃ bhāṣyaṃ, kintu viśeṣaviṣayaṃ sāmānyaviṣayaṃ siddhasādhyatā iti, te 'nena nirākriyante /
ubhayorapi viśeṣatvopapatteḥ /
yatra viśeṣasyaivānugamastatra viśeṣaviṣayatvaṃ, sāmānyānugametu sāmānyaviṣayatvam /
na ca siddhasādhyatvaṃ deśāntarakālāntarasebandhasyāgṛhītasya grahaṇāditi prāgeva varṇitam ityanumānavādaḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection: There is nothing here other than conjunction and disjunction. [Reply:] For it is observed that when a serpent slithers, though the conjunction and disjunction between the ground and the serpent are equal for both, the cognition 'it is the serpent alone that moves' takes hold, not [that] the ground [moves]. Therefore, there exists in the serpent a reality called 'motion' which is the basis of this cognition. It must be accepted that the presence and absence of this cognition [that something moves] is due to the presence and absence of that [motion in the serpent and ground respectively]. And it has been said that this [cognition] cannot be inferential. Therefore, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> does not have this intent; rather, [the objection of] 'proving what is already proved' (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>) pertains to what has a specific object versus what has a general object — [and] those are refuted by this, since both can be specific. Where only the specific is tracked, there is specificity of object; where the general is tracked, there is generality of object. And the objection of proving what is already proved does not [apply], since what is unapprehended — namely the connection with another location and another time — is being apprehended. This has been explained earlier. Thus [ends] the discussion of inference.

body.text:
śāstraṃ śabdavijñānādasaṃnikṛṣṭer'the tacchābdaṃ nāma pramāṇam /
tallokasiddhatvānna parīkṣitavyam /
tacca dvavidhaṃ pauruṣeyamapauruṣeyaṃ ceti /
tatra pauruṣeyamāptavākyam /
apauruṣeyaṃ ca vedavākyam /
ubhayamapyanāptapraṇītatvadoṣavirahātsvataśca śabdasyāduṣṭatvātpramāṇam /
tacca punardvividham- siddhārthe vidhāyakañceti dvividham- upadeśakamatideśakaṃ ca /
itthamidaṃ kartavyamityupadeśaḥ /
yathā loke- dadhighṛtasūpaśālyādibhirdevadatto bhojayitavyā iti /
vedepi- prayājāvaghātādiprakāreṇa darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargaṃ kuryāditi tadvadidaṃ kartavyamityatideśaḥ /
yathā- loke devadattavadyayajñadatto bhojayitavyā iti /
vedepi- sauryeṇa kuryādyathāgneyeneti /
śabdāntarādibhiḥ śrutiliṅgādibhiḥ śrutyarthādibhiśca vicitro 'yamupadeśo bhedaviniyogakramānavabodhayati /
vacanānāmadheyacodanāliṅgaiścātideśoṣa'nyatra vihitasyanānāpadārthaviśaṣṭasya prakārasya tatpratipādakasya vā śāstrasya vidhyantāparanāmadheyasyāntena saṃbandhaṃ vikāraṃ bādhaṃ vā bodhayatītyūhanīyam /
asaṃnikṛṣṭagrahaṇaṃ ca pūrvavattāddrūpyaparyayaparicchedanirāsārthamā /
etadeśināṃ tu tadanarthakameva syāt /
viparītaparicchinne tāvannāstyeva śabdājjñānam /
yadi syāt puruṣadoṣāṇāṃ śabde saṃkrāntyanabhyupagamāt svābhāvikameva śabdasyāprāmāṇyaṃ syāditi vedāprāmāṇyaṃ syāt /
yadi paraṃ tadrūpaparicchinnaviṣayasyānuvādasya nirāsaḥ syāt /
taccāyuktam /

children.text: tasyāpi śāstratvāt /
children.translated_text: since that [restatement] too is <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative teaching).

children.text: nahi tasyāpyaprāmāṇyam /
children.translated_text: For that too is not invalid,

children.text: anubhūtitvāt /
children.translated_text: because it is a [form of] cognition.

children.text: pratyakṣādyantarbhāvābhāvācca śāstratvamevetyāstāṃ tāvat //
children.translated_text: And since it cannot be included under perception and the like, it is indeed <s>śāstra</s> (verbal testimony) — but let that be for now. //

body.translated_text: <s>Śāstra</s> (verbal testimony): The cognition arising from words regarding an object not in contact [with the senses] — that is the means of knowledge called verbal testimony (<s>śābda</s>). Since that is well-established in common experience, it need not be examined [further]. And it is of two kinds: of human origin (<s>pauruṣeya</s>) and not of human origin (<s>apauruṣeya</s>). Of these, that of human origin is the statement of a trustworthy person (<s>āptavākya</s>). That not of human origin is the Vedic statement. Both are valid means of knowledge because they are free from the fault of being composed by an untrustworthy person, and because words are intrinsically reliable. And this is again of two kinds: regarding established [facts] and regarding what is to be done — [or alternatively] two kinds: instructive (<s>upadeśaka</s>) and analogical-transfer (<s>atideśaka</s>). 'This is to be done in such-and-such a way' is instruction — as in ordinary life: '<s>Devadatta</s> is to be fed with curds, ghee, broth, rice, and the like.' In the Veda too: 'One should perform the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> sacrifices in the manner of <s>prayāja</s>, animal slaughter, and the like for the sake of heaven.' 'This is to be done like that' is analogical transfer — as in ordinary life: '<s>Yajñadatta</s> is to be fed like <s>Devadatta</s>.' In the Veda too: 'One should perform with the <s>Saurya</s> [rite] as with the <s>Āgneya</s>.' This instruction, varied by different words and so forth, by <s>śruti</s> (direct statement), <s>liṅga</s> (indicative mark), and the like, and by the meaning of <s>śruti</s> and the like, teaches the distinctions, assignments, and sequence [of ritual elements]. And the analogical transfer, through statements, names, injunctions, and indicative marks, teaches the connection, modification, or supersession of a procedure — enjoined elsewhere and qualified by various subsidiary elements — or of the <s>śāstra</s> that teaches it — with the <s>vidhyanta</s> (the injunctive ending), another name [for the primary injunction]. This should be reflected upon. And the qualification 'not in contact [with the senses]' is, as before, for the purpose of excluding the determination of similarity and the like [which falls under perception]. But for the <s>Ekadeśins</s> (those who hold a partial view), this [qualification] would be purposeless. For with regard to what is misapprehended, there is simply no cognition from words. If there were, then since the faults of the speaker are not accepted as transferring to the words, the intrinsic invalidity of words would follow — and thus the invalidity of the Veda would follow. If, however, this is meant to exclude <s>anuvāda</s> (restatement) whose object is apprehended in its true form — that is improper,

body.text: aulukyamatānuvādaḥ /
body.translated_text: Recapitulation of the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> (<s>Aulūkya</s>) view:

body.text:
idaṃ ca asyedaṃ kāraṇaṃ saṃbadhyekārthasamavāyivirodhi ceti laiṅgikamityunumānalakṣaṇamabhidhāya etenaiva śābdaṃ vyākhyātam iti kāśyapīyāḥ pratyakṣānumānaṃ ca dve eva pramāṇe iti bruvāṇaḥ saugatāścānumānādabhinnamiti manyante /
tatra yattāvatpadārthajñānaṃ tadavagatārthaviṣayatvātpramāṇameva na bhavatīti kiṃ tasya bhedābhedaparīkṣayā /
yattu vākyārthajñānaṃ tadagṛhītasaṃbandhaireva padārthairupajāyamānaṃ nānumānaśaṅkāmarhati /
nahi sarvairvākyārthaviśeṣaiḥ saṃbandhagrahaṇamasti /
naca saṃbhavatyanantaiḥ saṃbandhagrahaṇam /
atyantāpūrvo 'pi vākyārthaviśeṣaḥ padārthairavagamyate dūradeśavārtāsviti sarvajanīnametat /
body.translated_text: 'This, and this is its cause, and what is related and what contradicts what inheres in the same locus — this is inferential (<s>laiṅgika</s>)' — having stated this definition of inference, [the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>] explain verbal testimony (<s>śābda</s>) by this very [inference]. 'Perception and inference alone are the two means of knowledge' — so say the followers of <s>Kaśyapa</s> (<s>Kāśyapīyas</s>); and the Buddhists (<s>Saugatas</s>) too consider [verbal testimony] as not different from inference. Therein, as for the cognition of individual word-meanings, since it has already-known objects, it is not even a means of knowledge [in the relevant sense] — so what is the point of examining its identity or difference [from inference]? But the cognition of sentence-meaning, which arises through word-meanings whose mutual relation has not been grasped — that does not deserve the suspicion of being inference. For there is no apprehension of the relation with all particular sentence-meanings. Nor is it possible to apprehend the relation with infinite [possible sentence-meanings]. Even a completely unprecedented particular sentence-meaning is understood through word-meanings — as in reports of distant lands — and this is common knowledge.

body.text:
yattvāptavākyatvādavisaṃvādānumānaṃ tadvākyārthāvagamottarakālatvānna tasyānumānatvamāpādayati /
vākyaśravaṇānantarameva hyāptānāprajñānānapekṣaireva padārthairvākyārtho 'vagamyate /
atyāntādṛṣṭapuruṣapraṇīte 'pi vākye 'vagate tu vākyārthe satyāsatyatvasaṃśaye praṇeturāptatvāvagame sati satyatvamanumīyamānaṃ na vākyārthāvagaterāptatvāvadhāraṇānapekṣajanmano 'numānatvamāpādayati /
tasmātpramāṇāntarameva loke śābdamityapauruṣeyasyāpi vedasya siddhaṃ prāmāṇyam /
ekadeśināṃ tu lokavacasāmanumānatvamaṅgīkurvatāṃ yathā vedaprāmāṇyaṃ na siddhyatitathoktam /
iti śabdapramāṇavādaḥ /
body.translated_text: And as for [the argument that] since [verbal testimony] is the statement of a trustworthy person, it is inference of non-deceptiveness — since that [inference of trustworthiness] comes after the understanding of the sentence-meaning, it does not render [the sentence-meaning cognition] inferential. For immediately upon hearing the sentence, the sentence-meaning is understood through the word-meanings alone, without depending on the knowledge of trustworthiness or untrustworthiness [of the speaker]. Even when a sentence composed by a completely unknown person is understood, and there is doubt about the truth or falsity of the sentence-meaning, the inference of truth upon ascertaining the trustworthiness of the author does not render the sentence-meaning cognition — which arises without depending on the ascertainment of trustworthiness — inferential. Therefore, verbal testimony is indeed a separate means of knowledge in common experience — and thus the validity of the <s>apauruṣeya</s> (authorless) Veda too is established. But for the <s>Ekadeśins</s> (holders of a partial view) who accept that ordinary speech is inferential — how the validity of the Veda cannot be established for them has been stated [earlier]. Thus [ends] the discussion of verbal testimony as a means of knowledge.

body.text: athopamānaparicchedaḥ /
body.translated_text: The section on <s>upamāna</s> (comparison/analogy):

body.text:
upamānamapi sādṛśyamasaṃnikṛṣṭer'the buddhimutpādayati /
yathā gavayadarśanaṃ gosmaraṇasya pūrvadṛṣṭe smaryamāṇer'the dṛśyamānārthasādṛśyajñānamupamānam /
yā sāvasmābhirnagare dṛṣṭvā gauḥ sānena gamayena sadṛśīti /
kiṃ punaḥ sādṛśyam /
arthāntarayogibhiḥ saṃbandhisāmānyairarthāntarasya tādṛśayogaḥ sādṛśyam /
yathā gojātiyogibhiḥ karmādyavayavasāmānyairgavayajāteryogo gavayasya gosādṛśyaṃ gavayasaṃyogibhiśca goryogastatsādṛśyam /
ata eva ca sāmānyayogātiriktamanyadeva tatvaṃ sādṛśyaṃ teṣāṃ prakarṣāprakarṣabhedaḥ kiṃnimitta iti cintanīyam /
na ca tattvāntaratve pramāṇamapi kiñcidastītyāstāṃ tāvat /
nacedamupamānaṃ pratyakṣāntargatam /
anindriyasaṃnikṛṣṭatvānnagarasthasya goḥ /
nacānumānamagṛhītasaṃbandhasyāpyupajāyamānatvāt /
evaṃ kilānumīyeta
body.translated_text: <s>Upamāna</s> (comparison) too — similarity produces cognition of an object not in contact [with the senses]. For example, the seeing of a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox), [which occasions] the remembrance of a cow — the cognition of similarity between the object being seen and the object being remembered, which was previously seen, is <s>upamāna</s>. 'That cow which we saw in the city — she is similar to this <s>gavaya</s>.' What, then, is similarity? The possession by one entity of common properties — general characteristics such as action, parts, and the like — that belong to another entity is similarity. For example, the possession by the <s>gavaya</s> species of the common characteristics such as action, parts, and the like that belong to the cow species — that is the similarity of the <s>gavaya</s> to the cow; and the possession by the cow of [properties] that belong to the <s>gavaya</s> — that is the [cow's] similarity [to the gavaya]. And precisely for this reason, since [similarity involves] something beyond mere commonality of universals, similarity is itself a distinct reality. What causes the gradations of more and less [similarity] is to be investigated. But whether there is any means of knowledge for its being a distinct reality — let that be for now. And this <s>upamāna</s> is not subsumed under perception, since the cow in the city is not in contact with the sense-organs [of the person in the forest]. Nor is it inference, since it arises even when the relation [between the terms] has not been grasped. For it would have to be inferred thus:

children.text: gaurgavayasadṛśo gavayasādṛśyapratiyogi tattatsadṛśaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yugapanna dṛṣṭavānekameva tu gāmupalabhya nagare vane gavayaṃ paśyati so 'pi gāṃ gavayasādṛśyaviśiṣṭāmupaminotyeva tasmānnānumānam /
children.translated_text: A cow is similar to a <s>gavaya</s>, being a counterpart of <s>gavaya</s>-similarity — [but] what is similar to each respective [thing] has been seen simultaneously. [However,] one has not seen [them together] — one has only perceived the cow in the city and sees the <s>gavaya</s> in the forest. And that person too compares the cow as qualified by <s>gavaya</s>-similarity. Therefore, it is not inference.

children.text: śābdatvaṃ tu na śaṅkyameva /
children.translated_text: And the possibility of it being verbal testimony is not even to be suspected.

children.text: ataḥ pramāṇāntaram, prasiddhatvācca na parīkṣitavyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is a separate means of knowledge; and since it is well-established, it need not be examined [further].

children.text: ityupamānavādaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the discussion of <s>upamāna</s> (comparison). //

body.text: arthāpattinirūpaṇam /
body.translated_text: The investigation of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption):

body.text:
arthāpattiriti dṛṣṭaḥ vār'tho 'nyathā nopapadyata ityarthakalpanā /
yathā jīvato devadattasya gṛhābhāvadarśanena bahirbhāvasyādṛṣṭasya parikalpanā /
pramitasyārthāntareṇa vinānupapannādupapādakalpanā sā arthāpattiḥ, anumānameva tarhi, tatrāpi vahnimantareṇānupapannāddhūmāhniḥ kalpyate /
syādevam /
yadyanupapannaṃ gamakaṃ syāt /
iha tu yannopapadyate tadeva gamyam /
gṛhābhāvena hi vinābahirbhāvo nopapadyate /
kimidānīmupapādakādanupapanne buddhirarthāpattiḥ /
ko doṣaḥ /
na khalu kaściddoṣaḥ /
kiṃ tvasau naivāsti /

children.text: na hyupapādakadarśanādanupapannārthe buddhirbhavati /
children.translated_text: For there is no cognition of the inexplicable from seeing the explanatory.

children.text: yadi syāt, vṛkṣatvadarśanācchiṃśapātvaṃ kalpyeta /
children.translated_text: If there were, then from seeing tree-hood, <s>śiṃśapā</s>-hood (being a particular tree species) would be postulated,

children.text: vṛkṣatvena vinā śiṃśapātvasyānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: since <s>śiṃśapā</s>-hood is inexplicable without tree-hood.

children.text: tasmādanupapannameva gamakaṃ nopapādakam* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, the inexplicable alone is the indicator, not the explanatory.

body.translated_text: <s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is the postulation of a fact when an observed or known matter cannot be explained otherwise. For example, seeing that <s>Devadatta</s>, who is alive, is absent from the house, one postulates his being outside, which has not been seen. It is the postulation of an explanatory fact from something known that is inexplicable without something else — that is <s>arthāpatti</s>. [Objection:] Then it is just inference, for there too fire is postulated from smoke, which is inexplicable without fire. [Reply:] It would be so if the inexplicable were the indicator. But here, what is to be understood is precisely what is inexplicable. For being outside is inexplicable without the absence from the house. [Objection:] Then is <s>arthāpatti</s> the cognition of the inexplicable from the explanatory? [Reply:] What is the defect? [Objection:] There is no defect at all, but rather it simply does not exist [as a separate means of knowledge].

body.text:
athocyate /
nāvinābhāvenānupapattirityucyate kiṃ tu saṃśayāpattiḥ /
yasya hi jīvanaṃ gṛhasaṃbandhyeva prāyaśo 'vagataṃ tasya gṛhābhāve dṛṣṭe jīvanaṃ sāṃśayikaṃ bhavadbahirbhāvakalpanayā samādhīyate /
tataśca prāgbahirbhāvakalpanāyā jīvanasya saṃdigdhatvānna liṅgatvam /
na hi sandigdhaṃ liṅgaṃ bhavati /
jīvanarahitañca gṛhābhāvamātraṃ mṛte 'pi sadbhāvādanaikāntikaṃ na bahirbhāvamanumāpayitumalam /

children.text: ato 'numānāsaṃbhavātpramāṇāntaramevedam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, since inference is not possible, this is indeed a separate means of valid knowledge.

children.text: yathā cānumāne niścitaṃ gamakam /
children.translated_text: And just as in inference the indicator is certain,

children.text: evamarthāpattau sandigdhaṃ gamakamiti darśanahalādabhyupagamyate /
children.translated_text: so in <s>arthāpatti</s> the indicator is doubtful — this is accepted by the school of <s>Darśanahala</s>.

children.text: saṃśayaścātra pūrvadṛṣṭarūpavisaṃvādāt //
children.translated_text: And the doubt here arises from the discrepancy with the previously observed pattern.

body.translated_text: Now it is said: the inexplicability does not mean 'impossibility without [it],' but rather the arising of doubt. For one who has generally observed that <s>Devadatta</s>'s being alive is associated with being in the house, when the absence from the house is seen, his being alive becomes doubtful, and this is resolved by the postulation of his being outside. Consequently, prior to the postulation of being outside, since being alive is doubtful, it cannot serve as a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>). For a doubtful [thing] cannot be a logical mark. And the mere absence from the house without being alive, since it exists even when [the person] is dead, is inconclusive and cannot establish being outside.

body.text: arthāpattisamādhānam /
body.translated_text: Resolution of the [objection regarding] <s>arthāpatti</s>.

body.text:
tadidamasaṃbaddham /
na hi saṃdigdhe jīvane bahirbhāvaḥ śakyate kalpayitum /
kathaṃ hi jīvati vā mṛto devadattaḥ iti saṃdihānastasya bahirbhāvaṃ kalpayet /
na hi bhāvābhāvasaṃśayasya
body.translated_text: This is incoherent. For when being alive is doubtful, being outside cannot be postulated. How indeed could one who is in doubt — 'is <s>Devadatta</s> alive or dead?' — postulate his being outside? For the doubt about existence and non-existence

body.text:
bahirbhāvakalpanayāpanodaḥ saṃbhavati /
sarvatra hi saṃśayasya nidānocchedāducchedo bhavati /
anyatarapakṣāvadhāraṇādvā /
na ca bahirbhāvakalpanayā tāvannidānocchedaḥ /
jīvanasya prāyeṇa gṛhasaṃbandhitvāttadviparyayo 'tra saṃśayahetutvenopanyastaḥ /
nacāsau bahirbhāve kalpite samucchidyate /
pratyuta viparyaya eva dṛḍhamavasthāpyate /
nacānyatarapakṣāvadhāraṇamapi vidyate jīvanabhāvābhāvau hyatra saṃdihyate /
nacānayoranyatarasyāpi bahirbhāvakalpanayā nirṇayo bhavati /
anyaddhi jīvanaṃ anyaśca bahirdeśasaṃbandhaḥ /
naca gṛhābhāvanibandhanārthāpattirjīvananirṇayāyālaṃ bhavati /
nahyevaṃ saṃbhavati yasmāddevadatto gṛhe nāsti tasmājjīvatīti, pratyuta pūrvaniścitameva jīvanaṃ gṛhābhāvādeva saṃdigdhaṃ kathaṃ tata eva nirṇīyate /
na hi saṃśayahetureva nirṇayaheturbhavati /
tasmājjīvanaṃ saṃdigdhaṃ tattāvadanyato niścitya paścādbahiḥsaṃbandhaḥ kalpayitavyaḥ /

children.text: yasmāddevadatto jīvati gṛhe ca nāsti tasmānnūnaṃ bahiravasthita iti /
children.translated_text: Since <s>Devadatta</s> is alive and is not in the house, therefore he must be situated outside.

children.text: na tu saṃdihyamāne jīvane tatkalpanaṃ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: But when being alive is doubtful, the postulation of that [being outside] is not possible.

children.text: yasmādavidyamāno gṛhe jīvati vā navā tasmādbahiḥ sthita ityasaṃbaddhameva syāt /
children.translated_text: Since he who is absent from the house may be alive or not — therefore [the conclusion that] he is situated outside would be incoherent.

children.text: tasmādbahirbhāvaniyataṃ gṛhābhāvasahitaṃ jīvanaṃ niścitya bahirbhāvaḥ kalpyata ityanumānamevedaṃ na pramāṇāntaramiti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, having ascertained that being alive, conjoined with absence from the house, is invariably connected with being outside, one postulates being outside — and this is just inference, not a separate means of valid knowledge.

body.translated_text: cannot be removed by the postulation of being outside. For everywhere, doubt is dispelled by the elimination of its root cause, or by the ascertainment of one of the two alternatives. The postulation of being outside does not eliminate the root cause. The fact that being alive is generally associated with being in the house, and its opposite, is presented here as the cause of doubt. And that [cause] is not eliminated when being outside is postulated; on the contrary, the very opposite is firmly established. Nor is there ascertainment of one alternative either — for what is doubted here is the existence or non-existence of being alive, and neither of these is determined by the postulation of being outside. For being alive is one thing and the connection with an outside location is another. The <s>arthāpatti</s> based on absence from the house cannot serve to determine [the fact of] being alive. For it is not possible to reason thus: 'since <s>Devadatta</s> is not in the house, therefore he is alive.' On the contrary, the being alive that was previously ascertained, having become doubtful precisely from the absence from the house — how can it be determined from that very same [absence]? For the cause of doubt cannot itself be the cause of determination. Therefore, being alive being doubtful, one must first determine it from some other source and then postulate the connection with outside.

body.text: siddhāntena tarkamatanirākaraṇam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the logician's position by the established doctrine.

body.text:
atrābhidhīyate- na tāvadgṛhābhāvamātraṃ liṅgaṃ mṛte 'pi saṃbhavāt /
na jīvanamātraṃ gṛhe 'pi sadbhāvāt /
ato jīvanasaṃsṛṣṭo gṛhābhāvo liṅgamiti vaktavyam /
prathamaṃ ca liṅgamavagamya paścālliṅgyanumānena bhavitavyam /
na tu liṅgāvagamasamaya eva liṅgyavagamaḥ /
atra ca na bahirbhāvāvagamamantareṇa gṛhābhāvo jīvanaṃ ca saṃsṛṣṭaṃ pratyetuṃ śakyate virodhāt /
jīvatā hyavaśyaṃ gṛhe vā bahirvā sthātavyamityasaṃdigdham /
ataśca bahirbhāvamanantarbhāvya jīvanagṛhābhāvau samuccitya pratipadyamānasyedṛśī pratipattirāpadyate devadatto gṛhe 'navasthito gṛhe vā bahirvāvasthita iti /

children.text: nacaivaṃ saṃbhavati bhāvābhāvayorekatra deśe samuccetamaśakyatvāt /
children.translated_text: And this is not possible, since existence and non-existence cannot be conjoined in the same location.

children.text: ato 'vaśyaṃ deśabhedenaiva devadattasya bhāvābhāvau samuccetavyau /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the existence and non-existence of <s>Devadatta</s> must be conjoined through difference of location alone.

children.text: tena bhāvābhāvasaṃsargabuddhyaiva bahurbhāvasya buddhatvānna paścātkiñcitprameyamasti /
children.translated_text: Hence, since being outside is already cognized through the very cognition of the conjunction of existence and non-existence, there is nothing further to be known afterwards.

children.text: āha ca vidyamānatvasaṃsṛṣṭagehābhāvadhiyānayā //
children.translated_text: And it is said: 'By this cognition of the absence from the house conjoined with existence, the existence displaced from the house comes to rest outside alone.'

body.translated_text: Here it is stated: the mere absence from the house is not the logical mark, since it is present even when [the person] is dead. Nor is being alive alone [the mark], since it is present even in the house. Therefore, the absence from the house conjoined with being alive must be stated as the logical mark. And first the mark must be apprehended, and afterwards the inference of the thing to be inferred should follow — not that the apprehension of the thing to be inferred occurs at the very time of apprehending the mark. But here, without the apprehension of being outside, the absence from the house and being alive cannot be cognized as conjoined, because of contradiction. For it is indubitable that one who is alive must be situated either in the house or outside. Therefore, for one who cognizes the conjunction of being alive and absence from the house without incorporating being outside, the following cognition would result: '<s>Devadatta</s>, not situated in the house, is situated either in the house or outside.'

body.text:
gehādutkālitā sattā bahirevāvatiṣṭhate iti /
nanu pramāṇāntaratvepi jīvanamātrasya gṛhābhāvamātrasya vāvagamakatvābhāvātsaṃsṛṣṭamubhayaṃ gamakamityaṅgīkartavyam /
saṃsṛṣṭadhiyaiva ca bahirbhāvasya buddhatvānna paścāt kiñcutprameyamavaśiṣyata iti tulyo 'yaṃ doṣaḥ /
ucyate- iyameva saṃsṛṣṭadhīrarthāpattirityavagamya śāmyatu bhavān kiṃ punastasyāḥ kāraṇam /
dvayorgṛhābhāvadajīvanayoḥ parasparapratighāta iti brūmaḥ /
yathā khalvekena nadyāstīre phalāni santītyukte pareṇa ca na santītyukte pareṇa na santītyukte balābalaviśeṣamajānānaḥ śrotā mithaḥ pratihatamubhayaṃ buddhyate /
nacānyataradapi tyuktuṃ gṛhītuṃ vā śaknoti /
tathāpi tu na
body.translated_text: Objection: even if it is a separate means of valid knowledge, since neither being alive alone nor absence from the house alone can indicate [being outside], the two conjoined must be accepted as the indicator. And since being outside is already cognized through the conjoined cognition, nothing remains to be known afterwards — so this defect is equal [for both positions]. Reply: understanding that this very conjoined cognition is <s>arthāpatti</s>, may you be at peace! What further is the cause of that [cognition]? We say: the mutual conflict between the two — absence from the house and being alive.

body.text:
satvāsatve samuccinoti virodhāt /
evamihāpi gṛhe vā bahirvāvasthito devadatta iti kenacitpramāṇena pratītam /

children.text: anyena ca gṛhe nāstīti tadubhayaṃ samuccitam parasparapratighāti pratīyate so 'yaṃ pratighāto na phalasadbhāvavadasamādheyaḥ kintu bahirbhāvakalpanayā samādhātuṃ śakyata ityetāvānviśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: And by another [means of knowledge] it is cognized that he is not in the house — the two cognized together are perceived as mutually conflicting. This conflict cannot be resolved as in the case of the existence of fruits [where one testimony overrides another], but can be resolved by the postulation of being outside — this much is the difference.

children.text: tena pramāṇasiddhayordvayorarthayoḥ parasparaṃ pratighātor'thāntarakalpanayā samādheyatvenālocyamānor'thāpatteḥ kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, when two objects established by valid means of knowledge are mutually conflicting, and the postulation of a further fact is contemplated for their resolution — this is the cause of <s>arthāpatti</s>.

children.text: tatsamādhānāya cārthāntarakalpanārthāpattiḥ pramāṇāntaramanumānāt /
children.translated_text: And for their resolution, the postulation of a further fact is <s>arthāpatti</s>, a means of valid knowledge separate from inference.

children.text: yaścāyaṃ pratītasya pramāṇāntareṇa pratighātaḥ sa evārthānupapattirityucyate //
children.translated_text: And this conflict of what has been cognized with another means of knowledge is precisely what is called <s>arthānupapatti</s> (impossibility of the matter).

body.translated_text: Just as when one person says 'there are fruits on the riverbank' and another says 'there are not,' a listener who does not know the relative strength [of the two assertions] cognizes the two as mutually conflicting. And he can neither abandon nor accept either one. Nevertheless, he does not conjoin existence and non-existence, because of contradiction. Similarly here too, it has been cognized by some means of valid knowledge that <s>Devadatta</s> is situated either in the house or outside.

body.text: arthāpattāvanumānasyāntarbhāvaśaṅkā /
body.translated_text: The suspicion of the subsumption of inference under <s>arthāpatti</s>.

body.text:
bhavatvarthāpattiḥ pramāṇaṃ anumānaṃ tvarthāpattāvevāntarbhavati /
tathāhi yatra yatra dhūmastatratatrāgnirityavagatam /
parvatasya ca dhūmavattāvagatā /
yadi parvate 'gnirna syāttadī dhūmavattā vā mithyā syāt /
sarvadhūmavatāṃ vāgimattvaṃ mithyā syāt kathaṃ tadubhayamapyamithyā syādityagnimatvaṃ kalpyata ityarthāpattireṣā /
syādevaṃ yadi sarvadhūmavatāmagnimattvamanumānādanyenāvagataṃ syāt /
natvevamasti /
dṛṣṭāntadharmiṣveva hi dhūmasyāgniniyamo 'vagato na sarvatra /
anumānastu sarvadhūmavatāmagnimattāvagatirityuktam /
na ca dṛṣṭāntadharmiṣvevāvagatasyāgniniyamasya sarvadhūmavadagnimattāṃ vinā kaścidvirodho yenārthāpattiḥ syāt /
tasmādasaṃkīrṇaviṣayatvādanumānenāvagataṃ tasya parvatādiṣu dhūmadarśanādyadāgnivijñānaṃ tadaddvedhāpi saṃbhavati dṛṣṭāntaparidṛṣṭaniyamasmaraṇādvānumānam /
pratighātalocanayāvārthāpattiḥ /
tasmādarthāpattiḥ pramāṇāntaram /
yāpi kvacidavasthitasya devadattasyānyatra sarvatrābhāvapratipattiḥ sāpyarthāpattiḥ /
tathāhi mūrtasyārthasya yugapatkārsnyenānekadeśasaṃbandho na ghaṭata iti svaśarīre 'vagatam /
svaśarīrasya hi kvacidavasthitasya tato 'nyatra sarvatrābhāvo dṛśyādarśanenāvagataḥ, ato 'nyasyāpi devadattāderyugupadanekadeśasaṃbandho nāstītyanumīyate /
tato devadattaṃ kvacitpratyakṣeṇāvagacchanyugapadanekadeśāsaṃbandhaṃ cānumānenāvadhārayannubhayopapattaye deśāntareṣu sarveṣvabhāvaṃ kalpayati /
nanvanumānamevedaṃ saṃbhavati devadatto 'dhunā sarvatra nāsti gṛhe 'vasthitatvānmadvaditi /
satyam /
devadattena sahaikadeśāvasthitasya saṃbhavati, yastu kvacidgṛhe 'vasthitastadanantaraṃ gṛhamapyatītya tṛtīye gṛhe devadattaṃ kenacitpramāṇenāvagatavān sa tadgṛhātirikte madhyagṛhe deśāntareṣu ca sarveṣvabhāvaṃ devadattasya kena liṅgena pratīyāt /
atha kvaciddevadattaṃ paśyan taddeśavyatirikte ca pratyāsanne deśe tadabhāvamavagacchannanyeṣāmapi sarvadeśānāṃ pratyāsannadevadattaddeśavyatiriktatvāttacchūnyatāmanumimīte /

children.text: tatrāpi viruddhāvyabhicāritvaṃ tadvadeva hi gamyate /
children.translated_text: even there, the counter-argument of conflicting non-deviation [applies], for it is understood in just the same way:

children.text: samīpadeśabhinnatvāccaitrādhiṣṭhitadeśavat /
children.translated_text: 'Because of being different from the nearby location, like the location occupied by <s>Caitra</s>'

children.text: iti vārtika eva dūṣaṇamuktam tasmādarthāpattireveyam /
children.translated_text: — thus the refutation has been stated in the <s>Vārtika</s> itself. Therefore, this is indeed <s>arthāpatti</s>.

children.text: etena bījādiṣvaṅkurajananaśaktikalpanā vyākhyātā //
children.translated_text: By this, the postulation of the generative capacity in seeds and the like is explained.

body.translated_text: Let <s>arthāpatti</s> be a valid means of knowledge — but inference is subsumed under <s>arthāpatti</s> itself. For thus: it has been ascertained that wherever there is smoke, there is fire. And the smokiness of the mountain has been ascertained. If there were no fire on the mountain, then either its smokiness would be false, or the fire-possession of all smoky things would be false — how can both be true? Therefore fire-possession is postulated — this is <s>arthāpatti</s>. [Reply:] It would be so if the fire-possession of all smoky things were known by a means other than inference. But that is not the case. For the invariable connection of smoke with fire is known only in the example-substrata, not everywhere. Inference, however, is the cognition of fire-possession for all smoky things — as has been stated. And there is no conflict in the fire-connection known only in example-substrata without the fire-possession of all smoky things, such that <s>arthāpatti</s> would arise. Therefore, since they have non-overlapping domains, when from seeing smoke on a mountain and the like the cognition of fire arises, this is possible in two ways: either it is inference through the remembrance of the invariable connection observed in example-substrata, or it is <s>arthāpatti</s> through the contemplation of conflict. Therefore, <s>arthāpatti</s> is a separate means of valid knowledge. And the cognition of the absence of <s>Devadatta</s>, who is situated somewhere, everywhere else — that too is <s>arthāpatti</s>. For thus: it has been ascertained through one's own body that simultaneous connection of a material object with multiple locations in its entirety is not possible. For one's own body, when situated somewhere, its absence everywhere else is known through seeing and not-seeing. Therefore, for another [person] like <s>Devadatta</s> too, it is inferred that there is no simultaneous connection with multiple locations. Then, perceiving <s>Devadatta</s> somewhere through direct perception and ascertaining through inference his non-connection with multiple locations simultaneously, one postulates his absence in all other locations to accommodate both. [Objection:] But this is possible as inference: '<s>Devadatta</s> does not exist everywhere now, because of being situated in the house, like myself.' [Reply:] True — this is possible for one who is situated in the same location as <s>Devadatta</s>. But one who, being situated in some house, then passes beyond that house and ascertains <s>Devadatta</s> in a third house by some means of knowledge — by what logical mark would he cognize <s>Devadatta</s>'s absence in the intermediate house and all other locations distinct from that house? If, seeing <s>Devadatta</s> somewhere and cognizing his absence in the nearby location distinct from that, he infers the emptiness of all other locations too because they are also distinct from the location where <s>Devadatta</s> is situated —
[Section] 80.

body.text:
kiṃ punaḥ śaktikalpanāṃ vinā nopapadyate bījādiṣu satsvaṅgurādyupapattidarśanāt asatsu cādarśanāt /
bījādīnāmaṅkurādikāraṇatvamavagamyate /
satsvapi bījeṣu mūṣikāghrāteṣvaṅkurānutpatterakāraṇatvaṃ pratibhāsate /
so 'yaṃ kāraṇatvākāraṇatvayorvirodhaḥ śaktikalpanayā samādhīyate- nūnamastyatīndriyamapi rūpaṃ yadbhāvāt kadācidaṅkurotpattiḥ yasya ca mūṣikā'ghrāṇena nāśātkadācidanutpattiriti kalpyate ghrāṇābhāvo 'pyaṅkurasya kāraṇam /
ghrāṇo ca sati tadabhāvādevānutpattyupapatteralaṃ śaktikalpanayeti cet /
na /
ghrāṇakriyāyāḥ kṣaṇikatvāduttarakālaṃ tadabhāve satyapyaṅkurānutpatteḥ /
prāgabhāvaḥ kāraṇaṃ na pradhvaṃsābhāva iti cet /
na /
abhāvatvāviśeṣāt /
na hi prāgabhāvapradhvaṃsābhāvayoḥ prāgūrdhvakālabhedaṃ muktvā kiñcidapi rūpavailakṣaṇyamasti, nacāvilakṣaṇe kāraṇe kāryavailakṣaṇyaṃ saṃbhavati /
prāgabhāvasya pradhvaṃsābhāvādvilakṣaṇamasti rūpamiti cet kalpyamevaṃ sati kiñcit /
taccābhāve kalpyatāṃ bījasvarūpe veti bījasya sākṣādaṅkukāraṇatvāttatraiva kalpayituṃ yuktam /
evaṃ yāgāderapūrvasvargādisādhanaśaktikalpanamūhanīyam /
kathaṃ punaḥ śaktimati yāge vinaṣṭe nirādhārā śaktiravatiṣṭhate, na nirādhārā bhaviṣyati /
ātmādhāratvāt /
kathamanyaśaktiranyatra syāt tathāvagamāt /
nāvaśyaṃ svāśrayaiva śaktiriti niyamo 'sti, sā hi kāryataḥ kalpyamānā yatraiva kāryāya
body.translated_text: But why cannot [the effect] be explained without postulating a potency (<s>śakti</s>)?
