Because when seeds and the like are present, the arising of sprouts and the like is observed, and when they are absent, it is not observed — [thus] the causal nature of seeds and the like with respect to sprouts and the like is apprehended. But even when seeds are present, when they have been gnawed by mice, the non-arising of sprouts leads to the appearance of non-causality. This contradiction between causality and non-causality is resolved by postulating a potency: 'Surely there exists a supersensible form, from whose presence the sprout sometimes arises, and from whose destruction by the gnawing of mice the sprout sometimes does not arise' — thus a potency is postulated. [Objection:] The gnawing too is a cause of the non-arising of the sprout; and the non-arising is explained by the absence of the gnawing when that [gnawing] exists — so there is no need to postulate a potency. [Reply:] No — since the act of gnawing is momentary, even at a later time when it is absent, the sprout does not arise. [Objection:] Prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) is the cause, not destruction-absence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>). [Reply:] No, because there is no difference in their nature as absences. For between prior absence and destruction-absence, apart from the temporal distinction of before and after, there is no difference whatsoever in form. And in a cause that is undifferentiated, difference in effect is not possible. [Objection:] Prior absence has a form different from destruction-absence. [Reply:] If so, something is merely being postulated. And let that be postulated either in the absence or in the nature of the seed — since the seed is the direct cause of the sprout, it is proper to postulate [the potency] there itself. Similarly, the postulation of a potency (<s>apūrva</s>) in sacrifices and the like as the means of attaining heaven and the like should be considered. [Objection:] But when the sacrifice, which possesses the potency, has been destroyed, how does the potency without a substratum persist? [Reply:] It will not be without a substratum, because it has the self (<s>ātman</s>) as its substratum. [Objection:] How can the potency of one thing reside in another? [Reply:] Because it is so apprehended. There is no necessary rule that a potency must reside only in its own substratum; for it, being postulated from the effect, should be postulated as residing in whatever [entity] is suitable for [producing] the effect —

children.text: kalpate tadgataiva kalpyā /
children.translated_text: it should be postulated as residing there.

children.text: sāceyaṃpūrvākhyātiryāgāśrayā satī yāgavināśānna svarganiṣpattaye paryāptayādityātmāśrayā kalpyate /
children.translated_text: And this [potency], called <s>apūrva</s>, having the sacrifice as its [original] substratum, since it is not sufficient for the production of heaven upon the destruction of the sacrifice, is postulated as having the self as its substratum.

children.text: yathāha- śaktiḥ kāryānumeyatvādyadgataivopayujyate //
children.translated_text: As it is said: 'Since potency is to be inferred from the effect, [it resides] in whatever is useful for [that effect];'

body.text: tatraiva sābhyupetavyā svāśrayānyāśrayāpi veti //
body.translated_text: 'it should be accepted as residing there — whether in its own substratum or in another.'

children.text: kathamātmāśrayā satī yāgaśaktiriti vyapadiśyate /
children.translated_text: How is it called 'the potency of the sacrifice' when it has the self as its substratum?

children.text: tasya hi phalasādhanatvamupapāpādayituṃ sā kalpyate tāvatā tacchaktitvam /
children.translated_text: For in order to establish [the sacrifice's] being the means of the result, that [potency] is postulated — and to that extent it is [called] the potency of that [sacrifice].

children.text: loke 'pi prasiddhametat tailapānasāmarthyācciravṛtte 'pi tasminbalapuṣṭyādikamadya me jātamiti laukikā vyavaharanti tasmādanavadyam //
children.translated_text: This is well-known even in the world — people say, by virtue of the efficacy of drinking oil, 'even though a long time has passed since then, strength and nourishment have arisen in me today.' Therefore, this is unobjectionable. //

body.text:
dṛṣcagrahaṇenaiva pratītimātragrahācchautasyāpi grahaṇe siddhe śrutārthāpatteḥ pramāṇagrāhiṇītvena dṛṣṭārthāpattito vailakṣaṇyamupapādayituṃ śrutagrahaṇaṇ /
tathāhi loke tāvat dvāraṃ dvāramityādiṣu saṃpūrṇārthapratipādanāya saṃvriyatāmityādiśabdāntaraṃ śrutaśabdaikavākthatvena
body.translated_text: Since by the word 'seen' (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>) alone, by way of apprehending mere cognition, even what is heard (<s>śauta</s>) would be included, the word 'heard' (<s>śruta</s>) is [separately mentioned] to establish the distinction from seen presumption (<s>dṛṣṭārthāpatti</s>) as apprehending through means of valid knowledge. Namely: in the world, in expressions like 'dvāraṃ dvāram' ('the door, the door') and the like, in order to convey the complete meaning, another word like 'saṃvriyatām' ('let it be closed') is construed as forming a single sentence with the heard word —

body.text: kalpyate* ////
body.translated_text: is postulated. ////

children.text: tathā vede 'pi viśvajitā yājetetyatra svargakāma iti vā svargārthamiti vā yenaiva śabdena śrutiśabdaikavākyabhūtena paripūrṇārthābhidhānaṃ saṃpadyate tadeva hṛdayamānīya śrutena saha melayitvā paripūraṇādvākyādvākyārthaḥ pratīyate, yathā sauryaṃ caruṃ nirvapedbrahmavarcasakāmaḥ ityādiṣu vidhiṣvitikartavyatāpratipādakaśabdāśravaṇādapūrṇeṣu tatpratipādakaśabdānapekṣayā codanāliṅgopasthāpitasyāgneyavidhekhyaṃśasya sādhyasādhanāṃśapratipādakabhāgāvanapekṣitatvādanādṛtya yastṛtīyoṃ'śa itthaṃbhāvo 'gnyatvādhānādirvidhyantatvena parikalpitastasya divacchabdena kalpitena, kintu ya evāyamāgneyavidhyantastasyaiva vyavahitasyāpi codanāliṅgabalopasthāpitasya vikṛtividhinā sahaikavākyatāmātramarthāpattyā kalpyate /
children.translated_text: Similarly, in the <s>Veda</s> too, in [the text] 'viśvajitā yajeta' ('one should sacrifice with the <s>Viśvajit</s>'), by bringing in from memory whatever word — 'svargakāmaḥ' ('one desiring heaven') or 'svargārtham' ('for the sake of heaven') — by which, forming a single sentence with the heard word, the expression of the complete meaning is accomplished, and combining [it] with the heard [text], from the completed sentence the sentence-meaning is apprehended. Just as in injunctions like 'sauryaṃ caruṃ nirvaped brahmavarcasakāmaḥ' ('one desiring Vedic splendor should offer a rice-cake to <s>Sūrya</s>') and the like, where the texts are incomplete due to the non-hearing of words conveying the manner of performance (<s>itikartavyatā</s>), without depending on those conveying words — the whole portion of the <s>Āgneya</s> injunction brought up by the indication of <s>codanā</s> (injunctive force), disregarding its third part, which is the specific manner such as placing fire and the like construed as being subsidiary to the injunction — not by a separately postulated word, but of this very <s>Āgneya</s> injunction-subsidiary, even though separated, brought up by the force of injunctive indication — merely the single-sentence-hood with the modified rite is postulated through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption).

children.text: nahyayamanuṣaṅgo yena vyavahitasya na syāditi /
children.translated_text: For this is not a restrictive connection such that it would not apply to what is separated.

children.text: atideśastvayaṃ vyavahitasyāpi kathañcidupasthānādupapanna eva /
children.translated_text: Rather, this is an extension (<s>atideśa</s>), and it is justified since even what is separated can be somehow brought into consideration.

children.text: tathā ca vakṣyati- vidhyaṃnto vā prakṛtivaccodanāyāṃ pravarteti vidhyanta iti pradhānavidhivarjitaṃ samastameva pauroḍāśikaṃ kāṇḍamabhidhīyata iti bhāṣyakāraḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus it will be said: 'The subsidiary of the injunction, like the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>), operates in the injunction' — 'subsidiary of the injunction' refers to the entire <s>Pauroḍāśika</s> chapter excluding the primary injunction — so says the commentator (<s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>). //

body.text:
nanvevaṃ śāstrātideśāṅgīkaraṇe daśamādyavirodhaḥ syāt, ūhabādhayoścāsiddhiḥ /
bhavedevaṃ yadi yathāśrutarūpameva vrīhinavahantīti vākyaṃ vikṛtiṃ nītvā tasya yathāsaṃbhavaṃ vikṛtividhinā sahaikavākyatā parikalpyeta /
yadi tathā kriyate tatra kṛṣṇalacarau vrīhiśabdasya havirlaṇārthatvāyogādavadhātasya bādhaḥ syāt /
evaṃ nīvārādiṣvapi vrīhaya evāvahantavyāḥ iti na nīvārādiṣvavahantirūhyeta /
natvevamasmābhirucyate kintu prakṛtau pradhānena sahaikavākyatayāvagatasyāsya yāvanparikaro tādṛgatidiśyate prakṛtau haviṣṭvāt, tallakṣaṇārtho, avaghātasya ca teṣu dṛṣṭaṃ prayojanaṃ tuṣavimocanaṃ saṃbhavatīti taddvāreṇāsya pradhānaikavākyatā /
tataśca- avaghātavituṣīkṛtairvrīhibhiḥ puroḍāśaṃ kṛtvā tena yajetetīdṛśaḥ prakṛtividhiḥ, tasya sākṣādavaghāto viśeṣaṇam, avaghātaviśeṣitavituṣīkaraṇaviśiṣṭaṃ hi haviryāgasya viśeṣaṇaṃ prakṛtau, atastadeva vikṛtāvākṛṣyate /
kṛṣṇalayāge ca kṛṣṇalaśabdasya havirvācinaḥ pratyakṣaśravaṇāttadvirodhātpuroḍāśaśabdo nivartate, tannivṛttyā ca vrīhīṇāmapi nivṛttiḥ /

children.text: na hi te kṛṣṇalānāṃ prakṛtitvena saṃbhavanti /
children.translated_text: For they [i.e., rice] cannot serve as the archetype for <s>kṛṣṇalas</s>.

children.text: vituṣīkaraṇaśabdo 'pi yo dvārapratipādakaḥ so 'pi kṛṣṇaleṣu tadasaṃbhavādanivṛtto 'vaghāta ityūhasyāpi siddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The word 'dehusking' too, which conveys the means, since it is inapplicable to <s>kṛṣṇalas</s>, is not superseded, [while] 'threshing' [is superseded] — thus the establishment of modification (<s>ūha</s>) too [is achieved].

children.text: daśamādye ca yāvacchrutānāmaṅgaśāstrāṇāmatideśamāśaṅkyā prakṛtyanvitānāṃ tena rūpeṇātideśaḥ /
children.translated_text: And in the tenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>] and the like, the extension of subsidiary <s>śāstras</s> that are heard — as connected with the archetype, in that form — is [meant].

children.text: nārthamātreṇa ityalamatiprasaṅgena* ////
children.translated_text: Not by meaning alone — thus enough of excessive elaboration. ////

body.translated_text: Objection: If scripture-based extension (<s>śāstrātideśa</s>) is thus accepted, there would be a contradiction with the tenth [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>] and the like, and the establishment of modification (<s>ūha</s>) and cancellation (<s>bādha</s>) [would be undermined]. This would be so if the sentence 'vrīhīn avahanti' ('they thresh the rice') were taken to the modified rite in its literal form and its single-sentence-hood with the modified injunction were postulated. If done so, in the <s>kṛṣṇala</s>-offering, since the word 'vrīhi' (rice), denoting the oblation material, would be inapplicable, there would be cancellation of the threshing. Similarly, even in [rites using] <s>nīvāra</s> and the like, since only rice would have to be threshed, threshing of <s>nīvāra</s> and the like would not be modified. But we do not say this. Rather, what is understood in the archetype as forming a single sentence with the primary [injunction] — its entire subsidiary apparatus is extended to [the modified rite] because of being an oblation-material in the archetype, having the characteristic of that [oblation-material]. And since the observed purpose of threshing — namely, dehusking — is possible in those [modified rites] too, single-sentence-hood of this [threshing] with the primary [injunction] is through that [purpose]. And thus, the archetypal injunction is: 'having made the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake) with rice dehusked by threshing, one should sacrifice with that' — of this, threshing is a direct qualifier; and the oblation material, qualified by dehusking specified by threshing, is the qualifier of the sacrifice in the archetype. Therefore, that alone is transferred to the modified rite. And in the <s>kṛṣṇala</s>-sacrifice, since the word '<s>kṛṣṇala</s>,' denoting the oblation, is directly heard, due to conflict with it, the word '<s>puroḍāśa</s>' is superseded, and with its supersession, rice too is superseded.

body.text:
nanvarthamevādhyāhṛtya vākyaṃ pūryatāṃ kiṃ śabdakalpanayā /
nārthamātreṇa pūraṇaṃ saṃbhavati, ekavākyabhūtapadadvayapratipāditā hi padārthā vākyārthaṃ pratipādayanti nānyathā /
na hi ānaya ityetāvatyukte gāmityanukte pratyakṣapratipanne 'pi gavi gavā sahānayanamanvīyate /
evaṃ ca vikṛtiṣu
body.translated_text: Objection: Let the meaning alone be supplied to complete the sentence — why postulate a word? [Reply:] Completion by meaning alone is not possible, for sentence-meanings are conveyed by the meanings of two words forming a single sentence — not otherwise. For when only 'bring' is said and 'cow' is not said, even though the cow is perceptually present, the bringing of the cow is not construed [with the sentence]. Similarly, in the modified rites

body.text: sauryādiṣvasamavetārthāgryādipadanivṛtternyūnasākāṅkṣamantravākyapūraṇāya sūryādipadāprakṣepādūhasiddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: such as <s>Saurya</s> and the like, since the words '<s>āgrya</s>' (first-fruit) and the like, whose meanings are not syntactically connected, are absent, for completing the deficient and expectant <s>mantra</s>-sentence, through the insertion of words like '<s>Sūrya</s>' and the like, the establishment of modification (<s>ūha</s>) [is achieved]. //

body.text: arthādhyāhārapakṣakhaṇḍanam //
body.translated_text: Refutation of the view that [mere] meaning is to be supplied:

children.text: arthādhyāhāravādināṃ tu sūryārthenādhyāhṛtena viśiṣṭaṃ nirvapāmipadameva prakāśayatīti nohaḥ sidhyet /
children.translated_text: For those who hold the view of supplying meaning, the word 'nirvapāmi' ('I offer'), qualified by the meaning 'to <s>Sūrya</s>' that has been supplied, would itself express [the complete meaning] — so modification (<s>ūha</s>) would not be established.

children.text: tathā yatrādhikāravākyer'thavādamātraṃ śrutaṃ pratitiṣṭhanti ha vā ya etā rātrīrupayantīti tatrāpi bhavanmate vidhyarthaṃ evādhyāhāryo na vidhiśabdaḥ, tataśca prākṛtasyopakārasya padārthānāṃ ca nāpūrvaidamarthyaṃ sidhyet /
children.translated_text: Similarly, where in an eligibility-sentence only an <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage) is heard — 'pratitiṣṭhanti ha vā ya etā rātrīr upayanti' ('they indeed become firmly established who perform these nights') — there too, on your view, only the meaning of an injunction should be supplied, not the injunctive word; and consequently, the unique relation of the archetypal subsidiary elements and the meanings would not be established.

children.text: satsvapi hyarthānāmākāṅkṣāsaṃnidhiyogyatveṣu nābhidhānamantareṇānvayasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: For even when the meanings have expectancy, proximity, and compatibility, without verbal expression, the syntactic connection cannot be established.

children.text: nacehāpūrvābhidhāyī śabdo 'sti yo 'pūrvaṃ prākṛtairanvitasteṣāmanvayaḥ nāpyutpattyapūrveṇānvaya eva syāt* ////
children.translated_text: And here there is no word conveying <s>apūrva</s> that would syntactically connect the <s>apūrva</s> with the archetypal elements; nor would there be connection with the origination-<s>apūrva</s> alone. ////

children.text: evaṃ prakṛtāvapi sarvebhyaḥ kāmebhyo darśapūrṇamāsau ityatra vidhiśabdasyānāmnānādanadhyāhārācca vidhyarthasyaiva svargakāmādhikārāpūrvādāgneyādyutpattyapūrvebhyaśca pṛthagbhūtasyādhyāhārānna samidādīnāmaidamarthyaṃ sidhyet /
children.translated_text: Similarly, even in the archetype, in [the text] 'sarvebhyaḥ kāmebhyo darśapūrṇamāsau' ('the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices [are performed] for all desires'), since the injunctive word is not mentioned and [its] meaning is not to be supplied, there would be the supply of the meaning of the injunction as separate from the eligibility-<s>apūrva</s> [connected with] 'svargakāma' (desiring heaven) and the origination-<s>apūrvas</s> from <s>Āgneya</s> and the like — and from this, the subsidiary relation of <s>samidh</s> (fuel-sticks) and the like would not be established.

children.text: na hi samidādiyajatayo 'vaghātādivadadhikārāpūrvānvitaṃ svārthāmabhidhātumalaṃ svāpūrvaviṣayatvavyāghātāt /
children.translated_text: For the <s>samidh</s> and other subsidiary sacrifices, unlike threshing and the like, cannot express their own meaning as connected with the eligibility-<s>apūrva</s>, because of the contradiction with being related to their own <s>apūrva</s>.

children.text: tasmādīdṛdṛśeṣvadhikāravidhiṣu vidhiśabda evādhyāhāryo nārthaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, in such eligibility-injunctions, it is the injunctive word itself that should be supplied, not [merely] the meaning. ////

body.text: kathaṃ ca vidhyarthasyātyantālaukikatayā pramāṇena tadābhāsena vā buddhāvāropayitumaśakyatvenābhimatasya buddhisaṃnidhānatmako 'dhyāhāro 'śrutavidhiśabdakeṣvadhikāravākyeṣu vā utpattivākyeṣu yadāgneyo 'kapālo 'māvāsyāyāmityādiṣu vā śakyate, ityakāmenāpi śabdādhyāhāro 'ṅgīkartavya ityāstāṃ tāvat //
body.translated_text: Moreover, how can the supply (<s>adhyāhāra</s>) — which consists in the bringing to mind — of the meaning of the injunction, which is accepted as utterly beyond worldly experience and as incapable of being placed in the mind by any means of valid knowledge or semblance thereof — [how can this] be [possible] in eligibility-sentences where there is no heard injunctive word, or in origination-sentences such as 'yad āgneyo 'kapālo 'māvāsyāyām' ('that the [cake] for <s>Agni</s>, without a potsherd [stand], on the new-moon day') and the like? Therefore, even one unwilling must accept the supply of a word. So let this stand. //

body.text: ityarthāpattivādaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [concludes] the exposition of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). //

body.text: abhāva(anupalabdhi) paricchedaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Abhāva</s> (non-existence) / <s>Anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) section.

body.text:
abhāvo 'pi pramāṇābhāvo nāstītyasyārthasyāsaṃnikṛṣṭasyeti /
kathaṃ punaḥ pramāṇābhāvaḥ pramāṇalakṣaṇaṃ viparītatvāt /
pūrvoktasadupalambhakapratyakṣādipramāṇapañcakābhiprāyo 'yaṃ pramāṇaśabdaḥ /

children.text: tadabhāvaśca ṣaṣṭhasya lakṣaṇamiti nānupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: And the absence of those [five] is the defining characteristic of the sixth — so there is no impropriety.

children.text: kimasya prameyam /
children.translated_text: What is its object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>)?

children.text: uktaṃ nāstītyarthasya iti /
children.translated_text: It has been stated: 'of which the meaning is that something does not exist.'

children.text: sarvaṃ hi vastu sadasadātmanā dvavidhaṃ, tadyadā yatra sadrūpeṇa bodhakānāṃ pratyakṣādīnāṃ sadrūpabodhanāyotpattuṃ yogyatve satyapi yo 'nutpādod daśyādarśanayogyanupalambhādiparyāyo bhāṣye pramāṇābhāvaśabdenoktasyenaivendriyaśabdādisthānīyena nāstīti pratīyate bhūtale 'tra ghaṭo nāstīti* ////
children.translated_text: For every entity is twofold — as existent and as non-existent. When, in a given case, perception and the like, which are capable of conveying [the entity's] existent form, although having the capacity to arise for conveying the existent form, do not arise — that non-arising, which is synonymous with 'visibility and non-seeing' (<s>dṛśyādarśana</s>), 'non-apprehension' (<s>anupalabdhi</s>), and the like, is stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> by the word 'absence of a means of valid knowledge' — and by this [non-apprehension], standing in the place of sense-organ, word, and the like, [the meaning] 'it does not exist' is apprehended, as in 'the pot does not exist here on the ground.' ////

body.translated_text: Non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>) too is a means of valid knowledge — 'the absence of a means of knowledge' is [the defining mark] 'of which the meaning is that something does not exist and which is not in contact [with the senses].' [Question:] But how can the absence of a means of valid knowledge be the defining characteristic of a means of valid knowledge, since they are contradictory? [Reply:] The word 'means of valid knowledge' (<s>pramāṇa</s>) here refers to the five means of valid knowledge — perception and the like — which were previously stated as apprehending what is existent.

body.text: yastu nāstitvamapahnutya
body.translated_text: But one who, denying [the reality of] non-existence,

body.text:
prameyābhāvātṣaṣṭhaṃ pramāṇaṃ nāstītyāha tasya dṛśyādarśanānantaraṃ nāstīha bhūtale ghaṭa ityevamupajāyamānasya jñānasya kimālambanam /
na bhūtalam /
satyapi ghaṭe prasaṅgāt /
tathā gavi yo 'śvo na bhavatīti pratyayo rūpe ca raso na bhavatīti tasya kimālambanam /

children.text: na gorūpam /
children.translated_text: Not the form of the cow —

children.text: tasya pratiyogyanapekṣapratītikatvāt /
children.translated_text: because its cognition does not depend on a counter-correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>).

children.text: aśvo na bhavatīti jñānasya pratiyogyapekṣatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because the cognition 'there is no horse [here]' depends on the counter-correlate.

children.text: gorūpālambanatve siṃhādāvaśvo 'yaṃ na bhavatīti pratyayo na syāt gorūpasya tatrābhāvāt* ////
children.translated_text: If [the cognition had] the form of the cow as its object, then in a lion and the like, the cognition 'this is not a horse' would not arise, since the form of the cow is absent there. ////

body.translated_text: says that there is no sixth means of valid knowledge because there is no object to be known — for him, what is the object of the cognition that arises immediately after 'visibility and non-seeing' in the form 'the pot does not exist here on the ground'? Not the ground — because [such cognition] would arise even when the pot exists. Likewise, for the cognition that 'there is no horse in the cow' and 'there is no taste in color' — what is their object?

children.text: atha yo 'śvādbhedo gavādiṣvanusyūtaḥ so 'syālambanamityucyate /
children.translated_text: Now, if it is said that the difference pervading cows and the like, which [is the difference] from a horse, is the object [of that cognition] —

children.text: ko 'yaṃ bhedo nāma, yadītaretarābhāvaḥ samāśritastarhyabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is this so-called difference? If mutual absence (<s>itaretarābhāva</s>) is resorted to, then [you have accepted] an absence.

children.text: atha pṛthaktvaṃ nāma guṇaviśeṣo bheda ityucyate, tatastasya dravyagatatvādguṇeṣu rūpādiṣu 'raso na bhavati rūpaṃ' 'rūpaṃ na bhavati rasaḥ' itītaretarābhāvapratyayo na syāt //
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, a particular quality called 'separateness' (<s>pṛthaktva</s>) is called difference, then since that resides in substances, in qualities such as color and the like, the cognition of mutual absence — 'taste is not color' and 'color is not taste' — would not arise. //

body.text: prabhākaramatakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the <s>Prābhākara</s> view:

body.text: yastu vaiyātyāt bhūtalapratītivyatirekeṇa ghaṭo nāstītyevaṃvidhā ghaṭo nāstītyevaṃvidhā pratītireva nāsti iti vadati, sa bhūtalādipratītimapyapahnuvīta, aviśeṣāt, ghaṭo 'tra bhūtale nāstīti vyavahārasya kiṃ kāraṇaṃ, dṛśye ghaṭe yadbhūtalamātraviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ tadasya kāraṇamiticet,
body.translated_text: But one who says, out of perversity, that there is no cognition of the form 'the pot does not exist' apart from the cognition of the ground [alone] — he might as well deny the cognition of the ground and the like too, since there is no distinction [in principle]. What is the cause of the practical usage 'the pot does not exist here on the ground'? [If one says:] 'when the pot is visible, the cognition that has only the ground as its object — that is its cause' —

children.text: tathāsati paṭavadbhūtalopalambhe ghaṭo nāstīti vyavahāro na syāt /
children.translated_text: in that case, upon perceiving the ground together with the cloth [on it], the practical usage 'the pot does not exist' would not arise,

children.text: bhūtalamātropalambhābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: because there would be no apprehension of the ground alone [without anything on it].

children.text: ghaṭaviviktabhūtalopalambha iti cet, ko 'yaṃ ghaṭavivekaḥ, yadi bhūtalarūpameva, ghaṭavatyapi prasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: [If one says] 'the apprehension of the ground as devoid of the pot' — what is this 'being devoid of the pot'? If it is the very nature of the ground, then [such cognition would arise] even when the pot is present.

children.text: ghaṭasaṃyogābhāvaścet, aṅgīkṛtastarhyabhāvaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: If [one says] it is the absence of contact with the pot — then you have accepted absence. ////

children.text: syānmatam, yadabhāvavādino 'bhāvajñānasya kāraṇaṃ tadevāsmākaṃ vyavahārakāraṇaṃ bhavatviti /
children.translated_text: One might think: whatever the advocate of absence holds to be the cause of the cognition of absence, let that very thing be the cause of our [everyday] usage —

children.text: naivaṃ vaktuṃ śakyam /
children.translated_text: this cannot be said.

children.text: mama hi dṛśyādarśanamabhāvajñānakāraṇam, adarśanaṃ ca darśanābhāvo nacāsau bhavatāṅgīkṛtaḥ, abhāvābhyupagamaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: For according to me, the non-perception of what is perceptible is the cause of the cognition of absence; and non-perception is the absence of perception — but that [absence] is not accepted by you, since [your accepting it] would entail the acceptance of absence [as a category].

children.text: pramāṇābhāvāṅgīkāre vā kimaparāddhaṃ prameyābhāvena* ////
children.translated_text: And if you accept the absence of a valid means of knowledge, what harm has been done by [accepting] the absence of the knowable [object itself]?

children.text: nanu prathamaṃ pratyakṣeṇa bhūtalaṃ gṛhītvā paścādabhāvo boddhavyastatrābhāvatrānātprāk yādṛśaṃ bhūtalajñānaṃ tādṛśādeva vyavahāro bhavatu /
children.translated_text: Objection: first, having apprehended the ground through perception, absence is to be cognized afterward. Prior to the cognition of absence, let the everyday usage arise from just such a cognition of the ground as existed [before].

children.text: tadidamuktottaram, tathāhi- yasyāmavasthāyāṃ bhūtalasvarūpajñānaṃ ghaṭatadabhāvayoścājñānaṃ jñānābhāvastena ghaṭatadabhāvajñānaśūnyaṃ bhūtalajñānaṃ tasyāmavasthāyāmasmābhirupeyate tadeva bhūtalamātravedanamityucyate* ////
children.translated_text: This has already been answered. For thus: in the state in which there is cognition of the ground's intrinsic nature but ignorance — that is, absence of cognition — of the pot and its absence, we accept that very cognition of the ground devoid of the cognition of pot and its absence in that state — and that is what is called 'mere cognition of the ground.'

children.text: svarūpamātraṃ dṛṣṭvācetyādiṣu mātraśabdena hi ghaṭatadabhāvavedanayorabhāva ucyate, bhūtalamātraṃ jñāyate na ghaṭastadabhāvo vetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: In [the expressions] 'having seen only the intrinsic nature' and the like, the word 'only' (<s>mātra</s>) denotes the absence of the cognition of the pot and its absence — the meaning being: only the ground is known, not the pot or its absence.

children.text: tena yadi bhavānapi ghaṭādijñānābhāvayuktaṃ bhūtalajñānamaṅgīkuryāt tato jñānābhāvāṅgīkartavya ityuktameva /
children.translated_text: Therefore, if you too accept a cognition of the ground conjoined with the absence of cognition of the pot and the like, then you must accept the absence of cognition — as has already been stated.

children.text: tena naivaṃ bhramitavyam- abhāvavādināpi svarūpamātraṃ dṛṣṭvā ca paścātkiñcitsmaraṇannapīti vadatā bhāvajñānātirekeṇa tanmātravedanamaṅgīkṛtam, tadeva dṛśye pratiyogini nāstīti vyavahārakāraṇatvānnāstīti śabdasyārthābhāvādbhūtalavedanameva kāraṇamiti vaktavyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should not be confused thus: 'Even the advocate of absence, when he says that after seeing only the intrinsic nature, remembering something, it is not [there] — by this he accepts the mere-that cognition over and above the cognition of a positive entity; and that very [cognition], since the counterpart [pot] is visible, causes the usage of nonexistence; and since the word nonexistence has no referent [in your view], mere ground-cognition is the cause.' For if so, the objection would apply even when the pot is present — and so the refutation stands.

children.text: tataśca ghaṭavatyapi prasaṅga iti sthitaṃ dūṣaṇam* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, even when the pot is present, the [unwanted] consequence [of absence-usage] would follow — and the refutation stands.

body.text: atha bhāve deśāntarasthe deśāntaragrahaṇaṃ kāraṇamiti mataṃ, tataḥ śābaleyasthitaṃ gotvaṃ dhāvaleye nāstīti vyavahriyeta, sthūṇāntarasthitaśca vaṃśaḥ sthūṇāntare 'nusyūto 'pi tatra nāstīti vyavahartavyaḥ syāt, ato 'trābhāva eva nāstīti vyavahārakāraṇam, nānyatra sadbhāvaḥ /

children.text: smaryamāṇe ghaṭe bhūtalavedanaṃ nāstīti vyavahārakāraṇamiticet /
children.translated_text: If [one says]: when the pot is being remembered, the cognition of the ground is the cause of the usage 'it is not [here]' —

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: no,

children.text: gṛhyamāṇasyāpi pārśvadeśeṣvabhāvavyavahārāt /
children.translated_text: because the usage of absence occurs even with respect to adjacent places where [the pot] is being perceived.

children.text: saṃpratyānītasya ca ghaṭasya gṛhyamāṇasyaiva prāgayamiha nāsīt iti prākkālīnābhāvavyavahārāt //
children.translated_text: And because, with respect to a pot that has just now been brought, even while it is being perceived, there is the usage of prior-temporal absence: 'this was not here before.'

body.translated_text: If [one says] that the apprehension [of a positive entity] situated in another place is the cause of the usage [of absence] when the positive entity is in another place — then the cowness residing in a brown cow should yield the usage 'it is not present' in a white cow; and a bamboo situated in one pillar, even though running through another pillar, should be said to be 'not there' in the latter — therefore, in this case, absence alone is the cause of the usage 'it is not [there],' not the existence [of the thing] elsewhere.

body.text: prabhākaramatānuvādaḥ //
body.translated_text: Summary of the <s>Prābhākara</s> view.

body.text:
nanu bhavanmate pramīyamānasya ghaṭasya prākkālīnābhāvajñānaṃ bhāvapramāṇabhāvo hyabhāvajñānakāraṇam /
na ca pramāyamāṇo 'pi ghaṭaḥ prākkālasaṃbandhitayā na pramīyate ataḥ prākkālasaṃbandhagocarapramāṇānudayāttatkālīnābhāvajñānaṃ yuktameveti cet /
na /
ayogyatvāt /

children.text: na hi prākkālasaṃbandho 'dhunā pramātuṃ yogyaḥ, yogyapramāṇābhāvaścābhāvajñānakāraṇaṃ na pramāṇābhāvamātram /
children.translated_text: For the prior-time relation is not fit to be cognized now; and it is the absence of a fit valid means of knowledge that is the cause of absence-cognition, not the mere absence of any valid means of knowledge.

children.text: prākkāle tu yogyasyaiva prāmāṇasyānudaya āsīt, na hi tadānīṃ ghaṭābhāvaḥ sannapi pramitaḥ pratiyogino ghaṭasyāparāmarśāt tadapekṣatvāccābhāvajñānasya, ata eva ghaṭābhāvo 'dhunā smaryata iti na yuktam /
children.translated_text: At the prior time, however, there was non-arising of a valid means of knowledge that was indeed fit [to operate then]. But even then, the absence of the pot, though existing, was not cognized — because the counterpart, the pot, was not at all apprehended, and because absence-cognition depends on [apprehension of] that [counterpart]. For this very reason, it is also improper to say that the absence of the pot is now remembered,

children.text: apramitasya smaraṇayogāt /
children.translated_text: since what was not cognized cannot be remembered.

children.text: yaścāyaṃ prākkālīnaḥ pramāṇānudayaḥ so 'dhunā pramāṇodayena naṣṭo nābhāvajñānamutpādayitumarhati, uddhṛtamiva netraṃ rūpabuddhim* ////
children.translated_text: And this non-arising of the valid means of knowledge that existed at the prior time has now been destroyed by the arising of [present] valid knowledge, and so it cannot produce absence-cognition — just as an eye that has been removed [cannot produce] color-cognition.

body.translated_text: Objection: on your view, how is the cognition of the prior-temporal absence of a pot that is [presently] being cognized [possible]? For the absence of a valid means of knowledge regarding a positive entity is the cause of absence-cognition. And a pot that is being cognized is not cognized as related to the prior time — therefore, due to the non-arising of a valid means of knowledge pertaining to the prior-time relation, the cognition of absence at that time is proper. Not so — because of unfitness.

body.text:
atha naṣṭo 'pi pramāṇānudayaḥ saṃprati smaryamāṇo hyastanāgnijñānam /
syādevaṃ yadi pramāṇābhāvo jñāyamānatayā meyābhāvaṃ bodhayet liṅgamiva liṅginam /

children.text: na ca tathā saṃbhavati anavasthāprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: But that is not possible, because of the consequence of infinite regress.

children.text: prameyābhāvaṃ bodhayet jñātavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [For] it must be known in order to communicate the absence of the knowable.

children.text: sopicābhāvatvādanyenābhāvajñānena jñātavyaḥ, so 'pyanyeneti na janmasahasreṇāpi ghaṭābhāvo 'vadhāryeta /
children.translated_text: And since it too is an absence, it must be known by another absence-cognition; and that [cognition] by yet another — thus even in a thousand births, the absence of the pot could never be ascertained.

children.text: tasmātsattāmātreṇaiva pramāṇābhāvo 'bhāvajñānamutpādayati netrādivadityaṅgīkartavyam, ataḥ pramīyamāṇasya ghaṭasya kathaṃ prākkālābhāvapramitiriti vaktavyam* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, it must be accepted that the absence of valid knowledge produces absence-cognition by its mere existence alone, like the eye and the like. Hence, it must be stated how the cognition of prior-temporal absence of a pot that is [presently] being cognized [is possible].

body.translated_text: If [one says]: even though the non-arising of valid knowledge is destroyed, it can produce [absence-cognition] by being remembered now, like the cognition of yesterday's fire — this would be so if the absence of valid knowledge, by being known, could communicate the absence of the knowable, like an inferential mark [communicates] what it marks.

body.text: ucyate- sattāmātreṇa jñānābhāvo jñāyābhāvaṃ bodhayatīti samyaguktam, astyeva tvadhunā dṛśyamānasyāpi ghaṭasya
body.translated_text: It is replied: it has been rightly said that the absence of cognition, by its mere existence, communicates the absence of [its] object. But even for a pot that is presently seen,

body.text: prākkālasaṃbandhagocarayogyajñānānudayaḥ, sahi prākkālisaṃbandhitayā smartuṃ yogyaḥ sannapi na smaryate, nacāvaśyaṃpramāṇābāva
body.translated_text: there is a non-arising of the fit cognition pertaining to the prior-time relation. For although it is fit to be remembered as related to the prior time, it is not remembered; and it is not necessarily [only] the absence of a valid means of knowledge

children.text: evābhāvasya bodhakaḥ smaraṇajñānasyāpi yogyatve satyanudayo bhāvaṃ bodhayatyeva, tena saṃprati dṛśyamāno 'pi ghaṭo yadi prāgapyāsīttato 'vaśyaṃ tatra sthitena pramitaḥ syāt, pramitaścādhunā smartavyaḥ syāt, evaṃ satyapi na smaryate so 'yaṃ smartavyaviṣayasmaraṇānudayaḥ saṃprati vidyamānaḥ saṃpratitanaṃ prākkālīnābhāvaviṣayaṃ vijñānaṃ janayatīti na kiñcidanupapannam /
children.translated_text: that communicates absence — even the non-arising of memory-cognition, when the fitness [for remembering] exists, communicates the [prior] existence [or non-existence]. Therefore, even a pot that is presently seen — if it had existed before, it would necessarily have been cognized by one situated there, and having been cognized, it should now be remembered. When, despite this, it is not remembered — this non-arising of memory regarding what should be remembered, being present now, produces the present cognition of prior-temporal absence. There is nothing improper in this.

children.text: bhāṣye ca pramāṇābhāvaśabdaḥ smaraṇābhāvasyāpyupalakṣaṇārthaḥ, tathā vārtike 'pi /
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, the term 'absence of valid means of knowledge' is intended to indicate the absence of memory as well; likewise in the <s>Vārttika</s>.

children.text: yadvā pramāṇasya smaraṇaphalatvāttadabhāvo 'pi phalataḥ pramāṇābāva eveti śakyate vaktum //
children.translated_text: Or, since memory is a result of a valid means of knowledge, its absence too can be called 'absence of a valid means of knowledge' in terms of result.

body.text: uktaprabhākarakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the above <s>Prābhākara</s> [position].

body.text:
nanu na sattāmātreṇa yogyānupalabdherabhāvabodhakatvaṃ yuktaṃ, satyāmapi tasyāṃ kadācidabhāvabuddhyanudayāt, asatyāmapi kadācidudayāt /
tathāhi yo 'ṅgulīyakabubhutsayā sasantamasāvapavarakadeśaṃ hastābhyāṃ sarvataḥ parāmṛṣṭavān tasya tāvat sarvadeśaparāmarśāt vastuto yogyānupalabdhirjātaiva, atha ca kiṃ sarvo deśaḥ parāmṛṣṭaḥ kiṃ vā kaściddeśo syāditi saṃdihāno yogyānupalabdheraniścayāt satyāpi tasyāṃ nāṅgulīyakasyābhāvamavadhārayati /
kadācittu sarvato 'parāmṛśyāpi sarvataḥ parāmṛṣṭamiti bhrāntyā yogyānupalabdhiṃ niścityāsatyāmeva tasyāṃ bhrāntyāṅgulīyakasyābhāvamavadhārayati /
tasmājjñātatayaiva yogyānupalabdhirabhāvajñānakāraṇamityabhyupagantavyam /
tathācānavasthāprasaṅgaḥ /
tasmātsvasaṃvedyā tanmātrasaṃvideva dṛśyasya pratiyogino 'bhāvo na tatvāntaram /-- /
nanu cābhāvalaṅgīkāre tanmātradhīrapi na kadācinnirūpayituṃ śakyate, na ca bhūtaladhīreva tanmātradhīḥ, saṃsṛṣṭadhiyo 'pi tanmātratāpātāt /
tatrāpi bhūtalāvabhāsāt /

children.text: ato ghaṭādivedanābhāve sati yā bhūtaladhīḥ sā tanmātradhīḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the cognition of the ground in the absence of the cognition of pot and the like — that is the 'mere-that' cognition.

children.text: evaṃ ca jñānābhāvāṅgīkārādabhāvapahnavo 'narthakaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, since the absence of cognition is accepted [even by you], the denial of absence is pointless.

children.text: kathaṃ tarhyetannirūpayitavm, tadabhidhīyate- ghaṭādyabhāvo 'sti prameyam /
children.translated_text: How then is this to be determined? It is stated: absence of pot and the like exists as a knowable entity.

children.text: yogyapramāṇānudayaśca tasya sattāmātreṇaiva netrādivadbodhako na jñātatayā, yato anavasthā syāt* ////
children.translated_text: And the non-arising of a fit valid means of knowledge communicates it by its mere existence alone, like the eye and the like — not as [something that must be] known; for otherwise, infinite regress would follow.

body.translated_text: Objection: it is not proper that fit non-apprehension (<s>yogyānupalabdhi</s>) produces absence-cognition by its mere existence — because even when it exists, the cognition of absence sometimes does not arise, and even when it does not exist, [absence-cognition] sometimes arises. For thus: one who, desiring to find a ring, has groped with his hands throughout a dark inner chamber and has touched every place — for him, fit non-apprehension has in fact occurred, since every place has been touched. And yet, doubting whether every place has been touched or whether some place remains, and being uncertain about the fit non-apprehension, he does not ascertain the absence of the ring even though that [non-apprehension] exists. On the other hand, sometimes without having touched everywhere, through the error [of thinking] 'I have touched everywhere,' he ascertains the fit non-apprehension and, even when it does not actually exist, erroneously ascertains the absence of the ring. Therefore, it must be accepted that fit non-apprehension causes absence-cognition only as known [i.e., as cognized]. And in that case, the consequence of infinite regress [would follow]. Therefore, what is self-cognized — that mere-that cognition alone — is [the cause]; the absence of a visible counterpart is not a separate entity. — But objection: if absence is not accepted, the mere-that cognition too can never be established, for even a composite cognition [of ground-with-pot] would fall under 'mere-that.' Even there, because of the appearance of the ground.

children.text: yattu satyāpi yogyānupalambho hi kāraṇaṃ tatra yogyatvaṃ jñātatayaiva kāraṇaṃ na sattāmātreṇa, tataḥ yogyatvaṃ kadācidajñātaṃ nābhāvamavadhārayati kadācittvavidyamānameva yogyatvaṃ bhrāntyā niścityābhāvamavadhārayati /
children.translated_text: As for [the objection] that even when fit non-apprehension exists, [absence-cognition does not always arise] — indeed, non-apprehension of the fit is the cause, and there the fitness [must be] known as the causal factor, not by mere existence alone. Therefore, sometimes the fitness is not known and absence is not ascertained; sometimes fitness that does not actually exist is erroneously ascertained and absence is determined.

children.text: upalabdhyabhāvastu sanmātratayā kāraṇaṃ na jñātatayā, tena nānavasthāpattiriti sarvamavadātam /
children.translated_text: The absence of apprehension, however, is a cause by its mere existence, not as known — therefore there is no infinite regress. Thus everything is clear.

children.text: ato 'styabhāvākhyaṃ prameyam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, absence is a knowable entity.

body.text: abhāvasyānupalabdhigamyatvam //
body.translated_text: Absence is known through non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>).

body.text:
na ca tadaindriyakam, indriyavyāpārābhāve 'pi tajjñānotpattidarśanāt /
yo 'hani prātaḥkāle gṛhe 'vasthito madhyandinasamaye pṛcchyate kimasmingṛhe prātaḥkāle māthuraḥ kiścitpuruṣaḥ śuklavāsā dīrghatamo lohitavarṇaḥ samāgataḥ iti sa tadānīmeva yogyasmaraṇānudayāttasyābhāvaṃ prātaḥkālīnamavadhārayati vinaivendriyavyāpāreṇa /
na ca prātaravagato 'bāvastadā smaryata iti vācyam /

children.text: pratiyogino māthurasya tadānīṃ kathañcidapi buddhāvanārohāt, abuddhisthe ca pratiyogini bhāve tadabhāvajñānasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: because the counterpart — the man from <s>Mathurā</s> — did not in any way enter his cognition at that time; and when the counterpart in the form of a positive entity has not been cognized, the cognition of its absence is not possible [then either].

children.text: evaṃ ca yatrāpīdānīmevānuparatendriyavyāpāreṇa saṃnihitadeśakālavarttyabhāvaḥ pratīyate tatrāpi yogyajñānānudayasyaiva kḷptasāmarthyasya kāraṇatvasaṃbhavānnendriyasya kāraṇatvaṃ kalpayituṃ śakyam /
children.translated_text: And thus, even where the absence of something present in a proximate place and time is cognized by one whose sensory activity has just now ceased, there too, since the established capacity of non-arising of fit cognition can serve as the cause, it is not possible to postulate the sense organ as the cause.

children.text: tasmānna pratyakṣo 'bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, absence is not perceptual.

children.text: nāpyanumeyaḥ, ajñātena tena kasyacilliṅgasya saṃbandhagrahaṇasaṃbhavāt* ////
children.translated_text: Nor is it inferable, since the apprehension of the relation of some inferential mark with that [absence], which is unknown, is not possible.

body.translated_text: And it [absence-cognition] is not perceptual, since its production is observed even in the absence of sensory activity. One who was present in the house in the early morning, when asked at midday, 'Did a certain person from <s>Mathurā</s>, wearing white garments, very tall, of ruddy complexion, come to this house in the early morning?' — he, at that very moment, through the non-arising of fit memory, ascertains that person's absence in the morning, without any sensory activity. Nor should it be said that the absence known in the morning is now remembered,

body.text: yadatra kaiściducyate- dṛśyasya sattādarśanavyāptā tena
body.translated_text: What some say here — that the existence of a visible [thing] is pervaded by its perception, and therefore

body.text:
vyāpakībhūtadarśananivṛttyā vyāpyasya dṛśyasya nivṛttiravasīyata iti tannirastam /
vyāpakanivṛttyā vyāpyanivṛttimanumimānenāvaśyaṃ dṛṣṭāntadharmiṣu nivṛttidvayamavagamya tato dṛśyanivṛttiranumātavyā, nivṛtteścābhāvātmikayai na pratyakṣeṇa grahaṇaṃ saṃbhavati, nivṛttyantareṇa tadanumāne tadapi nivṛttirūpatvānnivṛttyantareṇānumātavyam tadapi tathetyanavasthāpattiḥ /
ato 'vaśyaṃ kvacitpramāṇāntarabhūtayānupalabdhyābhāvaḥ pratyetavyaḥ /

children.text: pramiteca tasminpaścādbhavatvanumānam /
children.translated_text: And once that [absence] has been known, inference can follow afterward.

children.text: siddhaṃ tāvadabhāvasya pramāṇāntaratvaṃ śabdopamānārthāpattayastu nāśaṅganīyā eva /
children.translated_text: Thus, the status of absence as a separate means of knowledge is established. Verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>), analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), and presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>), however, are not even to be questioned [as valid means].

children.text: ataḥ siddhaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ pramāṇam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the sixth means of knowledge is established.

children.text: etāvantyeva ca pramāṇāni* ////
children.translated_text: And these are the only [six] means of knowledge.

body.translated_text: through the cessation of perception, which is the pervader, the cessation of the visible [thing], which is the pervaded, is ascertained — that is refuted. For one who infers the cessation of the pervaded through the cessation of the pervader must necessarily first apprehend both cessations in exemplary instances, and then infer the cessation of the visible [thing]. And since cessation, having the nature of absence, cannot be apprehended by perception, [and] to infer it through another cessation — that [cessation] too, being of the nature of cessation, would need to be inferred through yet another cessation — the consequence of infinite regress [follows]. Therefore, in some case, absence must necessarily be known through non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>), which is a separate means of knowledge.

body.text:
yattvadhikaṃ saṃbhavākhyaṃ pramāṇaṃ sahasrādisaṃkhyayāvayavabhūtaśatādisaṃkhyāvagatiḥ āḍhakapramāṇenāvayavakuḍavaparimāṇāvagatiḥ kaiścidiṣyate, tadavinābhāvanimittatvādanumānameva /
vaṭevaṭe vaiśravaṇaḥ ityādikaṃ caitihyaṃ pramāṇameva na bhavati nirṇayābhāvāt /
prāmāṇyepi vā'game 'ntargatatvānna pramāṇāntaram /
prātibhākhyamapi pramāṇaṃ kaiścidiṣṭaṃ śvaste bhrātāgantetyādikaṃ, tattu liṅgādyābhāsajaṃ, aniścāyakatvādevāpramāṇam /
ato yatkāśyapīyaiḥ pratibhāgamyamṛṣīṇāṃ dharmādharmatvamāśritam tadasāram /

children.text: lokaprasiddhirapi pratyakṣāntargataiveti na pramāṇāntaram /
children.translated_text: Common knowledge (<s>lokaprasiddhi</s>) too is included within perception, and so it is not a separate means of knowledge.

children.text: ataḥ ṣaḍeva pramāṇāni /
children.translated_text: Therefore, there are only six means of knowledge.

children.text: tathā ca bhagavadrāmāyaṇe rāma ṣaḍyuktayo loke yābhiḥ sarvo 'nudṛśyate iti /
children.translated_text: And thus in the blessed <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>: '<s>Rāma</s>, there are six means of reasoning in the world, by which everything is ascertained.'

children.text: ityābhāvavādaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [concludes] the discussion of [the doctrine of] absence.

body.translated_text: As for the additional [means] called <s>saṃbhava</s> (inclusion) — the cognition of a hundred and so forth, which are component parts of a thousand and other numbers, and the cognition of the measure of the component <s>kuḍava</s> from the <s>āḍhaka</s> measure — which some accept [as a separate means]: since it is occasioned by invariable concomitance, it is nothing but inference. And <s>aitihya</s> (tradition), such as 'in every banyan tree there is <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>' — that is not a valid means of knowledge at all, due to the absence of determinate cognition. Or, even if it were valid, since it is included within <s>āgama</s> (authoritative testimony), it is not a separate means. The [means] called <s>prātibha</s> (intuition), accepted by some — such as 'tomorrow my brother will come' — arises from semblances of inferential marks and the like, and since it does not produce certainty, it is not a valid means. Therefore, what the followers of <s>Kāśyapa</s> have maintained — that the <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> status [of things] apprehended by seers through intuition is authoritative — that is without substance.

body.text: citrādyaihikaphalacodanāsvākṣepaḥ //
body.translated_text: Objection regarding injunctions of <s>Citrā</s> and other [rites] having visible results.

body.text: lokaprasiddhasvataḥprāmāṇyadarśanena pratyakṣādīnāṃ tadantargatasyāpi ca śāstrasya svataḥprāmāṇyāt codanālakṣaṇor'tho dharmaḥ
body.translated_text: Having established the thesis that <s>dharma</s> is an object defined by Vedic injunction (<s>codanālakṣaṇa</s>), through the demonstration of the commonly known intrinsic validity [of cognition] and through the intrinsic validity of the scripture which is included within perception and the other [means of knowledge],

body.text: iti pratijñāter'the sādhite saṃprati animittaṃ vidyamānopalambhanatvāt ityanena citrādicodanānāmaihikaphalānāṃ pratyakṣādibhirasaṃvādena visaṃvādena ca prāmāṇyamākṣipyate, pūrvoktastu nanvatathābhūtaṃ ityākṣepaḥ paralokaphalasvargakāmādicodanāviṣaya iti viṣayabhedādapaunaruktyam* ////
body.translated_text: now, by [the argument] 'without ground, because of the apprehension of what is present,' the validity of injunctions such as <s>Citrā</s> and the like — which have visible results — is challenged on account of their non-conformity and conflict with perception and the other [means of knowledge]. The previously stated objection, however — 'but it is not so' — pertains to injunctions of otherworldly results such as '<s>svargakāma</s>' (one desiring heaven) and the like; and since the subject matter differs, there is no repetition.

body.text:
nanu ca nanvatathābhūtamapyarthaṃ brūyāccodaneti codanāmātraparigrahādaviśeṣeṇaivāsāvākṣepaḥ tathehāpi yadā tāvadasau vidyamānāsīt tadā phalaṃ na dattavatī /
yadā phalamutpadyate tadāsau nāsti kathamasatī phalaṃ dāsyatītyākṣepasya svargakāmacodanāsvapi tulyatvādaviśeṣatvamiti nāsti viṣayabhedaḥ /
ucyate- pūrvākṣepastāvatparalokaphalaviṣaya eva /
tatra hi pramāṇāntarāpekṣaḥ śabdo na svātantryeṇa pramāṇam /
na ca codanārthe pramāṇāntaramasti ato 'pramāṇaṃ codanetyayamākṣepaḥ, sa cāyaṃ paralokaphalaviṣaya eva bhavati /
paśukāmacodanāsu hi yadi tāvatkarmānantarameva paśvādīnyupalabhyante tato 'pekṣitamūlapramāṇalābhātsiddhyati codanāyāḥ prāmāṇyam /
atha nopalabhyate tataḥ pramāṇāntarabādhenaiva sukhaprāmāṇyamabhidhātuṃ śakyata iti kimākṣepasārūpyapratipādanavyasanena /

children.text: tasmātsa tāvatparalokaphalaviṣaya eva /
children.translated_text: Therefore, that [earlier objection] pertains only to otherworldly results.

children.text: ayaṃ tvaihikaphalaviṣaya /
children.translated_text: This [present objection], however, pertains to this-worldly results.

children.text: na hi pāralaukikasya phalasyānantarakālānupalabdhyā nirāsaḥ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: For the negation of an otherworldly result through its non-observation immediately [after the rite] is not possible,

children.text: na hi tenānantaraṃ bhavitavyam, janmāntarabhāvitatvāt* ////
children.translated_text: since it need not [arise] immediately, as it is destined to be experienced in another birth. ////

body.translated_text: Objection: 'But an injunction (<s>codanā</s>) might declare even something that is not truly so' — since this objection applies to injunction in general, it is indiscriminate. Similarly here too: when it [the injunction] was existing [at the time of the ritual], it did not give the result; when the result arises, it [the injunction] no longer exists — how can a non-existent [injunction] give the result? Since this objection applies equally to injunctions regarding the desire for heaven, there is no difference [between the two cases] — thus there is no distinction of subject matter. Reply: The earlier objection pertains only to results in the next world. For there, words depend on another means of knowledge and are not independently a means of knowledge. And there is no other means of knowledge for the object of injunction — hence 'the injunction is not a valid means of knowledge' is the objection, and this pertains only to otherworldly results. For in injunctions regarding the desire for cattle and the like, if cattle and the like are observed immediately after the ritual performance, then the validity of the injunction is established through obtaining the required foundational means of knowledge. But if they are not observed, then validity can easily be stated through the very sublation by another means of knowledge — so what is the point of laboriously demonstrating resemblance to the objection?

body.text:
nanu asatī kathaṃ phalaṃ dāsyatītīdaṃ tulyam /
neti brūmaḥ- apūrvadvāreṇa saṃbhavāt /
svargo hi svabhāvāddehāntarānubhavanīyatvādanantarāsaṃbhavitvena śāstrārthāvadhāraṇavelāyāmeva kālāntare niścīyata ityapūrvamantarbhāvyaiva tatra śāstrārtho 'vadhāryate, tacca cirasthāyīti kāraṇasyāvināśātsaṃbhavati kālāntare svargasyotpattiḥ /
paścādayastvanantaramapi saṃbhavantīti tatsādhanatvena codyamānānāṃ citrādīnāṃ śāstrārthāvadhāraṇasamaye 'pūrvapraṇāḍīsamāśrayaṇe kāraṇaṃ na kiñcidastīti svarūpeṇaiva phalasādhanatvaṃ śāstrārtho 'vadhāryate /
tathācānantarameva palena bavitavyam /
body.translated_text: Objection: 'How can a non-existent [cause] give the result?' — this [difficulty] is the same [in both cases]. We say: No — because it is possible through the medium of <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit). For heaven, by its very nature, since it is to be experienced in another body, and since it cannot arise immediately, is ascertained — at the very time of determining the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s> — as [arising] at a later time; thus the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s> is determined with <s>apūrva</s> included within it. And since that [<s>apūrva</s>] is long-lasting, because the cause is not destroyed, the arising of heaven at a later time is possible. But results such as cattle and the like, which can arise immediately — when injunctions regarding <s>citrā</s> and the like are examined as their means, at the time of determining the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s>, there is no reason to resort to the mediation of <s>apūrva</s>; hence the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s> is determined as [the rite's] being the direct means to the result. And thus the result must arise immediately.

body.text: kālāntare karmasvarūpasya vinaṣṭatvāt kāraṇatvābhāvāt, anantaraṃ ca phalamanupalabdhyaiva nirastamityaprāmāṇyaṃ citrādicodanānām //
body.translated_text: Since the essential nature of the ritual action is destroyed at a later time, causality is absent; and since the immediate result is negated by non-observation alone — therefore the injunctions regarding <s>citrā</s> and the like are invalid. //

body.text: citrādīcodanāsvākṣepaparihārau /
body.translated_text: The objection and its resolution regarding injunctions about <s>citrā</s> and the like:

body.text:
nacānuṣṭhānānantaraṃ phalānupalabdhyaiva śāstrārthe 'pūrvamantarbhāvayituṃ śakyate śāstrārthāvadhāraṇapūrvakaṃ hyanuṣṭhānaṃ nānuṣṭhānapūrvakaṃ śāstram, tasmādaihikānāmatrākṣepa iti yukto viṣayabhedaḥ /
viṣayabhedācca nyāyopi bhidyate /

children.text: paralokaphalāsu pramāṇāpekṣitatvāmākṣepanyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the case of otherworldly results, the mode of objection is through the need for [another] means of knowledge.

children.text: atratu pramāṇāntaravirodha iti nyāyabhedādapaunaruktyam /
children.translated_text: But here, [the objection is through] contradiction with another means of knowledge — thus, owing to the difference in the mode [of objection], there is no redundancy.

children.text: athavā pūrvoktaṃ svamate sūtrāṇi vyācakṣaṇo sūtritamevākṣepaṃ darśitavān /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, having previously explained the <s>sūtras</s> according to his own view, [the commentator] presented the objection as formulated by the <s>sūtra</s> itself.

children.text: idānīṃ tu vṛttikāramatena sūtreṇaivākṣepaḥ kriyate* ////
children.translated_text: But now, according to the view of the <s>Vṛttikāra</s> (the author of the commentary), the objection is made by the <s>sūtra</s> itself. ////

body.translated_text: And it is not possible to include <s>apūrva</s> in the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s> [only] after non-observation of the result following performance — for performance presupposes the determination of the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s>, not the other way around; the <s>śāstra</s> is not dependent on performance. Therefore, the [present] objection pertains to this-worldly [results] — thus the distinction of subject matter is justified.

body.text: tadiha /

children.text: citrādivākyāni pramāṇānyapramāṇāni veti vicāryate /
children.translated_text: It is examined whether the sentences regarding <s>citrā</s> and the like are valid means of knowledge or not.

children.text: tadarthaṃ ca kiṃ teṣāṃ pramāṇāntaravirodho 'sti na veti /
children.translated_text: And for that purpose — whether there is contradiction with another means of knowledge or not.

children.text: tatra phalānāmanantaramupalabdhavyānāmanupalambhādatatsādhanatvaṃ citrādīnāmavagamyate /
children.translated_text: There, since the results — which ought to be observed immediately — are not observed, the inefficacy of <s>citrā</s> and the like [as means to those results] is understood.

children.text: tadidaṃ pratyakṣāvisaṃvāde 'vaśyaṃbhāvini sati tadabhāvādaprāmāṇyam* ////
children.translated_text: This [amounts to]: when non-discordance with perception is necessarily expected, [the injunction's] invalidity [arises] from the absence of that [expected result]. ////

body.translated_text: Here then:

body.text:
kvacittu pratyakṣavirodhādapramāṇyaṃ sa eṣa yajñāyudhī yajamāno 'ñjasā svargaṃ yātīti yajñāyudhīti hi yajñāyudhasaṃyogāccharīramucyate, yajamānaśabdo 'pi hi kartṛvacanastasyaiva vācako nātmanaḥ, tasya sarvagatatvenābhimatasya kriyovirahiṇaḥ kartṛtvāyogādyajñāyudhasaṃyogābhāvācca, saṃyogābhiprāyaścāyaṃ yajñāyudhīti śabdaḥ pātracayanastutyarthatvāt, na svasvāmisaṃbandhābhiprāyaḥ /
prāgapi pātracayanāttatsaṃbhavāt śarīrasya ca pratyakṣaviruddhaṃ svargamanam /

children.text: na ca kālāntare 'pi saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: Nor is it possible at a later time,

children.text: yātīti vartamānāpadeśāt, bhasmībhūtasya ca kālāntare 'pi tadasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: because the [text] uses the present tense 'goes' (<s>yāti</s>), and because for what has been reduced to ashes, that [going to heaven] is impossible even at a later time.

children.text: na ca śarīravyatiriktaḥ kaścidātmāsti tasmādapramāṇam /
children.translated_text: And there is no self distinct from the body — therefore [the injunction] is invalid.

children.text: evamapauruṣeyasyāpyaprāmāṇye svargakāmacodanāyāmapi nāśvasituṃ yuktamityapramāṇyamevāyātam* ////
children.translated_text: Thus, if the invalidity of even the authorless [Veda] is [established], then one should not trust the injunction regarding the desire for heaven either — and so invalidity is the conclusion. ////

body.translated_text: But in some cases, invalidity arises from direct contradiction with perception — [for example,] 'This very sacrificer, armed with sacrificial implements, goes directly to heaven.' For <s>yajñāyudhī</s> (armed with sacrificial implements) refers to the body, due to its conjunction with the sacrificial implements; and the word <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) too, being an agent-denoting word, denotes that [body] alone, not the self. And [the body is observed to be cremated, so]

children.text: evaṃ pratyakṣānupalabdhivirodhena pratyakṣavirodhena cākṣipte prāmāṇye virodhaparihāramupekṣyaiva kāraṇadoṣanirākaraṇena pūrvoktameva svataḥprāmāṇyaṃ svapakṣasādhanatvena siddhāntavādī darśayati- autpattikastu śabdasyārthena saṃbandhastasya jñānamupadeśa iti /
children.translated_text: Thus, when validity has been challenged through contradiction with non-observation by perception and through direct contradiction with perception, the <s>Siddhāntavādin</s> (proponent of the established doctrine), setting aside the resolution of the contradiction, demonstrates the previously stated intrinsic validity (<s>svataḥprāmāṇya</s>) as the means of establishing his own position — through the removal of defects in the cause [of cognition].

children.text: pūrvaṃ hi pratyakṣādīnāṃ svataḥprāmāṇyasya lokasiddhātvāttadantargatatvācca śāstramapi puruṣānupraveśābhāvātpuruṣāśrayatvācca śabdadoṣasyāduṣṭemeva śāstramataḥ pramāṇamityuktam /
children.translated_text: For previously, since the intrinsic validity of perception and the like is well-established in common experience, and since <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) is included within that [class of valid cognitions], and since there is no interference by any person [in authorless scripture], and since verbal defect — which depends on a person — does not exist in unfaulty scripture, therefore scripture is a valid means of knowledge — so it was stated.

children.text: iti citrākṣepavādaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the discussion of the <s>citrā</s>-objection. //

body.text: śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandhākṣepaḥ /
body.translated_text: The objection regarding the relation between word and meaning:

body.text:
evaṃ saṃbandhanityatayāprāmāṇyaṃ nirākṛtya svataḥprāmāṇye sthāpite, paraḥ punarāha- syādetat naiva śabdasyārthenāsti saṃbandhaḥ kuto 'sya pauruṣeyatāpauruṣeyatāveti /
tathāhi na tāvatsaṃyogo 'sti tadbhāve hi kṣurādiśabdoccāraṇe mukhyasya pāṭanāpi syāt /

children.text: na ca kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ, dvayorapi nityatvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor is there a cause-effect relation, since both are eternal.

children.text: nanu varṇasphoṭajātyādivikalpena vyaktyākṛtisaṃbandhādivikalpena ca bāhyayoḥ śabdārthayordurnirūpatvādgakārādyākāraṃ vijñānameva śabdaḥ, tajjanitaṃ ca gavādyākāravijñānamevārthaṃ iti kāryakāraṇatvameva śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: Since the external word and meaning are difficult to determine — due to the variety of alternatives such as phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>), <s>sphoṭa</s> (meaning-bearing whole), universal (<s>jāti</s>), and the like [for word], and individual (<s>vyakti</s>), form (<s>ākṛti</s>), relation (<s>saṃbandha</s>), and the like [for meaning] — the word is simply the cognition having the form of 'g' and the like, and the meaning is simply the cognition having the form of cow and the like generated by it — thus there is indeed a cause-effect relation.

children.text: naivam /
children.translated_text: Not so.

children.text: nirālambanajñānānutpatteḥ, saṃbandhāntaraṃ tu nāśaṅganīyameva* ////
children.translated_text: Because cognition without a basis (<s>nirālambana</s>) does not arise. And another relation need not even be suspected. ////

body.translated_text: Thus, having refuted invalidity through the eternality of the relation [between word and meaning], and having established intrinsic validity, the opponent again says: 'Granted — but the word has no relation with the meaning at all; whence then [the question of] its being of human or non-human origin?' For there is no conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) [between word and meaning], since they are of different nature.

body.text: pratyāyyapratyāyakatvaṃ saṃbandha iti
body.translated_text: [If one says] 'the relation is that of what-is-to-be-conveyed and what-conveys (<s>pratyāyyapratyāyakatva</s>)' —

body.text:
cet na /
asati saṃbandhe pratyāyakatvāsaṃbhavāt /
kena saṃbandhena śabdor'thaṃ pratyāyayatītyetadeva hi nirūpyate /
tatra pratyāyakatvādeva pratyāyakatvamityātmāśrayadoṣāpattiḥ, tasmānnāsti saṃbandhaḥ /
asati ca saṃbandhe vastvantarasya vastvantarabodhakatvāsaṃbhavādanirūpitahetuviśeṣaṃ svapnajñānavadyādṛcchikaṃ śabdārthajñānaṃ na pramāṇaṃ bhavitumarhati /
laukikastu vyavahāro 'satyapi śabdaprāmāṇye
body.translated_text: No. Because in the absence of a relation, the capacity to convey is impossible. 'By what relation does the word convey the meaning?' — this is precisely what is being investigated. To say 'by the very capacity to convey' [would mean that] the capacity to convey [depends on] the capacity to convey — and thus the fault of self-dependence (<s>ātmāśraya</s>) would arise. Therefore, there is no relation [on this account].

children.text: pramāṇāntaravaśātkathañcitsaṃgacchetāpi /
children.translated_text: [The relation] might somehow be established through another means of knowledge.

children.text: vaidikastu vyavahāraḥ śabdaikaśaraṇatvādanādartavyaḥ syānnirmūlatvāt* ////
children.translated_text: But Vedic usage, since it depends solely on words [and has no other support], would have to be disregarded, being without foundation. ////

children.text: syādevaṃ yadyasaṃbandhaḥ śabdārthayoḥ, asti tu saṃbandhaḥ pratyāyya ityayameva saṃbandho bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: It would be so if the word had no relation with the meaning; but there is a relation — 'what-is-to-be-conveyed' will itself be the relation.

children.text: yaccendriyaliṅgādivatsaṃnikarṣavyāptyādisaṃbandhānapekṣamarthapratipādanam idamevābhidhānamityucyate, tadeva ca saṃjñāsaṃjñitvaṃ, tenocyate saṃjñāsaṃjñilakṣaṇaḥ saṃbandha iti* ////
children.translated_text: That capacity to convey meaning which — unlike sense-contact, pervasion, and the like [required for] sense-organs and inferential marks — does not depend on relations such as proximity, pervasion, and the like — this alone is called <s>abhidhāna</s> (denotation). And that is the same as the relation of name and named (<s>saṃjñāsaṃjñitva</s>). Hence it is said: 'The relation is characterized as that of name and named.' ////

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ śabdasyārthapratipādane pramāṇam, śabdānantaramarthapratipattireva /

children.text: nanviyamabhiprāyānumānadvāreṇaivopapannā, neti brūmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: This [understanding] is explained through the inference of the speaker's intention. We say: No.

children.text: arthābhiprāyaśūnyenāpi svāpādyavasthāyāṃ paravaśaprayuktairapi śabdairarthapratipattidarśanāt /
children.translated_text: Because even for one devoid of any intention regarding the meaning — in a state of sleep and the like — understanding of meaning is observed from words uttered by another under external compulsion.

children.text: tathā puruṣāntarakṛtamapauruṣeyaṃ vā vedavākyamanarthajñairapi prayujyamānaṃ vyutpannānāmarthabuddhiṃ janayatyeva, tasmāt pratyāyakaḥ śabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, a Vedic sentence, whether composed by another person or authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>), when uttered even by those ignorant of its meaning, generates understanding of meaning in those who are learned. Therefore, the word is a conveyor [of meaning].

children.text: kimiti tarhi prathamaśravaṇe na pratyāyayati, sahakārivirahātsaṃjñātvagrahaṇamapi śabdasyārthe pratyayato 'ṅgaṃ netrasyevālokaḥ, tena yaḥ puruṣāntarebhyo ayaṃ puruṣāntarebhyo ayaṃ śabdo 'sya saṃjñeti jñātavān tasyaiva pratyāyayati nānyasyeti na doṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: Then why does it not convey [meaning] at the first hearing? Because of the absence of the auxiliary condition — the apprehension of the conventional designation (<s>saṃjñātva</s>) is also an auxiliary to the cognition [of meaning] from words, like light for the eye. Therefore, one who, from other persons, [learns that] 'this word is the name of this [thing]' —

body.translated_text: What, then, is the means of knowledge for the word's capacity to convey meaning? It is precisely the understanding of the meaning immediately upon [hearing] the word.

body.text: śabdārthasaṃbandhānityatve ākṣepaḥ /
body.translated_text: The objection regarding the non-eternality of the word-meaning relation:

children.text: nanvemastu nāma saṃbandhaḥ, sa tu pauruṣeya iti tvaduktyaivāpannam /
children.translated_text: Objection: Let there be a relation; but it is of human origin — this follows from your own statement.

children.text: tathāhi na hi śabdasyārthena saṃyogagādātmyādisaṃbandhaḥ kintu pratyāyakatvam /
children.translated_text: For the word has no relation with the meaning such as conjunction, identity, and the like; rather, [the relation] is the capacity to convey.

children.text: tacca puruṣādhīnamityuktam, ato devadattādiśabdasyeva asyārthasyeyaṃ saṃjñetyevaṃ saṃbandhe kṛte paścācchabdasyārthapratipādanamiti siddhaṃ pauruṣeyatvam* ////
children.translated_text: And that has been said to depend on a person. Therefore, just as with the word <s>Devadatta</s> and the like — 'this name is the designation of this meaning' — after the relation has been established [by convention], the word conveys the meaning. Thus the human origin [of the relation] is established. ////

children.text: iti saṃbandhākṣepaḥ pūrvākṣiptaṃ saṃbandhanityatvamasamādhāyedānīṃ atha gaurityatra kaḥ śabdaḥ iti kayā saṃgatyā kena vā prayojanena śabdasvarūpaṃ nirūpyate, saṃgatistāvatprāsaṅgīkā saṃbandhaprastāvāt saṃbandhinorapi śabdārthayoḥ prastutatvātsvarūpaṃ nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the objection regarding the relation. Without having resolved the previously raised [question of] the eternality of the relation, now [the author asks] 'What then is the word in <s>gau</s> (cow)?' — by what connection and for what purpose is the nature of the word investigated? The connection is incidental (<s>prāsaṅgikā</s>), arising from the occasion of [discussing] the relation.

children.text: prayojanamapi tadavayavāśritānāmūhādīnāṃ satyatvaṃ, niravayave hi vākye pade vā vācake 'vayavānāṃ mṛṣātvāt tadāśritānyapi kāryāṇi mṛṣā bhaveyuḥ* ////
children.translated_text: And the purpose is to establish the reality of <s>ūha</s> (adaptation) and the like, which depend on the parts [of words]. For if the word or sentence that denotes were partless, then since the parts would be unreal, the operations depending on them too would be unreal. ////

children.text: kiñca saṃbanghasiddhyarthamavaśyaṃ varṇānāṃ vācakatvaṃ samarthanīyam, anyathā hi teṣāṃ saṃgatyābhāvādvācakabhāvo nirādhāratvānna syānnatarāṃ nityatvamiti tatsiddhyarthaṃ vācakatvaṃ samarthayituṃ śabdasvarūpaṃ nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: Moreover, in order to establish the relation [between word and meaning], it is necessary to demonstrate that the phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) have denotative capacity. For otherwise, since they would have no connection [with meaning], their denotative status would be baseless and could not exist — still less their eternality. Therefore, in order to establish that [eternality], the denotative capacity is to be demonstrated, and [for that] the nature of the word [must be investigated].

children.text: ki gaurityatra varṇā eva śabdaḥ, uta tebhyor'thāntaramityetatprādhānyena nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: The primary investigation is this: In <s>gau</s>, are the phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) alone the word, or is it something distinct from them?

children.text: varṇāvayava-gatva-gośabdāvayavi-jātinirākaraṇaṃ tu prāsaṅgikam /
children.translated_text: The refutation of [the theories of] a whole (<s>avayavin</s>) composed of phonemes, the universal of 'cowhood' (<s>gatva</s>), the word <s>go</s> (cow) as a composite whole, and the universal [of words] — these are incidental.

children.text: varṇā eva śabda ityavadhāraṇasamarthanārtham* ////
children.translated_text: [They serve] the purpose of establishing the definitive [claim] that phonemes alone are the word. ////

body.text:
tatra varṇānāmapi pudgalākhyānavayavānārhatāḥ saṃgirante tattvavayavānupalambhādayuktam /
pratyakṣeṇa tāvadavayavā nopalabhyante, varṇeṣu sākalyavaikalyagrahaṇābhāvāt /
nānumānena, taiḥ saha kasyacilliṅgasya saṃbandhāgrahaṇāt /

children.text: na ca sāmānyato dṛṣṭam, nahi yadyadvastu tasya tasyāvaśyamavayavairbhavitavyam, paramāṇūnāṃ niravayavatvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor is there a general inference (<s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>), for it is not the case that whatever entity exists must necessarily have parts — since atoms (<s>paramāṇus</s>) are partless.

children.text: te 'pi sāvayavā iti cet, tadavayavā api tathā syustataḥ paramapi tathetyekasyaiva māṣāvayavino 'nantāvayavitvaṃ syāt, tataścaikenaiva māṣeṇa tilena vā sarvaṃ jagadvyāpyeta, anantairavayavairmūrtairanyonyasyāvarakāśamaprayacchadbhiranantadeśavyāpteḥ /
children.translated_text: [If one says] 'they too have parts' — then their parts too would be the same, and so on further — thus even a single bean-part would have infinite parts. And consequently, a single bean or sesame seed would pervade the entire universe, since infinite material parts

children.text: tasmānniravayavāḥ paramāṇavo varṇāśca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, atoms and phonemes are partless.

children.text: tathā gatvajātirautvajātiśca niṣprāmāṇikaiva* ////
children.translated_text: Similarly, the universal of 'going' (<s>gatvajāti</s>) and the universal of sound (<s>autvajāti</s>) are without any evidential support. ////

body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>Ārhaṭas</s> (Jains), who assert that even phonemes have parts called <s>pudgalas</s> (material particles) — that is unjustified, since parts are not observed in phonemes. For parts are not perceived by perception, since there is no apprehension of completeness or incompleteness in phonemes. Nor by inference, since [there is no observed] relation of any [effect] with them.

body.text:
nanu drutavilambitamadhyeṣūdāttānudāttasvariteṣu sānunāsikaniranunāsikayorhrasvadīrghapluteṣu ca pratyabhijñāyamānā jātiḥ kathaṃ nāstīti śakyate 'bhidhātum /
satyam /
pratyabhijñā, sātu pratyabhijñā, sātu vyaktekatvādevopapannā /
drutādibhedābhāsastu drutādyavasthābhedālambano na vyaktibhedamāpādayitumalaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Objection: In fast, slow, and medium [pronunciations]; in <s>udātta</s> (acute), <s>anudātta</s> (grave), and <s>svarita</s> (circumflex) [accents]; in nasalized and non-nasalized [forms]; and in short, long, and protracted [vowels] — the universal (<s>jāti</s>) being recognized [as the same throughout] — how can it be said not to exist? True, there is recognition; but that recognition —

body.text: gatvādijātinirākaraṇam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the universal of 'going' (<s>gatvajāti</s>) and the like:

body.text:
bhedābhedāvabhāso 'pi dvedhā bhavati /
kvacidbhedo dharmiviṣayo yathā śābaleyādiṣvayaṃ gaurayaṃ
body.translated_text: The appearance of difference-and-non-difference too is of two kinds. Sometimes the difference pertains to the substratum (dharmin), as in [the case of] Śābaleya and the like — 'this is a cow, that is a cow,'

children.text: gaurayamiti jāterātmalābhaḥ /
children.translated_text: where the universal (jāti) gains its identity [through different substrata].

children.text: kvacittu bhedābhāvabhāso dharmādabhedāvabhāsaśca dharmiṇamālambate-ekasminneva devadatte yuvāyaṃ vṛddho 'yaṃ kṛśo 'yamiti na tatra jātiraṅgīkriyate /
children.translated_text: But sometimes the appearance of non-difference from a property and the appearance of non-difference pertain to the substratum — in one and the same <s>Devadatta</s>, 'he is young, he is old, he is thin' — and there no universal is admitted.

children.text: tadiha drutādiṣu dharmiviṣayo 'bhedo dharmiviṣayastu bhedaḥ tathāhi īdṛśo 'trāvabhāsaḥ anenāyamakāro drutamuccārito 'nena vilambitamiti na tu ayamakāro druto 'yaṃ tu vilambita iti yena dharmibhedo jātiścāṅgīkriyetām* ////
children.translated_text: Here then, in rapid [pronunciation] and the like, the non-difference pertains to the substratum and the difference pertains to the property. For the appearance here is of this kind: 'this letter a was pronounced rapidly by this [speaker], and slowly by that one' — not 'this letter a is rapid, and that one is slow,' which would require accepting substratum-difference and a universal.

body.text: nanu kārśyādīnāṃ kramavartitvādekasmindevadatte yuktaḥ samāveśaḥ, anunāsikādīnāntu dharmāṇāṃ yugapadanekavaktruccārite varṇe samavetānāṃ kathamekavarṇaviṣayatvam /

children.text: na hi viruddhadharmāneko dharmī yugapadbibharti /
children.translated_text: For a single substratum does not bear contradictory properties simultaneously.

children.text: satyam /
children.translated_text: True.

children.text: natvete paramārthato varṇadharmā dhvanidharmāstvete varṇe kevalamābhāsante, yathālpe mahati ca darpaṇe yugapaddṛśyamāne mukhe 'lpatvaṃ mahatvaṃ ceti /
children.translated_text: But these are not in reality properties of the phoneme; they are properties of the sound-tokens (<s>dhvani</s>) which merely appear in the phoneme — just as when a face is seen simultaneously in a small and a large mirror, smallness and largeness [appear].

children.text: tasmādvarṇasya vyaktyekatve 'pi na virodha ityaprāmāṇikī gatvādijātiḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though the phoneme is a single individual, there is no contradiction — hence the universal of 'cow-hood' (<s>gatva</s>) and the like is unwarranted by evidence.

body.translated_text: Objection: since qualities like thinness and the like occur successively, their co-existence in one <s>Devadatta</s> is proper. But as for properties like nasality and the like, which are simultaneously present in a phoneme pronounced by multiple speakers at once — how can they pertain to a single phoneme?

body.text: evaṃ gośabdāvayavyapi
body.translated_text: Similarly, the composite word-whole (<s>avayavin</s>) of the word 'go' (cow) too [does not exist],

children.text: gakārādīnāmayaugapadyātsarvagatatvāccāvayavyārambhāsāmarthyāt /
children.translated_text: because the letters 'g' and the like do not occur simultaneously, because they are omnipresent, and because of the incapacity to produce a composite whole from parts.

children.text: sarvatra hi kāraṇaparimāṇādadhikaṃ kāryaparimāṇam tantupaṭayoriva na ca vibhubhyo varṇebhyaḥ parimāṇādhikyaṃ kasyacidbhavati, ato nāsyavayavī /
children.translated_text: For everywhere, the magnitude of the effect is greater than the magnitude of the cause, as in the case of threads and cloth. But nothing has a greater magnitude than the omnipresent phonemes. Therefore, there is no composite whole [of the word].

children.text: tadabhāve ca tadādhāraṃ gośabdatvaṃ dūrāpāstam /
children.translated_text: And in the absence of that, 'cow-word-hood' (<s>gośabdatva</s>) which depends on it is thoroughly rejected.

children.text: tasmādvarṇa eva śabdaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, the phoneme alone is the word.

children.text: āha- gṛhṇīma etat- avayavāvayavigadvādikaṃ nāstīti /
children.translated_text: The [opponent] says: we accept this — that the composite-whole-and-parts doctrine and the like does not hold.

children.text: natu varṇā eva śabdā iti /
children.translated_text: But not that phonemes alone are words.

children.text: arthapratyayānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because cognition of meaning would be inexplicable.

children.text: tathāhi - nahyekākṣaravijñānādarthadhīrupajāyate //
children.translated_text: For cognition of meaning does not arise from the knowledge of a single syllable,

body.text: vācaśca kramavartitvātsāhityaṃ nāvakalpate //
body.translated_text: and since speech occurs successively, simultaneity is not possible.

body.text: ucyate- yathāgneyādikarmāṇi kramavartini santyapi //
body.translated_text: Reply: just as the <s>Āgneya</s> and other ritual acts, though occurring successively,

body.text: saṃhatya kurvate kāryamekaṃ varṇāstathaiva naḥ //
body.translated_text: produce a single effect collectively — so too phonemes, according to us.

body.text: varṇānāmarthapratyāyakatvam /
body.translated_text: The capacity of phonemes to convey meaning.
