children.text: nanu kramavartināmapyutpattyapūrvavaśena yuktaṃ sāhityam, varṇānāṃ tu katham /
children.translated_text: Objection: for successive [ritual acts], simultaneity is proper through the medium of <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency); but how for phonemes?

children.text: teṣāmapi saṃskāreṇa bhaviṣyati tatsadbhāve kiṃ pramāṇam, yadevāgneyādiṣu /
children.translated_text: For those too, it will be through <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression). What is the evidence for its existence? The very same as for <s>Āgneya</s> and other [rituals].

children.text: yathāhi teṣāṃ śāstreṇa saṃhatyakāritāvagamātsvarūpataśca tadasaṃbhavādapūrvaṃ dvāraṃ kalpyate, tathā varṇānāmapyekaikaśo 'bhidhānādarśanātsakaloccāraṇe cāvagamātsaṃhatyakāritve niścite svarūpeṇāsaṃbhavātsaṃskārakalpanaṃ yuktameva, tadvadeva caikakartṛtvaṃ kramaviśeṣaścādriyate viparyayeṇārthābhidhānādarśanāt //
children.translated_text: For just as, since the <s>śāstra</s> teaches their collective efficacy and since this is impossible through their own nature, <s>apūrva</s> is postulated as the medium — so too for phonemes, since individual pronunciation is not seen to denote [meaning], and since comprehension occurs upon complete utterance, collective efficacy being established, and this being impossible through their own nature, the postulation of <s>saṃskāra</s> is entirely appropriate. And similarly, single authorship and a specific order are required, since meaning is not seen to be conveyed in reverse order.

body.text: sphoṭavādakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the <s>sphoṭa</s> (meaning-bearing word-essence) doctrine.

body.text:
nanvevaṃ prativarṇaṃ saṃskārakalpanādekakalpanā syāt tadvaramekameva śabdatvaṃ kalpitam /
naivam /
dṛśyādarśanena nirastavat /

children.text: śabdo hi pratyakṣagrāhyo 'bhyupagamyate, na ca pratyakṣeṇa kiñcitprakāśate /
children.translated_text: For the <s>sphoṭa</s> is accepted as perceptible, yet nothing is perceived [beyond the phonemes].

children.text: tena nāstītyavagacchāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore we conclude it does not exist.

children.text: tvayāpi hi śabdatvaṃ kalpayitvā punaḥ saṃskārakalpanāvaśyaṃ kartavyā /
children.translated_text: For even you, having postulated <s>sphoṭa</s>, must still postulate <s>saṃskāra</s>.

children.text: dhvanayo hi na pratyekaṃ sphoṭamabhivyañjati, sāhityaṃ ca kramavartināṃ saṃskāradvārameveti tulyaṃ tatkalpanam* ////
children.translated_text: For the sound-tokens do not individually manifest the <s>sphoṭa</s>, and the simultaneity of successive [tokens] is only through the medium of <s>saṃskāra</s> — so the postulation is equal.

body.translated_text: Objection: since the postulation of a <s>saṃskāra</s> for each phoneme would be required, a single postulation would be preferable — so better to postulate a single <s>sphoṭa</s> (word-essence). [Reply:] Not so — it is refuted by seeing-and-not-seeing [i.e., non-perception of a competent entity].

children.text: syānmatam /
children.translated_text: One might think:

children.text: pratyekameva nādāḥ śabdamabhivyañjanti, nacaivamuttaranādavaiyarthyam, pūrve hi nādāḥ śabdasphuṭamabhivyañjanti uttarottare sphuṭaṃ sphuṭataraṃ ca vyañjantīti nottareṣāmānarthakyam /
children.translated_text: the sound-tokens individually manifest the word [<s>sphoṭa</s>], and the later tokens are not purposeless — for the earlier tokens manifest the word indistinctly, while each succeeding one manifests it more and more distinctly, so the later ones are not purposeless.

children.text: yadyevaṃ tato ya evottare nādāḥ sphuṭābhivyaktisamarthāstaireva bhavitavyamalaṃ pūrveḥ* ////
children.translated_text: If so, then the later tokens alone, which are capable of distinct manifestation, should suffice — the earlier ones are unnecessary.

children.text: nanu na kaścidapi nādaḥ svato 'sya sphuṭābhivyaktiṃ karoti kintu sarve te pratyekaṃ vyañjakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: no single token by itself produces distinct manifestation; rather, all of them are individually manifestors.

children.text: sa tu na drāgeva sphuṭamavabhāsate prathamamasphuṭāvabhāsitaḥ san punaḥ punaḥ śrūyamāṇaḥ sphuṭaḥ bhavati, tadyathā dūrādavasthitaḥ sahakāraḥ prathamaṃ hastipalālakūṭādisādhāraṇarūpeṇa pratibhātaḥ punarālocyamāno vṛkṣātmanā prakāśate punaḥsahakārātmanā sphaṭo bhavati tadvadeva draṣṭavyam* ////
children.translated_text: But it does not become distinctly manifest immediately — having been first manifested indistinctly, when heard again and again it becomes distinct. Just as a mango tree seen from afar first appears in the general form common to an elephant, a haystack, and the like; upon looking again, it is perceived as a tree; then it becomes distinctly [perceived] as a mango tree — so too should this be understood.

children.text: yadyevaṃ ya eva te pūrvai nādāstairevābhyasyamānairīdṛśī sphuṭābhivyaktiḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: If so, then the same earlier tokens, when repeated, would produce such distinct manifestation.

children.text: uttarairvā kevalairabhyasyamānaiḥ, tatra vijātīyanādāśrayaṇamanarthakam* ////
children.translated_text: Or the later ones alone, when repeated — and in that case, the resort to heterogeneous tokens is pointless.

body.text: tathā
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: pratyekaṃ hi vyañjakatve satyuttarairasphuṭābhivyaktiḥ pūrvaiśca sphuṭābhivyaktiḥ syāditi vyutkrameṇāpyuccāraṇaṃ syāt, ato 'pekṣitakramaviśeṣānekavijātīyanādasamuccayāśrayaṇādavaśyaṃ pūrvanādāhitasaṃskārasahitāntimanādābhivyaṅgyaḥ sphoṭa ityavaśyāṅgīkartavyamiti tulyā saṃskārakalpanā /
children.translated_text: if each [token] individually has manifesting capacity, then later [tokens] would produce indistinct manifestation and earlier ones distinct manifestation — and so pronunciation even in reverse order should work. Therefore, since [the manifestation] necessarily depends on a specific order and the collection of many heterogeneous tokens, the <s>sphoṭa</s> must be manifested by the last token assisted by <s>saṃskāras</s> deposited by prior tokens — and so the postulation of <s>saṃskāra</s> is equal [on both views].

children.text: yadvā tavaiveyaṃ saṃskārāntakalpanā, matpakṣe tu smṛtihetubhireva saṃskāraiḥ siddhyatyarthāvagatiriti na saṃskārāntaraṃ kalpayitavyama* ////
children.translated_text: Alternatively, this additional postulation of <s>saṃskāra</s> is yours alone; in our view, the comprehension of meaning is accomplished by the very <s>saṃskāras</s> that are causes of memory, so no additional <s>saṃskāra</s> need be postulated.

body.text:
nanu mamāpi ta eva bhaviṣyanti /
na /

children.text: teṣāṃ smṛteranyatrāvyāpārāt /
children.translated_text: because those [saṃskāras] do not operate for anything other than memory.

children.text: matpakṣe tu smṛtireva janayantor'thapratipattiṃ saṃskārā janayanti /
children.translated_text: But in our view, the <s>saṃskāras</s> produce the comprehension of meaning precisely by producing memory.

children.text: tathāhi pratyekavarṇānubhavabhāvitaiḥ saṃskāraiḥ saṃhatya sarvavarṇagocaraikā smṛtirjanyate /
children.translated_text: For thus: through <s>saṃskāras</s> conditioned by the experience of each individual phoneme, a single memory encompassing all the phonemes collectively is generated.

children.text: tasyāṃ ca yugapadavabhāsamānā varṇā vinaiva saṃskārāntareṇa saṃhatyārthapratyayaṃ janayanti* ////
children.translated_text: And in that [memory], the phonemes appearing simultaneously, without any additional <s>saṃskāra</s>, collectively produce the cognition of meaning.

body.translated_text: Objection: those same [saṃskāras] will serve in my view too. Reply: no,

body.text: tvatpakṣe tu naivaṃ saṃbhavati, tathāhi nādā hi na jñāyamānatayā sphoṭaṃ vyañjayanti, na ca yugapatsattāsti kramavartitvāt, ataḥ saṃskāradvārameva sāhityamityavarjanīyaṃ saṃskārāntarakalpanam* ////
body.translated_text: But in your view, this is not possible. For the sound-tokens do not manifest the <s>sphoṭa</s> by being cognized [simultaneously]; nor do they have simultaneous existence, since they occur successively. Therefore, their simultaneity is only through the medium of <s>saṃskāra</s> — so the postulation of an additional <s>saṃskāra</s> is unavoidable.

body.text:
atha matam /
satyaṃ na smṛtihetubhiḥ sphoṭābhivyaktiḥ, ye tu varṇopalabdhihetavo nādajanyāḥ śrotragatāḥ saṃskārāstaireva varṇānāmiva sphoṭābhivyaktirbhaviṣyati kiṃ saṃskārāntarakalpanayeti /
tadayuktam /

children.text: teṣāṃ kṣaṇikatvāt /
children.translated_text: because they are momentary.

children.text: nahyadyavarṇopalabdhihetuḥ saṃskāro 'ntyavarṇaśravaṇavelāyāmavatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: For the <s>saṃskāra</s> that is the cause of perception of the first phoneme does not persist at the time of hearing the last phoneme.

children.text: yadyavatiṣṭhate tato visarjanīyaśravaṇavelāyāmapi gakāraśravaṇamanuvarteta, tasmātkṣaṇabhaṅginaste, ato na teṣāṃ saṃhatya sphoṭābhivyañjakatvaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: If it did persist, then even at the time of hearing the <s>visarjanīya</s> (final aspiration), the hearing of the 'g' sound would continue. Therefore, they are destroyed in an instant; hence they cannot collectively manifest the <s>sphoṭa</s>.

children.text: pratyekābhivyaktau cottarottareṣāmanarthakatvamityuktam* ////
children.translated_text: And the purposelessness of each successive [token] in individual manifestation has been stated.

body.translated_text: If it is held: true, the <s>sphoṭa</s> is not manifested by the memory-causing [saṃskāras]; but those <s>saṃskāras</s> residing in the ear, produced by the sound-tokens, which are causes of phoneme-perception — by those very ones the manifestation of the <s>sphoṭa</s> will occur, just as of the phonemes. Why postulate additional <s>saṃskāras</s>? [Reply:] That is not right,

body.text: athavā dhvaniyoga eva śrotrasaṃskāro nānyaḥ, tasya ca vispaṣṭameva bhaṅgukatvamityuktam* ////
body.translated_text: Alternatively, the contact of the sound-token itself is the <s>saṃskāra</s> in the ear, and nothing else; and its fragility is quite evident — as has been stated.

children.text: athavā dhvanisaṃyoga eva śrotrasaṃskāro nānyaḥ, tasya ca vispaṣṭameva bhaṅguratvaṃ gatvaratvādghavanīnām /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the conjunction of the sound-token itself is the <s>saṃskāra</s> in the ear, and nothing else; and its fragility is quite evident, due to the transient nature of sound-tokens.

children.text: tasmādanye sthāyinaḥ saṃskārāḥ kalpyāḥ, tathā varṇātiriktaḥ śabdaḥ kalpya iti bahvapramāṇakamāpannam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, other enduring <s>saṃskāras</s> must be postulated; and similarly, a word distinct from phonemes must be postulated — thus much that is without evidence is incurred.

children.text: matpakṣe tu dṛḍhasmṛtiviparivartināṃ varṇānāṃ vācakatvānna kiñcidūnam* ////
children.translated_text: But in our view, since the phonemes that recur in firm memory are the denoters, nothing is lacking.

body.text: nanu yugapatsmaryamāṇānāṃ vācakatve vyutkrameṇāpyuccāritā varṇā vācakāḥ syuḥ, na, tatkramasyāpyaṅgatvāt /

children.text: kaḥ punaḥ kramo 'ṅgam, na hi varṇānāṃ vibhūnāṃ nityānāṃ ca svarūpataḥ kramavattvam /
children.translated_text: But what order is a component? For phonemes, being omnipresent and eternal, do not inherently have sequentiality.

children.text: na pratītikramaḥ, tasyāḥ smṛtirūpāyā ekatvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor is it the sequence of cognitions, since the [memory-]cognition is single.

children.text: evaṃ tarhi dhvanikramo yo varmeṣvāropitaḥ pratibhāsate so 'ṅgamityadoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then let the sequence of the sound-tokens (<s>dhvani</s>), which is superimposed on the phonemes and appears [as their sequence], be the component — and there is no fault in this.

children.text: tasmādvyañjakānāṃ dhvanīnāṃ krameṇa vyaṅgyeṣu varṇeṣu samāropitena tadvantaḥ smaryamāṇā varṇā vācakāḥ nānyaḥ śabdo 'stīti siddham //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the phonemes, being remembered as possessing [a specific] order superimposed by the sequence of the manifesting sound-tokens, are the denoters — there is no other entity called 'word.' This is established.

body.translated_text: Objection: if phonemes remembered simultaneously are the denoters, then phonemes uttered even in reverse order would be denoters. [Reply:] No, because that [specific] order too is a necessary component.

body.text: iti sphoṭavādaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the discussion of the <s>sphoṭa</s> doctrine.

body.text: padārthanirūpaṇopakramaḥ /
body.translated_text: Commencement of the investigation of the referent of words (<s>padārtha</s>).

children.text: atha gaurityasya śabdasya kor'thaḥ iti vācyanirūpaṇopakramavyājenākṛtisadbhāvaṃ pratipādayati saṃbandhanityatvasiddhaye /
children.translated_text: Now, under the pretext of investigating the referent — 'what is the meaning of the word go (cow)?' — the existence of the <s>ākṛti</s> (form/universal) is established, for the purpose of proving the eternality of the [word-meaning] relation.

children.text: nahyasatyāmākṛto vyaktibhiḥ śabdasyāpauruṣeyaḥ saṃbandhaḥ tāsāmanityatvāt, upalakṣaṇasyāpi nityasyābhāvādākṛtyabhāve, tasmādākṛtirasti nāstīti vicāryate /
children.translated_text: For without <s>ākṛti</s>, the word cannot have a non-human-made (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) connection with individuals, since they are non-eternal; and in the absence of <s>ākṛti</s>, there is no eternal entity even as a secondary indicator. Therefore, whether <s>ākṛti</s> exists or not is investigated.

children.text: sādhite tu tatsadbhāve saiva śabdābhidheyetyākṛtyadhikaraṇe vakṣyate //
children.translated_text: And once its existence is established, [the thesis] that it alone is the referent of words will be stated in the <s>Ākṛtyadhikaraṇa</s>.

body.text: bauddhamatena jātikhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of universals (<s>jāti</s>) according to the Buddhist view.

children.text: tatra saugatāḥ svalakṣaṇameva paramārthaṃ manyamānā nākṛtisadbhāvaṃ manyante /
children.translated_text: Among these, the <s>Saugatas</s> (Buddhists), considering only the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) as ultimately real, do not accept the existence of <s>ākṛti</s>.

children.text: tathāhi- pṛthaktve vyaktito jātirdṛśyeta pṛthageva sā /
children.translated_text: For thus: 'If the universal is different from the individual, it would be seen separately;

children.text: abhede vyaktimātraṃ syādvedhā cenna virodhataḥ //
children.translated_text: if non-different, there would be mere individuals. If [one says] both — no, because of contradiction.'

body.text:
na hi saiva tatonyā cānanyā ca saṃbhavati viruddhatvādbhedābhedayoḥ /
yadi ca bhinnā jātiḥ sā sarvagatā vyaktiṣveva vā, na tāvatsarvagatatvam, antarāle 'nupalabdheḥ /
vyaktisthā cedvyaktāvutpannāyāṃ tasmindeśe prāgasatī kathaṃ tasyāmupalabhyate, na tāvattatrotpadyate /
nityāyā utpattyayogāt /
na ca vyaktyantarādāgacchati
body.translated_text: For the same thing cannot be both different and non-different, since difference and non-difference are contradictory. And if the universal is different, is it omnipresent or only in the individuals? It is not omnipresent, since it is not perceived in the intervening [space]. If it is situated in the individual, then when an individual arises in a particular place, [the universal] which was previously non-existent there — how is it perceived in it? It does not arise there,

body.text: amūrtatvāt, tasmiṃśca vyaktyantare 'nupalabdhiprasaṅgāt /

children.text: nacāṃśenāgatāṃśena ca tatraiva sthiteti śakyaṃ nityatvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor can it be said that part of it came while another part remained there, since it is eternal [and partless].

children.text: nacānyetra yāti amūrtatvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor does it go elsewhere, since it is incorporeal.

children.text: vyaktyantare ca pūrvamevānasthitā jātiriti punaḥpraveśe dviguṇopalabhyeta /
children.translated_text: And if the universal, which was not previously situated in another individual, were to enter again, it would be perceived as double.

children.text: yathāhuḥ- nāyāti na ca tatrāsīdati paścānna cāṃśavat //
children.translated_text: As they say: 'It does not come, nor was it there before; nor afterwards [does it depart] in parts;

body.translated_text: since for an eternal [entity], origination is impossible. Nor does it come from another individual, since it is incorporeal, and because its non-perception in that other individual would follow.

body.text: jahāti pūrvaṃ nādhāramaho vyasanasaṃtati- iti* ////
body.translated_text: it does not leave its former substratum — oh, what a chain of difficulties!'

body.text:
vyaktau ca vartamānāṃ yadyekasyāṃ vyaktau kārtsnyena varteta vyaktyantareṣu na syāt /
nahyekā matī yugapadanekatra kārtsnyena varteta vyaktyantareṣu na syāt /
nahyekā satī yugapadanekatra kārtsnyena vartituṃ śaknoti /
nacāvayavaśo vartate niravayavatvāt /
kathaṃ ca nānāvidhāsvatītānāgatavartamānāsu vyaktiṣvavayavaśo vṛttiḥ saṃbhāvyeta /
vyaktau ca vartamānehapratyayamanubhavet /
dhāsvatītānāgatavartamānāsu vyaktiṣvavayavaśo vṛttiḥ saṃbhāvyeta /
vyaktau ca vartamānehapratyayamanubhavet /
naceha gotvamiti kasyacitpratītirasti kiṃ tviyaṃ gauriti //-- /
atha vyakterātmaiva jātirna tadādhāraṃ vastvantaramiti cet, naivaṃ yuktam, kathaṃ hi nānābhūtānāmanityanāṃ vyāvṛttasvabhāvānāmekarūpā nityānuvṛttasvabhāvā ca jātirātmā syāt trailokyasaṃkaraprasaṅgāt* ////
body.translated_text: And if it exists in the individual: if it were to exist in one individual in its entirety, it would not exist in other individuals. For a single entity cannot exist simultaneously in multiple places in its entirety. Nor does it exist through parts, since it is partless. And how could existence through parts be conceived in individuals that are of various kinds — past, future, and present? And if it existed in the individual, one would experience the cognition 'here.' But no one has the cognition 'cow-hood is here'; rather, [the cognition is] 'this is a cow.' If the self of the individual is itself the universal and not some other entity depending on it — even so, this is not proper. For how could the self of things that are diverse, non-eternal, and of mutually exclusive natures be a universal that is of a single form, eternal, and of a persistent nature? — since the confusion of all three worlds would follow.

body.text:
na ca pramāṇamapi kiñcidākṛtisadbhāve saṃbhavati, na tāvatpratyakṣam /
na hi jātiḥ svaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ janayati nityatvābhyupagamāt /
nityānāṃ ca sarvārthakriyāsvasāmarthyāt /

children.text: na hi jātiḥ svaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ janayati nityatvābhyupagamāt /
children.translated_text: and eternal things are incapable of all causal efficacy.

children.text: nityānāṃ ca sarvārthakriyāsvasāmarthyāt /
children.translated_text: [Repeated:] For the universal does not generate a cognition having itself as object, since it is accepted as eternal.

children.text: nacājanakasya viṣayatvaṃ saṃbhavati tallakṣaṇatvādviṣayatvasya /
children.translated_text: And something that does not generate [cognition] cannot be an object, since objecthood is defined by that [capacity to generate cognition].

children.text: tasmadvikalpākāramātraṃ sāmānyam, alīkaṃ vā* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, the universal is merely a conceptual form (<s>vikalpākāra</s>), or else it is unreal.

body.translated_text: Nor is there any means of valid knowledge for the existence of <s>ākṛti</s>. Not perception, to begin with — for the universal does not generate a cognition having itself as object, since it is accepted as eternal,

body.text: nanu yathā jñānavaicitryopapatteḥ* ////
body.translated_text: But [it is argued:] because the variety of cognitions can be explained [without universals]. ////

body.text: arthaśūnyā api vikalpā vicitrārthakriyāsamarthasvalakṣaṇābhimānino jāyamānāstatra vyavahārārthinaṃ pravartayantaḥ paramparayā tatprabhavatayā tatprāpayanto maṇimiva maṇiprabhāviṣayamaṇibuddhirvyavahārāvisaṃvādino bhavantīti na lokayātrāsthiteḥ kaścidvirodhaḥ tasmānnāsti jātiḥ* ////
body.translated_text: Even conceptual cognitions devoid of [real] objects, arising with the pretension of referring to unique particulars (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) that are capable of diverse causal efficacy, prompt the person seeking practical activity to engage [with things], and indirectly, as originating from those [particulars], lead to the attainment of those —

children.text: etenāvayavidravyaṃ pratyūḍham, tasyāpyavayavabhedādivikalpākṣamatvāt /
children.translated_text: By this, the composite substance (<s>avayavidravya</s>) is also refuted, since it too is incapable of being the object of conceptual construction due to the differentiation of its parts.

children.text: sthūlāvabhāsastu saṃcitānekarūpādiparamāṇuvaśādeva keśoṇḍrkāvabhāsavadupapanno nāvayavikalpanāyālam /
children.translated_text: But the gross appearance is explained merely by the accumulated atoms of multiple forms and the like — like the appearance of a circle of fire from a whirling brand — and does not suffice for the conceptual construction of a composite whole.

children.text: tadabhāve ca nirādhāratvāddūrāpāstaṃ gotvādisāmānyam* ////
children.translated_text: And in its absence, the universal such as cow-ness and the like, being without a substratum, is far removed [from reality]. ////

children.text: kathamasatyekarūpe sāmānye 'tyantavilakṣaṇāni svalakṣaṇānyavilakṣaṇarūpaṃ vikalpaṃ janayanti /
children.translated_text: How, in the absence of a single real form that is a universal, do completely distinct unique particulars (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) produce a conceptual cognition of a non-distinct form?

children.text: janayanti cet kimiti kānicideva govikalpaṃ janayanti kānicidevāśvavikalpam, narvāṇi sarvam* ////
children.translated_text: And if they do produce [it], why do only some produce the concept 'cow' and only some the concept 'horse,' and not all [produce] everything? ////

children.text: sāmānyavādino vā kathaṃ vilakṣaṇarūpā vyaktayo vilakṣaṇasāmānyātmakatvaṃ tadāśrayatvaṃ tadabhivyañjakatvaṃ vā bhajante /
children.translated_text: Or, for the proponent of universals — how do individuals (<s>vyakti</s>) of distinct forms partake of the nature of a distinct universal, or become its substratum, or become its manifesters?

children.text: bhajanticetkimiti kāścideva vyaktayaḥ kenacideva sāmānyena saṃbadhyante na sarvāḥ sarvaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And if they do partake, why do only certain individuals connect with only a certain universal, and not all with all?

children.text: svabhāvāditi cet, asmākamapi tulyamidamuttaram //
children.translated_text: If [one says] 'by their nature' — for us too, this answer is the same. //

body.text: svamatena jātisthāpanam /
body.translated_text: Establishment of <s>jāti</s> (universal) according to one's own doctrine:

children.text: atha vyaktīnāmapyavilakṣaṇarūpasāmānyasaṃbandhasiddhyarthaṃ paramavilakṣaṇarūpamabhyupagamyate tatastenāpi saṃbandhasiddhyarthamaparāparāsāmānyāpekṣayāmanavasthā syāt /
children.translated_text: Now, if to establish the connection of individuals too with the universal of a non-distinct form, an absolutely distinct form is posited — then, for establishing the connection with that too, a further distinct universal would be required, and so on in an infinite regress —

children.text: tasmādvikalpamātramevedam, na paramārthataḥ sāmānyaṃ nāma kiñcit* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, all this is mere conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>); in ultimate reality, there is no such thing as a universal. ////

body.text: atrābhidhīyate- pratyakṣabalasiddhasya sāmānyasya kutarkataḥ //
body.translated_text: To this it is replied: A universal established by the force of perception —

body.text: na śakyo 'pahnavaḥ kartuṃ sarvaṃ vijayate hi tat //
body.translated_text: cannot be denied by mere sophistry; for that [perception] prevails over everything. //

body.text:
sarveṣvapi vastuṣu iyamapi gauriyamapi gauḥ, ayamapi vṛkṣo 'yamapīti vyāvṛttānuvṛttākāraṃ pratyakṣaṃ deśakālāvasthāntareṣvaviparyastamudīyamānaṃ sarvameva tarkābhāsaṃ vijitya dvyākāraṃ vastu vyavasthāpayat kenānyena śakyate bādhitum, na hi tato 'nyadbalavattaramasti pramāṇam, tanmūlatvātpramāṇāntarāṇāṃ tadbādhasāmarthyābhāvāt /
kiñcānumānānyapi sāmānyāpekṣatvātsutarāṃ sāmānyaṃ samarthayante na tu bādhituṃ śaknuvanti, nahi yadyapekṣaṃ tattasya bādhaṃ
body.translated_text: In all things — 'this too is a cow, this too is a cow,' 'this too is a tree, this too' — the perception that has both the form of exclusion and continuity, arising uncontradicted in different places, times, and conditions, [prevails over] everything —

children.text: śaknoti kartum /
children.translated_text: [sophistry] cannot accomplish [its denial].

children.text: tadbādhe hi svātmāpi na siddhyet tadapekṣatvāt* ////
children.translated_text: For in contradicting that [perception], even one's own self would not be established, since it depends on that. ////

body.text:
tathāhi bhedābhedavikalpena sāmānyaṃ nirākurvatāvaśyamevaṃ vaktavyam- yadvastu tadbhinnamabhinnaṃ vā bhavati sāmānyamapi yadi vastu syāttato 'nenāpi bhinnenābhinnena vā bhavitavyam /
na ca dvedhāpi saṃbhavati tasmādavastu iti /
evaṃ ca vadatā vastutvaṃ sāmānyamaṅgīkāryam, anyathā kathaṃ vastutvasya
body.translated_text: For thus, one who refutes the universal through the conceptual distinction of difference and non-difference must necessarily say: 'Whatever is a real thing is either different or non-different; if the universal too were a real thing, then by this too —'

body.text: bhedābhedābhyāṃ vyāptatvādvyāpakānupalabdhyā sāmānyasya vastutvaṃ na saṃbhavatīti bhaṇituṃ śakyam //-- /

children.text: nanvaulapādhiko vastuśabdo na jātinimittakastatkathamanena jātyāpattiḥ /
children.translated_text: But the word 'thing' (<s>vastu</s>) is adventitious (<s>aupādhika</s>), not caused by <s>jāti</s> — so how does <s>jāti</s> apply to it?

children.text: ucyate- jātirvā bhavatūpādhirvā sarvathā tāvatsāmānyarūpamapekṣitavyam /
children.translated_text: It is replied: Let it be <s>jāti</s> or an adventitious condition — in any case, a universal form must be relied upon.

children.text: aupādhikānāmapi mūlopalakṣaṇamekamantareṇātmalābhābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: For even adventitious [properties] cannot obtain their own existence without a single fundamental defining mark (<s>mūlopalakṣaṇa</s>).

children.text: na ca vyāvṛttaikarasaṃ sarvaṃ vastujāmamabhyupagacchataḥ saugatasya kvacidapi kiñcidapyanuvṛttaṃ rūpaṃ saṃbhavatītyaupādhiko vyavahāro durghaṭa eva, tasmātsarvapramāṇasiddhaṃ sāmānyaṃ na śakyamapahnotum* ////
children.translated_text: And for the Buddhist who holds that all things are raw [i.e., bare particulars], uniform in the flavor of exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>), no continuous form whatsoever is possible anywhere — hence even adventitious usage is utterly impossible —

body.translated_text: Since [everything] is pervaded by difference and non-difference, through the non-apprehension of the pervader, it can be declared that the real existence of the universal is not possible. //—/

body.text: kaḥ punarvikalpānāṃ parihāraḥ, na tāvadaparihṛtā api śaknuvanti sāmānyamapahnotuṃ, teṣāmapi tadapekṣatvādityuktaṃ tathāpi parihāro 'bhidhīyate //
body.translated_text: What then is the resolution of the objections (<s>vikalpa</s>)? Even unresolved, they cannot deny the universal, since they too depend on it — as stated. Nevertheless, a resolution is offered: //

body.text: jātivyaktyorbhedābhedavicāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Investigation of the difference and non-difference of <s>jāti</s> and <s>vyakti</s>: //

body.text:
bhedābhedavikalpe tāvatkecidāhuḥ- bhinnameva sāmānyaṃ vyaktibhyaḥ /
na ca pṛthagupalabdhiprasaṅgo vyaktisaṃbandhitvāt /
kaḥ punaḥ saṃbandhaḥ, samavāyaḥ /
kaḥ punarasau, ayutasiddhānāmihapratyayahetuḥ saṃbandha iti kecit /
tattvayuktam /

children.text: ihapratyayāsiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: because the cognition 'here' is not established.

children.text: iyaṃ gauriti hi sarvadā sarveṣāṃ pratītirnehagotvamiti /
children.translated_text: For the cognition of everyone at all times is 'this is a cow,' not 'here is cowness.'

children.text: kāceyamayutasiddhiḥ, yutasiddhyabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is this inseparable relation (<s>ayutasiddhi</s>)? The absence of separable relation (<s>yutasiddhi</s>).

children.text: kā punaryutasiddhiḥ, pṛthaggatimatvaṃ pṛthagāśrayāśritatvaṃ vā, tadabhāvo 'yutasiddhiḥ* ////
children.translated_text: And what is separable relation? Having separate movement, or resting on a separate substratum — the absence of that is inseparable relation. ////

body.translated_text: Regarding the conceptual distinction of difference and non-difference, some say: The universal is simply different from the individuals. And there is no unwanted consequence of separate apprehension, because of its being connected with individuals. What then is the connection? <s>Samavāya</s> (inherence) —

children.text: yadyevamavayavāvayavinoḥ saṃbandhaḥ samavāyo na syāt, vināpyavayavicalanenāvayavānāṃ calanāt, avayavino 'vayavānāṃ ca svāvayavāśrayatvāt /
children.translated_text: If so, then the relation between parts and the whole would not be <s>samavāya</s>, since even without the movement of the whole, the parts move, and both the whole and the parts rest on their own respective parts as substratum.

children.text: tathā sāmānyasya vyaktyāśrayatvāt vyakteśca svāvayavāśritatvādasti pṛthagāśrayāśrayitvamiti samavāyānupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, since the universal rests on the individual as substratum, and the individual rests on its own parts, there is resting on a separate substratum — hence <s>samavāya</s> would be untenable.

children.text: tasmādevaṃ vaktavyam- yena saṃbandhenādheyamādhāre svānurūpāṃ buddhiṃ janayati, svākāreṇa bodhayatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it should be stated thus: That relation by which the superimposed [property] produces in the substratum a cognition conforming to itself — meaning, it reveals [the substratum] through its own form —

children.text: sa saṃbandhaḥ samavāya iti* ////
children.translated_text: that relation is <s>samavāya</s>. ////

children.text: yadi jātyātmanā vyaktiḥ pratīyate tato jātivyaktyorabheda eva pratītibalādāpadyate kathaṃ bhedābhyupagamaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the individual is cognized in the form of the <s>jāti</s>, then by the force of that cognition, non-difference of <s>jāti</s> and <s>vyakti</s> would follow — how then can difference be maintained?

children.text: ucyate- gaurayaṃ śāvaleyo gaurayaṃ bāhuleya ityubhayatra gavākāro 'nuvartamāno dṛśyate, śāvaleyabāhuleyākārau tu vyāvartete, tadyapi tayoḥ śābaleyagavākārayorabhedaḥ syādekānuvṛttāvitaro 'pyanuvarteta, tadvyāvṛttau vā gavākāro 'pi vyāvarteta /
children.translated_text: It is replied: 'This is a cow, the <s>Śābaleya</s>; this is a cow, the <s>Bāhuleya</s>' — in both cases, the cow-form is seen as continuous, while the <s>Śābaleya</s>-form and <s>Bāhuleya</s>-form are seen as excluded. Although in both cases the <s>Śābaleya</s>-cow —

children.text: kiṃ ca tasyāmeva vyaktāviyaṃ gauriti gavātmanā pratīyamānāyāmapi neyaṃbuddhigobuddhyorgaurirgauritivatparyāyatvaṃ pratīyate tasmānnābhedaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Moreover, even when in that very individual cognized in the form of a cow — 'this is a cow' — the 'this'-cognition and the 'cow'-cognition are not cognized as synonymous, like 'Gaurī' and 'Gaurī' [referring to the same entity]. Therefore, there is no non-difference. ////

children.text: kathaṃ tarhi tādrūpyaṃ vyakteḥ pratīyate /
children.translated_text: How then is the similarity of form (<s>tādrūpya</s>) of the individual cognized?

children.text: idameva hi tādrūpyaṃ vyakteryat tat samavāyaḥ saṃbandhaḥ, tasyaiṣa mahimā yenādhāramādheyaṃ svabuddhyānurañjayati tasmādadoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This very similarity of form of the individual is that — namely, the relation of <s>samavāya</s>. This is its greatness, that the substratum is colored by the superimposed [property] through its own cognition. Therefore, there is no fault.

children.text: athavā tādātmyapratīterabhedopyastu, pūrvoktanyāyena bhedo 'pi, tasmātpramāṇabalena bhinnābhinnatvameva yuktam* ////
children.translated_text: Or, from the cognition of identity, let there be non-difference too; and by the previously stated reasoning, difference too. Therefore, by the force of the means of knowledge, being both different and non-different is alone proper. ////

children.text: nanu viruddhau bhedābhedau kathamekatra syātāṃ na virodhaḥ sahadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: But difference and non-difference are contradictory — how can they obtain in the same [thing]? There is no contradiction, because of their being seen together.

children.text: yadi hi idaṃ rajataṃ nedaṃ rajatamitivatparasparopamardena bhedābhedau pratīyeyātāṃ tato viruddhyeyātāṃ, na tu tayoḥ parasparopamardena pratītiḥ iyaṃ gauritibuddhidvayamaparyāyeṇa pratibhāsamānamekaṃ vastu dvyātmakaṃ vyavasthāpayati- sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ hyabhedamāpādayati aparyāyatvaṃ ca bhedam, ataḥ pratītibalādavirodhaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: For if difference and non-difference were cognized through mutual negation, like 'this is silver' and 'this is not silver,' then they would be contradictory. But they are not cognized through mutual negation — 'this [is a cow]' —

body.text:
apekṣābhedācca /
tathāhi gorūpeṇa nirūpyamāṇayā jātyā vyaktirabhedena pratīyate gaurayaṃ śābaleya iti /
yadā tu jātirvayaktyantarātmanā nirūpyate tadeyaṃ vyaktisato bhinnarūpāvasīyate yo 'sau bāhuleya gauḥ so 'yaṃ śābaleyo na bhavatīti /
evaṃ dharmiṇo dravyasya
body.translated_text: And because of the difference of the aspects. For thus: when the individual is examined in the form of the <s>jāti</s>, it is cognized as non-different — 'this is a cow, the <s>Śābaleya</s>.' But when the <s>jāti</s> is examined in the form of another individual, then —

children.text: rasādidharmāntararūpeṇa rūpādibhyāṃ bhedo dravyarūpeṇa cābhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: in the form of other properties such as taste and the like, there is difference from form and the like; and in the form of substance, there is non-difference.

children.text: tathāvayavinaḥ svarūpeṇāvayavairabhedo 'vayavāntararūpeṇa tvavayavāntarairbheda ityūhanīyam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the whole, in its own form, is non-different from its parts; but in the form of other parts, there is difference from other parts — thus it should be understood.

children.text: tatra yathā dīrghahrasvādīnāṃ viruddhasvabhāvāmāmapyapekṣābhedādekatrāpyaviruddhaṃ pratītibalādaṅgīkriyate tathā bhedābhedayorapi draṣyavyaṃ pratītyaviśeṣāt //
children.translated_text: Just as long and short and the like, though of contradictory natures, are accepted by the force of cognition as non-contradictory even in the same [thing], due to the difference of aspects — so too should it be seen for difference and non-difference, by the authority of cognition —

body.text: prābhākaramatena bhedābhedāsamānādhikaraṇye ākṣepaḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection according to the <s>Prābhākara</s> view against the non-co-referentiality of difference and non-difference:

body.text: kaścitpunarāha- pratītireva bhedābhedabhāsinī na saṃbhavatīti vilakṣaṇarūpā pratītirhi bhedāvabhāsaḥ tadyena bhedapratibhāsasamaye jātirūpaṃ vyaktirūpaṃ ca pratītam, tenābhedapratītivelāyāṃ tayoranyataratpratyetavyam, tatraikasya dviravabhāso 'yaṃ bhavet, na punaritareṇābhedaḥ pratīto bhavati, tasmānnāsti bhedābhedayorekatra pratītiḥ* ////
body.translated_text: Someone further says: A cognition that manifests both difference and non-difference is simply not possible. For a cognition of a distinct form is the manifestation of difference; when at the time of the manifestation of difference, the form of <s>jāti</s> and the form of <s>vyakti</s> —

body.text: tadidamasāram /

children.text: na hi vastudvayapratītireva bhedapratītiḥ tadbhāve 'pyabhāvāt /
children.translated_text: For the cognition of two things is not itself the cognition of their difference — since [difference-cognition] is absent even when both are present.

children.text: prathamaṃ vyaktidarśane 'pi hyasti jātivyaktyordvayoḥ pratītirnaca tadā tayorbhedaḥ pratīyate vyaktyantaradarśanena tu jāteranvayātpūrvavyakteśca vyatirekādanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ jātivyaktyorbhedo 'vadhāryata iti bhavato 'pi siddhāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: For even upon first seeing an individual, there is the cognition of both <s>jāti</s> and <s>vyakti</s>; yet their difference is not cognized then. It is only upon seeing another individual, through the continuity of <s>jāti</s> and the exclusion of the former individual, that —

children.text: tathā devadattamupalabhya kālāntare tatsadṛśaṃ yajñadattaṃ dūrātpaśyan pūrvopalabdhaṃ ca devadattaṃ smaran vastutastadvilakṣaṇameva puruṣagadvayaṃ pratyeti tathāpi na bhedamavadhārayati saṃśete hi kiṃ sa evāyaṃ devadattaḥ kiṃ vānya iti /
children.translated_text: Likewise, having perceived <s>Devadatta</s>, at another time, seeing <s>Yajñadatta</s> who resembles him from a distance, and remembering the previously perceived <s>Devadatta</s>, one cognizes a pair of persons who in reality are completely distinct —

children.text: tasmādvastudvayapratītireva bedapratītirityuktam* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, it has been stated that the mere cognition of two things is itself the cognition of their difference. ////

body.translated_text: This is without substance.

children.text: tathā tameva devadattaṃ kiṃ vānyaḥ iti /
children.translated_text: Likewise, [seeing] that very <s>Devadatta</s> — 'is it he or another?' —

children.text: tasmādvastudvayapratītireva bhedapratītirityuktam* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, it has been stated that the mere cognition of two things is itself the cognition of their difference. ////

body.text:
tathā tameva devadattaṃ kālāntare dūrātpaśyannapi kiṃ sa evāyamutānya iti /
saṃdihāno vastugatyaikameva pratiyannapi nābhedamavadhārayayitumalaṃ bhavati, tasmānna vastudvayapratītireva bhedapratītiḥ /
nāpyekavastupratītirevābhedapratītiḥ, kintvanyo 'yamiti buddhirbhedāvabhāsaḥ ananyo 'yamiti cābhedāvabhāsaḥ /
asti ca śābaleyabāhuleyāvupalabhyamānasya ayaṃ
body.translated_text: Likewise, even when seeing that very <s>Devadatta</s> from a distance at another time — 'is this the same one or another?' — doubting, and cognizing by the force of the thing only one [entity], one is unable to ascertain non-difference —

children.text: gaurayamiti gauḥ ityabhedāvabhāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This is a cow' — thus 'cow' is the manifestation of non-difference.

children.text: anyaḥ śābaleyādbāhuleya iti ca bhedāvabhāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: And '<s>Bāhuleya</s> is different from <s>Śābaleya</s>' is the manifestation of difference.

children.text: tasmādupapannaṃ bhinnābhinnatvam* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, being both different and non-different is well-established. ////

body.text: nanvanuvṛttā nityānutpattivināśadharmā ca jātiḥ, viparītasvabhāvā ca vyaktiḥ, kathaṃ tayauraikyam /

children.text: nahyekameva vastvanuvṛttaṃ vyāvṛttaṃ nityamanityamutpattivināśadharmakamataddharmakaṃ ca saṃbhavati trailokyasaṃkaraprasaṅgāt, jātirapyevamanityatvādidharmā syāt, vyaktirapi nityatvādidharmā /
children.translated_text: For one and the same thing cannot possibly be both continuous and excluded, eternal and non-eternal, characterized by origination and destruction and not so — since confusion of the three worlds would follow; and <s>jāti</s> too would thus be non-eternal and so forth —

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault.

children.text: nānākāraṃ hi tadvastu kenacidākāreṇa nityatvādikaṃ kenaciccānityatvādikaṃ bibhranna virotsyate /
children.translated_text: For that thing, being of manifold forms, bearing eternality and the like through one form and non-eternality and the like through another, will not be contradictory.

children.text: jātirapi vyaktirūpeṇānityā vyaktirapi jātyātmanā nityeti nātra kācidaniṣṭāpattiḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Jāti</s> too, in the form of <s>vyakti</s>, is non-eternal; and <s>vyakti</s> too, in the nature of <s>jāti</s>, is eternal — thus no undesired consequence arises here. //

body.translated_text: But <s>jāti</s> is continuous, eternal, and characterized by non-origination and non-destruction; and <s>vyakti</s> is of opposite nature — how can there be identity of the two?

body.text: jāteḥ sarvagatatvādyākṣepatatparihārau //
body.translated_text: Objection regarding the omnipresence of <s>jāti</s> and its resolution: //

body.text:
yattu sarvagatā vyaktigatā vā jātiriti vikalpitaṃ, tadapi vyaktyātmatvābhidhānādeva parihṛtam /
vyakterhyasāvātmā kathamanyatra syāt /
nanvevaṃ vyaktideśe vyaktyutpatteḥ prāgavidyamānā jātiḥ kathaṃ tatra paścādbhavati, svakāraṇānniṣpadyamānā vyaktirjātiviśeṣātmanā saṃbaddhaivotpadyate nityatvāt /
nacānyatra āgacchati amūrtatvāt /
ucyate- yo 'pi deśāntarādāgatyānena deśena saṃyujyate so 'pi prāgasmindeśe 'vidyamāna eva kathamanena deśena saṃyogamanubhavati kāraṇavaśāditi vyaktam, evaṃ jātirapi kāraṇavaśādeva vyaktisaṃbandhamanubhavati /
iyāstu viśeṣaḥ- saṃyujyamānaḥ pūrvatrāvasthito 'nantaradeśena prathamaṃ saṃyujyate tatastadanantaradeśeneti krameṇa deśāntaralasaṃyogaṃ gacchati /
tādātmyasamavāyayostvanantaradeśamanapekṣyaiva svakāraṇato niṣpattiḥ /
na hi saṃyogasya svabhāvaḥ sa eva tādātmyasya samavāyasya vāṅgīkartavyaḥ /
pramāṇābhāvāt, vilakṣaṇasvabhāvatvādbhāvānām /
body.translated_text: As for the dilemma — whether the universal (<s>jāti</s>) is omnipresent or resides in [each] particular — that too has been resolved by the statement that it is the very nature of the particular. For since it is its nature, how could it be elsewhere? Objection: if so, how does the universal, which did not exist [in a location] prior to the arising of the particular in that place, come to be there afterward? The particular, being produced from its own cause, arises already connected with the specific universal as its nature, because of [the universal's] eternality. Nor does it come from elsewhere, because of [the universal's] incorporeality. It is replied: even one who comes from another place and conjoins with this place — he too did not exist in this place previously — yet how does he come to experience conjunction with this place? Evidently, through the force of the cause. Likewise, the universal too experiences its relation with the particular through the force of the cause alone. But there is this difference: one who conjoins [spatially], being stationed previously elsewhere, first conjoins with the adjacent place, then with the place next to that — and thus gradually arrives at conjunction with the other place. But for identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), the production [occurs] from one's own cause without depending on adjacent places. For the nature of conjunction should not be accepted as identical with that of identity or inherence — because there is no valid means of knowledge [for that identification], and because entities have distinct natures.

body.text: tasmādadoṣaḥ* ////
body.translated_text: Therefore, there is no fault.

children.text: yadvāstu sarvagataṃ sāmānyam, na ca sarvatropalabdhiprasaṅgaḥ vyaktīnāmabhivyañjakatvāt /
children.translated_text: Or, let the universal be omnipresent — and there would be no consequence of it being perceived everywhere, because the particulars serve as its manifestors.

children.text: sarvagatamapi sāmānyaṃ vyakterevātmā tatsamavetaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: The universal, even if omnipresent, is either the very nature of the particular or is inherent in it.

children.text: saṃyuktasamavāyasaṃnikarṣeṇa ca sāmānyasyopalambhaḥ, tena ca saṃnikarṣo vyaktideśe eva saṃbhavati nānyatreti na sarvatropalabdhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And the apprehension of the universal occurs through the contact called 'conjunction-with-what-is-inherent' (<s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s>); and that contact is possible only at the place of the particular, not elsewhere — therefore it is not perceived everywhere.

children.text: abhede 'pi jātivyaktyorbhedasyāpi vidyamānatvānnityatvānnityatvādivatsarvagatatvāsravagatatvamapi nānupapannam* ////
children.translated_text: Even though there is non-difference between the universal and the particular, since difference too exists [between them], just as eternality and non-eternality [coexist], so too omnipresence and non-omnipresence are not impossible.

body.text:
yattu kārtsnyena vā avayavaśo vā vṛttiriti vikalpitam, tadapyayuktam /
bhedāpekṣaṃ hi kārtsnyaṃ na ca sāmānyasya svarūpato 'vayavato vā bhedosti ekatvādanavayavatvācca /
niravayavatvādevāvayavavaśo 'pi vṛttirabhāvyaiva /
tasmādvyaktiṣu jātirvartata ityetāvadevātra vaktuṃ śakyate pramāṇato 'vagamāt, na kārtsnyabhāgavibhāgaḥ pramāṇābhāvādasaṃbhāvācca /
tathāvayavino 'pyavayaveṣu na kārtsnyaṃ saṃbhavati bahutvābhāvāttadepakṣatvācca kṛtsnatvavyavahārasya /
avayavaśo vṛttirapyavayavāntarābhāvādayuktaiva /
kimidānīmekarūpaiva sāmānyasya vyaktiṣvavayaveṣu cāvayavino vṛttiḥ /
netyucyate /

children.text: sāmānyaṃ pratyekaṃ vartata, avayavīṃ tu vyāsajyetyevaṃ viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The universal resides in each [particular] individually, whereas the whole resides pervadingly — this is the distinction.

children.text: vyaktyantaramanapekṣyaiva vyaktyantare vartamānā svānurūpāṃ buddhiṃ janayantī jātiḥ pratyekaṃ ityucyate na tu kātsnyena vṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: The universal, residing in one particular without depending on another particular, producing a cognition conforming to itself, is said to reside 'in each individually' — its residence is not 'in entirety.'

children.text: avayavī tvavayavāntarāṇyapekṣyāvāntare vartamānaḥ svākāraṃ buddhiṃ janayan vyāsajya vartata iti vyapadiśyate /
children.translated_text: The whole, however, residing in one part while depending on the other parts, producing a cognition of its own form, is designated as residing 'pervadingly.'

children.text: nahyekasyāmeva vyaktau gobuddhivadekasminneva tantau paṭabuddhirutpadyate //
children.translated_text: For just as the cognition of cow [arises from] a single particular, the cognition of cloth does not arise from a single thread alone.

body.translated_text: As for the dilemma — whether [the universal] resides in its entirety or in parts — that too is improper. For 'entirety' presupposes difference, and there is no difference in the universal either in its intrinsic nature or in its parts, since it is one and partless. And because it is partless, residence in parts too is impossible. Therefore, all that can be said here is: 'the universal resides in the particulars' — this much is known from valid means of knowledge. The distinction of entirety versus parts cannot be made, due to the absence of a valid means of knowledge and the impossibility [of such a distinction]. Likewise, even in the case of a whole (<s>avayavin</s>) with respect to its parts, entirety is not possible, due to the absence of plurality [in the whole] and because the usage of 'entirety' depends on that [plurality]. Residence in parts too is improper, since there are no further sub-parts [of the whole]. What then — does the universal reside in the particulars and the whole in its parts in a single, uniform manner? No, it is said:

body.text: saṃyogavicāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Discussion of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>).

children.text: saṃyogasyedānīṃ kathaṃ saṃyogiṣu vṛttiḥ kiṃ jātivat kiṃvāvayavivat /
children.translated_text: Now, how does conjunction reside in the things conjoined — like a universal, or like a whole?

children.text: ubhayavilakṣaṇeti brūmaḥ /
children.translated_text: We say: it is different from both.

children.text: sa hi saṃyogyantaramapekṣya saṃyogyantare vartate nānapekṣyeti na jātitulyatvam /
children.translated_text: For it resides in one conjunct depending on the other conjunct, not independently — so it is not like a universal.

children.text: ekatraiva ca svānurūpāṃ janayati buddhim idamanena saṃyuktamidamanena iti, tenāvayavināpi nātīva tulyatvamityubhayavailakṣaṇyam* ////
children.translated_text: And in a single [conjunct] alone it produces a cognition conforming to itself — 'this is conjoined with that, that is conjoined with this' — and therefore it is not entirely like a whole either. Thus it is different from both.

body.text:
atha saṃyogaḥ kimeka eva dvayoḥ saṃyoginoruta pratisaṃyogi bhinnāveva saṃyogau /
kāśyapīyāstāvat saṃyogamubhayorvyāsaktamekaṃ manyante vayaṃ tu yathā idamanena sadṛśamidamaneneti pratiyoginamapekṣyetaratretarasyāvagamyamānaṃ sādṛśyaṃ pratidharmibhinnaṃ bhavati tathā saṃyogasya tādṛśabuddhiviṣayatvādbhedameva rocayāmahe /
prakṛtamanusarāmaḥ- tasmānna vṛttivikalpādapi jātyapahnavaḥ /
yattu nityatvājjāteḥ svaviṣayajñānajananāsāmarthyānna grāhyatvamiti /
tadasat /

children.text: nityānāmapyarthakriyāsāmarthyaṃ kṣaṇabhaṅganirākaraṇe vakṣyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: we shall state in the refutation of momentariness that even eternal entities have the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>).

children.text: na ca hetulakṣaṇaṃ grāhyatvam /
children.translated_text: And apprehensibility does not have the definition of being a cause [of something].

children.text: jñānajanyaphalabhāgitvalakṣaṇaṃ hi taditi śūnyavāde varṇitam /
children.translated_text: For it has the definition of being a beneficiary of the result produced by cognition — as was explained in [the section on] the <s>Śūnyavāda</s> (doctrine of emptiness).

children.text: tasmādayamapyadoṣaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, this too is not a fault.

body.translated_text: Now, is conjunction a single [entity] belonging to two conjuncts, or are there two distinct conjunctions, one for each conjunct? The followers of <s>Kāśyapa</s> (the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>) hold that conjunction is a single [entity] pervading both. We, however, since similarity — apprehended as 'this is similar to that, this is similar to that' with reference to the respective counterpart — is distinct for each locus, prefer distinctness [of conjunction] as well, because conjunction is the object of such [relational] cognition. Let us return to the topic at hand: therefore, the denial of universals is not [justified] even by the dilemma concerning [their mode of] residence. As for [the objection] that because the universal is eternal, it lacks the capacity to produce cognition of its own object and therefore is not apprehensible —

children.text: yattu svalakṣaṇaireva svānubhavadvāreṇa gavādivikalpodayasaṃbhavādaprāmāṇikī jātivikalpaneti tadapyasāram /
children.translated_text: As for [the Buddhist objection] that since the arising of conceptual constructions such as 'cow' and the like is possible through unique particulars (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) alone, by means of one's own experience, the conceptual construction of universals lacks validity — that too is without substance.

children.text: na hi jātirna dṛśyate yenaivamupālambhaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: For it is not the case that the universal is not perceived — [if it were so,] only then would such a criticism be appropriate.

children.text: upajāyamānaṃ tu jñānaṃ svaviṣayabhūtāṃ jātimupasthāpayatīti nedṛśānāṃ pralāpanāmavasaraḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Rather, the cognition that arises presents the universal, which is its own object — so there is no occasion for such prattle.

children.text: kathañcātyantavilakṣaṇāni svalakṣaṇānyekarūpaṃ vijñānaṃ janayanti tadatadrūpiṇo bhāvāstadatadrūpahetujāḥ iti sthiteḥ /
children.translated_text: And how can utterly dissimilar unique particulars produce a uniform cognition? For the established [principle] is: entities that are of such-and-such nature arise from causes that are of such-and-such nature.

children.text: bhavato vā kathaṃ vilakṣaṇānāṃ viśeṣāṇāmekarūpasāmānyasaṃbandhakāraṇatvamiticet, dātmyaṃ samavāyaṃ vā bhajante* ////
children.translated_text: If [one asks]: on your [Mīmāṃsā] view too, how can dissimilar particulars serve as the cause of the relation with a uniform universal? — [We reply:] they partake of identity or inherence [with the universal].

children.text: nanu hetavo vilakṣaṇaḥ kathamekavidhasāmarthyayuktāni svalakṣaṇāni janayanti /
children.translated_text: Objection: if the causes are dissimilar, how can the unique particulars they produce be endowed with a uniform capacity?

children.text: na janayeyuryadi vilakṣaṇāḥ syuste 'pi tvekajātīyā eva //
children.translated_text: They would not produce [a uniform result] if they were [truly] dissimilar — but they too are of the same class.

body.text:
nanvevaṃ tatsaṃbandhasidhyarthaparāparajātyapekṣāyāmanavasthā /
naiṣa doṣaḥ, yathā tālabījamekajātīyaṃ pariṇāmaparaṃparayā tālajātīsaṃbaddhāṃ
body.translated_text: Objection: if so, in establishing that same-class relation, one would need to resort to higher and lower universals, leading to infinite regress. This is not a fault. Just as a palm seed, being of one class, through a series of transformations, produces

body.text:
vyaktimupajanayati, sāpi tathaiva svakāraṇabhūtabījasamānajātīyaṃ bījāntaram /
tathaikajātīyacchukrādgojātīyavyaktiniṣpattiḥ, tasyāṃ ca
body.translated_text: a particular connected with the palm-class, and that [particular] likewise [produces] another seed of the same class as the seed that was its cause —

children.text: tajjātīyaśukraniṣpattiriti nātyantaṃ tādātmyāpattiḥ /
children.translated_text: so too, from semen of one class, a particular of the cow-class is produced, and in that [particular],

children.text: tasmādastyekamākṛtijātisāmānyaśabdābhilapanīyaṃ śābaleyādiṣvanugatam //
children.translated_text: semen of that same class is produced — thus there is no complete identity-collapse. Therefore, there exists something — denoted by the words <s>ākṛti</s> (form), <s>jāti</s> (class), and <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) — that is common to the brown cow and others.

body.text: ityākṛtivādaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus [concludes] the <s>ākṛtivāda</s> (discussion of [universals as] form).

body.text: sādṛśyādīnāṃ sāmānyatvakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of similarity and the like as universals.

children.text: naca sādṛśyameva sāmānyaṃ tadbuddhyabhāvāta, sa evāyamiti pratītirna tattatsadṛśa iti /
children.translated_text: Nor is similarity (<s>sādṛśya</s>) itself the universal, because the cognition [associated with universals] is absent [in the case of similarity]. The cognition is 'this is the very same [kind]' — not 'this is similar to that.'

children.text: na ca sarvasāmānyāpahnavavādinaḥ sādṛśyamapi saṃbhavati bhūyovayavasāmānyātmakatvāttasya //
children.translated_text: And for one who denies all universals, even similarity is not possible, since it is constituted by a universal of common components.

body.text:
na cātadvyāvṛttirūpamapi samānyamanaṅgīkṛtavidhirūpasāmānyena śakyate pratyetum /
 agovyāvṛttiṃ hi pratīyatāvaśyaṃ prathamameva gauḥ pratyetavyaḥ /
na hi tebhyo vyatirekarūpamapahāyāśvādivyaktīnāṃ prātisvikena rūpeṇa saṃbhavati /
teṣāmanantānāṃ buddhāvanārohāt, anārūḍheṣu ca teṣu tadvyāvṛttirūpasya goḥ pratyetumaśakyatvāt /

children.text: gaurgauriti ca vidhirūpaṃ sāmānyamavagamyamānaṃ kathaṃ nivṛttirūpaṃ śakyamaṅgīkartum /
children.translated_text: And when a positive universal is being apprehended as 'cow, cow' — how can a negative form be accepted?

children.text: tasmādidamatipelavaṃ darśanam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this is an extremely flimsy doctrine.

children.text: tasmādasti jātiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the universal (<s>jāti</s>) exists.

children.text: ityapohavādaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [concludes] the <s>apohavāda</s> (discussion of [the Buddhist] exclusion theory).

body.translated_text: Nor can a universal in the form of 'exclusion from what is not that' (<s>atadvyāvṛtti</s>) be cognized without accepting a universal in positive form. For in order to cognize 'exclusion from non-cow,' one must first cognize 'cow.' For the particulars of horses and the like cannot [be distinguished] by their own individual forms alone, setting aside their form of difference [from cow]. Since those [non-cow particulars] are infinite, they cannot all enter cognition; and when they have not entered cognition, the cow as having the form of exclusion from them cannot be cognized.

body.text: avayavavicāraḥ /
body.translated_text: Discussion of the whole (<s>avayavin</s>).

body.text:
etenāvayavi vyākhyātaḥ /
tasyāpyavayavebhyo bhedo 'bhedo veti vikalpe bhedaṃ samavāyasaṃbandhamavayavaguṇebhyaśca tatra viśeṣaguṇānāmutpattimacakṣate vaiśeṣikāḥ /
ye ca svasamavetaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭāḥ svāśrayasyaikajātīyasya paricchedakāste viśeṣaguṇā ityāhuḥ /
vayaṃ tu bhinnābhinnatvam /
nahitantubhyaḥ śiraḥpāṇyādibhyo nāvayebhyo niṣkṛṣṭaḥ paṭo devadatto vā pratīyate /
tantupāṇyādayo 'vayavā eva paṭādyātmanā pratīyante /

children.text: vidyate ca devadatte asya hastaḥ śira ityādiḥ kiyānapi bhedāvabhāsa ityupapannamubhayātmakatvam /
children.translated_text: And in <s>Devadatta</s>, there is some appearance of difference — 'his hand,' 'his head,' and so forth — thus the dual nature is established.

children.text: tasmādavayavānāmevāvasthāntaramavayavī na drāvyāntaram /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the whole is merely another state of the parts themselves, not a different substance.

children.text: ta eva hi saṃyogaviśeṣavaśādakadravyatāmāpadyatesa tadātmanā ca mahatvaṃ paṭajātiṃ ca vibhrataḥ paṭabuddhyā gṛhyante /
children.translated_text: For those very [parts], through a particular conjunction, attain the status of a single substance, and bearing in that form [the properties of] largeness, cloth-class, and the like, they are apprehended through the cognition of cloth.

children.text: tena paṭātmanā teṣāmekatvam avayavātmanā tu nānātvamupapannam* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, their oneness is in the form of cloth, while their multiplicity in the form of parts is also proper.

body.translated_text: By this, the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) is also explained. With respect to the dilemma of whether it is different from or identical with its parts — the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> hold [that there is] difference, the relation of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), and the production of specific qualities (<s>viśeṣaguṇa</s>) distinct from the qualities of the parts. And they say that the specific qualities — which are qualified by the qualifiers inhering in themselves and which delimit an entity of the same class as their substratum — are the specific qualities. We, however, [hold] that it is both different and non-different. For neither cloth nor <s>Devadatta</s> is cognized as extracted from their threads and head-hands-and-other-parts respectively. The parts such as threads and hands are themselves cognized as having the nature of cloth, <s>Devadatta</s>, and so forth.

children.text: yadapi rūpādayaḥ kārye guṇamārabhate ityuktaṃ tadapari guṇadvayapratītyabhāvīnnātītavāsmabhyaṃ rocate /
children.translated_text: As for the statement that 'in the effect, [the cause's] qualities originate a [new] quality' — that is not favored by us either, because no cognition of two [distinct] qualities [is observed].

children.text: yadi hi dvau guṇau pratīyeyātāṃ tantuṣvekaḥ paṭe cāparastataḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaṃ pratipadyeyātām /
children.translated_text: For if two qualities were cognized — one in the threads and another in the cloth — then a cause-effect relationship between them could be admitted.

children.text: yatrāpi nānārūpaiḥ śuklakṛṣṇaraktapītaistantubhirārabhyate paṭastastrāpi ta eva varṇāḥ paṭagatāḥ pratīyante na rūpāntaram //
children.translated_text: Even where a cloth is woven from threads of various colors — white, black, red, yellow — even there, those very same colors are cognized as belonging to the cloth, not a different color.

body.text: citraikarūpanirākaraṇam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the single 'variegated' color.

body.text:
nanu citraḥ paṭa iti pratīyate na tu śuklaḥ pūta iti vā, tasmāccitrākhyaṃ rūpāntaramatrotpannam /
naivam /
citraṃ lokavirodhādevāyuktamaṅgīkartum /
nānārūpāṇāmapi cāvayavabhedadvāreṇaikasminnapi paṭe samavāyo nānupapannaḥ /
etena saṃyogajasaṃyogo nirasto veditavyaḥ /
yathā devadattasaṃyoga eva tasminkuṇḍalisaṃyogo bhavati tathā tantuturīsaṃyoga eva tantau paṭabhāvamāpanne paṭaturīsaṃyogo bhavati na saṃyogāntaraṃ pratītyabhāvādityalamativistareṇa /
tasmādastyevāvayavī /--
vṛttiḥ svāvayaveṣvasya vyāsajyeti pradarśitam //
body.translated_text: Objection: what is cognized is 'a variegated cloth,' not 'a white cloth' or 'a yellow cloth' — therefore a distinct color called 'variegated' has arisen here. Not so. It is improper to accept 'variegated' [as a single color], precisely because of the conflict with common experience. And the inherence of multiple colors, even in a single cloth, is not impossible through the medium of the distinction of parts. By this, the 'conjunction-born conjunction' is to be understood as refuted as well. Just as the conjunction with <s>Devadatta</s> is itself the conjunction of the ring [on his finger] — so too, the conjunction of the thread with the loom, when the thread attains the state of cloth, is itself the conjunction of the cloth with the loom — no separate conjunction [is needed], since no [separate] cognition [of one] is observed. Enough of excessive elaboration. Therefore, the whole indeed exists. Its residence in its own parts has been shown to be pervading.

body.text: tenāsyavayavidravyaṃ sāmānyaṃ cāsti sarvagam //
body.translated_text: Therefore, the substance that is the whole exists, and so does the universal, which is omnipresent.

body.text: ityavayavivādaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [concludes] the <s>avayavivāda</s> (discussion of the whole).

body.text: varṇānāmabhidhātṛtvamākṛteścābhidheyatām //
body.translated_text: Having stated the denotative power of phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) and the denotability of form (<s>ākṛti</s>),

body.text: kathayitvātha saṃbandhakathaiva prakṛtocyate //
body.translated_text: the discussion of the relation [between word and meaning], which is the topic at hand, is now stated.

body.text: jñāpyajñāpakabhāvaśca saṃbandhaḥ prāgudīritaḥ //
body.translated_text: The relation of 'that which is to be made known' and 'that which makes known' was previously stated.

body.text: tannityatvaṃ yadākṣiptaṃ tatsamādhīyate 'dhunā //
body.translated_text: The eternality of that [relation], which was implied, is now addressed.

children.text: evaṃ hi pūrvamuktam- yasmātprathamaśravaṇe śabdor'thaṃ na pratyāyayati tasmānnāsya svābhāvikamindriyavatpratyāyakatvam /
children.translated_text: For thus it was previously stated: 'Since at the first hearing, a word does not convey its meaning, therefore its capacity to convey — like a sense organ — is not natural.'

children.text: asyāyamarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This is its meaning' —

children.text: iti puruṣeṇa kathite pratyāyayati tato nūnamasya puruṣakṛtaṃ pratyāyakatvamiti pauruṣeya eva saṃbandha iti* ////
children.translated_text: when stated by a person, it conveys [the meaning]; therefore its capacity to convey must certainly be person-made — thus the relation is human-made (<s>pauruṣeya</s>).

body.text: tatrābhidhīyate- nahyasyāyamartha iti
body.translated_text: To this it is replied: 'this is its meaning' is not

body.text: saṃbandhakaraṇamidam, prasiddhasaṃbandhakathanaṃ hyetat /

children.text: kathamavagamyate arthāntarakathane bahubhirnivāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: How is this known? Because when [someone states] a different meaning, he is corrected by many.

children.text: yo hi kaścit kasmaicit gośabdasyāśvaṃ gavayaṃ vārthamāha tamanye nivārayanti nāyamasyārthaḥ sāsnādimānasyārtha iti, saṃbandhakriyāpakṣe ca devadattādivadyenaiva saṃbandhaḥ kriyate sa evārtha iti nivāraṇaṃ nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: For when someone tells another that the meaning of the word 'cow' (<s>go</s>) is horse or <s>gavaya</s> (wild cow), others correct him: 'that is not its meaning; its meaning is what possesses a dewlap and the like.' And on the view that the relation is created [by convention], just as with <s>Devadatta</s> and the like, [whatever meaning] is established by the very person who creates the relation would be the meaning — so correction would be impossible.

children.text: tasmānna tāvadarvācīnaḥ puruṣā asya śabdasyāyamartha iti vadantopi tatsaṃbandhakartṛtvenāśaṅkanīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, contemporary persons, even when saying 'this is the meaning of this word,' are not to be suspected of being the creators of that relation.

children.text: yadiparamevaṃ syāt sargādikāle bhagavatā prajāpatinā sarvameva sthāvarajaṅgamaṃ dharmādharmau ta sṛṣṭvā saṃvyavahārāya ca śabdānāmarthaiḥ saṃbandhaṃ kṛtvā dharmādharmapratipādanāya ca kṛtasaṃbandhaiḥ padairvedānkṛtvātmajebhyo marīcyādibhyaḥ śabdārthasaṃbandho vedāśca pratipāditāstairapyanyebhyastairapyanyebhya ityevaṃ pūrvapūrvebhyaḥ pratipadyottarottareṣāṃ śabdārthapratipattirvyavahāraśceti* ////
children.translated_text: If, however, the case were thus: at the beginning of creation, the blessed <s>Prajāpati</s>, having created all movable and immovable [beings] as well as <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, having established the relation of words with their meanings for the sake of everyday usage, and having composed the <s>Vedas</s> with words whose relations had been established for the purpose of communicating <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, taught the word-meaning relation and the <s>Vedas</s> to his sons <s>Marīci</s> and the others; and they to others, and they to yet others — thus, from predecessors to successors, the understanding of word-meaning and everyday usage [has been transmitted].

body.translated_text: the making of the relation — for this is the statement of an already established relation.

body.text:
tadapyayuktam /
itthaṃbhāve pramāṇābhāvāt prathamaśrutāvapratītireva pramāṇaṃ sāmayikatve hyapratipannasamayānāmapratītiḥ pratipannasamayānāṃ ca pratītirdevadattādiśabdavadupapannā bhavati, svābhāvike tu pratyāyakatve
body.translated_text: That too is improper. Because there is no means of knowledge for such [conventional] status. In the first hearing itself, the very non-cognition is the means of knowledge; for if [word-meaning relation] were conventional, those who have not learned the convention would have non-cognition, and those who have learned it would have cognition —

body.text:
prathamaśravaṇe 'pi pratītiḥ syāditicenna /
svābhāvikamapi pratyāyakatvamavagataṃ sadarthapratipattau nimittaṃ nāpratipannamiti yuktaiva prathamaśravaṇer'thasyāpratītiḥ /
na ca sargādirnāma kaścitkālo 'sti, sarvadāhīdṛśameva jagaditi dṛṣṭānusārādavagantumucitam /
na tu sa kālo 'bhūt yadā sarvamidaṃ nāsīditi /
pramāṇābhāvāt /
mantrārthavādetihāsapurāṇādiḥ pramāṇamiti cet /
na /
vedānāṃ pauruṣeyasaṃbandhāpekṣāṇāṃ svayaṃ ca pauruṣeyāṇāṃ śākyādigranthavadatīndriyārthe prāmāṇyāsaṃbhavāt /

children.text: tadaprāmāmye ca tanmūlānāṃ dharmaśāstrīdīnāṃ dūranirastameva prāmāṇyam /
children.translated_text: And if that [Veda] were invalid, then the validity of <s>dharmaśāstra</s> and the like, which are based on it, would be far removed indeed.

children.text: sarvābhāve ca sṛṣṭirapi na saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: And if everything were non-existent, even creation would not be possible.

children.text: mṛttatantvādyupādānena hi ghaṭādīnyupādīyante /
children.translated_text: For pots and the like are produced with clay, thread, and other material causes.

children.text: sarvābhāve hi kenopādena sarvamidamupādeyam //
children.translated_text: For if everything were non-existent, by what material cause would all this be produced? //

body.translated_text: If [one objects:] 'There would be cognition even at first hearing' — no. Even natural capacity to convey [meaning], once known, serves as a cause for the apprehension of meaning; it is not the case that what is not known [can serve thus] — hence cognition at first hearing is justified —

body.text: advaitamatena pūrvapakṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection from the <s>Advaita</s> position:

body.text:
syānmatam /
ātmaivaiko jagadādāvāsīt sa eva svecchayā vyomādi pariṇamati bījamiva vṛkṣarūpeṇa, cidekarasaṃ brahma kathaṃ jaḍarūpeṇa pariṇamatīti cet /
na paramārthataḥ pariṇāmaṃ brūmaḥ kintvapariṇamate pariṇatavadekameva sadanekadhā mukhamivādarśādiṣvavidyāvaśādvivartamānamātmaivātmānaṃ cidrūpaṃ jaḍarūpamivādvitīyaṃ sadvitīyamiva paśyati /

children.text: seyamavidyopādānā svapnaprapañcavanmahadādiprapañcasṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: This creation of the manifold world beginning with <s>mahat</s> and the like has <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) as its material cause, like the manifold world of dreams.

children.text: tathāca sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma, ātmaivedaṃ sarvaṃ naiha nānāsti kiñcane ityādayo bahavo 'dvetavādāḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus: 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>,' 'All this is the <s>Ātman</s> alone,' 'There is no diversity here whatsoever' — and many other statements affirming non-duality.

children.text: tathā indro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate iti bhedāvagatervyaktameva māyānibandhanatvaṃ darśitam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, '<s>Indra</s> moves in many forms through <s>māyā</s>' — here, since the cognition of difference is clearly shown to be based on <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: tathā lokāstaṃ parāduryo 'nyatrātmano lokānvidetyādinānātmadarśane nindā mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyatīti ca nānātvadarśananindā sarvamidamadvitīyameva brahma pāramārthikaṃ bhedadṛṣṭiścāvidyopādānetyetamarthaṃ prakaṭayatīti //
children.translated_text: Likewise, 'Those worlds pierce him who knows worlds other than the <s>Ātman</s>' — thus there is censure of seeing non-self. 'He goes from death to death who sees diversity here' — thus there is censure of seeing multiplicity. 'All this —'

body.translated_text: It may be thought: The one <s>Ātman</s> alone existed in the beginning of the world; He alone by His own will transforms into space and the like, as a seed into the form of a tree. If [one asks:] How does <s>Brahman</s>, which is of the uniform nature of consciousness, transform into an inert form? —

body.text: uktādvaitamatakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the aforementioned <s>Advaita</s> position:

body.text:
kimidānīmasannevāyaṃ prapañcaḥ /
omiticet /
na /
pratyakṣavirodhāt /
tathā ca pratyakṣaṃ prapañcasadbhāvagrāhakaṃ pratyakṣasūtre /
nacāgame pratyakṣabādhaḥ saṃbhavati pratyakṣasya śīghrapravṛttatvena sarvebhyo balīyastvāt /
na ca paurvāparyanyāyena pravṛttameva pratyakṣamāgamena paścādbādhyata iti vācyam /
āgamasya pratyakṣeṇa pravṛttivirodhāt /
āgamapravṛttisamaye 'pi hi bedaprapañcamupadarśayat pratyakṣamāgamapravṛttimeva niruṇaddhi /
yathā khalūtpattumupakramamāṇa eva ghaṭo daṇḍenāhanyamāno notpattuṃ prabhavati tathāgamopi /
kiñca prapañcābhāvaṃ pratiyatāvaśyamāgamopi prapañcāntargatatvādasadrūpatayā pratyetavyaḥ /
kathaṃ
body.translated_text: Is this manifold world then simply non-existent? If yes — no. Because it contradicts perception. And thus, perception that grasps the reality of the manifold world [is established] in the <s>sūtra</s> on perception. And perception cannot be contradicted by scripture —

body.text: cāgamenaivāgamasyābhāvaḥ pratīyeta, asadrūpatayā hi pratīyamāno na kasyacidapyarthasya pramāṇaṃ syāt, prāmāṇye vā nāsatvam //
body.translated_text: And [if] the non-existence of scripture itself were to be known through scripture, then, being cognized as having a non-existent form, it would not be a means of knowledge for anything at all; or if it were valid, then it would not be non-existent. //

children.text: kaścitpunarāha prapañcasya nāsatvaṃ brūmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Someone further says: We do not assert the non-existence of the manifold world.

children.text: pratyaśrakṣādi pramāṇataḥ siddhatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because it is established through means of knowledge such as perception and the like.

children.text: nāpi paramārthataḥ satvaṃ ātmajñānena bādhyamānatvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor [do we assert] its ultimate reality, because it is sublated by the knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s>.

children.text: tasmātsadasadbhāvanirvācyo 'yaṃ prapañca iti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this manifold world is indescribable as either existent or non-existent. //

body.text:
tadidamasāram /
sato 'nyatvamevāsatvam, tadyadi prapañcaḥ sanna bhavati vyaktamasannevāyam, asatvābhāve vāsatvāpattiḥ, sadasatvayorekaniṣedhasyetaravidhināntarīyakatvāt /
na ca vidhādvayarahite vidhāntaraṃ sambhavati athāpi yanna kadācitpratīyate tadasat, yathā śaśaviṣāṇam,yatpratītaṃ kadācidbādhyate tatsat yathātmatatvaṃ, prapañcastu pratīyamānatvādbādhyamānatvācca bhāvābhāvābhyāsanirvācca iti matam /
tadanupapannam, lokavirodhāt /
yaddhi pratītaṃ bādhyate mṛgatoyapajjusarpādi tadasadeveti hi laukikī prasiddhiḥ /
na hi śaśaviṣāṇādīnāṃ mṛgatoyādīnāṃ ca kaścidviśeṣo loke, soyaṃ prapañcopi bādyate cet asanneveti nānirvācitatvam /

children.text: athāpi lokaprasiddhimanādṛtya vṛddhayādivatparibhāṣārūpeṇānirvācya ityucyate, tathāpyayuktam - prapañcasya bādhyatvābhāvāt, na tāvatsaṃsārāvasthāyāmāgamena bādhaḥ sambhavatītyuktam /
children.translated_text: Even if, disregarding common understanding, it is said to be 'indescribable' in the manner of a technical convention like <s>vṛddhi</s> and the like — even so, it is improper, because the manifold world is not sublated. For in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>, there is no scripture [that sublates it] —

children.text: muktasya tu bādhakajñānaṃ nāśaṅkanīyameva pralīnasarvakaraṇatvāt, karaṇābhāve ca jñānāsambhavāt /
children.translated_text: And for the liberated one, sublating knowledge is not even to be apprehended, since all sense-organs have dissolved; and in the absence of sense-organs, knowledge is impossible.

children.text: nacāsmaryamāṇasya prapañcasyābhāvaḥ śakyate pratyetum /
children.translated_text: And the non-existence of the manifold world that is not being remembered cannot be cognized.

children.text: naca tasyāmavasthāyāṃ sambhavati smaraṇamaṃ sarvasaṃskārāṇāmucchinnatvāt tasmānna bādhasambhavaḥ //
children.translated_text: And in that state, remembering is not possible, since all impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) have been destroyed. Therefore, sublation is not possible. //

body.translated_text: This is without substance. Being other than existent is simply non-existence. If the manifold world is not existent, it is clearly non-existent; and in the absence of non-existence, existence would follow. For when one of the pair — existence and non-existence — is negated, the other —

body.text: yaccāvidyākṛto 'yaṃ prapañca iti, sā kasya na brahmaṇastasya svacchavidyārūpatvāt /

children.text: nahi bhāskare timirasyāvakāśaḥ sambhavati /
children.translated_text: For there is no possibility of darkness in the sun.

children.text: naca jīvānām /
children.translated_text: Nor of the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls).

children.text: teṣāṃ brahmātirekeṇābāvāt bhrāntyabhāvādeva ca tatkāraṇabhūtaṃ vastvantaramapyanupapannameva /
children.translated_text: Since they do not exist apart from <s>Brahman</s>; and since delusion itself does not exist, any other entity that would be its cause is also untenable.

children.text: brahmātirekeṇa bhrāntijñānaṃ tatkāraṇaṃ cāpyupagacchatāmadvaitahāniḥ* ////
children.translated_text: For those who admit deluded knowledge apart from <s>Brahman</s>, and its cause as well — for them the loss of non-duality [follows]. ////

body.translated_text: And as for [the claim] that this manifold world is produced by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — whose [ignorance is it]? Not <s>Brahman</s>'s, since its nature is pure knowledge.

body.text:
tatkiṅkṛtā ca brahmaṇo vidyā, na hi kāraṇāntaramasti /
svābhāvikīticet kathaṃ vidyāsvabhāvamavidyāsvabhāvaṃ syāt /
svābhāvikatve cāsyāḥ kena vināśaḥ syāt /

children.text: āgamikaṃ dhyānādi tajjanyaṃ vā svarūpajñānaṃ brahmāvidyāṃ nāśayatīti cet, na, nahyāgamo vā dhyānādayo vā tajjanyaṃ vā jñānaṃ nityajñānātmakabrahmātiriktamasti yadavidyāṃ nāśayet /
children.translated_text: If [one says] that scripturally prescribed meditation and the like, or the self-knowledge born from them, destroys <s>Brahman</s>'s <s>avidyā</s> — no. For neither scripture, nor meditation and the like, nor the knowledge born from them, [can exist] apart from <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is eternal knowledge —

children.text: tadvaramasmānmāyāvādānmāhāyānikavādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Better then is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> doctrine than this <s>Māyāvāda</s>.

children.text: yatra nīlapītādivaicitryaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvo baddhamuktādivyavasthā ca saṃtānabhedena samarthyate /
children.translated_text: Where the variety of blue, yellow, and the like, the causal relation, and the distinction of bound and liberated are explained through the difference of [mental] streams (<s>saṃtāna</s>).

children.text: nityamekarasaṃ niṣprapañcamātmānamupeyuṣāṃ tu samastalokavedajavyavahārocchittireva syāt* ////
children.translated_text: But for those who resort to the <s>Ātman</s> as eternal, of uniform essence, and devoid of the manifold — the complete destruction of all worldly and Vedic usage would follow. ////

body.translated_text: And what is the cause of <s>Brahman</s>'s knowledge? For there is no other cause. If [one says] 'it is natural' — then how would what is of the nature of knowledge be of the nature of ignorance? And if it is natural, by what would its destruction be accomplished —

body.text:
yadapyāhuḥ- ajñānajanyaḥ prapañco jñānena vināśyate mṛgatoyavat svapnaprapañcavacceti /
tadapyayuktam- yadi kulālādivyāpārasthānīyenājñānena ghaṭavadutpannaḥ prapañco musalasthānīyena jñānena
body.translated_text: And what they say — 'the manifold world, born of ignorance, is destroyed by knowledge, like the water of a mirage, like the world of a dream' — that too is improper. If, by <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance) standing in the place of the activity of a potter and the like, [the world] is produced like a pot —

body.text: nāśyate, tathāpi nāsatvaṃ prapañcasya syāt, utpattivināśayogādinityatāmātraṃ syānnātyantābhāvaḥ* ////
body.translated_text: even if it were destroyed, the non-existence of the manifold world would not follow; there would only be non-eternality due to the possibility of origination and destruction, not absolute non-existence. ////

body.text: kena ca jñānena nāśaḥ, nātmajñānena, virodhābhāvāt /

children.text: niṣprapañcātmajñāneneticet, na, tatrātmajñānāṃśasyāvirodhāt /
children.translated_text: If [one says] 'by the knowledge of the self as devoid of the manifold' — no, because there is no contradiction regarding the self-knowledge aspect therein.

children.text: niṣprapañcatvajñānaṃ vināśakamiti pāriśeṣyādāpannam- prapañcābhāvaśca niṣprapañcatvaṃ, na ca vidyamānaṃ prapañce tadabhāvajñānamutpattumarhati /
children.translated_text: If 'the knowledge of being-devoid-of-the-manifold is the destroyer' follows by elimination — but being-devoid-of-the-manifold is the absence of the manifold, and the knowledge of that absence cannot arise while the manifold is present.

children.text: jñānena hyutpannena prapañco nāśayitavyaḥ prāk ca jñānātsadrūpa eva prapañcastisminsadrūpe 'vasthite kathaṃ tadabhāvaviṣayasya jñānasyotpattiḥ /
children.translated_text: For the manifold is to be destroyed by knowledge once it arises; but prior to knowledge, the manifold exists in its real form; and while it persists in its real form, how can knowledge whose object is its absence arise?

children.text: tatra jñānotpattau satyāṃ prapañcasya nāśaḥ, tadvināśe ca sati tadabhāvaviṣayajñānotpattiritītaretarāśrayatvam* ////
