children.translated_text: If knowledge arises, the manifold is destroyed; and if it is destroyed, then knowledge having its absence as object arises — thus there is mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>). ////

body.translated_text: And by what knowledge is it destroyed? Not by self-knowledge, because there is no contradiction [between the two].

children.text: etena mṛgatṛṣṇikājalasya jñānavināśyatvaṃ pratyūḍham /
children.translated_text: By this, the claim that mirage-water is destroyed by knowledge is also refuted.

children.text: na hi tajjalaṃ sat paścānnāśyate prāgapi hi tatra naiva jalaṃ, ajalameva hi raśmiprataptamūṣaraṃ bhrāntyā jalātmanāvagataṃ paścādbādhakena yathāvasthitarūpamavagamyata ityalamanena bālajalpitena //
children.translated_text: For that water does not exist [as real] and is later destroyed; rather, even before, there was no water there at all. The desert, heated by [sun]rays, was apprehended through delusion as having the nature of water; and afterwards, by sublating [knowledge], the true state —

body.text: ityadvaitamatanirāsaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus the refutation of the <s>Advaita</s> position. //

body.text: ardhajaratīyādvaitavādena pūrvapakṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Objection from the 'half-old' (<s>ardhajaratīya</s>) <s>Advaita</s> view: //

children.text: kecittvaupaniṣadāḥ paramārthata evātmā prapañcarūpeṇa svecchayā pariṇamatīti manyante,tathā ca sā sadeva somyedamagra āsīdekamevādvitīya tadaikṣata bahusyāṃ prajāyeya ityekasyaiva sanmātrarūpatayā prāgavasthitātmano 'nekavyomādibhedabhinnaprapañcarūpeṇa bījasyeva pariṇāmo darśitaḥ, tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūta ityaupaniṣadāṃ vādāḥ purāṇavādāścāsminnarthe śataśo dṛśyante /
children.translated_text: Some followers of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, however, hold that the <s>Ātman</s> in ultimate reality transforms by its own will into the form of the manifold world. And thus, 'That which existed, O <s>Somya</s>, in the beginning was Being alone, one without a second; It willed: Let me become many —'

children.text: puruṣa evedaṃ sarvaṃ neha nānāsti kiñcana ityādi tu dharmibhedābāvābhiprāyam, tadyathaiko vṛkṣaḥ prādeśamātrādūrdhvaṃ nānāśākho 'vasthito dūrasthairnānāvṛkṣā iti, tathā nāmarūpaprapañcaṃ nānārūpaṃ paśyatāṃ, mūlakāraṇasyaikasyātmano 'yaṃ nānārūpaḥ pariṇāma ityevamajānatāṃ tattvakathanārthā evaṃvidhā vādāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'All this is the <s>Puruṣa</s> alone; there is no diversity here whatsoever' and the like — this refers to the absence of difference in the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). Just as a single tree, from above a span, stands with many branches, yet those standing far away [perceive it as one] —

children.text: sarvamekasyaiva vistāro na kiñcidatra nānāstīti* ////
children.translated_text: everything is the expansion of one alone; nothing diverse exists here. ////

children.text: ye ca punarasattvavādāḥ prapañcaviṣayā avidyāvādā bhrāntivādā māyāvādāśca te sarve prapañcasyānityatvādaupacārikāḥ /
children.translated_text: And those statements affirming non-existence, concerning the manifold world — doctrines of <s>avidyā</s>, doctrines of delusion, doctrines of <s>māyā</s> — all those are figurative (<s>aupacārika</s>), due to the non-eternality of the manifold world.

children.text: yathā mṛgatoyarajjusarpasvapnaprapañcādayaḥ kiñcitkālamāvirbhūya paścādvilīyante tathā bhedaprapañcarūpo brahmapariṇāmo 'pyāvirbhavati vilīyate cetyāvirbhāvatirobhāvadharmakatvasāmyādasannityupacaryate, tasya cāsatkalpatve tadviṣayasya jñānasyāpi siddhyatyaupacārikaṃ bhrāntitvam /
children.translated_text: Just as mirage-water, rope-snake, dream-world and the like appear for some time and then dissolve — so too the transformation of <s>Brahman</s> in the form of the manifold of differences appears and dissolves — thus —

children.text: māyānibandhanatvaṃ ca indro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate ityādiṣu yuktamupacāreṇa vaktum /
children.translated_text: And the statement that [the world] is based on <s>māyā</s> — '<s>Indra</s> moves in many forms through <s>māyā</s>' and the like — can properly be stated figuratively.

children.text: ātmaivaikaḥ satyaḥ ici ca tasyaiva nityatvāducyate, yathā go aśvā eva paśavo 'nyetvapaśava iti tadevaṃ draṣṭavyam* ////
children.translated_text: And 'the <s>Ātman</s> alone is the one reality' — this is said because of its eternality. Just as 'cows and horses alone are animals; others are non-animals' — thus it should be understood. ////

body.text:
yastvevaṃvidhānvādānyathāśrutārthāngṛhṇāti sa paśvantareṣvapaśutvavādaṃ ādityo yūpaḥ ityādi ca yathāśrutaṃ gṛhṇīyāt /
atha tatra pramāṇāntaravirodhaḥ so 'trāpi samānaḥ /
athārthavādatvāttatra na yathāśrutārthagrahaṇaṃ, tadapi samānam /
prapañcasyāpyasatyatvaṃ vairāgyajananārtham, ātmanaśca paramārthatvaṃ mumukṣūṇāmutsāhajananārthaṃ /
vispaṣṭaṃ caitanmṛtpiṇḍavikāradṛṣṭāntadarśanāt /
tataśca yathā kāraṇabhūtamṛtpiṇḍajñānena mṛnmayo vikāraḥ sarvo vijñāto bhavati śarāvādivikāro hi vācārambhaṇaṃ nāmadheyamātraṃ mṛttikasyaiva satyaṃ, evaṃ prapañcasyeva satyaṃ, evaṃ prapañcopi sadvijñānena vijñāto bhavati vikāro hi vācārambhaṇaṃ nāmadheyamātraṃ sadityeva satyamityukte jñāyata etat yathāvirbhāvatirobhāvadharmā nānāvidho vikāraḥ śarāvādiḥ prapañco mṛttikā ca sarvatrānapāyinī teṣāṃ kāraṇaṃ kāryakāraṇayoścāvasthāmātrabhedātsvarūpabhedābhāvātkāraṇajñānena tatsarvaṃ kāryamavasthābhedenājñātamapi svarūpeṇa jñātaṃ bhavati /

children.text: tathā prapañcopyāvirbhāvatirobhāvadharmānavasthāyī tatkāraṇaṃ cātmā sadrūpaḥ sarvānuyāyī nāpāyadharmā /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the phenomenal world too is characterized by appearance and disappearance, non-permanent; and its cause, the self, having the nature of Being (<s>sat</s>), pervading all, does not have the character of departing.

children.text: tasminvijñāte sarvaṃ tadātmakamavijñātamapi vyāsarūpeṇa samāsena jñātaṃ bhavatītyetadatra vivakṣitamiti, tasmādekasyaivātmanaḥ pariṇāmo 'yaṃ bhedaprapañco nanvasanneva /
children.translated_text: When that [self] is known, everything that is of its nature, even when not known in its expanded form, becomes known in summary — this is what is intended here. Therefore, this manifold world of difference is a transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) of the one self alone, and is not at all unreal.

children.text: asatve hi kathaṃ sadvijñānena vijñātaḥ syācchaśaviṣāṇavat /
children.translated_text: For if it were unreal, how could it become known by the knowledge of Being — like hare's horns?

children.text: na hi mṛtpiṇḍe vijñāte sati śaśaviṣāṇaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati tathā prapañcopi syāt, tatastu prastutahānireva syāt ekopyātmāntaḥkaraṇopādhibhedādbhinno jīva ityucyate jīvabhedācca bandhamuktivyavasthāpyupapanneti* ////
children.translated_text: For when the lump of clay is known, hare's horns do not become known; similarly, the phenomenal world too [would not become known if unreal]. Rather, there would be a departure from the very topic at hand. Even the one self, due to the distinction of inner-organ adjuncts (<s>antaḥkaraṇopādhi</s>), is called the different individual soul (<s>jīva</s>); and through the difference of individual souls, the arrangement of bondage and liberation too is justified. ////

body.translated_text: But one who takes such [<s>Upaniṣadic</s>] statements as conveying their literal meaning — he would have to take literally statements like 'non-animal-hood in other animals' and '<s>Āditya</s> (the sun) is the sacrificial post' and the like as well. If [you say] there is contradiction with other means of knowledge there — that is equally the case here. If [you say] there, because they are <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passages), the literal meaning is not taken — that is equally [applicable] here. The unreality of the phenomenal world is for generating dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), and the supreme reality of the self is for generating enthusiasm in those seeking liberation. And this is clearly seen from the illustration of the lump of clay and its modifications. Thus, just as by the knowledge of the lump of clay that is the cause, all its modifications become known — for modifications like dishes and the like are mere verbal designation, a name only, clay alone being the reality — so too the phenomenal world becomes known through the knowledge of Being (<s>sat</s>); for modification is mere verbal designation, a name only, Being alone is the reality — from this it is understood: just as the various modifications like dishes and the like, characterized by appearance and disappearance, are the phenomenal world, and clay, persisting everywhere without departing, is their cause, and since between cause and effect there is merely a difference of state, not a difference of essential nature, by the knowledge of the cause all that effect, even when not known through the difference of state, becomes known in its essential nature.

children.text: tadidamayuktam /
children.translated_text: This is unjustified.

children.text: cidrūpasyātmano jaḍarūpapariṇāmāsaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: Because transformation into an insentient form is impossible for the self, which is of the nature of consciousness (<s>cit</s>).

children.text: ekatve cātmanaḥ sarvaśarīre me duḥkhamiti, pāde me mukhaṃ śirasi me vedanetivat sarvasukhaduḥkhopalabdhiśca syāt /
children.translated_text: And if the self were one, in all bodies there would be apprehension of all pleasure and pain — just as 'my pain is in the foot,' 'my face is on the head,' 'I feel' — so too all pleasure and pain would be apprehended.

children.text: antaḥkaraṇopādhibhedādabhinno jīva ityucyate jīvabhedācca bandhamuktivyavasthāpyupapanneti* ////
children.translated_text: Due to the distinction of inner-organ adjuncts (<s>antaḥkaraṇopādhi</s>), the one [self] is called the different individual soul (<s>jīva</s>); and through the difference of individual souls, the arrangement of bondage and liberation too is justified. ////

body.text:
tadidamayuktam /
cidrūpasyātmano jaḍarūpapariṇāmāsaṃbhavāt /
ekatve cātmanaḥ sarvaśarīreṣu pratasaṃdhānaṃ syāt- devadatto 'haṃ yajñadatto 'hameveti, tathā devadattaśarīre me sukhaṃ yajñadattaśarīre me duḥkhamiti, pāde me sukhaṃ śirasi me
body.translated_text: This is unjustified. Because transformation into an insentient form is impossible for the self, which is of the nature of consciousness. And if the self were one, there would be recognition (<s>pratisaṃdhāna</s>) across all bodies — 'I am <s>Devadatta</s>, I am <s>Yajñadatta</s>'; likewise, 'I have pleasure in <s>Devadatta's</s> body, I have pain in <s>Yajñadatta's</s> body' — just as 'I have pleasure in the foot, in the head I

children.text: vedanetivat sarvasukhaduḥkhopalabdhiśca syāt /
children.translated_text: feel' — so too all pleasure and pain would be apprehended.

children.text: antaḥkaraṇabhedādvyavastheticet /
children.translated_text: [If one says] 'the arrangement [of distinct experiences] is due to the difference of inner organs (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>)' —

children.text: acetanatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because [the inner organ] is insentient.

children.text: nahyantaḥkaraṇaṃ sukhaduḥkhe anubhavati acetanatvāt, ātmā tvanubhavitā sa ca sarvatraika iti kaḥ pratisaṃdhānaṃ vārayet, tasmādidamapi nātīva sundaramiti //
children.translated_text: For the inner organ does not experience pleasure and pain, since it is insentient; but the self is the experiencer, and it is one everywhere — so who would prevent recognition [across bodies]? Therefore, this too is not very elegant. //

body.text: ityātmapariṇāmavādanirāsaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [concludes] the refutation of the doctrine of self-transformation (<s>ātmapariṇāmavāda</s>). //

body.text: sāṃkhyamatena pūrvapakṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) according to the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine:

body.text:
ātmabhedaṃ prakṛtipariṇāmaṃ ca jagat sāṃkhyā manyante /
dvividhaṃ ca sāṃkhyaṃ nirīśvaraṃ seśvaraṃ ca /
body.translated_text: The <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> hold that the world is [characterized by] plurality of selves and transformation of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). And <s>Sāṃkhya</s> is of two kinds: without God (<s>nirīśvara</s>) and with God (<s>seśvara</s>).

body.text:
nīrīśvaravādistāvagadāhuḥ- prakṛtiracetanā triguṇātmikā pradhānaśabdābhidheya mahadādiviśeṣaparyantena prapañcarūpeṇa cetanānāmupabhogāya pariṇāmatīti /
seśvaravādino 'pyevamāhuḥ, iyāṃstu viśeṣaḥ- puruṣaśabdābhidheyamīśvaraṃ kleśakarmavipākāśayairaparāmṛṣṭamāśritya prakṛtirjagatsṛjatīti /
yathā hi saṃskṛtaṃ kṣetramadhiṣṭhāya tatsaṃparkavaśādbījamaṅkurādikrameṇa mahāntaṃ vṛkṣamārabhate tathā sarvavyāpinī prakṛtistatsaṃparkavaśānmahadahaṅkāratanmātrādikrameṇa pariṇamantī viśeṣāntaṃ prapañcamārabhaca iti /
itihāsapurāṇeṣvapi prāyeṇaitadeva matam /
seyaṃ prakṛtyupādānā sṛṣṭiḥ, īśvarastu nimittamātram /
kṣetrajñāstu bhoktāraḥ, prakṛtireva tu sarvakāryāṇāṃ kartrīti bhogyā /
sā ca sarvatraikā bhoktṝṇāṃ ca bhedādbaddhamuktavyavasthopapattiḥ /
tathā ca- ajāmekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇāṃ bahvīḥ prajā janayantīṃ sarūpāḥ /
ajo hyeko juṣamāṇo 'nuśete jahātyenāṃ bhuktabhogamajo 'nyaḥ iti vyaktameva bhogyāyāḥ dāstarhyaipaniṣadāḥ kathaṃ, availakṣaṇyeneti brūmaḥ- bhedaśabdo hi vailakṣaṇyavacano loke prasiddhaḥ /
tathāhi susadṛśeṣu vaktāro bhavanti, nāsyāsya ca kaścidbhedo 'stīti, tathātmanāmapi narapaśutiryagbhedabhinnaśarīravartināṃ śarīrasaṃbandhamapohya kevalaṃ naijarūpeṇa nirūpyamāṇānāṃ padmarajaḥparamāṇudvayavanna kiñcidapi vailakṣaṇyamastītyanenābhiprāyeṇaikatvavādā nānātvaniṣedhavādāśca /
etadabhiprāyameva caitadapi bhadavadvāsudevavacanam- vidyāvinayasaṃpanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini /

children.text: śuni caiva śvapāke ca paṇḍitāḥ samadarśinaḥ iti /
children.translated_text: 'in a dog, and in a dog-cooker (<s>śvapāka</s>), the wise see the same.'

children.text: tathaiva indro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īryate iti svayamavilakṣaṇo 'pyātmā narapaśvādivicitraśarīrasaṃparkavaśādbhrāntyā svayamapi vilakṣaṇarūpaḥ pratīyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, '<s>Indra</s> moves through <s>māyā</s> in many forms' — the meaning is: the self, though itself without dissimilarity, due to contact with the various bodies of humans, animals, and the like, is mistakenly perceived as itself having different forms.

children.text: ye ca bhuktānāṃ kṣetrajñānāmīśvareṇa sahaikatvādāstepyatyantasāmyādvailakṣaṇyābhāvācca /
children.translated_text: And those [statements] about the identity of the liberated <s>kṣetrajñas</s> with God — those too are due to utmost similarity and absence of dissimilarity.

children.text: tathā ca śrutyantaram, yadā paśyaḥ paśyate rukmavarṇaṃ kartāramīśaṃ puruṣaṃ brahmayonim //
children.translated_text: And another <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'When the seer sees the gold-colored one, the maker, the Lord, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the womb of <s>Brahman</s>' —

body.translated_text: The proponent of the godless [<s>Sāṃkhya</s>] says: <s>Prakṛti</s>, which is insentient and constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s>, designated by the word '<s>pradhāna</s>' (the primal), transforms into the form of the phenomenal world — from <s>mahat</s> (the great) onwards to the specific elements — for the enjoyment of the sentient [souls]. The theistic [<s>Sāṃkhya</s>] proponents say the same, but with this distinction: depending on God, designated by the word '<s>puruṣa</s>' (person), who is untouched by afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), <s>karma</s>, fruition (<s>vipāka</s>), and latent impressions (<s>āśaya</s>), <s>Prakṛti</s> creates the world. For just as a seed, relying upon a cultivated field, through contact with it, produces a great tree through the sequence of sprout and the like — so too <s>Prakṛti</s>, all-pervading, through contact with that [God], transforming through the sequence of <s>mahat</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, <s>tanmātras</s>, and the like, brings about the phenomenal world ending in the specific [elements]. And in the <s>Itihāsas</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s> too, this is generally the doctrine. This creation has <s>Prakṛti</s> as its material cause, and God is merely the efficient cause. The <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (field-knowers, i.e., individual souls) are the experiencers, while <s>Prakṛti</s> alone is the agent of all effects and thus the object of enjoyment. And that [<s>Prakṛti</s>] is one everywhere; and due to the difference of experiencers, the arrangement of the bound and the liberated is justified. As [the <s>Śvetāśvatara</s> says]: 'The unborn one (<s>ajā</s>), one, red-white-and-black, producing many offspring of similar form — one unborn [soul] lies with her, enjoying; another unborn [soul] leaves her, his enjoyment having been had.' Clearly the <s>Upaniṣads</s> [describe] the enjoyable [<s>Prakṛti</s>] — but how [can Upaniṣadic statements of non-difference be reconciled]? 'Through dissimilarity,' we say — for the word 'difference' (<s>bheda</s>) is well-known in the world as meaning dissimilarity. Thus, regarding things that are very similar, speakers say: 'there is no difference between this one and that one.' Similarly, even of selves — residing in bodies differentiated by the distinctions of human, animal, and beast — when examined merely in their own nature, setting aside bodily connection, there is not even the slightest dissimilarity, like two atoms of lotus pollen. With this intention are the statements of oneness and denials of plurality. And with this very intention is the statement of the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>: 'In a learned and humble <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, in a cow, in an elephant,'

children.text: tadā vidvānpuṇyapāpe vidhūya nirañcanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyamupaiti itīśvarasādṛśyāpattimeva muktasya darśayati /
children.translated_text: 'then the wise one, shaking off merit and demerit, stainless, attains the supreme equality' — this shows that the liberated [soul] attains similarity to God, not identity.

children.text: tathā bhagavatā vāsudevenāpyuktam- idaṃ jñānamupāśritya mama sādharmyamāgatāḥ //
children.translated_text: Likewise, the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s> too has said: 'Having resorted to this knowledge, having attained similarity of nature (<s>sādharmya</s>) with Me —'

body.text: sarge 'pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca iti* ////
body.translated_text: 'they are not born even at creation, nor are they distressed at dissolution.'

children.text: yattu mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ iti bhagavadvacanaṃ tatsvāmibhṛtyabhāvaparam- yathā khalvamātyā rājñoṃśā vyapadiśyante tathā jīvopīśvarāṃśa ityucyate /
children.translated_text: As for the statement of the Lord — 'My own part (<s>aṃśa</s>), eternal, having become a living being in the world of the living' — that pertains to the master-servant relation: just as ministers are called parts of the king, so the <s>jīva</s> is called a part of God.

children.text: anyathā jīvatvanāśātsanātanatvānupapattiḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Otherwise, since <s>jīvahood</s> would be destroyed [if the <s>jīva</s> were literally a part of <s>Brahman</s>], the eternality [stated in the verse] would be unjustified. ////

children.text: yānyapi vibhedajanake jñāne nāśamātyantikaṃ gate /
children.translated_text: 'When the knowledge that generates distinction is completely destroyed,'

children.text: ātmano brahmaṇo bhedamasantaṃ kaḥ kariṣyati ityādīni purāṇavacanāni teṣāyamevārthaḥ- vailakṣaṇyamātmano brahmaṇaścānyatvamatyantamavidyamānamevājñānanimittamajñāne vinaṣṭe svayameva vilīyata iti /
children.translated_text: 'who will create the non-existent difference between the self and <s>Brahman</s>?' — and the like <s>Purāṇa</s> statements have this meaning: the dissimilarity between the self and <s>Brahman</s>, their otherness, which is utterly non-existent, is caused by ignorance; when ignorance is destroyed, it dissolves by itself.

children.text: vispaṣṭaṃ hi parāparapuruṣayorbhede gītādipūpadarśitaḥ- uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the difference between the higher and the lower <s>puruṣa</s> is clearly shown in the <s>Gītā</s> and the like: 'But the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> is another, called the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>);'

children.text: upadraśaṣṭānumantā ca kartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ //
children.translated_text: 'the witness, the approver, the consenter, the agent, the enjoyer, the Great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>);'

children.text: paramātmeti cāpyukto dehe 'sminpuruṣaḥparaḥ iti /
children.translated_text: 'and the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, called the Supreme Self, in this body.'

children.text: alamatidūraṃ gatvā /
children.translated_text: Enough of going too far.

children.text: tasmātprakṛtyupādāneyaṃ prapañcasṛṣṭiriti nānupādānopālambhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this creation of the phenomenal world has <s>Prakṛti</s> as its material cause — so there is no reproach of [there being] no material cause. //

body.text: sāṃkhyamatakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine:

body.text: atrābhidhīyate- kathaṃ khalvekarūpā prakṛtirnarapaśutiryagbhedabhinnaṃ prapañcamārabhate nahyavilakṣaṇaṃ
body.translated_text: Here it is replied: How indeed does <s>Prakṛti</s>, being of a single form, bring about the phenomenal world differentiated by the distinctions of human, animal, and beast? For an undifferentiated

body.text:
kāraṇaṃ vilakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ nirmātumarhati /
kṣetrajñagatadharmādharmasahāyavaicitryādvaicitryamitacet /
na /
antaḥkaraṇavṛttitvāddharmādarmayoḥ, antakaraṇasya ca kāryavargāntaḥpātitvāt sarvasya mahadādeḥ kāryasya prākṛtapratisaṃcāre prakṛtau vilīnatvāddharmādharmāvapi tasyāmavasthāyāmavidyamānāveveti na tadbalena vaicitryam /

children.text: mahadādivikārārambhe cāsyāḥ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ, svarūpameveticet sarvadā'rambhaprasaṅgastataḥ pralayānupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: And what is the cause for [<s>Prakṛti's</s>] commencing the transformation into <s>mahat</s> and the like? If [one says] 'its own nature' — then there would be the absurd consequence of creation at all times, and hence dissolution would be unjustified.

children.text: īśvarecchayā vikriyata icicet /
children.translated_text: [If one says] 'it transforms by God's will (<s>icchā</s>)' —

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: īśvarasya samastakleśarahitasyāpāstasamastakāmasyecchāsaṃbhāvāt, icchāyāścāpyantaḥkaraṇadharmatvāt tasminkāle tadasaṃbhavāt* ////
children.translated_text: Because will is not possible for God who is free from all afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) and whose all desires are completely extinguished; and because will too is a property of the inner organ, and at that time [of dissolution] that [inner organ] does not exist. ////

body.translated_text: cause cannot produce a differentiated effect. [If one says] 'the variety is due to the variety of the assistance of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> residing in the <s>kṣetrajñas</s>' — no, because <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are modifications of the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), and the inner organ is included among the effects. Since all effects from <s>mahat</s> onwards, at the time of the <s>prākṛta</s> dissolution, are dissolved into <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> too are non-existent in that state — so there is no variety by their force.

children.text: kiñca prākṛte pralaye prakṛtamātramātmānaśca kevalamavatiṣṭhante, sarve cātmāno nirviśeṣāḥ sarveṣāṃ caitanyamātrarūpatvāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, at the time of <s>prākṛta</s> dissolution, only <s>Prakṛti</s> and the selves remain alone; and all selves are without distinction, since all are of the mere nature of consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>).

children.text: naca dharmādharmakṛtamapi vailakṣaṇyamātmānāṃ saṃbhavati, tayorātmadharmatvābhāvāt, antaḥkaraṇavṛttitvāt tasya ca tadānīmabhāvādityuktam /
children.translated_text: Nor is even the dissimilarity produced by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> possible for the selves, since those two are not properties of the self — they are modifications of the inner organ, and that [inner organ] is non-existent at that time, as stated.

children.text: evaṃ ca dharmādharmarahiteṣu nirviśeśeṣu puruṣeṣvavasthiteṣu sargakāle prakṛtiḥ śarīrārambheṇātmano badhnātīti cet, ye pūrvasṛṣṭau sthitāḥ, ye ca brahmahatyākāriṇasteṣāṃ sarveṣāmaikavidhyameva syāt pūrvakṛtayordharmādharmayornaṣṭatvat* ////
children.translated_text: And thus, when the <s>puruṣas</s> are established as devoid of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> and without distinction — if [one says] at the time of creation, <s>Prakṛti</s> binds the selves by commencing bodies — then for those who were established in the previous creation and for those who were murderers of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, there would be uniformity for all, since the previously performed <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> have been destroyed. ////

body.text:
nanu nāśo nāma nātyantābhāvaḥ kintu kāraṇe kāryāṇāṃ tirobhāvamātraṃ vināśaḥ, utpattirapi vidyamānānameva kāraṇe kāryāṇāmāvirbhavamātraṃ sarvaṃ kāryāṇāṃ na syāt, tantubhyaḥ paṭo mṛtto ghaṭa iti /
yathāhuḥ- asadakaraṇādupādānagrahaṇātsarvasaṃbhavābhāvāt /

children.text: śaktasya śakyakaraṇātkāraṇabhāvācca satkāryam iti /
children.translated_text: 'because what is capable produces only what it is capable [of producing], and because of the nature of the cause — [therefore] the effect pre-exists (<s>satkārya</s>).'

children.text: tathā- nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ iti bhagavadvāsudevavacanam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the statement of the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>: 'The unreal never comes to be; the real never ceases to be.'

children.text: tasmātpralaye dharmādeḥ śaktyātmanavasthitatvāttadvaśena yuktaṃ sṛṣṭivaicitryam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, since <s>dharma</s> and the like subsist in the state of potency (<s>śakti</s>) during dissolution, the variety of creation is justified by their force.

children.text: naitadevam- na hi mṛtpiṇḍāvasthāyāṃ vā kapālāvasthāyāṃ vā ghaṭarūpamasti dṛśyādarśanavirodhāt* ////
children.translated_text: This is not so — for the form of the pot does not exist in the lump-state or in the potsherd-state, because of the contradiction of visibility and non-seeing. ////

body.translated_text: Objection: Destruction does not mean absolute non-existence; rather, the disappearance of effects into their cause alone is destruction, and origination too is merely the manifestation of effects already existing in the cause — so there would be no [real destruction] of any effects; cloth from threads, pot from clay, and so on. As they say: 'Because the non-existent cannot be produced, because of the dependence on a material cause, because of the impossibility of everything [arising] from everything,'

body.text: yattu nāsato vidyate bhāvaḥ iti vacanaṃ tadātmābhiprāyaṃ, pūrvatra hi natvevāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ //
body.translated_text: As for the statement 'the unreal never comes to be' — that has the self as its intended meaning. For previously [in the <s>Gītā</s>]: 'Never indeed was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these rulers of men;'

body.text: nacaiva nabhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param, ityātmanityatvaṃ
body.translated_text: 'nor will any of us ever cease to be hereafter' — the eternality of the self

body.text: pratipādayitumupakrāntamevānenocyate- nāvidyamānasyātmana utpattirna vidyamānasya vināśaḥ sarve evātmano 'nutpattivināśadharmāṇo nityā iti, na punaḥ kāryajātasya sarvasya nityatvābhiprāyam, asarvagatatvādanupalabdhivirodhāccetyuktam* ////
body.translated_text: was begun to be established; and with this same [intent] it is said: 'the non-existent self is not born, nor does the existent [self] perish; all selves are of the nature of non-origination and non-destruction, eternal.' But [this statement] is not intended [to convey] the eternality of all effects. [The <s>Sāṃkhya</s> view] has been refuted because [effects] are not omnipresent and because of the contradiction with non-apprehension. ////

children.text: yadi paramupādānopādeyayorabhedamāśritya mṛdātmanādau ghaṭo vyavasthita ityucyate, na ca tāvatā kāryasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Even if, relying on the non-difference of the material cause and the effect, it is said that the pot subsists in the clay-nature and the like — even so, the effect is not thereby accomplished.

children.text: nahi mṛdavasthena ghaṭe nodakāharaṇaṃ kriyate /
children.translated_text: For water cannot be fetched with [a pot] in the state of clay.

children.text: tathā dharmādharmāvapi svarūpeṇāvidyamānau prakṛtyātmanā sthitāvapi na svakāryāya paryāpyāviti na tadvaśena vaicitryasaṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, even though <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, non-existent in their own form, subsist in the <s>Prakṛti</s>-nature, they are not sufficient for their own effect — hence variety by their force is impossible.

children.text: pramāṇamapi mahadādikrameṇa prakṛtipariṇāme kiñcinnāsti- puruṣavacasāṃ pramāṇāntaragocarārthe pramāṇatvāsaṃbhavāt, vedānāmapi poruṣeyatvāditarapuruṣavacanavadapramāṇyāt* ////
children.translated_text: Moreover, there is no valid evidence whatsoever for the transformation of <s>Prakṛti</s> through the sequence of <s>mahat</s> and the like — since human statements cannot have validity regarding objects within the scope of other means of knowledge, and since the <s>Vedas</s> too, being of human origin [on the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> view], would be invalid like other human statements. ////

body.text:
yadi cu sṛṣṭipralayaparamparāmanādimaṅgīkṛtya pratisṛṣṭi sarveṣāṃ caiva nāmāni karmāṇi ca pṛthakpṛthak /
 vedaśabdebhya evādau pṛthaksaṃsthāśca nirmame ityādivacanaiḥ ṛtuliṅganyāyena nāmaprabhāvavyavahāravastūtpattyā śabdānāmanādyarthasaṃbaddhānāṃ vedānāṃ ca nityatvamāśritya prāmāṇyamaṅgīkriyate, tathāpyekasya prajāpateḥ saṃpradāyapravartakatve kṛtakāśaṅkā syādeva /
atha punaḥ aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi saṃpradāyapravartakāḥ ityādivacanānurodhena bahūnāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ sṛṣṭyantarādhītaṃ vedaṃ smaratāṃ suptapratibuddhanyāyena saṃpradāyapravartakatvamāśritya kṛtakāśaṅkāṃ nirasya nityatā samarthyeta, tathāpyanupādānāṃ jagannirmāṇamaśakyamabhyupagantuṃ, (prakṛtyādīnāṃ hyupādānatvaṃ nirastam /) aupaniṣadāstu sṛṣṭipralayavādāḥ paurāṇikāścārthavādatayā netavyāḥ /

children.text: bhavatu caivaṃ tathāpi nāsmākaṃ kācitkṣatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Let it be so even thus — still, there is no harm to our position,

children.text: saṃbandhanityatvavedaprāmāṇyayoravighātāt //
children.translated_text: since the eternality of the [word-meaning] relation and the validity of the Veda remain unimpaired. //

body.translated_text: If, however, accepting the beginningless series of creation and dissolution, [one holds that] at each creation, 'He fashioned separately the names and actions of all, and their distinct forms, from the words of the Veda alone' — and relying on such statements, the validity [of the Veda] is accepted on the basis of the eternality of the Vedas and of words that have been eternally connected with meanings, through the <s>ṛtuliṅganyāya</s> (analogy of seasonal signs) and by virtue of the arising of name-based, power-based, convention-based, and object-based [correspondences] — even so, if a single <s>Prajāpati</s> is the initiator of the tradition, the suspicion of [the Veda] being created would indeed arise. But if, in accordance with statements such as 'eighty-eight thousand are the initiators of the tradition,' the eternality [of the Veda] is maintained by relying on many great sages — who remember the Veda studied in a previous creation — being the initiators of the tradition, by the analogy of one who has slept and awakened (<s>suptapratibuddha</s>), and thus the suspicion of [the Veda] being created is removed — even so, the creation of the world without a material cause cannot be accepted (for the material-causality of <s>Prakṛti</s> and the like has been refuted). And the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> and <s>Purāṇic</s> doctrines of creation and dissolution are to be interpreted as <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory/laudatory passages).

body.text: iti sāṃkhyamatanirāsaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the refutation of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> view. //

body.text: vaiśeṣikamatena pūrvapakṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) according to the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> doctrine:

children.text: vaiśeṣikāstu- pauruṣeyatvameva śabdārthasaṃbandhānāṃ vedānāṃ cāṅgīkurvanto 'numānena sṛṣṭipralayāvīśvaraṃ ca siṣādhayiṣantaḥ prayogamāracayanti- trividhaṃ hi vastujātaṃ saṃpratipannacetanakartṛkaṃ ghaṭādi, saṃpratipannātatkartṛkaṃ vyomādi, vipratipannatatkartṛkaṃ mahīmahīdharadūrvāṅkurādi, tatrāntimamadhikṛtyocyate- kṣityādikaṃ buddhimatkartṛkaṃ kāryatvāt ghaṭādivat /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, accepting that the word-meaning relations and the Vedas are of human origin, and wishing to establish creation, dissolution, and God (<s>Īśvara</s>) through inference, construct the following argument: There are three kinds of entities — those known to have a conscious maker, like a pot; those known not to have such a maker, like space; and those about which there is dispute, like the earth, mountains, and sprouts of grass. Regarding the last of these, it is said: Earth and the like have an intelligent maker, because they are effects — like a pot.

children.text: kāryatvaṃ ca kṣityādeḥ sāvayavatvāt ghaṭādivat* ////
children.translated_text: And the effecthood of earth and the like [is established] because they have parts — like a pot. ////

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ pṛthivyādeḥ samavāyikāraṇam, pārthivāpyataijasavāyīyaparamāṇujātaṃ yathāsvaṃ pṛthivyaptejovāyūnāṃ samavāyikāraṇaṃ, na hi pralaye paramāṇūnāṃ pralayo 'smākamasti sāṃkhyādivat /
children.translated_text: What, then, is the inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>) of earth and the like? The class of atoms — earthy, watery, fiery, and airy — are the inherent cause of earth, water, fire, and air respectively. For we [<s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>] do not [accept] the dissolution of atoms at the time of cosmic dissolution, unlike the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and others.

children.text: kāryadravyāṇi tu dvyaṇukādīni sarvāṇyeveśvarecchayā viśliṣṭāvayavāni pralīyante, paramāṇavastu mitho 'saṃyuktāstiṣṭhanti vyomādayaśca kṣetrajñāścātmīyadharmādharmayuktā evāvatiṣṭhante /
children.translated_text: But all effect-substances — dyads and the like — dissolve when their parts are separated by the will of God. The atoms, however, remain mutually unconjoined; and space and the like, and the individual souls (<s>kṣetrajñas</s>), endowed with their own merit (<s>dharma</s>) and demerit (<s>adharma</s>), continue to exist.

children.text: sargakāle punarīśvarecchāṃ kṣetrajñādṛṣṭaṃ ca nimittamāsādya paramāṇuṣu karmāṇyutpadyante tadvaśācca mithaḥ saṃyuktāścatuṣṭayepi paramāṇalo dvyaṇukādikrameṇa yathāsvaṃ pṛthivyādikaṃ bhūtacatuṣṭayamārabhante /
children.translated_text: At the time of creation, motions arise in the atoms, having as their efficient cause the will of God and the unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) of the individual souls. And by the force of those [motions], the atoms, mutually conjoined in all four [classes], produce the four gross elements — earth and the like — in stages, through dyads and the like, each according to its kind.

children.text: nimitabhūtakṣetrajñādṛṣṭavaicitryācca jarāyujāṇḍajodbhijjasvedajabhinnaṃ śarīrabhedamīśvarecchākāritasaṃyogaviśeṣavaśātparamāṇava ārabhante //
children.translated_text: And due to the variety of the unseen merit of the individual souls that serves as the efficient cause, the atoms, by the force of specific conjunctions brought about by the will of God, produce the variety of bodies — viviparous, oviparous, plant-born, and moisture-born. //

body.text: vaiśeṣikamatakhaṇḍanam /
body.translated_text: Refutation of the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> view:

body.text:
nanvedapi yuktam- nahīcchāmātreṇa prayatnamantareṇa paramāṇuṣu spandotpattiḥ saṃbhavati, icchākāritaprayatnavaśena śarīraspandotpattiradyatve 'pi dṛśyate /
īśvaro 'pi prayatata iti cet /
na /
aśarīrasya prayatnāsaṃbhavāt /

children.text: sarvagatā api hyātmānaḥ śarīrapradeśa eva prayatnamārabhante na bahiḥ, ataḥ śarīrāpekṣaḥ prayatnaḥ /
children.translated_text: For even all-pervading selves initiate effort only at the location of the body, not outside it; hence effort depends on a body.

children.text: pralayakāle ca sarvakāryāṇāṃ pralayādīśvaraśarīramapi pralīnamiti kathamaśarīraḥ prayateta /
children.translated_text: And at the time of dissolution, since all effects dissolve, God's body too has dissolved — so how can a bodiless [God] make effort?

children.text: nacāśarīrasyecchāpi saṃbhavati muktātmanāmiva /
children.translated_text: Nor is even will possible for a bodiless [being], just as for liberated souls.

children.text: nāpi jñānaṃ saṃbhavati- indriyāderabhāvāt* ////
children.translated_text: Nor is knowledge possible — because of the absence of sense-organs and the like. ////

body.translated_text: Objection: This too is reasonable. [Reply:] For movement in the atoms is not possible through mere will without effort (<s>prayatna</s>). Even in the present, it is seen that bodily movement arises through effort caused by will. [If one says] 'God too makes effort' — no, because effort is impossible for one without a body.

children.text: nityamasya jñānaṃ nityā cecchā nityaśca prayatna iti cet, na, sarvajñānecchāprayatnānāmanityatvavyāpteḥ /
children.translated_text: [If one says] 'His knowledge is eternal, His will is eternal, and His effort is eternal' — no, because all knowledge, will, and effort are pervaded by non-eternality [i.e., are invariably non-eternal].

children.text: śakyate hi prayoktum- kṣityādikaṃ nāśarīricetanakartṛkaṃ na nityaprayatnanityecchānityajñānakartṛkaṃ kāryatvāt ghaṭavaditi* ////
children.translated_text: For it can be argued: Earth and the like do not have a bodiless conscious being as their maker, nor one with eternal effort, eternal will, and eternal knowledge — because they are effects, like a pot. ////

children.text: nanu ghaṭasyāpīśvarakartṛkatvamastyeveti sādhyahīno dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: Even a pot has God as its maker — so the example lacks the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). [Reply:]

children.text: tathāpi kulālasyāpi kartṛtvānna kevaleśvarakartṛkatvaṃ ghaṭasya, tataścaivaṃ prayoktavyaṃ- kṣityādikaṃ na kevalāśarīryātmādikartṛkaṃ ghaṭāvaditi, vastutvādvyomādivaditi hetudṛśaṣṭāntau sarvathāpi nirdeṣau /
children.translated_text: Even so, the pot is not made by God alone, since the potter too is a maker. Therefore, the argument should be formulated thus: Earth and the like do not have solely a bodiless self and the like as their maker — like a pot. Or: [Earth and the like are not made by an intelligent maker,] because they are real things — like space. Thus the logical mark and example are valid in every way.

children.text: tathā kṣityādikaṃ na buddhimatkartṛkaṃ śarīrikartṛkatvavirahāt vyomavaditi sākṣādeva pratisādhanaṃ kartavyam /
children.translated_text: Similarly, a direct counter-proof should be made: Earth and the like do not have an intelligent maker, because they lack a bodily maker — like space.

children.text: atheśvaraśarīraṃ nityamaṅgīkṛtya pralaye 'pi saśarīrameveśvaramabhyupagacchet, tataḥ sāvayavatvamīśvaraśarīre naikāntikaṃ na kṣityādeḥ kāryatvaṃ sādhayet, saśarīrakartṛkatvaṃ ca dūrvāṅkurādīnāmanupapannamanupalabdhivirodhāt* ////
children.translated_text: If, however, one accepts God's body as eternal and maintains that God possesses a body even during dissolution, then the fact of having parts would not conclusively [establish] effecthood of earth and the like, since God's body too has parts [yet is eternal]; and a bodily maker of grass sprouts and the like would be untenable, because of the contradiction with non-observation [of any such maker]. ////

body.text:
kiñca pratikāryaṃ prayatnabhedena bhavitavyam, anyo hi pādasaṃcaraṇe prayatnaḥ anyaśca bāhūddharaṇe, tathā sati yadyapīśvare prayatno nityaḥ syāttathāpi tasyaikatvānna vicitrakāryodayahetutvaṃ saṃbhavatīti vyartha evāsau /
yadi tvanantakāryānurūpā anantā sargakāle 'pyavasthānāt, saṃyojakasya ca sargahetoḥ pralayakālepyavasthānāt ubhayoḥ parasparavidhātānna sṛṣṭiḥ syāt na pralayaḥ /
yacca kṣetrajñādṛṣṭavaicitryopapattiriti, tadapyayuktam- nahi dṛṣṭakāraṇavailakṣaṇyantareṇādṛṣṭavailakṣaṇyamātrātkāryavailakṣaṇyaṃ siddhyati /
nahyadṛṣṭaśatenāpi tālabījamantareṇa
body.translated_text: Moreover, there must be a different effort for each effect — for the effort in moving the foot is different from that in raising the arm. This being so, even if God's effort were eternal, since it is one, it cannot be the cause of producing varied effects — hence it is useless. If, however, [God's efforts] are infinite, corresponding to infinite effects — since they would exist even at the time of creation, and since the conjoining [cause] that brings about creation also exists during dissolution, both being mutually determining — there would be neither creation nor dissolution. And the [claim] that the variety [of creation is explained] through the variety of the unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) of individual souls — that too is unjustified. For without a difference in the observed cause, the mere difference in unseen merit cannot establish a difference in the effect. For not even by a hundred [factors of] unseen merit can

body.text:
tālavṛkṣo niṣpadyate /
vināpi bījamīśvaramahimnā sarvaṃ siddhyatīti cet /
na /
tatraiva pramāṇābhāvāt /
nityatve hi vedānāmavasite tatprāmāṇyabaleneśvarasyāparicchedyo mahimā, sṛṣṭipralayau
body.translated_text: a palmyra tree be produced without a palmyra seed. [If one says] 'even without a seed, everything is accomplished by the power of God' — no, because there is no means of knowledge for that very [claim]. For only when the eternality of the Vedas has been established, by the force of their validity, is the immeasurable power of God [accepted]; as for creation and dissolution,

children.text: ṛtuliṅganyāyamāśritya sidhyeyurna vā /
children.translated_text: they may or may not be established through the <s>ṛtuliṅganyāya</s> (analogy of seasonal signs).

children.text: vedāṃstvanādṛtya dṛṣṭānusāreṇa parvate ivānumānamatyantālaukiker'the pravartayatāmupekṣaivottaramityuparamyate /
children.translated_text: But for those who, disregarding the Vedas, extend inference — following observed [analogies] — to utterly transcendent matters, as in the case of a mountain — mere disregard is the sufficient reply. Thus we desist.

children.text: tasmānna sargādikāle 'pi saṃbandhakāraṇam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even at the time of creation and the like, there is no [human] cause of the [word-meaning] relation. //

body.text: śabdārthasaṃbandhasya nityatvam /
body.translated_text: The eternality of the word-meaning relation:

children.text: aśakyaṃ ca kartuṃ sarvaśabdānāṃ saṃbandhakaraṇam- yadā na kaścidapi śabdaḥ kenāpyarthena saṃbaddhaṃ āsīt tadā kathaṃ saṃbandhaḥ kriyeta- saṃbandhaṃ hi kurvatāvaśyaṃ kenacidvākyena sa kartavyaḥ- gauḥ sāsnādimānityādinā /
children.translated_text: And it is impossible to establish the relation for all words [by convention]. For when no word whatsoever was connected with any meaning, how could the relation be made? One who would create the relation must necessarily do so through some sentence, such as 'a cow is [an animal] possessing a dewlap and the like.'

children.text: nacāprasiddhamarthapratipādakatvena sāsnādiśabdamarthapratipādanāya śaknoti kartoccārayituṃ, tathā hastasaṃjñādayopi, pratipādakatvāsiddheḥ* ////
children.translated_text: But one cannot utter the word <s>sāsnādi</s> ('possessing a dewlap and the like') for the purpose of conveying meaning, since its capacity to convey meaning is not yet established. The same applies to hand-gestures and other [means of designation], since their conveying capacity too is unestablished. ////

children.text: nanvevamaprasiddhasaṃbandhasya kathamanapyanupapannam- yadyapi hi tadā vaktuḥ prasiddhasaṃbandhatvātsaṃbandhakathanāya vākyoccāraṇaṃ saṃbhavati tathāpi śrotāro 'prasiddhasamastapadārthā bālāḥ kathaṃ vākyena saṃbadhaṃ pratipadyeran, tasmātkaraṇavatkathanamapyanupapannam /
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, then even the communication [of the relation through convention] for one whose relation [of words and meanings] is unestablished would be equally impossible. For even if the speaker, whose knowledge of the relation is established, can utter a sentence to communicate the relation, still, the hearers — children whose knowledge of all word-meanings is unestablished — how would they understand the relation through a sentence? Therefore, communication, like creation [of the relation], is impossible.

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault.

children.text: kathayitustāvanna karturivāśaktiḥ- upāyasaṃbhavāt, pratipattārastūpāyābhāvānna pratipadyanta iti dṛṣṭaviruddham, dṛśyante hyaprasiddhasamastaśabdārthā bālā vṛddhebhyaḥ saṃbandhaṃ pratipadyamānāḥ* ////
children.translated_text: For the communicator, unlike the creator [of the relation], has no incapacity — since means [of communication] are available. But [the claim] that the recipients cannot understand because of the absence of means — this contradicts experience. For children whose knowledge of all word-meanings is unestablished are observed learning the relation from elders. ////

children.text: kiñcāstyupāyo bālānāṃ- nāvaśyaṃ saṃbandhakathanāvākyenaiva vṛddhebhyo bālāḥ saṃbandhaṃ pratipadyante, kintu yadā vṛddhāḥ prasiddhasaṃbandhāḥ svakāryārthena vyavaharanti tadā teṣāmupaśṛṇvanto bālāḥ saṃbandhaṃ pratipadyante /
children.translated_text: Moreover, there is a means for children: It is not necessarily through a sentence explicitly stating the relation that children learn the relation from elders. Rather, when elders — whose knowledge of the relation is established — transact their own affairs, then children, overhearing them, learn the relation.

children.text: yadā hi kenacidgāmānayetyuktaḥ kaścitsāsnādimantamānayati tadā samīpastho bālo 'vagacchati yasmādayametadvākyaśravaṇānantaramasminnarthe pravartate tasmādasmādvākyādayamarthaḥ pratyāyita ityevaṃ saṃmugdharūpeṇāvagataṃ pratyāyakatvaṃ paścādbahuṣu prayogeṣvanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ vākyabhāgānāṃ padānāṃ padabhāgānāṃ ca prakṛtipratyayānāṃ vākyārthabhāgeṣu pādartheṣu vivacyate, tasmānna pauruṣeyaḥ saṃbandha iti na tadvaśena puruṣāpekṣāstīti siddhamanapekṣaṃ vedānāṃ prāmāṇyam //
children.translated_text: For when someone, told 'bring a cow,' brings [an animal] possessing a dewlap and the like, a child standing nearby understands: 'Since this person, immediately upon hearing this sentence, acts regarding this object, therefore this meaning is conveyed by this sentence.' The capacity to convey meaning, thus understood in a vague form, is subsequently, through many usages, differentiated by the methods of agreement and difference (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) — for sentence-parts (words), word-parts, and stems and suffixes — in their respective sentence-meaning-parts and word-meanings. Therefore, the [word-meaning] relation is not of human origin; and since there is no dependence on a person through it, the validity of the Vedas as independent [of any author] is established. //

body.text: iti saṃbandhākṣepaparihāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the resolution of the objection regarding the relation. //

children.text: yaccānnantaraphalānupalabdhyā citrādīnāṃ na paścādiphalatvamiti syādevam /
children.translated_text: And the [claim] that from non-observation of immediate results, the <s>citrā</s> rites and the like do not have delayed results — it would be so

children.text: yadi pratyakṣādipañcakameva pramāṇaṃ syāttadā hyanantaraphalopalambhādeva tatsādhanatvaṃ syāt nānyathā, śabdasyāpi tu pramitijanakatayā pratyakṣādivatpramāṇatvāt tenaca citrādīnāṃ paśusādhanatvāvagamādasatyapyanantaropalambhe siddhyati tatsādhanatvam //
children.translated_text: if only the five [means] beginning with perception were means of knowledge. For then, only from the observation of an immediate result would [the rite's] being a means [to that result] be established, not otherwise. But since verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) too, being a generator of valid cognition, is a means of knowledge like perception and the like, and since the <s>citrā</s> rites and the like are understood through it as means to cattle — even without immediate observation, their being means [to results] is established. //

body.text: citrādiviṣayakākṣepaparihārāḥ /
body.translated_text: The resolution of objections regarding <s>citrā</s> and the like:

body.text: nanu pramāṇāntaravirodhādapramāṇyamityuktaṃ, na, tadabhāvāt, nahi śabdo 'nantarameva citrāphalasādhanamiti brūte yena virodhaḥ syāt, sādhanatvameva pratipannaṃ tanmātravacanāt, tasya cāpūrvadvāreṇa kālāntare 'pi tailapānādivatphalasādhanatvopapatteḥ* ////
body.translated_text: Objection: It was said that [their] invalidity [arises] from contradiction with another means of knowledge. [Reply:] No, because that [contradiction] does not exist. For verbal testimony does not say that <s>citrā</s> is a means to its result immediately — so how would there be contradiction? Only the bare fact of being a means is conveyed, since [the text] states only that much. And since its being a means to the result is possible even at a later time through the medium of <s>apūrva</s>, like drinking oil [whose medicinal effect comes later] — ////

body.text: yattu prāganuṣṭhānācchāstrārthāvadhāraṇavelāyāṃ nāpūrvamantarbhāvitāmityuktaṃ, yadyapyevaṃ tathāpi paścādevamavagacchati- sādhanatvamātre 'pi śabdenokte bhrāntyā mayā sākṣātsādhanatvameva pratipannaṃ taccedānīmanyathā jātam, ato nūnamasya kenāpi dvāreṇa kālāntare phalamiti* ////
body.translated_text: As for what was said — that <s>apūrva</s> was not included [in the meaning of the <s>śāstra</s>] at the time of determining the meaning, before performance — even if that is so, still, afterwards one understands thus: 'When the <s>śāstra</s> stated merely the fact of being a means [to the result], I mistakenly understood it as being a direct means; that has now turned out otherwise. Therefore, this [rite] must produce its result at a later time through some medium.' ////

body.text:
prāgapi ca śakyamevāpūrvamavagantum anekeṣāmaṅgapradhānakarmaṇāṃ kṣaṇikānāmapūrvamantareṇa yaugapadyāsaṃbhavāt, paśvādīnāṃ ca dṛṣṭakāraṇāpekṣatvānna kṣaṇamātreṇotpattiḥ saṃbhavatītyavaśyaṃbhāvyapūrvam /
na ca paścādyutpattimātraṃ phalam upabhogasya tu cirakālatvāt yāvadupabhogamavasthāsyamānena kenacidbhavitavyam /
na ca kriyāyāstāvankālamavasthānaṃ saṃbhavatītyapūrvamaṅgīkartavyamiti taddvāreṇa
body.translated_text: And even beforehand, <s>apūrva</s> can be understood — since for the many momentary subsidiary and primary ritual acts, simultaneity [of all of them producing the result] is impossible without <s>apūrva</s>; and since cattle and the like, depending on observed causes, cannot arise in a mere instant — <s>apūrva</s> is necessarily to be accepted. Moreover, the mere subsequent arising is not [all that constitutes] the result; since enjoyment extends over a long time, there must be something that persists for the duration of the enjoyment. And since the ritual action cannot persist for that long — <s>apūrva</s> must be accepted. Through that medium,

body.text: yuktaṃ karma kālāntare phaladamiti nānantarānupalabdhyā śāstrasya bādhaḥ //
body.translated_text: it is reasonable that the ritual produces its result at a later time — hence the <s>śāstra</s> is not invalidated by non-observation of an immediate [result]. //

body.text:
iti citrākṣepaparihāraḥ /
 /
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the resolution of the <s>citrā</s>-objection. //

body.text: ātmavādārambhaḥ /
body.translated_text: The commencement of the <s>ātmavāda</s> (doctrine of the self):

body.text: yattu pratyakṣaviruddhaṃ vacanamupanyastaṃ sa eṣa yajñāyudhī yajamāno 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokaṃ yātītyetacchabdena pratyakṣaṃ śarīraṃ yajñāyudhasaṃyuktamupadiśatīti /

children.text: tadabhidhīyate- arthavādatvādasyānyaparatvānna svārthe pramāṇāntaravirodho doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: To that we reply: Since this is an <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory/laudatory passage), it is subordinate to another [injunction], and [therefore] contradiction with another means of knowledge regarding its own [literal] meaning is not a fault.

children.text: na ca virodho 'pi vidyate /
children.translated_text: Moreover, there is no contradiction at all.

children.text: nahyanena śarīrasya svargagamanamucyate kintarhyātmano yasyaitaccharīraṃ , so 'pi hi śarīraśarīriṇorabhedopacāreṇa śarīrasthena yajñāyudhitvena pratyakṣatvena ca vyapidiśyate /
children.translated_text: For by this [statement], it is not said that the body goes to heaven; rather, [it refers to] the self (<s>ātman</s>) whose body this is. That [self] too is designated — by the figurative identification of the body and the embodied [self] — as possessing sacrificial implements through [the implements] being on the body, and as perceivable.

children.text: ātmano vā svargagamanaṃ śarīre upacaryata iti nāsti virodhaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Or, the going to heaven of the self is figuratively attributed to the body — so there is no contradiction. ////

body.translated_text: As for the statement contradicting perception that was cited — 'This very sacrificer, armed with sacrificial implements, goes directly to the heavenly world' — this, through the word [<s>yajñāyudhī</s>], describes the body, conjoined with sacrificial implements, as perceivable.

children.text: yajamānaśabdo 'pi tasyaiva yāgasvāmitvātkartṛtvācca vācakaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the word <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) too denotes that [self] alone, because of its being the master of the sacrifice and the agent [of the ritual].

children.text: na ca śakyate tasya kāpilavadakartṛtvaṃ vaktuṃ- śrutivirodhāt, sarvatra hi kartṛbhoktṛśabdayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: And it is not possible to say, like the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, that [the self] is not an agent — because it would conflict with <s>śruti</s>. For everywhere, the words 'agent' (<s>kartṛ</s>) and 'enjoyer' (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) are seen to be co-referential [with the same subject].

children.text: yathātraiva- yajamānaḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ yātīti /
children.translated_text: As here itself: 'The sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>) goes to the heavenly world.'

children.text: tathā ya evaṃ vidvānagniṃ cinute ṛdhnotyeva ya evaṃ vidvāndvirātreṇa yajate svargakāmeva saṃkalpaṃ prati kartṛtvamuktam* ////
children.translated_text: Likewise: 'He who, knowing thus, piles the fire,' 'He prospers who, knowing thus, sacrifices with the two-night [rite]' — thus agenthood is stated precisely with respect to the one who desires heaven, in relation to his resolve.

body.text: saṃbhavati ca svargagatasyāpyātmano yāgajñānaprayatnasaṃkalpādiṣu sākṣādeva kartṛtvaṃ, na hi vayaṃ spandameva kriyāmupagacchāmo vaiśeṣikavat, yenātmanaḥ kartṛtvaṃ na syāt,
body.translated_text: And it is possible for the self, even when it has gone to heaven, to have direct agenthood with respect to sacrifice, knowledge, effort, resolve, and the like. For we do not accept, like the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, that movement (<s>spanda</s>) alone is action,

children.text: dhātvarthamātrasya kriyātvāt /
children.translated_text: since the mere meaning of a verbal root constitutes action (<s>kriyā</s>).

children.text: spandeṣvapi prayojakatvenāsyaiṣa kartṛtvaṃ saṃbhavati, prayatnena hyasau śarīraṃ spande prayojayati /
children.translated_text: Even with respect to movements, the self's agenthood is possible through its being the impeller — for it impels the body to move through effort (<s>prayatna</s>).

children.text: sākṣāttu na saṃbhavati, sarvagate spandasyāsaṃbhavāt- ityanenābhiprāyeṇa purāṇeṣūpaniṣatsu cākartṛtvavādāḥ //
children.translated_text: But direct [production of movement] is not possible, since movement is impossible for an omnipresent [entity] — with this intent, the statements of non-agenthood in the <s>Purāṇas</s> and <s>Upaniṣads</s> [are made].

body.text: śarīrākiriktātmasādhanam /
body.translated_text: Proof of the self as distinct from the body.

body.text:
kiṃpunaḥ śarīravyatiriktātmasadbhāve pramāṇaṃ prāṇanādiliṅgaṃ sukhādayaśca prāṇanādiśabdena koṣṭhyasya vāyorūrdhvadhogamanavṛttiviśeṣasya prāṇanādiśabdavācyasya hetubhūtaḥ prayatna ucyate saca sukhādayaśca na śarīradharmāḥ saṃbhavanti, ayāvaccharīrabhāvitvāt /
ye hi kāryadravyavartino viśeṣaguṇā rūpādayaste virodhiguṇāntarādvā dravyavināśādvā vinaśyanti, prāṇanādayastu tadbhāvepi naśyanti mṛtāvasthāyāmiti na śarīraguṇāḥ /
tathā jñānamapyayāvaccharīrabhāvitvādeva na śarīradharmaḥ /

children.text: tathā ye pratyakṣiviṣayāḥ na śarīraguṇaste svayamiva parairapi yathā gṛhyante yatha rūpādayaḥ, sukhādayastu pratyakṣā api santo na parapratyakṣagrāhyāḥ tasmānna śarīraguṇāḥ, tadidamapi dvayaṃ sukhādīnāṃ śarīraguṇatvaṃ nivārayadanyaguṇatāṃ sūcayati /
children.translated_text: Moreover, those properties of the body that are objects of [others'] perception are apprehended by others just as by oneself — like color and the like. But pleasure and the like, even though perceptible [to the subject], are not apprehended by others' perception — therefore they are not properties of the body. This pair of [arguments] too, while preventing [the status of] pleasure and the like as body-properties, indicates that they are properties of something else.

children.text: yo 'sāvanyaḥ sa ātmā /
children.translated_text: That other [entity] is the self (<s>ātman</s>).

children.text: kiñca sarvaṃ eva viśeṣaguṇāḥ karaṇe 'pi vartamānā eva kāryadravyaguṇatāṃ bhajante, na ca śarīrakāraṇabhūteṣu pārthivaparamāṇuṣu caitanyamastīti kathaṃ śarīraguṇatā caitanyasya syāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, all specific qualities, even when existing in the cause, partake of being qualities of the effect-substance. But consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) does not exist in the earth-atoms that are the cause of the body — so how could consciousness be a property of the body?

children.text: tasmādanyaścetanaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is another conscious [entity].

body.translated_text: What then is the valid means of knowledge for the existence of a self distinct from the body? Vital breath (<s>prāṇana</s>) and the like as inferential marks, and pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and the like — by the term '<s>prāṇana</s> and the like,' it is the effort (<s>prayatna</s>) that is the cause of the specific upward and downward movements of the internal air, denoted by words like '<s>prāṇana</s>,' that is referred to. That [effort], as well as pleasure and the like, cannot be properties of the body, because they do not last as long as the body. For the specific qualities such as color and the like that reside in an effect-substance are destroyed either by a contrary quality or by the destruction of the substance — but vital breath and the like perish even while the body persists, in the state of death. Therefore they are not properties of the body. Likewise, knowledge too is not a property of the body, precisely because it does not last as long as the body.

body.text: dehābhinnātmasādhanam /
body.translated_text: Proof of the self as non-different from the body [— refutation thereof].

body.text: kaścitpunarāha- sarvathā vittiṣu tāvadvettāvabhāsate anyathā svaparavedyayoranatiśayaprasaṅgāt /

children.text: na ca śarīrasya karacaraṇādyavayavasaṃniveśaviśiṣṭasyāsti tathāvabhāsaḥ, ato 'nyaḥ śarīrādātmeti /
children.translated_text: And the body, as characterized by the specific arrangement of hands, feet, and other limbs, does not so appear. Therefore, the self is other than the body.

children.text: tattvayuktam- saṃniveśapratibhāse 'pi śarīrapratibhāsasaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: That is not correct — because even without the appearance of [bodily] arrangement, the appearance of the body is possible.

children.text: nahi saṃniveśa eva śarīraṃ, śarīradharmo hi saṃniveśaḥ saṃbhavati ca dharmāpratibhāso 'pi dharmiṇaḥ pratibhāsaḥ, anyathā ātmanopi pratibhāso na syāt taddharmāṇāṃ sarvagatatvādīnāmarthavittiṣvapratibhānāt /
children.translated_text: For arrangement is not the body itself — arrangement is a property of the body. And the appearance of the property-bearer is possible even without the appearance of the property. Otherwise, the self too would not appear [in cognition], since its properties such as omnipresence and the like do not appear in object-cognitions.

children.text: nacaikāntikamarthavittiṣu vettṛbhānaṃ, artha eva hi tadā bhāsate na vettā* ////
children.translated_text: Nor is the appearance of a knower invariable in object-cognitions — for at that time, it is the object alone that appears, not the knower.

body.translated_text: Someone further says: in all cognitions, a knower invariably appears — for otherwise there would be no difference between self-knowledge and knowledge-by-others.

body.text:
na ca svaparavedyayoranatiśayaḥ /
na hi vedittṛbhāsanakṛto 'yamatiśayaḥ kintu kasyacideva kiñcidābhāsate nānyasya ityetāvānatiśayo nānyaḥ, tasmānna jñātṛpratibhāsena śarīravivekasiddhiḥ, kintu pūrvoktādeva kāraṇāt- jñānasukhādīnāṃ śarīraguṇatvāsaṃbhavāt tato 'nya
body.translated_text: Nor is there [no] difference between self-knowledge and others' knowledge. For this difference is not created by the appearance of a knower; rather, the difference is merely that something appears to someone and not to another — nothing more. Therefore, the distinction from the body is not established by the appearance of a knower. Rather, [it is established] only by the previously stated reason — the impossibility of knowledge, pleasure, and the like being properties of the body; therefore another

body.text: eteṣāmāśrayaḥ sa evātmā //
body.translated_text: is their substratum — that is the self.

body.text: bauddhamatena vijñānātmavādaḥ //
body.translated_text: The vijñānavāda (consciousness-only theory) according to the Buddhist view.

children.text: saugatāstvāhuḥ- siddhe jñānasukhādīnāṃ guṇatve guṇakalpanā /
children.translated_text: The Buddhists say: 'When the quality-status of knowledge, pleasure, and the like is established, the postulation of a [separate] quality-bearer [is made].'

children.text: na tu tatsiddhamasmākaṃ tāvanmātropapattitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But that [quality-status] is not established for us, since it is possible that they exist merely as themselves.'

children.text: nahyāśrayamantareṇa jñānamātramanupapannaṃ svatantrameva jñānaṃ kiṃ neṣyate sukhādayo 'pi jñānaviṣayāḥ svatantrā eva anyasyāśrayasyānupalabdheḥ /
children.translated_text: For knowledge is not impossible without a substratum — why is self-sufficient knowledge not accepted? Pleasure and the like, too, are objects of knowledge and are self-sufficient, since no other substratum is apprehended.

children.text: jñānameva ca nīlamahaṃ jānāmīti jñātṛtvena viparyāsitadarśanairadhyavasīyate nānyaḥ pramāṇābhāvāt* ////
children.translated_text: And it is knowledge itself that is determined as the knower by those whose vision is distorted, through [the cognition] 'I know blue' — there is no other [knower], due to the absence of a valid means of knowledge.

children.text: nanu jñānasyāpi kṣaṇikatvātkathaṃ pūrvedyurupalabdhe paredyuḥsmaraṇamicchā pratyabhijñā ca /
children.translated_text: Objection: since knowledge too is momentary, how is there memory, desire, and recognition on the following day regarding what was apprehended the day before?

children.text: nahi svayamanupalabdhe tāni saṃbhavanti- nahi devadattenopalabdher'the yajñadattasya smaraṇādīni saṃbhavanti /
children.translated_text: For those [mental acts] are not possible with respect to what was not apprehended by oneself — just as <s>Yajñadatta</s> cannot have memory and the like regarding what was apprehended by <s>Devadatta</s>.

children.text: satyam- na saṃbhavanti saṃtānabhede samānāyāṃ tu saṃtatāvekenopalabdhe 'nyasya smaraṇādyupapannaṃ dṛṣṭatvāt, nahyupalabdhuḥ smartuścaikatvaṃ kvacidapi dṛṣṭaṃ, ekasya sthāsnoḥ puruṣasya kvacidapyanupalabdhatvāt, tasmājjñānameva jñātṛ nānyo jñātāstīti* ////
children.translated_text: True — they are not possible when there is a break in the continuum (<s>saṃtāna</s>). But within the same continuum, when one [moment of consciousness] has apprehended, it is proper for another [subsequent moment] to have memory and the like, since this is observed. For the identity of the apprehender and the rememberer is never observed anywhere, since no enduring, permanent person is ever apprehended. Therefore, knowledge itself is the knower — there is no other knower.

body.text: atrocyate- pratyabhijñāyate kartā yaḥ pūrvāparakālayoḥ //
body.translated_text: To this it is replied: the agent is recognized (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) across earlier and later times.

children.text: tasya sthāsnoḥ bhedo vijñānātkṣaṇabhaṅgurāt /
children.translated_text: His difference from cognition, which is momentary, [is thereby established].

children.text: viṣayapratyabhijñānānupapatterjñāturekatvakalpanāyāṃ syādapyetaduttaraṃ- saṃtānaikatvādevopapadyata iti /
children.translated_text: If the postulation of the knower's unity is based on the impossibility of explaining the recognition of objects [otherwise], then this reply might work — [the Buddhist would say] 'it is explained by the unity of the continuum alone.'

children.text: yadā tu jñātaivaikaḥ pūrvāparakālayoḥ pratyabhijñāyate- yo 'haṃ pūrvamadrākṣaṃ sa evāhamanupaśyāmīti tadā pratyabhijñayaiva jñāturekatvāvagamāt, vijñānasya ca kṣaṇikatvāttato 'nyo jñātā siddho bhavatīti* ////
children.translated_text: But when it is the knower himself who is recognized as one across earlier and later times — 'I who saw before am the very same I who see now' — then, since the unity of the knower is known through recognition itself, and since cognition is momentary, the knower is established as other than cognition.

body.text: kimahaṃpratyayagocaro jñātā syāt, tathā sati śarīrameva jānāmi kṛśo 'haṃ gacchāmyahamiti kārśyādibuddhisāmānādhikaraṇyādahaṃbuddhergocaraḥ, ātmanaśca sarvagatasya kārśyādyanupapatteḥ* ////
body.translated_text: [One might ask:] would the knower be the object of the I-cognition (<s>ahaṃpratyaya</s>)? If so, it would be the body itself — since [one says] 'I know,' 'I am thin,' 'I go,' and the I-cognition is co-referential with cognitions of thinness and the like, making the body its object. And for the self, which is omnipresent, thinness and the like are impossible.

children.text: ucyate- jñātṛviśayastāvadahaṃpratyaya ityavivādam, yo hi parāmṛśati sa svātmānamahamiti parāmṛśati parānidamiti /
children.translated_text: It is replied: that the I-cognition pertains to the knower is beyond dispute — for one who apprehends, apprehends himself as 'I' and others as 'this.'

children.text: tena niḥsaṃśayamasya jñātṛgocaratvaṃ śarīrasya ca jñātṛtvaṃ nirākṛtaṃ, ato 'tyantasaṃsṛṣṭayorekatvabhrāntyā sāmānādhikaraṇyapratītiruṣṇatoyapratītivat bhāsvarāyaḥpiṇḍapratītivacca //
children.translated_text: Therefore, its pertaining to the knower is beyond doubt. And the body's knower-status has been refuted. Therefore, due to the error of identity [arising from] extreme intermixture of the two [body and self], the co-referential cognition [of 'I' with bodily attributes] is like the cognition of hot water [where the heat belongs to fire, not water], or the cognition of a glowing iron ball [where the glow belongs to fire].

body.text: śarīrātmanorbhedopapādanam /
body.translated_text: Demonstration of the difference between body and self.

body.text:
tathā vyatirkabuddhirapi dṛśyate mamedaṃ śarīraṃ kṛśamiti ṣaṣṭhyāsmadarthasya śarīravyatirekāt, śarīrasya ca paraviṣayedaṅkārāspadatvāt, tato 'smādvivekāvabhāsātpūrvoktanyāyena ca śarīrasyājñātṛtvāt, abhedāvagamasya ca saṃsargadoṣavaśena bhrāntyāpyupapatteḥ, pūrvābhyastasmṛtyanubandhena ca vinā jātasya harṣabhayaśokapratipattyanupapatteḥ /
jātismarāśca kecidadyatve 'pi dehāntararahovṛttaṃ vṛttāntaṃ saṃbodhayanta upalabhyanta ityupalabdhisiddhaḥ śarīrātmanabhedaḥ /
yadyapi cānena prakāreṇa śarīrātmanorvispaṣṭo bhedo na siddhyet tathāpi tāvadabhedo 'pi na vispaṣṭaḥ- mama śarīramiti vivekasyāpi pratibhāsāt /
tatra saṃmugdhe tattve śrutārthāpattyā sākṣācchrutyā vā nirṇayaḥ /
svargakāmādiśrutayo hi śarīrātiriktaṃ paralokaphalopabhogayogyaṃ kartāramantareṇānupapadyamānāstamākṣipanti tābhiścākṣiptaṃ sākṣādevopaniṣadaḥ samarthayanti avanāśi vā are 'yamātmā ityevamādaya iti siddhaḥ śarīrātirikto mānasapratyakṣarūpo 'haṃpratyayagamyo jñātā /
kathaṃ punarjñāturjñeyatvaṃ, nahyekasya kartṛtvaṃ karmatvaṃ ca svātmani kriyāvirodhātsaṃbhavaci, tasmānnāhaṃvittirnāma ghaṭādivittivyatirekeṇa kācidasti, ghaṭādivittāveva tu viṣayavadātmā bhāsata ityuktam /
body.translated_text: Likewise, a cognition of distinction is also seen: 'this body of mine is thin' — since the genitive case-form indicates the difference of the first-person referent from the body, and since the body is the locus of the demonstrative pronoun 'this' which pertains to another. Therefore, from this appearance of distinction, and from the previously stated reasoning that the body is not a knower, and since the cognition of non-difference can be explained even as an error due to the fault of [habitual] association, and since the arising of joy, fear, and sorrow in a just-born [infant] is impossible without the continuation of memories habituated in previous [lives] — and since certain persons who remember their past lives (<s>jātismarāḥ</s>) are observed to recount secret events of other bodies [i.e., past lives] even in the present — therefore, the difference between body and self is established through observation. Even if the difference between body and self is not clearly established in this way, still, the non-difference too is not clear — since the appearance of distinction in 'my body' also manifests. When the truth is thus confused, the determination [is to be made] through <s>śruti</s> and <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), or through direct <s>śruti</s>. For <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'one desiring heaven' and the like are impossible without an agent who is distinct from the body and capable of enjoying the fruits in the other world — and they imply such [an agent]. And what is implied by them, the <s>Upaniṣads</s> directly affirm: 'This self is indeed indestructible' and similar [passages]. Thus, the knower is established as distinct from the body, cognizable through the I-cognition which has the nature of mental perception (<s>mānasapratyakṣa</s>). But how can the knower be a knowable? For the agenthood and objecthood of one and the same [entity] with respect to the same action is impossible due to the contradiction of action in oneself. Therefore, there is no such thing as self-cognition separate from the cognition of a pot and the like — rather, in the cognition of a pot and the like, the self appears along with the object — thus it has been said.

body.text: ātmano mānasāhaṃpratyayagamyatvam /
body.translated_text: The self is cognizable through the mental I-cognition.

body.text: kaḥ punarayaṃ svātmani kriyāvirodho nāma, yasyāṃ kriyāyāṃ yaḥ kartā na sā tasminneva svaphalaṃ
body.translated_text: But what is this 'contradiction of action in oneself'? In whatever action someone is the agent, that [action] does not produce its own result

body.text:
janayatītyarthaḥ /
kiṃ punaḥ saṃvittikriyāyāḥ phalaṃ, bhāsanaṃ, kimidaṃ kartari na bhavati /
omiticet, kathaṃ tarhyasau bhāsate /
nahyasati bhāsate bhāsata iti śakyate vaktuṃ, tasmādarthavittiṣvapyātmano bhāsanābhyupagame 'pi svātmani kriyāvirodhastulya eva /

children.text: vyavahārayogyatāmātraṃ saṃvitte palaṃ nānyaditicet bhavatvevam /
children.translated_text: If [one says]: the result of consciousness is merely the fitness for practical activity, nothing else — so be it.

children.text: asti tāvatphalam /
children.translated_text: There is at least a result.

children.text: tacca viṣayeṣvivātmanyapi saṃvittito jāyata ityaṅgīkṛtaṃ bhavadbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And that [result] arises from consciousness with respect to the self just as with respect to objects — this has been accepted by you.

children.text: atastulyo virodhaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, the contradiction is the same.

body.translated_text: in that very [agent] — this is the meaning. But what is the result of the action of consciousness? Manifestation (<s>bhāsana</s>). Does this not occur in the agent? If [one says] no — then how does he [the self] appear at all? For it cannot be said that something appears when it does not appear. Therefore, even when the self's manifestation in object-cognitions is accepted, the contradiction of action in oneself is equally [present].

children.text: yadi paramārthavirodhamudbhāvya satyapyātmanaḥ kriyājanyaphalabhāgitve karmasaṃjñā karmavibhaktiṃśca na bhavatītyucyate parasamavāyikriyāphalabhāgitvaṃ karmatvam ityabhidhānāt taccāyuktam /
children.translated_text: If, having shown a real contradiction, one says that even though the self is a beneficiary of the result produced by action, it does not receive the designation and case-ending of grammatical object (<s>karma</s>) — since objecthood is defined as being a beneficiary of the result of an action inhering in another — that is improper.

children.text: śabdasādhutvaṃ hi prayogato 'vagantavyam /
children.translated_text: For the correctness of a word-form must be determined from actual usage.

children.text: asti cātmanaḥ svakartṛkāyāmeva kriyāyāṃ karmavyavahāro loke vede ca- yadhā tāvadbhāṣya eva svasaṃvedyaḥ saṃbhavatīti karmavācī kṛtyapratyayaprayogaḥ vedepi ātmānamupāsīta ātmānaṃ veda ātmā jñātavyaḥ ityanekaśaḥ prayogaḥ //
children.translated_text: And there is usage in both the world and the <s>Veda</s> of the self as grammatical object in an action whose agent is itself: as in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> itself, 'self-cognizable is possible' — a usage of the passive suffix (<s>kṛtya</s>) with the self as object; and in the <s>Veda</s> too: 'one should meditate on the self,' 'he knows the self,' 'the self is to be known' — such usages are numerous.

body.text:
na ca ganturgamane karmatvaṃ prayogābhāvāt śabdasādhutve hi prayogaparavaśā vayaṃ na svayamīśmahe /
yathāhi calanārthatve samāne gacchatiḥ sakarmakaḥ calatiścākarmakaḥ prayogasya tathā darśanāt /
eva jñātuḥ karmatvaṃ gantuścākarmatvaṃ bhaviṣyati /
tasmānmānasāhaṃpratyayagamya ātmā /
tathā ca śrutiḥ sa mānasīna ātmā janānām, iti /
tena yadyapi viṣayavittivelāyāmevātmāvabhāsastathāpi na viṣayavittikartṛtayāvabhāsastathāpi na viṣayavittikartṛtayāvabhāsaḥ kintu mānasāhaṃpratyayakarmatayāvabhāso na tadvittikarmatayāvyāpteḥ /

children.text: nanu śarīravadātmanyapyahamabhimāno bhrāntareva, na, bādhābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: just as with the body, the I-identification with the self too is merely erroneous. No — because there is no sublation.

children.text: yogināmasti bādha iti cet, napramāṇābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: If [one says] yogins have sublation — no, because there is no valid means of knowledge [for such sublation].

children.text: tathā ca yo 'pi yogasya parāṃ kāṣṭhāmupagatāḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus: even those who have reached the highest state of <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: yogeśvarāste 'pi kurvantyātmanyahaṃmatīm //
children.translated_text: the lords of <s>yoga</s>, employ the I-cognition with respect to the self.

body.translated_text: But the traveler is not a grammatical object with respect to his own traveling, since there is no [such] usage. For in the correctness of word-forms, we are dependent on usage and do not determine [it] by ourselves. For just as, with the meaning of movement being the same, 'gacchati' takes an object while 'calati' does not, as is observed from usage — so too, the knower may have objecthood and the traveler may not. Therefore, the self is cognizable through the mental I-cognition. And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'He is the mental self of beings.'Therefore, even though the self appears only at the time of object-cognition, it does not appear as the agent of object-cognition; rather, it appears as the object of the mental I-cognition — since [its appearance] is not pervaded by [the role of] being the object of that [object-]cognition.

body.text:
ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayastathā /
tānyahaṃ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha parantapa /
yasmātkṣaramatīto 'hamakṣarādapi cottamaḥ /

children.text: evamādāvahaṃśabdaḥ parasminpuṃsi hi dhruvam /
children.translated_text: in such [passages], the word 'I' assuredly refers to the Supreme Person.

children.text: na hi mahadvikāro 'haṅkāraḥ kṛtsnasya prabhavaḥ, nāpi kṣarākṣarābhyāmuttamaḥ, nāpi brahmaśabdavācye pradhāne garbhaṃ dadhāti, puruṣasaṃparkakṛtatvātprakṛtikṣobhasya /
children.translated_text: For neither is <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (the evolute of <s>mahat</s>) the origin of the entire [universe], nor is it higher than the perishable and imperishable, nor does it place the seed in <s>Prakṛti</s> (the entity denoted by the word '<s>brahma</s>') — since the disturbance of <s>Prakṛti</s> is caused by contact with <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: tathopaniṣatsvapi- brahma vā idamagra āsīt tadātmānamevāvedahaṃ brahmāsmi iti mantravarṇopi ahaṃ manurabhavaṃ sūryaśca iti /
children.translated_text: Likewise in the <s>Upaniṣads</s>: 'In the beginning, this was <s>Brahman</s> alone; it knew itself: I am <s>Brahman</s>.' Even the <s>mantra</s> verse [says]: 'I became <s>Manu</s> and <s>Sūrya</s>.'

children.text: tasmādahaṃpratyayagamyatvāmātmano 'nicchintaḥ śrutivirodhādevopekṣaṇīyāḥ* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, those who do not accept that the self is cognizable through the I-cognition are to be disregarded, precisely because they conflict with <s>śruti</s>.

body.translated_text: 'I am the origin and dissolution of the entire universe'; 'I know all of them, but you do not know, O scorcher of foes'; 'Since I transcend the perishable and am higher even than the imperishable' —

children.text: yattu nirmuktāhaṅkāramamakāravacanaṃ tadapi paurvāparyeṇa parāmṛṣyamāṇaṃ nāhaṅkārasvarūpaniṣedhārtha bhavati, evaṃ hi tadvacanaṃ- nāsya kaścinnāyaṃ kasyacit nirmuktāhaṅkāramamakāra evāyamiti /
children.translated_text: As for the statement about being 'free from I-sense and mine-sense' — that too, when considered in context, does not mean the negation of the essential nature of the I-sense. For the statement reads thus: 'He belongs to none, and none belongs to him — he is free from I-sense and mine-sense.'

children.text: tadayamarthaḥ- yasmānnāsya kaścittasmānnirmuktamamakāraḥ, yasmānnāyaṃ kasyacittasmānnirmuktāhaṅkāra iti /
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: since he does not belong to anyone, he is free from the sense of 'mine'; since he does not belong to anyone, he is free from the sense of 'I.'

children.text: yadyahaṅkārasvarūpaniṣedhaḥ syāt, na pūrveṇa saṃbadhyeta- yasmānnāyaṃ kasyacittasmādasminnahaṃbhāvo bhrāntiriti kiṃ kena saṃgatam, tasmānnāyamahantāsvarūpaniṣedhaḥ kiṃ tarhi janmaṃsaṃbandhitayātmanyahaṃmatiḥ ahamasya pitāhamasya putra ityādiḥ sa bhrama ityevaṃ saṃgataṃ bhavati* ////
children.translated_text: If there were a negation of the essential nature of the I-sense, it would not connect with the preceding [passage] — 'since he does not belong to anyone, therefore the I-sense in him is delusion' — what connection would there be? Therefore, this [passage] is not about the denial of ego-ness —

children.text: ayamātmā na kasyacidapi putrādirūpeṇa saṃbandhī, janyajanakabhāvasya śarīraviṣayatvāt, śarīraṃ hi śarīrājjāyate natvātmātmāntarāt, tasmādanyasaṃbana adhitayātmanyahaṃmatiḥ kṛśādimaticcharīrādvivekamabudhyamānānāṃ bhrāntiriti /
