children.translated_text: This <s>Ātman</s> is not related to anyone in the form of son and the like, since the relation of produced and producer pertains to the body alone. For body is born from body, not <s>Ātman</s> from another <s>Ātman</s>. Therefore, the negation of relation with another —

children.text: tadidamasyānyasaṃbandhiniṣedhena putrādiviṣayasnehanivartanena vairāgyajananārthamucyate, nāhaṅkārasvarūpasyāyaṃ niṣedho 'nupayogādasaṃgatatvāt pramāṇāntaravirodhāt ahaṃ brahmāsti iti vacanavirodhācca /
children.translated_text: This is said for the purpose of generating dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) by negating his relation with others and removing attachment to sons and the like — this is not a negation of the essential nature of the I-sense, being both useless and incoherent, and contradicting the means of knowledge —

children.text: tasmādahaṃpratyayagamyo jñātā śarīrātirikta indriyavyatiriktaśca //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the knower, apprehended through the I-cognition, is distinct from the body and distinct from the sense-organs. //

body.text: indriyātmanorbhedaḥ //
body.translated_text: The difference of the sense-organs from the self: //

body.text: kathamindriyabhedaḥ, indriyābhāve 'pi jñāturekasya pratyabhijñānāt yo 'haṃ rūpamadrākṣaṃ so 'haṃ
body.translated_text: How is the difference from the sense-organs [established]? From the recognition of the single knower even in the absence of [particular] sense-organs — 'I who saw the form am the same I who —'

children.text: spṛśāmīti, yo 'hamagrahīṣaṃ so 'haṃ smarāmīti /
children.translated_text: 'touch'; 'I who grasped [through the senses] am the same I who remember.'

children.text: manastu pratyakṣasiddhasya jñātū rūpādijñāneṣu vyatiriktakaraṇādhīnatvāt sukhādijñāneṣu bhavitavyaṃ karaṇenetyevaṃ kalpyata iti nāsya jñātṛtvamāśaṅkanīyam* ////
children.translated_text: As for the mind (<s>manas</s>) — since the knower, established through perception, depends on distinct instruments for the cognitions of form and the like, it is postulated that there must be an instrument for the cognitions of pleasure and the like as well. Hence, its status as the knower is not to be suspected —

body.text: yetu kartṛtayaivātmasiddhirnasa karmatayetyāhusteṣāmātmani smaraṇapratyabhijñāne nopapadyeyātām, tatrāpi hi pūrvakālasaṃbandhitvenātmanaḥ pratibhāso 'ṅgīkaraṇīyaḥ,
body.translated_text: Those who say that the self is established only as agent and not as object — for them, remembering and recognition regarding the self would be untenable; for there too, the self appears as connected with a prior time —

body.text: na ca sāṃparte smaraṇe pūrvakālasaṃbandhinaḥ kartṛtvaṃ saṃbhavatīti kathaṃ kartṛtayā siddhyet, tasmādahaṃpratyayakarmatayaivātmanaḥ siddhiriti ramaṇīyam* ////
body.translated_text: And agenthood of what is connected with a prior time is not possible in present remembering — so how would it be established as agent? Therefore, the self is established as the object of the I-cognition alone — this is elegant —

children.text: atha svaprakāśatvamātmanaḥ sukhādīnāṃ ca kiṃ neṣyate, svaprakāśasya kasyacidapyadarśanāt sarvasyaiva hi vastunaḥ paraprakāśyatvaniyamāt /
children.translated_text: Now, why is self-luminosity of the self and of pleasure and the like not accepted? Because nothing self-luminous is ever observed — for there is a universal rule that all things are illuminated by something other [than themselves].

children.text: svaprakāśatve cātmā suṣuptāvapi prakāśeta, na ca prakāśate, yathoktam- acetanayanneva suṣupta ityucyate iti* ////
children.translated_text: And if [the self were] self-luminous, the self would shine even in deep sleep. But it does not shine, as stated: 'In deep sleep, it is as if unconscious.' ////

children.text: na tu suṣuptāvapi prakāśata evātmā svābhāvikaparamānandayuktaḥ, anyathā katham sukhamahamasvāpsam iti prabodhe pratisaṃdhānaṃ syāt, arthāntaraṃ tu na kiñciccharīramindriyamanyadvā vastu prakāśata ityetāvān svapradāgakābhyāṃ suṣupterbhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: But the self does indeed shine even in deep sleep, endowed with its natural supreme bliss — otherwise, how could there be the recollection upon waking, 'I slept happily'? But nothing else —

children.text: naitadevam- saṃvidvirodhāt, na hi suptānāmātmā sukhaṃ vā prakāśate, nahyabhāsamānaṃ vyavahāramātreṇa prakāśata iti śakyamaṅgīkartum* ////
children.translated_text: This is not so — because it contradicts awareness. For neither the self nor happiness shines for those who are asleep. And it cannot be accepted that what does not appear is luminous merely through verbal usage. ////

body.text: ki ca - suṣvāpādutthitāścaivaṃ nirvidyante hi kāmukāḥ /

children.text: vṛtheyamantareṇaiva kāminīṃ yāminī gatā /
children.translated_text: 'This night has passed in vain without the beloved.'

children.text: āśliṣṭāmapyabuddhvaināṃ nirvidyante mayā /
children.translated_text: Not having been aware of her even while embracing her, they become disenchanted —

children.text: bhuktvā ca paramānandaṃ tasya ca smaraṇādayam /
children.translated_text: And having experienced supreme bliss, from the memory of it, this [disenchantment] —

children.text: svalpālpasukhahānyaivaṃ nirvedo nāvakalpate //
children.translated_text: This disenchantment cannot be explained merely by the gradual loss of small pleasures. //

body.translated_text: Moreover: Lovers who have risen from sleep become disenchanted thus —

body.text: tatsukhaṃ vismṛtaṃ cetsyātsukhamasvāpyamityayam /

children.text: vyavahāro na yujyeta, duḥkhānanubhave tviyam /
children.translated_text: would not be justified. But since there was no experience of suffering, this

children.text: sukhavyavahṛtistasmādguṇavṛttyeti niścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: usage of 'happiness' is established as being by way of a secondary quality (<s>guṇavṛtti</s>).

children.text: prabuddhā hi suṣuptāvavagataṃ kicidapi duḥkhamasaṃsmarantaḥ smaraṇānutpattyaiva suṣuptyavasthāyāṃ me na kiñcidapi duḥkhamāsīdityavagamya tatraiva sukhavyavahāraṃ guṇavṛttyā kurvanti, tathā ca vyavaharanti- etāvantaṃ kālamahamātmānamapyabuddhvā śayito 'smīti /
children.translated_text: For those who have awakened, not remembering any suffering experienced in deep sleep — by the very non-arising of remembrance, understanding that 'no suffering at all was mine in the state of deep sleep' — and thereupon [attributing] happiness to that very [state] —

children.text: tasmātsuṣuptāvaprakāśātmanaḥ svaprakāśatvam, ato mānasapratyakṣagamya evāyamiti sthitam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the self does not shine in deep sleep, [it is] not self-luminous. Hence it is established that it is apprehended only through mental perception (<s>mānasa-pratyakṣa</s>). //

body.translated_text: If that happiness were forgotten, then the usage 'I slept happily' —

body.text: ātmano vyāpakatvam /
body.translated_text: The all-pervasiveness of the self:

body.text:
sa punarayamātmā aṇuḥ śarīraparamāṇo vibhurveti cintanīyam /
tatrāṇuparimāṇatve yugapacchiraḥpādayorvedanānupapattiḥ /
ayaugapadye 'pyatiśaighyyādyaugapadyāvagatiriti cet, syādevaṃ yadyaṇutvaṃ kutaścitsiddhaṃ syāt, tadasiddhau dṛṣṭānusārādanaṇutvameva yuktam /

children.text: tatra śarīraparimāṇatve sāvayavaḥ syāt, tatra dvividhameva hi niravayavadravyam- aṇu vibhu vā, tadasau śarīrasaṃmitaḥ san sāvayavaḥ syāt, tatra bahvavayavakalpanā tāvatāṃ cānyūnanadhikānāmavayavānāṃ puttikāhastidehayoratisaṃkocavistārakalpanaṃ nātīva hṛdayamanurañjayati, tasmādvibhutvameva yuktam /
children.translated_text: If of body-size, it would have parts. For only two types of partless substance exist: atomic and all-pervading. Being co-extensive with the body, it would have parts. And if it had many parts —

children.text: tathā ca śrutiḥ- anantamapāram iti /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'infinite and boundless.'

children.text: bhagavadgītāsu ca vacanam- nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇuracalo 'yaṃ sanātanaḥ iti /
children.translated_text: And the statement in the <s>Bhagavadgītā</s>: 'Eternal, all-pervading, stable, immovable, and primeval.'

children.text: ye copaniṣatsvaṇutvavādāḥ purāṇeṣu ca aṅguṣṭhamātraṃ puruṣam ityādayaste sūkṣmagrahaṇagocaratvābhiprāyāḥ* ////
children.translated_text: And those statements of atomic size in the <s>Upaniṣads</s> and in the <s>Purāṇas</s> — 'the <s>Puruṣa</s> of the measure of a thumb' and the like — these refer to the scope of subtle apprehension. ////

body.translated_text: Now, is this self atomic, of the size of the body, or all-pervading? This is to be considered. If it were of atomic size, the simultaneous experience of sensations in the head and feet would be impossible. And even if non-simultaneous, [one might say] it appears simultaneous due to extreme speed —

children.text: nanu vibhutve sarvaśarīreṣveka evātmāstu kiṃ nānātmabhirabhyupagataiḥ,naivam- ekatve sati yathā paraṇabhede 'pi karturekatvāccakṣuṣā dṛṣṭamarthaṃ yajñadattaḥ pratyabhijānāti- yamahamadarśaṃ tamahaṃ spṛśāmīti, tathā devadattaśarīrasthenātmanā dṛṣṭamarthaṃ yajñadattaḥ pratyabhijānīyāt, śarīrabhede 'pyātmanasaḥ, śarīrabhede 'pyātmanaḥ pratyabhijñāturekatvāt /
children.translated_text: But if [the self is] all-pervading, let there be only one self in all bodies — what need for many selves? Not so — for if there were oneness, then just as when there is oneness of the agent even when the instruments differ, what is seen by the eye, the sacrifice —

children.text: karturekatve 'pi manobhedādvyavastheti cet, na, karaṇatvānmanasaḥ, karaṇabhedasya cakṣurāderbhedavyavasthāpakatvāyogādityuktam* ////
children.translated_text: If [one says:] Even though the agent is one, there is differentiation due to the difference of minds — no, because the mind is [merely] an instrument, and it has been stated that the difference of instruments like the eye and the like cannot establish the differentiation [of experiences]. ////

body.text: cakṣurādikaraṇānāmavyavasthāpakatve 'pi manaḥ karaṇaṃ
body.translated_text: Even if the eye and other instruments cannot establish differentiation, the mind as an instrument

children.text: vyavasthāpakamiti cet na, karaṇatvāviśeṣāt /
children.translated_text: establishes it — if so, no, because there is no distinction [of the mind] from [other] instruments.

children.text: syādapyeṣā kalpanā yadyekātmatve dṛḍhaṃ pramāmaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: This supposition might be entertained if there were a strong proof for the oneness of the self.

children.text: na tu tadasti /
children.translated_text: But there is none.

children.text: yetvātmaikatvavādāḥ śrutiṣu smṛtiṣu purāṇeṣu vā te nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyamupaiti mama sādharmyamāgatāḥ uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ ityādibhirātmabedavacanaiḥ pratyakṣādibhiśca virodhānnaikāntataḥ śaknuvantyātmaikatvaṃ niścāyayitum* ////
children.translated_text: And those statements in <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, and <s>Purāṇas</s> affirming the oneness of the self — these are [contradicted] by statements affirming the difference of selves, such as: 'The stainless one attains supreme equality,' 'Having attained similarity to Me,' 'But the Supreme Person is other' —

body.text: vacanānāṃ hi mitho virodhe siddhavastuviṣayatvena ca vikalpāsaṃbhave pramāṇāntarānnirṇayaḥ syāt, tacca pramāṇāntaraṃ bheda eva samarthamityaikātmyavādānāmavailakṣaṇyaparatvaṃ pūrvoktanyāyenāvagantavyam* ////
body.translated_text: For when statements mutually contradict each other, and since they concern an established entity where the option-interpretation is not possible, determination must be from another means of knowledge. And that other means of knowledge is capable [of establishing] difference alone — thus the doctrine of self-oneness —

body.text: vispaṣṭaṃ caitadvāyudṛṣṭāntopādānāt- veṇurandhrādibhedena bhedaḥ ṣaḍjātisaṃjñitaḥ //
body.translated_text: And this is clearly [shown] from the adoption of the analogy of wind: 'Through the differentiation of the holes of the flute, there is a differentiation called the six [notes] —

children.text: abhedavyāpino vāyostathā tasya mahātmanaḥ iti /
children.translated_text: 'of the wind that pervades without difference; so too of that great soul.'

children.text: na hi vāyudravyaṃ sarvatraikaṃ vyaktibhedasya spaṣṭatvāt, avilakṣaṇasvabhāvasya tu vāyorveṇurandhrākṛtaṃ ṣaḍjādivailakṣaṇyaṃ, evātmano 'pi paśumanuṣyādivailakṣaṇyaṃ dehasaṃbandhakṛtaṃ na svābhāvikamityayamevārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the substance wind is not one everywhere, since the difference of individuals is evident. But wind, being of undifferentiated nature, has the differentiation into <s>ṣaḍja</s> and the like produced by the holes of the flute. Similarly, the self too, in animal, human, and other [bodies] —

children.text: vāyoriti tasyeti caikavacanaṃ sāmānyābhiprāyam, tasmātpratiśarīraṃ bhinnā evātmānaḥ nityāḥ sarvagatā evaṃ ca baddhamuktādivyavasthāpi yuktatarā bhavati //
children.translated_text: The singular number in 'of wind' and 'of that' is with the intention of the universal. Therefore, the selves are distinct for each body, eternal, and all-pervading. And thus the distinction of bound and liberated and the like becomes more reasonable —

body.text: ityātmavādaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus the doctrine of the self. //

body.text: mokṣavādārambhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Beginning of the doctrine of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>):

children.text: kaḥ punarayaṃ mokṣo nāma, vicitravāsanāvaśena vicitranīlapītādirūpeṇa pravahato jñānasaṃtānasya niḥśeṣavāsanocchedānnīlapītādivaicitryaṃ hitvā kevalaṃ saṃvinmātreṇāvasthānamiti kecit /
children.translated_text: What then is this [thing] called <s>mokṣa</s>? [According to some:] The stream of knowledge, which flows in the form of various blue, yellow, and the like under the influence of various impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) — through the complete destruction of impressions, abandoning the variety of blue, yellow, and the like, [achieves] mere —

children.text: aparetu dīpasaṃtānasyeva jñānasaṃtāpanasyoparamam /
children.translated_text: Others [say it is] the cessation of the stream of knowledge, like the cessation of a stream of lamp-flames.

children.text: ubhayamapyetadbāhyārthābhāvamūlamiti tatsadbhāvapratipādanenaiva nirākṛtam* ////
children.translated_text: Both of these are rooted in the denial of external objects — hence they are refuted by the very establishment of the existence of those [external objects]. ////

body.text:
apare tu prapañcavilayamapavargamāhuḥ /
avidyānirmito hi prapañcaḥ svapnaprapañcavat prabodhenaiva brahmavidyayā avidyāyāṃ vilīnāyāṃ svayameva vilīyate /
tathāhi śrutiḥ yatra hi dvaitamiva bhavati taditara itaraṃ paśyati yatra tvasya sarvāmātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyet
body.translated_text: Yet others say that liberation is the dissolution of the manifold world. For the manifold world, constructed by <s>avidyā</s>, like the world of a dream, is dissolved by itself when <s>avidyā</s> is dissolved through awakening, i.e., the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> —
thus. ////

body.text:
tadidamapi prapañcasyāvidyānirmitatvanirāraṇena paramārthatvapratipādanānnirastameveti ātmaivedaṃ sarvamiti sarvasyātmā bhoktetyarthaḥ /
yathā yaḥ kāmayeta rāṣṭraṃ syāmiti rāṣṭrasya bhoktetyarthaḥ /
yathā kāmayeta sarvamidaṃ bhaveyamiti sarvasya bhoktā bhaveyamityarthaḥ /
tathā- ātmā sarvamiti sarvasyātmā bhoktetyarthaḥ /
yattu yatra hi dvaitamiva bhavatīti dvaitabhāvasya bhrāntitvavacanaṃ tadaupacārikam- yathā khalu svapnaprapañcendrajālamṛgatoyādiḥ kiyantañcitkālaṃ dṛṣṭipathamāpannaḥ paścādvilīno bhogyatāmativartate tathāyaṃ śarīrendriyaviṣayarūpaprapañco 'pyasyātmanaḥ kiyantañcitkālamupabhogyaḥ san paścādvināśādanupabhogyo bhavatītyanena sādṛśyena bhrāntirityupacāreṇocyate puruṣāṇāṃ viṣayabhogeṣvāsthānivartanena muktāvabhiruciṃ janayituṃ, yadapi yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūditi muktāvātmano 'dvitīyatvacanaṃ tadapi na prapañcasvarūpaniṣedhārthaṃ kitu sata eva prapañcasyātmasaṃbandhaniṣedhārthaṃ, asyetivacanāt, nahyatraitāvaducyate yatra sarvamātmaivābhūditi, kiṃ tarhi, yatra tvasya sarvamātmaiveti /
tenāsyāyamarthaḥ- yatra yasyāmavasthāyāṃ muktāvityarthaḥ /
asya ātmano dṛśyatvena darśanasādhanatvena darśanāyatanatvena vā na kiñcidanyasaṃbandhi vidyate kintvātmaivāsya sarvaṃ nānyakiñcit tadā kena kaṃ paśyediti /
yathā loke yasya na kiñcidapi bāndhavo vittaṃ vāsti sa evaṃ vadati- na me kañcidasti ahameva sarvaṃ tatra saṃbandhyantaraṃ na kiñcidastītyetāvadvivakṣitam, evaṃ muktāvātmaivātmanaḥ sarvamiti saṃbandhyantarābhāvamātraṃ vivakṣitaṃ na prapañcasvarūpabhāvaḥ, tasmānna prapañcavilayo mokṣaḥ kintu prapañcasaṃbandhavilayaḥ /
tredhā hi prapañcaḥ puruṣaṃ badhnāti bhogāyatanaṃ śarīraṃ bhogasādhanānīndriyāṇi bhogyāḥ śabdādayo viṣayāḥ /
bhoga iti ca sukhaduḥkhaviṣayo 'parokṣānubhava
body.translated_text: This too is refuted by the refutation of the manifold world's being constructed by <s>avidyā</s> and by the establishment of its ultimate reality. And 'all this is the <s>Ātman</s> alone' — meaning, the self of everything is the experiencer. Just as whoever desires —

body.text: ucyate tadasya trividhasyāpi bandhasyātyantiko vilayo mokṣaḥ* ////
body.translated_text: It is stated: The absolute dissolution of this threefold bondage is <s>mokṣa</s>. ////

body.text:
kimidamātyantikatvaṃ pūrvotpannānāṃ śarīrendriyaviṣayāṇāṃ vināśaḥ, anutpannānāṃ cātyantiko 'nutpādaḥ /
kathamatyantānutpattiḥ, utpādakayordharmādharmayorniḥśeṣayoḥ parikṣāyāt /
so 'yaṃ prapañcasaṃbandho bandhasyadvimokṣaśca mokṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: What is this absoluteness? The destruction of previously arisen body, sense-organs, and objects, and the absolute non-origination of those not yet arisen. How is absolute non-origination [possible]? When <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, the producers —

body.text: ānandamokṣavādaḥ /
body.translated_text: The doctrine of blissful liberation:

children.text: nanvevamaśeṣadharmakṣayānmuktasya na kicidsukhaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: But then, through the complete destruction of all <s>dharma</s>, the liberated one would have no happiness whatsoever.

children.text: tataścāpuruṣārtho mokṣaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: And consequently, <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) would not be a human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>).

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ- na hi dharmajanyo muktasyātmanaḥ tathā satyutpattimattvāt vināśī syāt tatrāpunarāvṛttiśrutervirodhaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault — for the self of the liberated one, [whose bliss is] not produced by <s>dharma</s>, would not, being such, be perishable due to having an origin; and the <s>śruti</s> declaring non-return would not be contradicted.

children.text: svābhāvikastvātmānandaḥ saṃsāreṇābhibhūtaḥ san nirmuktasaṃsārasyābhivyaktau bhogyo bhavati svābhāvikatve cānandasya ānandaṃ brahme tyādiśrutisahasraṃ pramāṇam* ////
children.translated_text: The bliss of the self is natural; being suppressed by <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly bondage), it becomes available for enjoyment when manifested for one who is freed from <s>saṃsāra</s>. And for the naturalness of bliss, thousands of <s>śrutis</s> such as '<s>Brahman</s> is bliss' serve as authority.

children.text: nanu sukhābhāve 'pi śrutirasti aśarīraṃ vāva santaṃ na priyāpriye spṛśataḥ iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: even for the absence of pleasure, there is a <s>śruti</s>: 'When one is indeed without a body, neither the pleasant nor the unpleasant touch him.'

children.text: satyam- viṣayasukhābhiprāyaṃ tvevañjātīyakam, anyathānandaśrutivirodhāt /
children.translated_text: True — but such statements are intended to refer to sensory pleasure; otherwise there would be contradiction with the <s>śrutis</s> declaring bliss.

children.text: atha sukhābhāvavacanabalenānandavacanameva duḥkhābhāvābhiprāyaṃ kimiti na vyākhyāyate sukhābhāvavacanānāmatyalpatvātteṣāmevānyathākaraṇaṃ yuktaṃ na bhūyasāmānandavacanānām /
children.translated_text: If [one asks]: by the force of the statements declaring the absence of pleasure, why not interpret the bliss-statements themselves as intended to mean the absence of suffering? — because the statements declaring the absence of pleasure are very few, so it is proper to interpret those few otherwise, not the numerous bliss-statements.

children.text: kiñcānandaśabdasya duḥkhābhāvaparatve 'tyantasvārthahāniḥ syāt, sukhaśabdasya tu sāmānyavacanasya viśeṣe 'pi vyākhyāne nātīva svārthahāniriti tadeva yuktam* ////
children.translated_text: Moreover, if the word '<s>ānanda</s>' (bliss) were taken to mean the absence of suffering, there would be an extreme loss of its primary meaning; but for the word '<s>sukha</s>' (pleasure), which is a general term, even when interpreted in a specific sense [i.e., sensory pleasure], the loss of primary meaning is not so great — hence that [interpretation] alone is appropriate.

body.text:
nanu vidyamāno 'pyānando 'nanubhūyamāno 'kiñcitkara eva, na ca muktasya sarvakaraṇahīnasyānandānubhavaḥ saṃbhavati /
svaprakāśa'yamānanda iti cenna, saṃsārāvasthāyāmaprakāśāt /

children.text: nanu tatrāpyānandasvabhāvaḥ puruṣaḥ prakāśata eva ātmani premotpatteḥ, satyamiti bruvāṇasyātisāhasikasya nottaraṃ vācyam /
children.translated_text: Objection: even there, the person whose nature is bliss does indeed shine forth, since love for the self arises. [Reply:] To one who boldly asserts 'true,' no answer need be given.

children.text: yadi saṃsāriṇo 'pi paramānandamanubhaveyustato muktasya na kaścidatiśaya iti tadevāpuruṣārthatvaṃ mokṣasyāpadyeta, ato balādasukharūpasyāyamabhibhūto na prakāśate /
children.translated_text: If even those in bondage were to experience supreme bliss, then the liberated one would have no superiority — and thus the very uselessness of <s>mokṣa</s> as a human goal would follow. Therefore, being forcibly of a nature that is not pleasant, it [the bliss] is suppressed and does not manifest.

children.text: ko 'yaṃ prakāśamānasyābhibhavo nāma, prakāśanivāraṇaṃ hyabhibhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is this 'suppression' of something that is manifest? For suppression means the prevention of manifestation.

children.text: na ca prakāśamānasyāprakāśanaṃ saṃbhavati, yadi tu naiva prakāśate saṃsārāvasthāyāṃ tasyāmavasthāyāmasataḥ prakāśasya muktāvasthāyāmutpadyamānasya kāraṇaṃ vaktavyam, vijñānameva ca prakāśākhyasya phalasya kāraṇaṃ taccendriyādhīnam, na ca muktasyendriyāṇi saṃbhavantīti kathamānandānubhavaḥ syāt* ////
children.translated_text: And the non-manifestation of what is already manifest is not possible. If, however, it does not manifest at all in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>, then a cause must be stated for the manifestation — which did not exist in that state — arising in the state of liberation. And the cause of the result called 'manifestation' is cognition alone, and that depends on the sense-organs. Since the liberated one does not have sense-organs, how can there be experience of bliss?

body.translated_text: Objection: even if bliss exists, if it is not experienced, it amounts to nothing. And for the liberated one, who is devoid of all instruments [of cognition], experience of bliss is not possible. [If one says:] 'This bliss is self-luminous' — no, because it is not manifest in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text:
ucyate- bāhyendriyāṇyeva muktasya nivartante manastu tasyāmavasthāyāmanuvartate ityānandaśrutibalādevādhyavasīyate /
evaṃ jñānaṃ ca na hi vijñāturvijñāterviparilopo vidyate iti śruteḥ, vijñānaghanaśruteśca, tasmānmuktāvasthāyāṃ mānasapratyakṣeṇa paramānandamanubhavannātmāvatiṣṭhate /

children.text: taduktam- nijaṃ yattvātmacaitanyamānandaśceṣyate ca yaḥ /
children.translated_text: As it has been said: 'That which is the self's own consciousness, and that which is its bliss,

children.text: yacca nityavibhutvādi tairātmā naiva mucyate iti /
children.translated_text: and that which is its eternality, omnipresence, and the like — from these the self is never liberated.'

children.text: yattu tasmātkarmamakṣayādeva hetvabhāvena mucyate /
children.translated_text: As for: 'Therefore, liberation occurs only through the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>, by the absence of a cause [of bondage].'

children.text: nahyabhāvātmakaṃ muktvā mokṣanityatvakāraṇam, iti vārtikaṃ tatparamatamityevamānandamokṣavādino matam* ////
children.translated_text: 'For apart from what is of the nature of absence, there is no cause of the eternality of liberation' — this <s>Vārtika</s> represents the other view. Thus is the position of those who hold the doctrine of blissful liberation.

body.translated_text: Reply: only the external sense-organs cease for the liberated one, but the mind continues in that state — this is determined by the very force of the <s>śruti</s> on bliss. Similarly with knowledge — for the <s>śruti</s> states: 'For the knower, there is no cessation of knowing,' and there is the <s>śruti</s> on '<s>vijñānaghana</s>' (mass of consciousness). Therefore, in the state of liberation, the self abides experiencing supreme bliss through mental perception.

children.text: apare tvāhuḥ- abhāvātmakatvavacanameva svamatamupapattyabhidhānāt ānandavacanaṃ tūpanyāsamātratvā paramatam /
children.translated_text: Others, however, say: the very statement that [liberation] is of the nature of absence is our own view, since it is accompanied by the statement of reasoning; the statement of bliss, however, being merely an introduction [of the opponent's view], is the other's position.

children.text: na hi muktasyānandānubhavaḥ saṃbhavati karaṇābhāvāc /
children.translated_text: For the experience of bliss is not possible for the liberated one, due to the absence of instruments [of cognition].

children.text: manaḥ syāditicet, na, amanaskatvaśruteḥ amanoṣaḍavāgiti //
children.translated_text: If [one says] the mind would serve — no, because of the <s>śruti</s> declaring the absence of mind: '<s>amanas</s> (without mind), <s>aṣaḍavāk</s> (without speech).'

body.text: mokṣāvasthāyāṃ jñānābhāvopapādanam /
body.translated_text: Demonstration that knowledge is absent in the state of liberation.

body.text: yattu na hi vijñāturvijñāterviparilopo vidyate iti tajjñānaśaktyabhiprāyam, anyathā hi suṣuptāvapi jñānānuvṛttiruktā
body.translated_text: As for 'there is no cessation of the knower's knowing' — that is intended to refer to the capacity for knowing. For otherwise, the continuation of knowing would be stated even in deep sleep,

body.text:
syāt sā ca saṃviddhiruddhetyuktam /
vispaṣṭaṃ cāsya śaktyabhiprāyatvam /
evaṃ hi śrūyate- yadvai tanna paśyati paśyanvai tanna paśyati, na hi draṣṭurdṛṣṭerviparilopo vidyate, avināśitvāt na tu taddvitīyamasti tato 'nyadvibhaktaṃ yatpaśyet evamanyānyapi vākyāni jighranvai
body.translated_text: and that is contradicted, since awareness ceases [in deep sleep]. And the intention of [referring to] capacity is quite clear.

body.text: tanna jighrati na hi ghrātughrāterviparilopo vidyate, na śrotuḥ śruterviparilopo vidyate, na spraṣṭuḥ spṛṣṭerviparilopo vidyate, na jñāturjñāterviparilopo vidyate tatra tatra dṛṣṭighrātiśrutispṛṣṭiśabdāścakṣurghrāṇaśrotratvagindriyajanyānāṃ rūpagandhaśabdasparśaviṣayāṇāṃ vācakāḥ nārthāntaraviṣayāṇāṃ nāpi vijñānasāmānyasya, nacaiṣāṃ jñānaviśeṣāṇāṃ vācakāḥ nārthāntaraviṣayāṇāṃ nāpi vijñānasāmānyasya, nacaiṣāṃ jñānaviśeṣāṇāṃ suṣuptau muktau vā kathañcidapyaparilopaḥ saṃbhavati, nahi tadānīmindriyāṇi santi nāpi gandhādayo jñāyante tadubhayābhāve ca na śrutyādiśabdavācyajñānaviśeṣāḥ saṃbhavanti* ////
body.translated_text: For thus it is stated: 'When one does not see, as it were — seeing indeed, one does not see; for there is no cessation of the seer's seeing, due to [its] imperishability. But there is no second thing separate from it that one could see.' And similarly other passages: 'Smelling indeed, one does not smell; there is no cessation of the smeller's smelling; there is no cessation of the hearer's hearing; there is no cessation of the toucher's touching; there is no cessation of the knower's knowing.' In all these, the words 'seeing,' 'smelling,' 'hearing,' 'touching' denote cognitions produced by the eye, nose, ear, and skin sense-organs respectively, having color, smell, sound, and touch as their objects — not cognitions of other objects, nor cognition in general. Nor is the non-cessation of these specific cognitions possible in any way in deep sleep or liberation, for at that time the sense-organs do not exist, nor are smell and the like cognized, and in the absence of both, the specific cognitions denoted by the words 'hearing' and the like are not possible.

children.text: nanu yathā prakāśyāsannidhāvapi savituḥ prakāśakatvaṃ nityam, evamindriyābhāve 'pi nityaiva dṛṣṭiriticet, sayādevam- yadi jñānamātraṃ dṛṣṭyādiśabdānāṃ vācyaṃ syāt, na tu tathāsti, lokaprasiddhyabhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: just as the illuminating capacity of the sun is eternal even in the absence of things to be illuminated, so too seeing is eternal even in the absence of sense-organs. [Reply:] It would be so if the words 'seeing' and the like denoted mere knowledge; but that is not the case, due to the absence of such well-established usage.

children.text: yathā lokaṃ ca śabdārthāvadhāraṇaṃ na yatheccham /
children.translated_text: And the determination of word-meanings is according to common usage, not according to one's wish.

children.text: na hi loke gandhādanyadghrāṇaṃ jighratītyucyate, gandhamapi yadā ghrāṇādanyenānumānādinā jānāti tadā na jighratītyucyate, tasmādghrāṇādīyajanyagandhādiviṣayajñānaviśeṣavācino ghrātyādiśabdāḥ, na ca teṣāṃ suṣuptau muktau vā saṃbhavatyaparilopaḥ, tasmādghrāṇādiśaktāveva prarocanārthaṃ ghrāṇādyupacāraḥ, yathā tema hyannaṃ kriyate iti śaktivartamānatvena prarocanārthaṃ kriyate iti vartamānatvopacāraḥ, tasmāt na jñātujñāterviparilopo vidyata ityedapi śaktyabhiprāyameva* ////
children.translated_text: For in common usage, one does not say 'the nose smells' something other than odor; and even when one knows odor through a means other than the nose, such as inference, one does not say 'one smells.' Therefore, the words 'smells' and the like denote specific cognitions produced by the nose and the like having smell and the like as objects. And their non-cessation in deep sleep or liberation is not possible. Therefore, the figurative attribution of 'smelling' and the like to the capacity alone is for the purpose of encouragement — just as in 'this food is being cooked,' the present tense is figuratively used for what exists as a potential, for the purpose of encouragement. Therefore, 'there is no cessation of the knower's knowing' — this too is intended to refer to capacity alone.

children.text: yattvādityaprakāśakatvavaditi, kiṃ tasya prakāśakatvamabhipretaṃ, yadi timirotsāraṇaṃ, tannityamasyeva sarvadā hyasāvavyavahiteṣu deśeṣu timiramutsādayatyeva, nanvevamātmā sarvadā śṛṇoti suṣuptāvaśravaṇāt /
children.translated_text: As for the [analogy of the] sun's illuminating capacity: what is meant by its 'illuminating capacity'? If it is the dispelling of darkness — that is indeed always his, for he always dispels darkness in unobstructed regions. [But] if so, then the self would always hear — [yet] there is non-hearing in deep sleep.

children.text: atha jñānajanakatvamāditya deśeṣu timiramutsādayatyeva, natvevamātmā sarvadā śṛṇoti suṣuptāvaśravaṇāt /
children.translated_text: If the illuminating capacity of the sun is the generating of knowledge — [regarding] regions..., he always dispels darkness in unobstructed regions. But the self does not always hear — [since] there is non-hearing in deep sleep.

children.text: atha jñānajanakatvamādityasya prakāśakatvam na tannityaṃ, tasmātsāmarthyameva tatrāpi nityaṃ, tasmājjñānaśaktyabhiprāyamidaṃ nityatvābhidhānam* ////
children.translated_text: If the illuminating capacity of the sun is the generating of knowledge — that is not eternal. Therefore, even there, only the capacity is eternal. Hence this statement of eternality is intended to refer to the capacity for knowledge.

children.text: eṣā hyatra vacanavyaktiḥ- yadetatsuṣuptau muktau vātmā na paśyati paśyanneva draṣṭuṃ śaknuvanneva na paśyati /
children.translated_text: For this is the verbal import here: when the self does not see in deep sleep or in liberation — seeing indeed, being capable of seeing, it does not see.

children.text: na hi draṣcurātmano yā darśanaśaktistasyāḥ kadācidapi lopo vidyate sāhyavināśinīti na draṣṭurdvitīyamanyaddarśanasādhanaṃ cakṣurvyāpārarūpaṃ dṛśyaṃ vā tasyāmavasthāyāsamasti yato darśanaṃ syāt, yadyapi dṛśyaṃ rūpādikaṃ svarūpatastasyāmavasthāyāmasti tathāpi dṛśyatā darśanayogyatā tasyāmavasthāyāṃ nāstīti tena rūpeṇābhāvāddṛśyaṃ nāstītyucyate, tasmātsādhanāntaravaikalyāttasyāmavasthāyāṃ na paśyati na śaktivaikalyāt, śaktistu na kadācidapi lupyata iti /
children.translated_text: For the seeing capacity that belongs to the seer, i.e., the self, never ceases, since it is imperishable. But there is no second thing — no other instrument of seeing in the form of eye-activity, nor any visible object — in that state, from which seeing might occur. Although the visible, such as form and the like, exists in its own nature in that state, still, visibility — the fitness for being seen — does not exist in that state; hence, due to the absence of that form [of fitness], it is said that the visible does not exist. Therefore, due to the deficiency of other means, one does not see in that state, not due to the deficiency of capacity; but the capacity is never destroyed.

children.text: evamanyeṣāmapi vākyānāṃ yojanā /
children.translated_text: Similarly is the interpretation of the other passages.

children.text: tathā jñānaśaktyaparilopa eva jñatrānāparilopa ucyate, jñātiśabdaścātrānumānādijñānaparaḥ cakṣurādijñānānāṃ svaśabdairuktatvāt* ////
children.translated_text: Likewise, the non-cessation of the knowing capacity alone is stated as the non-cessation of the knower. And the word 'knower' here refers to knowledge through inference and the like, since knowledge through the eye and the like has been mentioned by their own respective words.

body.text:
evaṃ vijñānaṃ brahma vijñānaghana ityādīnāmapi śaktiparatvaṃ veditavyam /
svayameva śrutyā śaktiparatvaṃ vyākhyātaṃ vijñānaghana evaitebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ samutthāyatānyevānu vinaśyatīti bhūtendriyanāśādātmāpi pramāṇāgocaratvamāpanno vinaṣṭa iva bhavatīti /
na tasyetaḥ pretasya muktasya saṃjñāstīti /
evaṃ yājñavalkyemanokte maitreyī codayatisma atraiva ṅagavān(?)māmohitavān vijñānaghana iti na cāsti saṃjñeti viruddhābhidhānāt iti /

children.text: ṣaṣṭhādhyāye tu vināśāvināśavirodhaścodayiṣyata iti vivekaḥ /
children.translated_text: But in the sixth chapter, the contradiction of destruction and non-destruction will be objected to — this is the distinction.

children.text: evaṃ codito yājñavalkyaḥ parihāramāha- na vā are ahaṃmoha parasparaviruddhaṃ bravīmi, alaṃ vā are idaṃ vijñānāya atrātmatattvaṃ sarvāsvavasthāsu vijñānāya samarthamityarthastena vijñānaghanatvābhidhānaṃ sāmarthyābhiprāyamiti vyākhyātam bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus challenged, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> gives the resolution: 'I am not saying anything contradictory — this is sufficient for knowing (<s>vijñānāya</s>)' — the meaning is that the self-reality is capable of knowing in all states. By this, the statement of being '<s>vijñānaghana</s>' is explained as intended to refer to capacity.

children.text: saṃbhavati ca śaktasyāpi jñānābhāva iti nāsti virodha ityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And since even for one possessing capacity, the absence of knowledge is possible — there is no contradiction. This is the intent.

children.text: anayā ca śrutyā sarvavijñānaśrutayaḥ śaktyabhiprāyā vyākhyātāḥ* ////
children.translated_text: And by this <s>śruti</s>, all <s>śrutis</s> regarding consciousness are explained as intended to refer to capacity.

body.translated_text: Similarly, passages like '<s>vijñānaṃ brahma</s>' (consciousness is <s>Brahman</s>) and '<s>vijñānaghana</s>' (mass of consciousness) should be understood as referring to capacity. The <s>śruti</s> itself explains the capacity-reference: '<s>vijñānaghana</s> — arising from these elements, it perishes along with them' — since through the destruction of the elements and sense-organs, the self too, having become inaccessible to means of knowledge, becomes as if destroyed. And 'there is no designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>) of this departed or liberated one.' Thus when <s>Yājñavalkya</s> stated this, <s>Maitreyī</s> raised the objection: 'Here indeed, sir, you have bewildered me — [first] saying mass of consciousness, and [then] there is no designation — since these are contradictory statements.'

body.text: yadi śaktirasti tatastasyāvasthāyāṃ tataḥ kena jñānānutpattiḥ jñānasādhanānāmindriyāṇāṃ jñeyānāṃ ca viṣayāṇāmabhāvāt /
body.translated_text: If the capacity exists, then why does knowledge not arise in that state? Because the sense-organs, which are the means of knowledge, and the objects to be known are absent.

children.text: tadāha yatra hi dvaitamiva bhavati taditara itaraṃ paśyati, yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyet ityādi, tadetatprāgeva vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: Hence it is said: 'Where there is, as it were, duality, there one sees the other' and 'but where everything has become one's own self, then by what would one see whom?' and so on — this has been explained earlier.

children.text: evamarthāntarajñāne sādhanābhāvānnirākṛte sati ātmānameva muktāvasthāyāṃ jānātvityāśaṅkyāha vijñātāramare kena vijānīyāt iti nahyātmāpi vināsādhanena jñātuṃ śakyate manasā khalvasau saṃsārāvasthāyāṃ jñāyate na ca muktasya manaḥsaṃbangho 'sti ataḥ kenātmānaṃ jānātviti vyakta eva muktasyātmajñānasyābhāve jñānaśaktimātrasyāvasthānaṃ śrutyā darśitaṃ, tasmānniḥsaṃbandho nirānandaśca mokṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: When knowledge of other things has thus been precluded due to the absence of means, if one raises the objection that the self should at least know itself in the liberated state — [the reply is:] 'O <s>Maitreyī</s>, by what would one know the knower?' For even the self cannot be known without a means — in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>, it is known through the mind, and the liberated one has no connection with the mind. Therefore, by what would one know the self? — thus the absence of self-knowledge for the liberated one is clearly shown by the <s>śruti</s>, and only the capacity for knowledge persists. Therefore, <s>mokṣa</s> is without any relation and without bliss.

body.text: ātmano jñānānandasvarūpatvasya khaṇḍanam //
body.translated_text: Refutation of the view that the self is of the nature of knowledge and bliss.

body.text:
nanu nātmano 'nyadvijñānamānando vā kintvātmaiva jñānamānandaśca vijñānaṃ brahma ānandaṃ brahma iti śruteḥ, ātmā ca suṣuptiturīyayorapi bhavatīti kathaṃ vijñānasya cānandasya cābhāvaḥ /
naitadevaṃ, yaddhi vastvantaraprakāśajananasvabhāvaṃ vastu yasminsati kimapyarthāntaraṃ prakāśata eva talloke vijñānaśabdenocyate, nacātmani sati kiñcidanyatprakāśata eva, vidyamāne 'pi
body.translated_text: Objection: knowledge and bliss are not different from the self; rather, the self itself is knowledge and bliss — as per the <s>śruti</s>: '<s>vijñānaṃ brahma</s>' (consciousness is <s>Brahman</s>), '<s>ānandaṃ brahma</s>' (bliss is <s>Brahman</s>). And the self exists even in deep sleep and <s>turīya</s> — so how can knowledge and bliss be absent? [Reply:] This is not so. For that entity which has the nature of generating the manifestation of other things — in whose presence something else necessarily becomes manifest — is called by the word 'knowledge' in common usage. But in the presence of the self, nothing else necessarily becomes manifest, even though it exists

body.text: tasminsuṣuptyavasthāyāmarthāntarasya kasyacidapyadarśanāt ato na jñānamātmā* ////
body.translated_text: in the state of deep sleep, since nothing whatsoever is perceived. Therefore, the self is not knowledge.

body.text:
nanu prakāśajananasvabhāvo 'pi sahakārivaikalyānna janayet /
satyaṃ na janayati /
yasmiṃstu sahakārisaṃnidhāne tatkṛte vānyasminnāgantuke sati niyamena prakāśata evārthāntaraṃ tajjñānaśabdavācyam /

children.text: tathā gītiśravaṇapriyāliṅganacandradarśanamadhurāsvādasurabhighrāṇādijanyamāhlādamānandasukhaśabdāvabhidadhāte, nacaivaṃrūpatvamātmāno 'sti, yathā hyanyasukheṣu sukharūpaṃ pratyabhijñāyate naivamātmani pratyabhijānīmo yenānandamiti ca saṃjñetyucyate na sā laukikī nāpi vaidikī /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the words '<s>ānanda</s>' and '<s>sukha</s>' denote the delight produced by hearing music, embracing a beloved, seeing the moon, tasting sweets, smelling fragrances, and the like. And the self is not of such a nature. For just as in other pleasures, the form of pleasure is recognized [through experience], one does not similarly recognize [pleasure] in the self — hence the designation 'bliss' [for the self] is neither worldly nor Vedic.

children.text: yadi paraṃ vṛddhyādivatparibhāṣyeta tadastu yathākāmam /
children.translated_text: If, however, it were to be stipulated [as a technical term], like '<s>vṛddhi</s>' (a grammatical term) and the like — then let it be as you wish.

children.text: yattu vijñānaṃ brahma ānandaṃ brahma iti ca sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ taddharmamātravacanatvena vartante, satyaṃ, na bāhulyena vartante, kadācittu guṇamātravacanānāmapi guṇini prayogo bhavati yathā śīto madhuro rasaḥ snigdho guruśceti rasaśabdo dravye prayujyate, anyathā śītādiśabdasāmānādhikaraṇyāyogāt /
children.translated_text: As for the co-referential usage (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) in 'consciousness is <s>Brahman</s>' and 'bliss is <s>Brahman</s>' — these function as denoting mere attributes [of <s>Brahman</s>]. True, they do not predominantly so function; but sometimes words denoting mere qualities are also used with reference to the substance possessing those qualities — as in 'the taste (<s>rasa</s>) is cold, sweet, oily, and heavy,' where the word <s>rasa</s> (taste) is used for a substance (liquid), since otherwise, the co-referential usage with the words 'cold' and the like would be impossible.

children.text: kiṃ ca rasaṃ hyevāyaṃ vidvān, sa eko brahmaṇa ānanda, iti ṣaṣṭhyānandādbrahma vyatiricyate* ////
children.translated_text: Moreover, [in the <s>śruti</s>] 'having known the <s>rasa</s> (essence), this knower [attains bliss],' and 'that one bliss of <s>Brahman</s>' — by the genitive case, bliss is distinguished from <s>Brahman</s>. ////

body.translated_text: Objection: even what has the nature of generating manifestation may not generate it due to the deficiency of auxiliary conditions. [Reply:] True, it does not generate [in that case]. But that in whose presence — whether the auxiliary condition is available or some other adventitious [factor] is present — something else necessarily becomes manifest — that is what is denoted by the word 'knowledge.'

body.text: kiṃ ca na me sāṃprataṃ kiñcidapi sukhaṃ duḥkhameva tu sarvātmanā mameti sukhābhāve duḥkhānubhave cānusaṃdhīyamānasyātmanaḥ kathamānandarūpatā syāt /

children.text: kiṃ ca svaprakāśānandarūpamātmānamabhyupagacchatāmasmākaṃ caitāvadavivādaṃ suṣuptitulyā muktiriti /
children.translated_text: Moreover, for us who accept the self as having the nature of self-luminous bliss — this alone is undisputed: that liberation is like deep sleep.

children.text: saṃsārānuvṛttyanuvṛttimātraṃ bhidyate anyatsarvaṃ tulyam /
children.translated_text: The only difference is the continuation of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) [in the latter case]; everything else is the same.

children.text: tathā ca śrutirapi- tā etāḥ prajā aharaharbrahmalokaṃ yanti /
children.translated_text: And the <s>śruti</s> too [says]: 'These beings go to the world of <s>Brahman</s> day after day;

children.text: aharaharāgacchanti iti suṣuptiṃ brahmalokaśabdena vadantī tulyatvametayordarśayati, suṣuptiścāsmākamapi gocaro na ca tatrānandānubhavo 'stīti vyaktametat, tasmānnirānando mokṣaḥ, duḥkhaparilopācca puruṣārthantvam* ////
children.translated_text: and they come back day after day' — by calling deep sleep 'the world of <s>Brahman</s>,' [the <s>śruti</s>] shows the identity of the two. And deep sleep is within our own experience — yet there is no experience of bliss therein. This is evident. Therefore, liberation is without bliss; and [it is] a human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) because of the cessation of suffering. ////

body.translated_text: Moreover, 'I have no pleasure at all at this present moment; there is only suffering in every respect for me' — for the self, which is reflected upon as having the absence of pleasure and the experience of suffering, how can there be a nature of bliss?

body.text: sukhalopādapuruṣārthatvamapīticet- naivamalpaṃ hi saṃsāre sukhaṃ tadapi sūrayaḥ //
body.translated_text: [If one says] 'It is not a human goal because of the loss of pleasure too' — [we reply:] Not so, for: 'The little pleasure that exists in <s>saṃsāra</s> — even that, the wise

body.text: bahuprayāsasādhyatvādduḥkhamevānujānate //
body.translated_text: consider to be suffering, because it is attainable only through great effort.'

body.text: janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhānyanudinaṃ nṛṇam //
body.translated_text: 'The sufferings of birth, death, old age, and disease befall human beings daily;

children.text: svayameva vināyatnānnipatanti sahasradhā /
children.translated_text: they descend by themselves in a thousand ways, without any effort [on one's part].'

children.text: vihitākaraṇānnityaṃ pratiṣiddhaniṣevaṇāt /
children.translated_text: 'From not performing what is enjoined, and from constantly engaging in what is prohibited,

children.text: mahadāmuṣmikaṃ duḥkhaṃ yatnairnāva gamyate //
children.translated_text: great suffering in the next life is not avoided by efforts.'

body.text: bahuduḥkhapariṣviktaṃ yannāma khalpakaṃ sukham //
body.translated_text: 'The so-called meager pleasure that is embraced by much suffering

body.text: surāpānādisukhavadvarjanīyam vivikinām //
body.translated_text: should be avoided by the discerning, like the pleasure of drinking liquor.'

body.text: evaṃbhūte 'pi saṃsāre ye raktāḥ sukhatṛṣṇayā //
body.translated_text: 'Even though <s>saṃsāra</s> is of such a nature, those who are attached to it through craving for pleasure —

body.text: na teṣāmadhikāro 'sti muktiśāstre kathañcana //
body.translated_text: they have no qualification whatsoever for the scripture of liberation.'

children.text: saṃsāsādvijante ye dṛṣṭalokaparāvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those who are disgusted with <s>saṃsāra</s>, having seen the highs and lows of the world —

children.text: ta eva khalu mucyante na tu yaḥ prākṛto janaḥ //
children.translated_text: they alone are indeed liberated, not the common person.'

body.text: teṣāmevāpargākhyaḥ puruṣārtho mahātmanām //
body.translated_text: 'For those great souls alone is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) the human goal;

children.text: teṣāmevādhikāraśca muktiṣāśtre manīṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: and for those wise ones alone is there qualification for the scripture of liberation.'

children.text: tenābhāvātmakatve 'pi mukternāpuruṣārthatā //
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, even though liberation is of the nature of absence [of pleasure and pain], it is not lacking in being a human goal.'

body.text: sukhaduḥkhopabhogo hi saṃsāra iti śabdyate //
body.translated_text: 'For the experience of pleasure and pain is what is called <s>saṃsāra</s>;

body.text: tayoranupabhogaṃ tu mokṣaṃ mokṣavido viduḥ //
body.translated_text: and the non-experience of both — that, the knowers of liberation know as liberation.'

body.text: śrutirapyetamevāha bhedaṃ saṃsāramokṣayoḥ //
body.translated_text: 'The <s>śruti</s> too declares this very distinction between <s>saṃsāra</s> and liberation:

body.text: na ha vai saśarīrasya priyāpriyavihīnatā //
body.translated_text: 'Indeed, for one who is embodied, there is no freedom from the pleasant and the unpleasant;

body.text: aśarīraṃ vā vasantaṃ smapṛśato na priyāpriye //
body.translated_text: but the pleasant and unpleasant do not touch one who is without a body.'

body.text: ānandātmakamātmānaṃ ye vadanti svaprabham //
body.translated_text: 'Those who say the self is of the nature of bliss and self-luminous —

body.text: tanmate 'pi ca saṃsārānmukteretāvatī bhidā //
body.translated_text: even on their view, the difference between <s>saṃsāra</s> and liberation is only this much:'

body.text: ātmā hyānandarūpo 'sau saṃsāre 'pi prakāśate //
body.translated_text: 'The self, being of the nature of bliss, manifests even in <s>saṃsāra</s>;

body.text: tāveva(?) sa mokṣe 'pi nādhikyaṃ tasya kiñcana //
body.translated_text: it is the same in liberation too — there is nothing additional for it.'

body.text: atha saṃsāravelāyāmānando na prakāśate //
body.translated_text: 'But if [you say] bliss does not manifest during <s>saṃsāra</s> —

body.text: nahyaprakāśanaṃ yuktaṃ svaprakāśasya vastunaḥ //
body.translated_text: it is not reasonable for a self-luminous thing not to manifest.'

children.text: yadyasau na prakāśeta kintarhyanyatprakāśate /
children.translated_text: 'If that [bliss] does not manifest, then what else does manifest?'

children.text: ātmasvarūpamiti cennanu cānanda eva tat //
children.translated_text: '[If you say] "the essential nature of the self" — but that is indeed bliss itself.'

children.text: taccetprakāśate nūnamānando 'pi prakāśate /
children.translated_text: 'If that [essential nature] manifests, then surely bliss too manifests.'

children.text: tena śabdādiviṣayajanyayoḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, the cessation of pleasure and pain produced by objects such as sound and the like

children.text: nivṛttireva saṃsārādapavarga itīryate /
children.translated_text: [in their separation] from <s>saṃsāra</s> alone is called liberation (<s>apavarga</s>).'

children.text: tataśca sukhalopena mukterna puruṣārthatā //
children.translated_text: 'And therefore, liberation is not [deprived of being] a human goal by the loss of pleasure.'

children.text: yadyasmākaṃ puruṣārthatā /
children.translated_text: 'If it were not a human goal for us —'

children.text: yadyasmākaṃ bhavettarhi tulyaiṣā bhavatāmapi /
children.translated_text: 'If [you say] it were so for us, then equally for you too;'

children.text: sukhaduḥkhahānimasatastasya bhūyo duḥkhavivarjanāt //
children.translated_text: 'the loss of pleasure and pain — for that which is non-existent — [is rather] the abandonment of further suffering.'

body.text: mokṣasya puruṣārthatvamāvayorubhayoḥ samam //
body.translated_text: 'The status of liberation as a human goal is equal for both of us.'

body.text: sukhaduḥkhavihīno 'to muktaḥ svastho 'vatiṣṭhate //
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, the liberated one, free from pleasure and pain, remains in [his] natural state.'

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: muktisvarūpakathanam //
body.translated_text: Description of the nature of liberation:

body.text:
kimidaṃ svastha iti, ye hyāgamamāpāyino dharmā buddhisukhaduḥkhecchādveṣaprayatnadharmāgharmāsaṃskārastānapahāya yadasya svaṃ naijaṃ jñānaśaktisattādravyatvādi tasminnavatiṣṭhata ityarthaḥ /
yadi tu saṃsārāvasthāyāmavidyamāno 'pyānando muktāvasthāyāṃ janyata ityucyate tato janimattvādanityo mokṣaḥ syāt /

children.text: kena cāsāvanubhāvyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And by what would that [bliss] be experienced?

children.text: na hi svaprakāśatvaṃ kasyacitsaṃbhavītyuktam /
children.translated_text: For it has been said that self-luminosity is not possible for anything.

children.text: na ca manasānubhavaḥ saṃbhavatīti muktasya manaso 'bhāvāt amanalaskatvaśruterityuktam /
children.translated_text: Nor is experience through the mind possible — since the liberated [soul] has no mind, due to the <s>śruti</s> that [the liberated state is] 'without mind' (<s>amanaskatva</s>).

children.text: ata eva nityo 'pyānandaḥ saṃsāradaśāyāmabibhūtatvādanubhūtopi muktāvabhibhave nivṛtte manasānubhūyate ityedapi nirastam* ////
children.translated_text: For the same reason, even the [claim that] eternal bliss, though overpowered during the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>, is experienced in liberation through the mind when the overpowering ceases — this too has been refuted. ////

body.translated_text: What does 'in [his] natural state' (<s>svastha</s>) mean? Those adventitious qualities — intellect, pleasure, pain, desire, aversion, effort, merit, demerit, and dispositions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) — that come and go: having abandoned these, [the self] abides in what is its own, innate [nature] — namely, the capacity for knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>), existence (<s>sattā</s>), substancehood (<s>dravyatva</s>), and the like. This is the meaning. But if it is said that bliss, which does not exist during the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>, is produced in the state of liberation — then, being subject to origination, liberation would be non-eternal.

body.text:
kiṃ ca sukhaviśiṣcātmānubhavaḥ puruṣārtho na sukhamātrānubhavaḥ, na ca muktāvātmānubhavaḥ saṃbhavati vijñātāramare kena vijānīyāt iti kaṇṭhenaiva śrutyā niṣiddhatvāt alaṃ vā are idaṃ vijñānāya iti ca śrutyā vijñānaśabdasya muktasya vijñānamaśakyamabhyupagantum /
nahyasyāḥ śruteḥ priyāpriyāsparśaśruteśca tattvakathanaṃ muktvā kathañcidanyaparatvaṃ saṃbhavati /
vijñānāśrutayastu śaktāveva vijñānopacāraṃ kurvanti prarocanārthatayetyupapannam /
evamānandaśrutayo 'pi puruṣārthatvasāmānyātsukhatvopacāreṇa prarocanārthatayā pravṛttāḥ /
yuktaṃ caitat vacanayorvirodhe 'nyato nirṇayaḥ iti /
virodhaścātrānandapriyābhāvavacanayoḥ /
na cābhāvavacanaṃ vaiṣayikābhiprāyam, itarattu svābhāvikābhiprāyamiti śakyaṃ vaktum /
ubhayatrāpi sāmānyopādānādatyantasamānaviṣayatvāt /
ataḥ pramāṇāntaravaśādānandavacanaṃ duḥkhābhāvaparam, itarattu yathāśrutamiti nyāyyam /
tasmātsukhaduḥkhādisamastavaiśeṣikātmaguṇocchedo mokṣaḥ /
sukhaduḥkhocchedaśca dharmādharmayorucchedāt,
body.translated_text: Moreover, the human goal is the experience of the self as qualified by pleasure, not the mere experience of pleasure. And the experience of the self is not possible in liberation, since the <s>śruti</s> explicitly declares: 'by what should one know the knower?' (<s>vijñātāram are kena vijānīyāt</s>). And from the <s>śruti</s> 'Enough — this is not for the purpose of knowing' (<s>alam vā are idaṃ vijñānāya</s>), it is impossible to accept the word <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) as [characterizing] the liberated state. For there is no way to construe these <s>śrutis</s> — the one about the non-touching of pleasant and unpleasant, and this one — as referring to anything other than their literal meaning. But the <s>śrutis</s> [that speak of] consciousness use the word <s>vijñāna</s> figuratively with reference to the mere capacity [for consciousness], for the purpose of inspiring [spiritual endeavor] — and this is appropriate. Likewise, the <s>śrutis</s> about bliss too, because of the commonality with [the concept of] a human goal, function through the figurative usage of [the word] 'pleasure,' for the purpose of inspiring [endeavor]. And this is fitting — for when there is a contradiction between [two sets of] statements, the determination [of meaning] is to be made from one [set]. And the contradiction here is between the statements about bliss and the statements about the absence of the pleasant. Nor can it be said that the statement about absence refers to adventitious [pleasure], while the other refers to innate [bliss] — since in both cases, the general terms are employed, [indicating] that the subject matter is completely the same. Therefore, by the force of another means of knowledge, the statements about bliss refer to the absence of suffering, while the other [statements about absence of pleasant and unpleasant] are to be taken literally. Hence, liberation is the destruction of all the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> qualities of the self, such as pleasure, pain, and the rest. And the destruction of pleasure and pain [results] from the destruction of merit and demerit;

body.text: dharmādharmayorucchedaścotpannānāṃ dharmādharmāṇāmupabhogena nityanaimittikakarmānuṣṭhānenātmajñānena ca virodhāt, utpādyānāṃ ca kāmyānuṣṭhānanimittānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ tadanuṣṭhānenānutpādāt, vihitākaraṇapratiṣiddhānuṣṭhānanimittānāṃ cādharmāṇāṃ vihitānuṣṭhānena pratiṣiddhākaraṇena ca parihārāt, asati śarīrārambhe pūrvaśarīranipāte cāśarīro 'vasthito mukto bhavati //
body.translated_text: and the destruction of merit and demerit [results from the following]: for merits and demerits that have already arisen — through the exhaustion by experiencing [their results], through the performance of obligatory and occasional rituals, and through knowledge of the self, which is incompatible [with them]; for merits that would otherwise be produced — namely those caused by the performance of desire-motivated rituals — through their non-production by abstaining from such performance; and for demerits caused by not performing what is enjoined and by performing what is prohibited — through their avoidance by performing what is enjoined and abstaining from what is prohibited. When there is no initiation of a [new] body, and when the previous body perishes, [the soul,] remaining without a body, is liberated. //

body.text: ātmajñānasya kratumokṣobhayopayogitvam /
body.translated_text: The utility of self-knowledge for both ritual and liberation:

body.text:
nanvātmajñānaṃ kratvartham /
satyam /
puruṣārthamapi ca tat saṃyogabhedāt /
yattāvat avināśī vā are 'yamātmā ityādinā śarīrādvyatiriktanityātmasvarūpasadbhāvajñānaṃ
body.translated_text: Objection: Self-knowledge is for the purpose of ritual action. True. But it also serves the purpose of the person (<s>puruṣārtha</s>), because of the difference in its connection. The knowledge of the existence of the eternal self distinct from the body, [as stated in:] 'this self is indeed imperishable' (<s>avināśī vā are 'yam ātmā</s>) and the like —

children.text: tatpāralaukikaphalakarmānuṣṭhānaupayikatvātkarmajñānavadeva sāmarthyataḥ kratusaṃyogātkratvartham /
children.translated_text: since it is useful for the performance of rituals that have otherworldly results, it serves the purpose of ritual action (<s>kratu</s>) through its connection [with ritual], just like knowledge of the [specific] rituals, by its own capacity.

children.text: yathāhi jyotiṣṭomodivākyādhyayanaṃ dṛṣṭenaivānuṣṭhānaupayikatvaṃ jñānaṃ janayatīti tadarthatayādhyayanavidhinā vidhīyate tathā avināśī vā areyamātmā ityādivākyānāmapyadhyayanavidhireva karmānuṣṭhānopayogyātmajñānārthatāṃ vidhatte /
children.translated_text: For just as the study of <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and other ritual sentences generates knowledge that is visibly useful for [ritual] performance, and is thus enjoined by the injunction of study for that purpose — so too, the injunction of study for sentences such as 'this self is indeed imperishable' (<s>avināśī vā are 'yam ātmā</s>) and the like prescribes [their study] for the purpose of self-knowledge that is useful for ritual performance.

children.text: tadyadi pramāṇāntareṇātmanaḥ śarīrādiviveko naikāntataḥ siddhyati tato dṛḍhavivekapratipādakānāmupaniṣadvākyānāṃ vispaṣṭameva phalam /
children.translated_text: If, however, the distinction of the self from the body and the like is not conclusively established through another means of knowledge, then the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> sentences that firmly convey [this] distinction have a manifest purpose.

children.text: yathoktam- ityāha nāstikyanirākariṣṇurātmāstitāṃ bhāṣyakṛdatra yuktyā //
children.translated_text: As stated: 'Wishing to refute materialism, the commentator (<s>Bhāṣyakṛt</s>) here [establishes] the existence of the self through reasoning. //

children.text: dṛḍhatvametadviṣayaḥ prabodhaḥ prayāti vedāntaniṣevaṇena iti /
children.translated_text: Firm [conviction] in this subject is attained through the cultivation of <s>Vedānta</s>.'

children.text: atha tvanyato 'pi siddhyati, tato yathaivānyathāpi kratujñānasaṃbhave 'dhyayanopāttavedavākyāvagatakarmarūpāṇāmeva puṃsāṃ karmasvadhikāraḥ tathaivādhyāyanopāttopaniṣadvākyāvagatātmatattvānāmevādhikāra ityadhyayanavidhibalādeva kalpyate* ////
children.translated_text: If, however, [the distinction of self from body] is established through other [means] as well, then just as when ritual knowledge is available from other sources, only those who have learned the form of the rituals through Vedic sentences acquired by study have qualification for those rituals — so too, only those who have learned the truth of the self through <s>Upaniṣadic</s> sentences acquired by study have qualification [for liberation]. This is to be understood by the force of the injunction of study alone. ////

children.text: yattvātmasadbhāvapratipādanopakrame vidhisarūpaṃ vākyam ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ ityādi tadvakṣyamāṇasyārthasyātigahanatvānmahopayogatvācca kathaṃ hi nāmālasyaṃ hitvā śraddhāviśeṣeṇa vakṣyamāṇamarthaṃ pratipadyetetyātāvanmātrārtham /
children.translated_text: As for the sentence resembling an injunction that appears at the beginning of the teaching about the existence of the self — 'the self is indeed to be seen' (<s>ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ</s>) and the like — since the subject matter to be expounded is exceedingly profound and of great utility, [the purpose of this injunction-like form is simply:] 'How indeed would one, abandoning laziness, understand the subject to be expounded with special faith?' — it serves only this much purpose [of exhortation].

children.text: tasmādetajjñānaṃ dṛṣṭopayogitvātkratvartham* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, this knowledge serves the purpose of ritual, because of its observed utility. ////

children.text: yāni punaritikartavyatāviśeṣayuktānyupāsanātmakāni vidhīyante teṣāṃ kratau dṛṣṭopayogābhāvādadṛṣṭaphalatvam /
children.translated_text: But the meditations (<s>upāsanās</s>) that are enjoined with specific procedural details — since they have no observed utility for ritual, they have unseen results (<s>adṛṣṭaphala</s>).

children.text: adṛṣṭaṃ ca phalaṃ vākyaśeṣāddvividhaṃ abhyudayarūpaṃ niḥśreyasarūpaṃ ca, sarvankāmānāpnoti so 'śnute sarvānkāmān ityādyabhyudayaphalam /
children.translated_text: And the unseen result, from the remainder of the sentence, is of two kinds: of the nature of prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and of the nature of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). 'He attains all desires, he enjoys all desires' and the like — these have prosperity as their result.

children.text: na sa punarāvartate ityādi niḥśreyasaphalamiti vivekaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'He does not return again' and the like — these have the highest good as their result. Such is the distinction. //

body.text: ātmanityatvenādhikaraṇopasaṃhāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Conclusion of the section through the eternality of the self: //

children.text: yattu vijñānaghana evaitebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ samutthāya tānyevānuvinaśyati na pretya saṃjñāsti ityanena brāhmaṇena bhūtacaitanyamuktamityāśaṅkyate tatsvayameva brāhmaṇenātreva mā bhagavanmohāntaṃ prāpitavānpūrvamajarāmṛtvamabhidhāyādhunā vināśītyabhidhānāditi pūrvapakṣaṃ codyākhyamuktvā siddhāntaparihāra uktaḥ /
children.translated_text: As for [the passage] 'Being a mere mass of consciousness (<s>vijñānaghana</s>), having arisen from these elements, it perishes along with them; after death there is no consciousness' — when it is suspected that this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage teaches that consciousness is [merely a product of] the elements, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> itself [provides the answer]: first speaking of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) — which is called an objection — 'O Revered One, you have led me to complete confusion, having first declared [the self to be] unaging and immortal, and now [declaring it to be] perishable' — and then the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) and its resolution are stated.

children.text: avināśī vā are 'yamātmānucchittidharmā ityuktvā kathaṃ tarhi vināśavacanamityāśaṅkya mātrāsaṃsargatvasya bhavatītyuktam /
children.translated_text: Having said 'this self is indeed imperishable, of indestructible nature' (<s>avināśī vā are 'yam ātmā anucchittidharmā</s>), and anticipating the question 'then how is the statement about destruction [to be explained]?' — it is said: 'that is because of the contact with <s>mātrās</s> (material elements).'

children.text: mātrāśabdena bhūtendriyāṇi dharmādharmau ca vikāraśabdavācyā ucyante* ////
children.translated_text: By the word <s>mātrā</s>, the gross elements, the sense-organs, and merit and demerit — which are denoted by the word <s>vikāra</s> (modification) — are meant. ////

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati- vijñānaghanaśabdena jñānaśaktisvabhāvasyātmano 'bhidhānam, sa hyetebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ samutthāya mukto bhūtvā tānyevānuvinaśyati bhūtavināśātso 'pi vinaṣṭa iva bhavatīti, bhūtastho hyasau svayaṃ pratyakṣeṇa vinaśyatītyucyate, tadanena prakāreṇa mātrāṇāmeva vināśa ityucyate nātmana ityavirodhaḥṣa /
children.translated_text: What is meant is this: By the word <s>vijñānaghana</s> (mass of consciousness), the self, whose nature is the capacity for knowledge, is denoted. Having arisen from these elements — i.e., having become liberated — it perishes along with them; i.e., when the elements perish, it too appears as if perished. For while residing in the elements, it itself is said to perish by perception. By this means, it is said that only the <s>mātrās</s> (material elements) perish, not the self — thus there is no contradiction.

children.text: taduktam- avināśī svarūpeṇa puruṣo yā tu nāśitā //
children.translated_text: As stated: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> (self) is imperishable in its essential nature; the destruction that is spoken of

body.text:
mātrāṇāṃ sādhikārāṇāṃ bhūtādīnāmasaṃjñitā iti /
kimidaṃ bhūtādīnāmasaṃjñiteti /
yadi tāvat na pretya saṃjñāstītyasya vyākhyānaṃ, tadayuktam /

children.text: na hi na pretya saṃjñāstītyanena bhūtādīnāmasaṃjñitvamucyate /
children.translated_text: For the [statement] 'after death there is no consciousness' does not say that the elements and the like lack consciousness.

children.text: kintarhyātmana eva muktasya saṃjñābhāvo 'nenocyate, tasyaivopāyābhāvena tatkena kaṃ paśyedityādinā vijñānāramare kena vijānīyādityantena vijñānābhāvopapādanāt /
children.translated_text: Rather, it says that the self itself, when liberated, has no consciousness — the impossibility of consciousness for it [being established] by the absence of means, through [<s>śruti</s> texts] from 'by what should one see' to 'by what should one know the knower' (<s>vijñātāram are kena vijānīyāt</s>), which establish the impossibility of consciousness [in liberation].

children.text: satyam /
children.translated_text: True.

children.text: nedamasya vyākhyānaṃ, prakaraṇārthopasaṃhārastvayaṃ - yata evaṃ pūrvoktena nyāyena bhūtacaitanyaṃ na saṃbhavati brāhmaṇenāpi tathaivoktam, tasmādbhūtendriyāṇāmasaṃjñitvamacaitanyam, anyastu nityaścetanaḥ tasya svargagamanasaṃbhavavānna svargaṃ lokaṃ yātītyasya pratyakṣavirodhaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is not an explanation of that [passage]; rather, this is a summation of the topic: Since, as argued above, the doctrine that consciousness is [merely a product of] the elements is not possible, and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passage itself says the same — therefore, the elements and sense-organs lack consciousness, are non-sentient; but there is another [entity] that is eternal and sentient. For that [self], the going to heaven is possible — hence 'he goes to the heavenly world' does not contradict perception. //

body.translated_text: is of the <s>mātrās</s> — the elements and the like — that are connected with [karmic] eligibility; it is their [mere] loss of designation.' What is this 'loss of designation of the elements and the like'? If this is meant as an explanation of 'after death there is no consciousness' — that is improper.

body.text: śabdānityatādhikaraṇam //6 //
body.translated_text: The section on the non-eternality of sound (<s>śabdānityatādhikaraṇa</s>): // 6 //

body.text: karmaike tatra darśanāt // Jaim_1,1.6 //
body.translated_text: Some [hold that sound] is an action, because that is observed. // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.6 //

body.text: asthānāt // Jaim_1,1.7 //
body.translated_text: Because of the impossibility of [an action] remaining. // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.7 //

body.text: karoti śabdāt // Jaim_1,1.8 //
body.translated_text: Because of the word 'makes' (<s>karoti</s>). // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.8 //

body.text: sattvāntare ca yaugapadyāt // Jaim_1,1.9 //
body.translated_text: And because of simultaneity in different loci. // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.9 //

body.text: prakṛtivikṛtyośca // Jaim_1,1.10 //
body.translated_text: And because of the original and the modified [forms]. // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.10 //

body.text: vṛddhiśca kartṛbhūmnāsya // Jaim_1,1.11 //
body.translated_text: 'And the augment [is explained] by the plurality of speakers.' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.11 //

body.text: samaṃ tu tatra darśanam // Jaim_1,1.12 //
body.translated_text: 'But the perception [of the word] there is the same.' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.12 //

body.text: sataḥ paramadarśanaṃ viṣayānāgamāt // Jaim_1,1.12 //
body.translated_text: 'Of what exists, the perception is ultimate, since the object does not newly come [into being].' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.12 //

body.text: prayogasya param // Jaim_1,1.14 //
body.translated_text: '[The perception is] subsequent to the utterance.' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.14 //

body.text: ādityavadyaugapadyam // Jaim_1,1.15 //
body.translated_text: 'Like the sun, [there is] simultaneity.' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.15 //

body.text: varṇāntaramavikāraḥ // Jaim_1,1.16 //
body.translated_text: 'A different phoneme is a non-modification [of the original].' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.16 //

body.text: nādavṛddhiparā // Jaim_1,1.17 //
body.translated_text: 'The augment [of vowels] is not ultimate [i.e., does not prove non-eternality].' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.17 //

body.text: nityastu syāddarśanasya parārthatvāt // Jaim_1,1.18 //
body.translated_text: 'But [the word] must be eternal, since the perception is for another's sake.' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.18 //

body.text: sarvatra yaugapadyāt // Jaim_1,1.19 //
body.translated_text: 'Because of simultaneity everywhere.' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.19 //

body.text: saṃkhyābhāvāt // Jaim_1,1.20 //
body.translated_text: 'Because of the absence of number.' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.20 //

body.text: anapekṣatvāt // Jaim_1,1.21 //
body.translated_text: 'Because of [its] independence.' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.21 //

body.text: prakhyābhāvācca yogasya // Jaim_1,1.22 //
body.translated_text: 'And because of the absence of perception of a [creative] connection.' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.22 //

body.text: liṅgadarśanācca // Jaim_1,1.23 //
body.translated_text: 'And because of the observation of a mark [of eternality].' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.23 //
