body.translated_text: 'And because of the observation of a mark [of eternality].' // <s>Jaim</s>. 1.1.23 //

body.text: śabdasyārthapratyāyayakatvaṃ svābhāvikamiti yadaktaṃ tadākṣipyate- śabdasyānityatvāt, na hyabhinavasya śabdasya
body.translated_text: What has been stated — that the capacity of words to convey meaning is natural — is now challenged: because of the non-eternality of words. For one cannot apprehend the natural meaning-conveying capacity of a novel word

body.text:
vṛddhavyavahāraparamparayā svābhāvikaṃ pratyāyakatvaṃ śakyate gṛhītum, agṛhītamapicetsvabhāvataścakṣurādivatpratyāyayet prathamaśravaṇe 'pi pratyāyayet, tasmādanityatve śabdasya devadattādiśabdavatpuruṣakṛtameva pratyāyakatvamāpadyate /
kathaṃ punarityatvaṃ śabdasya, prayatnānabhivyaṅgyatve sati tadanantaramupalabdherghaṭādivattajjanyatvamadhyavasīyate /
anyathā kimiti tadanantaramevopalabhyate na pūrvaṃ, upalabdhasya ca drāgeva tirobhāvādvināśitvamadhyavasīyateṣa nacāsiddhamanabhivyaṅgyatvam, abhivyaktyayogāt /

children.text: sā hi pratibandhakanirāsena vā saṃskāraviśeṣānena vā /
children.translated_text: For that [manifestation] would be either through the removal of an obstruction or through a particular refinement (<s>saṃskāra</s>).

children.text: na tāvatpratibandhanirāsaḥ- pratibandhakānupalabdheḥ /
children.translated_text: First, it is not the removal of an obstruction — because no obstruction is perceived.

children.text: stimitā vāyavaḥ śrotramācchādyāvasthitāḥ śabdopalabdhiṃ pratibadhnanti, teṣu prayatnotthāpitaiḥ kauṣṭhyairvāyubhirutsāriteṣūpalabhyate śabda iti cet /
children.translated_text: [If one says] 'the still air-currents, covering the ear, obstruct the perception of sound; when they are displaced by the abdominal air-currents set in motion by effort, the sound is perceived' —

children.text: evaṃ tarhi sarve śabdāḥ śrotraṃ prāpyāvasthitāḥ pratibandhakeṣūtsariteṣu yugapacchrūyeran* ////
children.translated_text: Then all sounds, stationed at the ear, would be heard simultaneously when the obstructions are displaced. ////

body.translated_text: through the tradition of the usage of the learned. Moreover, if even without apprehension [of the convention], [the word] were to convey meaning naturally, like the eye and the like, it should convey meaning even at the first hearing. Therefore, if words are non-eternal, their capacity to convey meaning, like the words '<s>Devadatta</s>' and the like, would be merely human-made. But how is the word non-eternal? Since it is not manifested by effort, and since it is perceived immediately after [effort], its product-nature is inferred, like a pot and the like. Otherwise, why is it perceived only immediately after [effort] and not before? And since what has been perceived quickly disappears, its destructibility is inferred. And it is not the case that its being non-manifestable is unestablished — because manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>) is untenable.

children.text: atha saṃskārādhānaṃ tatrāpi traividhyaṃ- śabdasya vā saṃskāramādadhyuḥ kauṣṭhyā vāyavaḥ śrotrasya vā ubhayorvā /
children.translated_text: Now, regarding the application of a refinement (<s>saṃskāra</s>) — even there, there is a threefold [possibility]: the abdominal air-currents would apply the refinement either to the sound, or to the ear, or to both.

children.text: śabdasya cet tasyaikatvātsarvagatatvādanavayavasaṃskārāyogāt srudhnasthairvāyubhiḥ saṃskṛtaḥ śabdaḥ pāṭaliputrepyupalabhyeta, tadidamuktaṃ- tatra sarvaiḥ pratīyeta ityādinā /
children.translated_text: If to the sound — since it is one, all-pervading, and without parts, and therefore incapable of being refined in parts — the sound refined by the air-currents at the throat would be perceived even in <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. This is what is stated: 'there, it would be perceived by all' and so on.

children.text: śrotrasaṃskārapakṣe 'pyayamevadoṣaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: The same fault [applies] in the case of the ear-refinement view as well. ////

children.text: yadi kāṇādakāpilavaidikamatenākāśamahaṅkāro digvā śrotraṃ tasyaikatvātsarvagatatvādanavayavatvācca sarvapaṃsāmekameva śrotraṃ syāttaccaikadeśasthairapi dhvānābhiḥ saṃska-tamiti kaḥ sarveṣāṃ śabdopalabdhiṃ vārayet /
children.translated_text: If according to the <s>Kāṇāda</s>, <s>Kāpila</s>, and Vedic view, ether (<s>ākāśa</s>), <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, or the direction (<s>dik</s>) is the organ of hearing — since it is one, all-pervading, and without parts, the organ of hearing would be one and the same for all people. And if that [organ] is refined even by sounds located in one place — then who would prevent the perception of sounds for all?

children.text: tadidam- ākāśaśrotrapakṣecetyādinā śrotrāderiyameva digityantena darśitam /
children.translated_text: This has been shown in the passage beginning with: 'If on the view that ether is the ear' — ending with: 'this alone is the direction of the ear and the like.'

children.text: asmiṃśca pakṣe śrotrasya sarvaśabdasādharaṇatvādekaśabdopalabdhyarthamapi saṃskṛtaṃ śrotraṃ prasaṅgātsarvānśabdānghaṭārthonmīlitamiva netraṃ samānadeśasthānpaṭādīnavabodhayet /
children.translated_text: And on this view, since the organ of hearing is common to all sounds, even when refined for the perception of one sound, the refined ear, by entailment, would reveal all sounds — like the eye opened for a pot, which also reveals cloths and the like in the same location.

children.text: tadidaṃ- sakṛcca saṃskṛtaṃ śrotramityādinā darśitam* ////
children.translated_text: This has been shown in the passage beginning with: 'And the ear, once refined' and so on. ////

children.text: ayaṃ ca doṣaḥ pūrvopakṣipte 'pi śabdasaṃskārapakṣe darśayitavyaḥ- sarve hi śabdāḥ śrotradeśe 'vasthitāstatraikasminsaṃkriyamāṇe balādanyeṣāmapi saṃskāraḥ syādeva /
children.translated_text: This fault should also be shown in the previously challenged view of sound-refinement: for all sounds stationed at the location of the ear — when one is being refined there — by force, the others too would inevitably be refined.

children.text: na hi samānadeśānāṃ samānendriyagrāhyāṇāṃ kasyacitsaṃskāraḥ kasyaciccāsaṃskāra iti vyavasthā saṃbhavati ghaṭādāvadarśanāt, tadidamuktaṃ- etadeva prasaṃktavyam ityādinā* ////
children.translated_text: For it is not possible to establish that, among things in the same location graspable by the same sense-organ, some are refined and others are not — since such [selectivity] is not observed in the case of pots and the like. This is what is stated: 'this very [fault] should be raised' and so on. ////

children.text: ubhayasaṃskārapakṣe tūbhaye 'pi doṣāḥ samuccitya darśayitavyāḥ, tathā sati hi kaiścideva kaścideva śabdaḥ śrūyata ityupapadyate, anyathā śrotravyavasthā cobhayamapi na syāt /
children.translated_text: On the view that both [sound and ear] are refined, both faults should be shown in combination. For only then [would it be the case that] a certain sound is heard by certain [people] — otherwise, there would be neither sound-differentiation nor ear-differentiation.

children.text: kica nānādeśasthaiśca vaktṛbhiruccāritaḥ śabdo yugapannānādeśeṣūpalabhyate tadekasya nityasyānupapannamiti śā0 bhāṣyam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, a sound uttered by speakers in different locations is perceived simultaneously in different locations. That is untenable for a single eternal [entity] — thus the <s>Śābara-Bhāṣya</s>.

children.text: tatra nityasyānupapannamiti pratijñā, ekasyeti hetuḥ, nityo hyasevakaḥ syāt ekasyānupapannaṃ nānādeśeṣūpalambhanamiti* ////
children.translated_text: Therein, 'untenable for an eternal [entity]' is the proposition; 'for a single [entity]' is the reason. For an eternal [entity] would be without parts; and perception of a single [partless entity] in different locations is untenable. ////

body.text:
nanu nāvaśyatvaṃ nityatve satyekatvaṃ bhavati, anekānyeva hi gakārādīni nityāni bhavantvityata āha- asati viśeṣe nityasya nānekatvam(śābhā) iti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- pratyabhijñākhyaviśeṣyapratyayabalena hyastanādyatanagakārayorekatvāvagamānnityatvamāśrīyate /
asticāsāvaviśeṣapratyayo yugapannānāvaktṛbhiruccārite 'pi gakāre nahi tatrāpi pratyayaviśeṣo 'sti, asati ca viśeṣe nityasya nānekatvaṃ saṃbhavati /
anekatve hi pratyabhijñāyā aprāmāṇyamasmākamiva bhavato 'pi syāt tadaprāmāṇyeca
body.translated_text: Objection: There is no necessity that, if eternal, [the word must be] one. Let the individual phonemes 'ga' and the like be many and each eternal. To this he says: 'in the absence of distinction, a plurality of the eternal is not [possible].' This is what is said: by the force of the recognition-cognition — 'the ga of yesterday and the ga of today are one' — from the apprehension of unity, eternality is resorted to. And that very cognition of non-distinction exists even when 'ga' is uttered simultaneously by different speakers — for there too, there is no distinct cognition. And in the absence of distinction, a plurality of the eternal is not possible. For if there were plurality, the invalidity of recognition would follow for you just as for us; and if recognition is invalid,

body.text: nityatvānupapattiḥ, tasmānnityatve satyekatvamaṅgīkartavyam, ekasya cānupapannaṃ nānādeśopalambhanamiti* ////
body.translated_text: eternality becomes untenable. Therefore, if eternal, oneness must be accepted; and perception of a single [entity] in different locations is untenable. ////

body.text: vārtike 'pi- yaugapadyopalambhādvā bhedo bhedācca kāryateti dvayamupakṣipya yathāyaugapadyopalambhādbhedo bhavati tathā darśitam- avibhutve hi yugapadityādinā tathā darśitam- nityatve tvekabuddhiḥ syāditi /

children.text: na hi nityatvavādinā pratyabhijñāyā bhrāntitvamiṣyate /
children.translated_text: For the proponent of eternality does not accept that recognition is erroneous.

children.text: tathā ca vakṣyate- api caikarūpye sati deśabhedena kāmaṃ deśā eva bhinnāḥ syurnatu śabdaḥ iti /
children.translated_text: And thus it will be said: 'Moreover, when there is identity of form, by the difference of locations, let the locations alone be different, not the word.'

children.text: na hi tadaprāmāṇye nityatvaṃ siddhyati pramāṇāntarābhāvāt, ato nityatve satyekatvaṃ syāttacca nānādeśopalambhena virudhyata iti, tataśca yaugapadyopalambhādbhedo bhede ca pratyabhijñāyā aprāmāṇyaṃ tadaprāmāṇye ca nityatvābhāvātkāryatvaṃ- tadetadānupūrvyaṃ svatantrasiddham /
children.translated_text: For if that [recognition] were invalid, eternality could not be established, due to the absence of another means of knowledge. Therefore, if eternal, there would be oneness, and that is contradicted by the perception in different locations. And thus, from the perception of simultaneity there is difference, and from difference the invalidity of recognition, and from that invalidity, the absence of eternality, hence product-nature — this entire sequence is independently established.

children.text: dṛḍhe cānityatve jīpavatsādṛśyātpratyabhijñā bhavati tasmādanityaḥ śabda iti prāpte //
children.translated_text: And when non-eternality is firmly established, recognition arises due to similarity, as with cows. Therefore, the word is non-eternal — so the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> concludes. //

body.translated_text: In the <s>Vārttika</s> too — having raised the two [arguments]: 'from the perception of simultaneity there is difference, and from difference there is product-nature' — it has been shown how from the perception of simultaneity there is difference: by the passage beginning with 'for if not all-pervading, simultaneously' and so on; similarly shown: 'but if eternal, there would be a single cognition.'

body.text: śabdanityatvopapādam /
body.translated_text: Justification of the eternality of words:

body.text:
abhidhīyate- prayatnānantaraṃ dṛṣṭairnaikāntyātkāryatā dhvaneḥ /
tadabhivyaṅgyapakṣe 'pi yujyate tatra darśanam /

children.text: yattu kathamabhivyaṅgyatvamiti, śrotrasaṃskāreṇeti brūmaḥ /
children.translated_text: As for [the question] 'how is it manifestable?' — we say: through the refinement of the ear.

children.text: yattvākāśasyāhaṅkārasya vā śrotratve tatsaṃskāratve ca sarvatra puṃsāmupalabdhiḥ syādityuktaṃ tatra brūmaḥ- yadi tayoḥ śrotratve bhavedayaṃ doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: As for the objection that 'if ether or <s>ahaṅkāra</s> were the organ of hearing, and if that [organ] were refined, there would be perception [of all sounds] for all people everywhere' — to that we say: that fault would arise if those two were the organ of hearing.

children.text: tatkarṇaśaṣkulībhavatu śrotraṃ sā ca pratipuruṣaṃ bhinneti nātiprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Let the ear-conch (<s>karṇaśaṣkulī</s>) be the organ of hearing — and that is different for each person; hence there is no over-extension.

children.text: yadyapi cākāśameva śrotraṃ tattu na sākṣātsaṃskriyate kintvadhiṣṭhānadvāreṇa, tataśca yadyapi śrotraṃ sarveṣāmekaṃ tathāpyadhiṣṭhānaṃ bhinnatvātsaṃskāravyavasthayā śravaṇasya vyavasthā bhaviṣyati* ////
children.translated_text: And even if ether itself is the organ of hearing, it is not directly refined, but [only] through the intermediary of the bodily substratum (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>). And thus, even though the organ of hearing is one for all, nevertheless, since the substratum is different [for each person], through the differentiation of the refinement, the differentiation of hearing will be established. ////

body.translated_text: It is replied: 'The product-nature of sound is [inferred] from the observation of [things perceived] after effort; but since there is no invariable concomitance, [that inference is not conclusive]. Even on the view that [the sound] is manifested by that [effort], the observation [of the sound after effort] is justified.'

children.text: nanvekatvesatīndriyasya yadyapyadhiṣṭhānāni bhinnāni tathāpyekenāpyadhiṣṭhānena saṃskṛtenendriyasya saṃskṛtatvātsarvapuṃsāmindriyaṃ saṃskṛtamiti sarveṣāmupalabdhiḥ syādeva /
children.translated_text: Objection: If the sense-organ is one, even though the substrata are different, nonetheless, when refined through even one substratum, the sense-organ as a whole becomes refined — hence the organ is refined for all people, and perception would [arise] for all.

children.text: taduktaṃ- nanvekasminnadhiṣṭhāne labdhasaṃskāramindriyam //
children.translated_text: This is stated: 'But when the sense-organ has received refinement at one substratum,'

body.text:
bodhakaṃ sarvahetuṣu syādekendriyavādinaḥ iti /
sarvadehavartināṃ puṃsāmityarthaḥ /
atrottaram- puṃsāṃ dehapradeśeṣu syādekendriyavādinaḥ iti /
sarvadehavartināṃ puṃsāmityarthaḥ /
atrottaram- puṃsāṃ dehapradeśeṣu
body.translated_text: 'it should be capable of revealing all objects — [so say] the proponents of a single sense-organ.' The meaning is: for people in all bodies. The reply to this: 'For people, in the locations of the body,'

children.text: vijñānotpattiriṣyate /
children.translated_text: 'the arising of cognition is accepted.'

children.text: tena pradhānavaideśyādviguṇā sā tu saṃskṛtiḥ iti /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, because of the remoteness from the principal [cognition], that refinement is doubly [qualified].'

children.text: ayamarthaḥ- svaśarīra eva bhogyāyatane sarvapuṃsāmapi jñānamutpadyate nānyatra, śabdajñānāṅgaṃ cāyamadhiṣṭhānasaṃskāraḥ pradhānasamānadeśatvaṃ cāṅgānāṃ guṇastena dehantaravartinaḥ puruṣasya yastvadehe niṣpādayitavyaṃ vijñānaṃ tasya taddehagata eva saṃskāro niṣpādako bhavati na dehāntaragataḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: cognition arises for all people only in their own bodies, which are the receptacle of experience, not elsewhere. And this refinement of the substratum is an auxiliary to sound-cognition, and the co-location with the principal [cognition] is a [necessary] quality of the auxiliaries. Therefore, for a person in another body, the refinement located in your body produces the cognition to be accomplished in that body [alone], not [the refinement] located in another body.

children.text: sā hi tatpradhānabhūtena jñānena videśatvādviguṇaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: For that [refinement], being remote from the principal cognition [of the other person], is doubly [disqualified]. ////

children.text: nanu saṃskāryasyaikatvāttaddūratvācca saṃskārāṅgabhāvasya deśabhedo 'kiñcitkara eva, yathā barhirekatvāttatsaṃskārāṇāmatithyākālānāmapyupasadagrīṣomīyāṅgātvaṃ na vihanyate tadvadatrāpi syāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: Since the thing to be refined is one, and since the status as auxiliary is remote from that [one thing], the difference of location is of no consequence — just as due to the oneness of the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass), the status of its refinements, the <s>atithya</s> and the like, as auxiliaries of the <s>upasad</s> and <s>grīṣomīya</s> [rites], is not obstructed — so too should it be here.

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: adarśanāt /
children.translated_text: Because it is not observed.

children.text: nahyekasminnadhiṣṭhāne sarveṣāṃ jñānamupalabhyate, ataḥ sādhāraṇamapīndriyaṃ vijñānasamānadesasaṃskārasacivameva jñānamukatpādayati nānyatheti darśanabalādadhyavasīyate tato nātiprasaṅgaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: For the cognition of all [people] does not arise at a single substratum. Therefore, it is determined by the force of observation that even a common sense-organ produces cognition only when assisted by refinement in the same location as the cognition — not otherwise. Hence there is no over-extension. ////

children.text: nacāvaśyamekamevendriyaṃ- yadyapyākāśamekamanavayavaṃ ca tathāpi tasya prādeśikairghaṭādibhirye saṃyogāste 'pi prādeśikāstataśca karṇaśaṣkulīsaṃyogānāṃ pratipuruṣaṃ bhinnatvāttadavacchinnasya cākāśasya śrotratvātsatyapi svarūpaikatve 'vacchinnarūpāṇāṃ śrotrāṇāṃ bhedādvyavasthāsiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor is it necessary that the sense-organ be only one — for even though ether is one and without parts, nonetheless, its conjunctions with spatially delimited things like pots and the like are also spatially delimited. And thus, since the conjunctions with the ear-conch are different for each person, and since ether delimited by those [conjunctions] is the organ of hearing — even though there is identity of essential nature, from the difference of the delimited organs of hearing, the establishment of differentiation [of perception is achieved].

children.text: evamahaṅkārabhāge digbhāge vā śrotre draṣṭavyam* ////
children.translated_text: Similarly, this should be understood when the organ of hearing is a portion of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> or a portion of direction (<s>dik</s>). ////

body.text: yattu sakṛcca saṃskṛtaṃ śrotraṃ sarvaśabdānprakāśayedityuktaṃ, tatrocyate- dhvanayo hi tālvādisthānaviśeṣasaṃparkādvijātīyā vilakṣaṇasāmarthyānniṣpadyante, tataśca kaścideva dhvaniḥ kasyacicchabdasyānuguṇaṃ saṃskāramādhatte na sarvasādhāraṇamityupalabdhivyavasthā kalpyate śabdasaṃskārapakṣe 'pi kaścideva dhvaniḥ kañcicchabdaṃ
body.translated_text: As for the objection that 'the ear, once refined, would reveal all sounds' — to that it is replied: sounds, being produced through contact with specific locations such as the palate and the like, are of diverse types and have distinct capacities. Therefore, a particular sound applies a refinement suitable to a particular word, not one common to all — thus the differentiation of perception is established. Even on the view of sound-refinement, a particular sound

children.text: saṃskaroti na sarvaḥ sarvamiti yuktataraiva vyavasthā /
children.translated_text: refines a particular word, not every [sound refines] every [word] — thus the differentiation is more reasonable.

children.text: dṛṣṭāca samānendriyagrāhyāṇāmapyabhivyañjakavyavasthā- sāvitraṃ hi tejo ghaṭādīnāmevābhivyañjakaṃ na nakṣatrāṇāṃ, nimbatvak candanagandhasyaivābhivyañjikā na gandhāntarāṇāṃ, tasmādadoṣaḥ* ////
children.translated_text: And the differentiation of manifestors is indeed observed even for things graspable by the same sense-organ: for solar light is the manifestor of pots and the like alone, not of stars; the bark of the neem tree is the manifestor of sandalwood fragrance alone, not of other fragrances. Therefore, there is no fault. ////

body.text: na ca śabdasaṃskāre sarvapuṃsāmupalabdiprasaṅgaḥ- dhvanīnāṃ prādeśikatvāttaddeśe śabdaḥ saṃskriyate na sarvatra, ataḥ saṃskṛtena śabdena yasyendriyaṃ saṃnikṛṣṭaṃ sa eva śṛṇoti nānya ityupapannam //
body.translated_text: Nor is there the over-extension of perception for all people in the case of sound-refinement: since sounds are spatially delimited, the word is refined at that [particular] location, not everywhere. Therefore, only that person whose sense-organ is in proximity with the refined word hears — not another. This is justified. //

body.text: śabdasyānekadeśopalambhaḥ //
body.translated_text: The perception of the word in multiple locations: //

body.text: yugapaddeśabhedaśca syādekasya sūryavat //
body.translated_text: 'And the [perception in] different locations simultaneously is possible for a single [entity], like the sun.' //

body.text: ye vindhyanilayā ye ca kāmarūpe vyavasthitāḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Those who dwell in the <s>Vindhya</s> [mountains] and those who are established in <s>Kāmarūpa</s>' //

body.text: prāgbhāge hyātmanaḥ sarvairudyanbhāsvānnirīkṣyate //
body.translated_text: 'in the eastern part, by all, the rising sun is observed;' //

body.text: pratyagbhāve tathāstaṃ yanmadhyāhne copari sthitaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'in the western part, [it is seen] as setting; and at noon, as stationed above;' //

body.text: bhinnāśca teṣāṃ prāgbhāgāstathā pratyak tathopari //
body.translated_text: 'and their eastern parts are different, and so the western, and so above;' //

body.text: teṣvasya dṛśyamānasya vispaṣṭā bhinnadeśatā //
body.translated_text: 'for this [sun] being seen by them, the perception in different locations is evident.' //

children.text: tathā yasminyāvaddūre deśe kaiścitsūryodayo dṛśyate taddeśavartino 'nyepi tataḥ parastāttāvati paśyanti tato 'pyasti bhedābhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, at whatever distant location some [people] see the sunrise, others at that very distance from that location also see it — hence there is both difference and non-difference [of location].

children.text: na ca sūryanānātvamāśaṅkanīyam, na hi kecidbhinnaṃ sūryaṃ paśyanti* ////
children.translated_text: And the plurality of the sun should not be suspected — for nobody sees a different sun. ////

body.text: ki punarekadeśasthasyaiva saviturnānādeśopalambhe kāraṇam, ucyate- atidūravartino 'sya yathāvaddeśamajānantaḥ svasaṃnidhimadhyasyanto deśabhedaṃ manyante /

children.text: vispaṣṭaṃ caitat /
children.translated_text: And this is quite clear.

children.text: tathāhi- yo 'parāhne yasminyāvaddūre deśe sūryaṃ paśyati- asminkṣetre 'sminparvate sūryaḥ iti, sa savitāramīkṣamāṇa eva taddeśe gatastataḥ parastāttathaiva taṃ paśyati tenāvagamyate sarveṣāṃ deśānāmagrataḥ sthito 'sau saṃnihitavadavabhāsata iti /
children.translated_text: For thus: one who, in the afternoon, sees the sun at whatever far-off location — 'the sun is on this field, on this mountain' — that same person, while still looking at the sun, having gone to that place and then beyond it, sees it in the same way. From this it is understood that [the sun], standing ahead of all locations, appears as if proximate.

children.text: ye cādityāpekṣayā stokadeśāḥ parvatāste 'pi dviyojanasthitānāṃ triyojanasthitānāṃ ca puruṣāṇāṃ tulyavadavabhāsante, tasmādekatve 'pi saṃbhavati nānādeśopalambhaḥ /
children.translated_text: And mountains too, which are small in comparison to the sun, appear the same to persons standing at two <s>yojanas</s> and to those standing at three <s>yojanas</s>. Therefore, even though [the sun is] one, perception from various locations is possible.

children.text: tathaikameva mukhaṃ bhinneṣvādarśeṣu yugapaddṛśyate* ////
children.translated_text: Likewise, a single face is seen simultaneously in multiple mirrors.

body.translated_text: What then is the cause of the perception of the sun, which exists in a single location, from various places? It is replied: since those who are very far from it do not know its actual location, and superimpose [the notion of] proximity to themselves, they think there is a difference of location.

body.text:
nanu pratibimbaṃ nāmārthāntaraṃ tatra dṛśyate /
na /

children.text: tasyābhāvādanupalambhācca, na hi mūrtamadhye mūrtāntaraṃ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: because it does not exist and is not observed. For a corporeal [entity] cannot exist within another corporeal [entity].

children.text: kiṃ ca śarāvasthamudakaṃ bhūmerupari nābhidadhne dhārayitvā tasyopariṣṭādaratridadhne svamukhaṃ kurvannudakasyādhastādaratrimātre mukhapratibimbaṃ paśyati, tasmiṃśca deśe pārśvasthāḥ puruṣā na kañcidapi paśyanti tena dṛśyādarśananirastaḥ pratibimbākhyor'tho na śakyo 'bhyupagantum /
children.translated_text: Moreover, one who holds water in a shallow vessel above the ground, placing it at navel-height, and positions his face at a distance of half-a-cubit above the water, sees the reflection of his face at a distance of half-a-cubit below the water. But persons standing beside [him] see nothing at all in that location. Therefore, since the visible [reflection] is negated by non-observation, the entity called 'reflection' cannot be accepted.

children.text: tasmādādarśatejasā jalena ca pratihataṃ nāyanaṃ tejaḥ parāvṛttyā gṛhṇātīti yuktam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is proper [to hold] that the visual ray, reflected by the luster of the mirror or by water, apprehends [the face] through reflection [of the ray].

children.text: tasmādanaikāntiko nānādeśopalambho na nānātvaṃ śabdasya sādhayati* ////
children.translated_text: Therefore, the perception from various locations, being non-conclusive [as evidence], does not establish the multiplicity of sound.

body.translated_text: Objection: what is seen there is a reflection, which is a different entity. No —

children.text: nanu savituḥ sāṃnidhyādhyāsādyuktā nānādeśāvagatiḥ śabde tu katham /
children.translated_text: Objection: the perception from various locations is justified in the case of the sun through the superimposition of proximity, but how [is it justified] in the case of sound?

children.text: sarvagatatvāt- sarvagato hi śabdo bhinnadeśairdhvanibhiḥ svesve deśe 'bhivyajyamāno bhinnadeśo 'vabhāsate, dhvanayo hi śrotradeśamāgatyāpi śabdaṃ vyañjayantaḥ svotpattidesamiva śabdaṃ bhāsayantīti darśanabalādabhyupagamyate* ////
children.translated_text: Because [sound is] all-pervading. For sound, being all-pervading, when manifested in their respective locations by resonances (<s>dhvani</s>) in different places, appears to be in different places. It is understood through the force of observation that the resonances, even when they reach the location of the ear, while manifesting the sound, cause the sound to appear as if at the location of their own origination.

body.text:
nanu prāpyakāri śrotraṃ, na ca dhvanyutpattideśaḥ śrotreṇa prāpyata iti kathaṃ tasya śrotreṇa grahaṇam, tadagrahe ca kathaṃ tadviśiṣṭaśabdagrahaḥ /
ucyate- nāyaṃ śrotratastadviśiṣṭaśabdapratyayaḥ, kiṃ tu śrotraṃ gi svadeśasthitaṃ śabdaṃ bodhayadapi na deśaviśiṣṭaṃ bodhayati kintu svarūpamātreṇa, yatastu diśa āgatā dhvanayastayā viśiṣṭaṃ śabdaṃ bodayanti, sā hi dik śrotraprāptā śakyate śrotreṇa grahītum, yadyapi na svātantryeṇa diśaḥ śrotragrāhyatvaṃ tathāpi rāve gṛhyamāṇe tadviśeṣaṇatayā atha ca viṣayeṣu sveṣu gṛhyamāṇeṣu tadviśeṣaṇatayā sarvairapīndriyairgṛhyate tadvat /
tataścāsyāṃ diśi śabda iti viśiṣṭagrahaṇaṃ tāvatsiddham /
body.translated_text: Objection: the auditory organ operates by contact, and the location of the resonance's origination is not reached by the ear — so how is it apprehended by the ear? And if that [location] is not apprehended, how is sound as qualified by that location apprehended? It is replied: this cognition of sound as qualified by [a particular] location does not arise from the ear. Rather, the ear, while producing awareness of the sound situated in its own location, does not produce awareness of it as qualified by location — [it produces awareness of the sound] only in its intrinsic nature. But the resonances that have come from a [particular] direction produce awareness of the sound as qualified by that [direction]. For that direction, having reached the ear, can be apprehended by the ear. Although the direction is not independently apprehensible by the ear, still — just as when color is being apprehended, [its qualifiers] are apprehended by that [visual sense] as qualifiers of it, and also when objects are being apprehended in their own [domains], [spatial direction] is apprehended by all the senses as their qualifier — so too [with sound and direction]. Therefore, the apprehension of [sound] as qualified by direction — 'the sound is in this direction' — is at least established.
